# Autodesk Fusion 360 `.f3d`: Format Specification

> **License:** This document is released under [CC-BY-4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Attribute to the cadmpeg project.

---

Record offsets, field widths, and endianness are also maintained as a machine-checked table in [`docs/layouts/f3d.md`](../layouts/f3d.md), generated from `docs/layouts/f3d.toml`. That table is the canonical source for the numbers; the prose below carries the semantics. `cargo test -p cadmpeg --test layout_tables` proves the two agree.

## 1. Container layer

`.f3d` is a **ZIP archive**. Entries may be stored, DEFLATE-compressed, or compressed with **zstd (ZIP method 93)**.

### 1.1 Payload families

| Path pattern                                                                     | Role                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<folder>/Breps.BlobParts/*.smb`, `*.smbh`                                       | ASM/ACIS exact B-rep streams, binary encoding (§2)                                                                                                                    |
| `<folder>/Breps.BlobParts/*.sat`, `*.smt`                                        | ASM/ACIS exact B-rep streams, text encoding (§1.1.3)                                                                                                                  |
| `<folder>/ProteinAssets.BlobParts/*.protein`                                     | nested ZIP archives with appearance/material assets                                                                                                                   |
| `<folder>/Design1/BulkStream.dat` (or `FusionDesignSegmentType1/BulkStream.dat`) | design recipes, material assignments, body map                                                                                                                        |
| `<folder>/*/MetaStream.dat`                                                      | per-segment object tables (GUID → entity-type registry)                                                                                                               |
| `<folder>/FusionACTSegmentType1/BulkStream.dat`                                  | Active Component Tree entity/appearance tables                                                                                                                        |
| `<folder>/FusionBrowserSegmentType1/BulkStream.dat`                              | Fusion UI browser tree                                                                                                                                                |
| `<folder>/Previews/*`, `<folder>/Images.BlobParts/*`                             | thumbnails / appearance images; never geometry                                                                                                                        |
| `<folder>/ParaMeshGeometry.BlobParts/*.paramesh`                                 | mesh-body geometry containers (§1.1.2)                                                                                                                                |
| `<folder>/OGS.BlobFolder/OGS/<scene>/*`                                          | display scene graph (`world`) and its vertex and index buffer arenas (`stream_mesh_NNN`, `Fusion_mesh_NNN`); each drawable node carries the design entity ID it draws |
| `<folder>/TSplines.BlobParts/*.tsm`                                              | T-spline control-cage source of Form bodies; the exact face geometry is the B-rep stream's `t_spl_sur` carriers                                                       |
| `Manifest.dat` (top-level and per-asset)                                         | document, asset, and segment registry (see §1.3)                                                                                                                      |
| `RedirectionsStream.dat` (top-level)                                             | external-reference table (see §1.4)                                                                                                                                   |
| `ComponentReferenceData.json` (top-level)                                        | component-reference slot (see §1.4)                                                                                                                                   |

`<folder>` is an asset-folder path component.

In an OGS `world` scene graph, each drawable node has zero or more attributes. An attribute is a length-prefixed name, a five-byte prologue, and its payload. A `VisibilityAttribute` payload is one byte with value `0` or `1`. On sketch-curve nodes, this value is drawable render-cache state. It does not give the display visibility of the owning Sketch. Sketch display visibility is in the typed Design sketch-container member (§3.1).

### 1.1.1 Form control cages

A `TSplines.BlobParts/*.tsm` entry is a UTF-8, line-oriented `TS0200` control-cage program. The first line is `#TS0200`. Its fixed declarations are `degree 3`, `cap-type`, `star-smoothness`, `units`, `end-conditions`, and `star-knot-rule`. Geometry coordinates are centimetres irrespective of the declarative `units 1 meters` line.

Topology uses zero-based indices in record order. An `f root flags` record defines a face and one half-edge in its boundary. An `e root scalar` record defines an edge and one of its two half-edges; `scalar` is a positive f64 knot interval, symmetric for both half-edges, and is nominally one. A `v root direction` record defines a control vertex. An `l next previous mate vertex face edge flags` record defines a half-edge: `next` and `previous` are reciprocal within a face ring, `mate` is reciprocal across an edge, `vertex` is the half-edge's terminal control vertex, `face` is the owning face index or `-1` on a boundary mate, and `edge` is the index of the owning edge. An `e` root and its mate carry the same `edge` value, and that value is the `e` record's own index. Starting at an `f` root and following `next` yields that face's directed edge ring. For an `e` root, the directed edge runs from the mate's terminal vertex to the root's terminal vertex. Every half-edge belongs to exactly one `e` root pair. An `ec edge flags` record marks the indexed edge as a crease. Vertex subdivision tags follow crease incidence: zero crease edges is smooth, one is dart, two is crease, and three or more is corner.

Each `106ek value` record is one cell of extension 106, the user-knot-interval
override vector. Its ordinal addresses the same ordinal `e` slot, including
deleted slots. Exact `-1.0` means no override: the effective interval is the
base interval stored by `e`. A finite value greater than or equal to zero is
an explicit override. Zero is a present interval and produces a repeated
knot. An explicit value equal to the base interval remains present. A deleted
edge slot requires exact `-1.0`.

A typed user-knot run has exactly one record per `e` slot, forms one
uninterrupted block after the final `e` record, and has valid finite values.
An incomplete, split, displaced, or invalid run remains native T-spline state.
An end-condition declaration does not create extension 106. The
`SUBD_CREASES` mirror form explicitly repeats each live edge's base interval
and stores `-1` for each deleted slot; these values have the same override
semantics as the independent intervals in a `MULTIPLE_KNOTS` form.

The user override follows the edge through an identity-preserving edit. A
writer emits one value per source edge slot when the extension is present:
the preserved override for a live edge, or `-1` for an inherited interval,
a deleted slot, or a new edge with no supplied override. Removing the extension
and assigning zero to every live edge are distinct operations. Neither
operation changes the base interval stored by `e`.

A bare `f`, `e`, `v`, `l`, or `0g` token with no operands is a deleted slot, not a malformed line. It consumes an index in its record order and defines no element, so every index in the program counts bare and populated records alike; half-edge reciprocity closes only under that rule, and no half-edge names a deleted `l` slot. A deleted slot has no counterpart in the Design segment's per-element records, whose counts equal the populated token counts alone.

Each `0g x y z weight` record defines a rational grip point. Without an explicit grip map, the grip records correspond positionally to the `v` records. An explicit map starts with `0m odd-grip-map`; each following `0m gvp vertex` or `0m gv vertex` marker corresponds to the next `0g` record. A `gvp` marker assigns that point to the indexed topology vertex, while `gv` marks a secondary grip. Every topology vertex has exactly one primary grip. The map has one marker per `0g` slot, counting deleted slots, and every marker precedes the first `0g` record. A deleted `0g` slot's marker is `0m gv -1`: the operand is signed, and `-1` is the only negative value and marks exactly the deleted slots.

A `0m cg vertex wedges S G` record describes the complete secondary-grip layout for one vertex and does not replace the primary topology map. The `root` operand of that vertex's `v root direction` record is the starting half-edge for its rotation fan. The fan follows `mate(next(h))`; each slot contributes `face(h)`, a face index or `-1` for the boundary gap. An interior vertex has one wedge per fan slot. A boundary vertex has `max(valence, 4)` wedges, with the missing slots inserted immediately after the gap slot as phantom slots. Phantom slots have no edge or sector face and their spoke length is zero. The `direction` word is `NORTH`, `EAST`, `SOUTH`, or `WEST`; wedge zero is the north slot, so fan slot `(k + o) mod wedges` is wedge `k`, where `o` is respectively `0`, `1`, `2`, or `3`.

`S` has one spoke length per wedge in north-anchored order. `G` is the concatenation of each wedge's block: `S[k]` spoke grips nearest-first, followed by `S[k] * S[(k + 1) mod wedges]` sector grips in row-major spoke order. A sector block belongs to the face following wedge `k`; a boundary-gap sector retains its full arity and uses `-1` entries for absent grips. The run length is not written and is `sum(S[k] + S[k] * S[(k + 1) mod wedges])`, fixing the record's arity at `2 + wedges + len(G)`. Every nonnegative entry of `G` indexes a secondary `0g` grip of the same vertex exactly once; `-1` marks an absent slot. A vertex with secondary grips has exactly one `0m cg` record, and a vertex without secondary grips has none. The `0m odd-grip-map` header precedes every `0m cg` record, and every grip-to-vertex marker precedes the first of them.

The terminal `tol` and `geom-tol` values are centimetres. `ver`, `behavior-version`, and `compat-version` identify the generating T-spline implementation. `100edges`, `100verts`, and `50000grip` records retain editor selections and do not change the committed cage topology.

A `105sym 0` record starts one cage-symmetry block. The following `105plane` record has twelve finite f64 coefficients arranged as three homogeneous columns: `(c0,c1,c2,c3)` is the plane origin, `(c4,c5,c6,c7)` is the first in-plane axis, and `(c8,c9,c10,c11)` is the second in-plane axis. The origin column ends in `1`; both axis columns end in `0`, and the two axes are unit and mutually orthogonal. The origin coordinates use the cage's centimetre coordinate scale; the neutral plane origin uses the same centimetre-to-millimetre conversion as `0g` points, while the axes are dimensionless and unchanged. Six `105a` correspondence records use the selectors `fr`, `er`, `vr`, `f`, `e`, and `v`. The remaining operands are index pairs. The `fr`, `er`, and `vr` maps name the forward face, edge, and vertex correspondences; `f`, `e`, and `v` contain their reverse correspondences. Every non-fixed pair occurs in both directions, and a fixed element occurs only as a self-pair in the forward map. All indices address populated slots in the corresponding topology-record domain. Symmetry correspondence describes editor state over the complete cage and does not add or remove neutral control-cage elements.

A `105sym 1` record starts a radial-symmetry editor block. Its `105plane` record has the same homogeneous plane-column layout and scale as a correspondence block. Its `105r segments` record has a positive integer `N`, and its `105r sweep` record has a finite f64 `W`. The six `105r ef`, `er`, `ff`, `fr`, `vf`, and `vr` records have an even number of native index operands, grouped as ordered source-target pairs. The first selector letter identifies the edge, face, or vertex domain. For `W = 1`, suffix `f` is the forward step by `+2*pi/N` and suffix `r` is the reverse step by `-2*pi/N`. The sweep scalar remains retained independently. The rotation axis is the cross product of the plane's first and second in-plane axes. The reverse relation is the pairwise inverse on resolved elements. An ordinary `N`-element orbit stores an `N-1`-pair directed path; it does not store the final wrap pair. Axial vertices can map to themselves.

In a domain with no deleted slots, an in-range radial operand is the same-numbered neutral element. A domain with deleted slots admits a neutral binding only where both raw-slot resolution and direct compact-index resolution produce the same live element. An out-of-range operand, disagreement between these resolutions, more than one source for the same target, or absence of an inverse pair prevents a neutral correspondence for the affected pair. The complete native map remains retained. A selector never falls through to another topology domain, a half-edge, a root index, or a geometric-nearest match. Forward face, edge, and vertex correspondences use `ff`, `ef`, and `vf` respectively. Raw reverse maps retain their selector and order. Persisted geometric inexactness does not change a topology-defined correspondence. A writer of dense all-live topology can use the neutral index as the native operand; a writer that retains deleted slots cannot infer a pre-deletion or post-deletion shift rule. The radial-symmetry records describe editor state over the complete cage and do not add or remove neutral control-cage elements.

An explicit Form cage-list record names its owning scope. After its indexed-record header, that record stores six zero bytes, `u8 1`, the owning scope's u64 record index, two zero bytes, a u32 cage count, and that many entries of `u8 1 + u64 cage-object reference + two zero bytes`. Its result-body bindings identify the B-rep bodies committed by the operation.

A class-325 Form cage table is 1850 bytes from its indexed header to its class-258 paired header and carries 32 entries. It stores nine zero bytes at offset 11, `u8 1` at offset 20, five zero bytes, a marked u64 result-record reference at offset 26, two zero bytes, and the u32 cage count at offset 37. The result-record reference names a class-407 record in the Form scope's reference members. The entries start at offset 41 and repeat every 30 bytes. Each class-325 Form cage entry is 30 bytes. Each entry stores a marked u64 class-289 cage-object reference, `u16 0`, a u64 type discriminator, a marked u64 class-273 companion reference, and `u16 0`. The 32 type discriminators are the values 307 through 338, each exactly once. The class-289 record is paired with class 258 and contains one marked u32 reference to a class-310 record. The frame's fixed tail follows the 32-entry run; the class-325 frame length is 890 plus 30 times its cage count.

A Form selection group has registered type `E079B079-016A-43C2-ACC7-9627B32A8960`, version 0, with base type `60F291CB-499B-4AB1-B0E5-340368671724`. It uses the counted selection envelope in §3.1. Its ordered members are EntityTracking records of type `C46D3EEB-40E1-43FA-83DC-9CB204335417`, version 1, with base type `FA85BB02-9D57-4E5E-A3A1-3D150C7ED082`. A member reference identifies a tracking record; it does not directly identify a cage object. The number of members and the number of T-spline entries do not establish a cage binding.

Each cage object reaches its surface through three indexed records. Its 200-byte class-301 record stores a marked u64 reference at offset 189 to a 33-byte class-373 wrapper. That wrapper stores ten zero bytes and a marked u64 reference at offset 21 to a 29-byte class-362 wrapper. The class-362 wrapper stores ten zero bytes and an unmarked u64 reference at offset 21 to a 665-byte class-457 record paired with class 264. The class-457 record stores the owning Form scope as a marked u64 reference at offset 317 and the cage surface as a marked u64 reference at offset 339.

A 132-byte Form serializer record stores ten zero bytes after its indexed header, the LP-UTF16 blob-part entry name `TSpline.<uuid>.tsm` at offset 21, and a marked u64 reference to the cage surface immediately after the name. Classes `315`, `349`, `360`, `431`, and `446` use the ordinary paired-header form. A class-335 serializer uses the same 132-byte primary frame followed by a class-331 header with a different record index; its fixed tail after the marked surface reference is zero, and its surface reference resolves to class `358`. The class-335 serializer is distinct from the 81-byte Form result-owner record. That entry name is the cage-to-archive join: every serializer name that has an active `TSplines.BlobParts` entry joins exactly one such entry. A serializer record can remain for a stale entry with no active blob part; that record does not add a neutral cage. The join is explicit, so it does not depend on archive order or on counting, and it divides the cages between two or more Form scopes. Each cage object's back reference agrees with the owning Form's cage list. A Form scope owns zero or more cages, and a document holding cages need not hold a Form scope; neither case changes the entry-name join. The `.tsm` program itself carries no identity and cannot be matched on content.

An ordinary Form serializer also admits an inline-typed same-segment surface reference from §3.1. Its inline GUID is the cage-surface type `22709494-9149-4A70-A829-7D748A7B5DB1`. The complete reference ends at the next indexed header.

A Form body record has type `FA1F0081-C9A1-4E14-8F25-D12DD868ED90`, version 9, 10, or 11, with base type `CB844AB6-240D-4FC9-9C9F-3679DC896D6F`. Its primary frame ends at its same-index paired header. Its first physical-material envelope contains four LP-UTF16 fields: an asset GUID, a library GUID or empty string, a material label or empty string, and a material token. The physical-material library id is `C1EEA57C-3F56-45FC-B8CB-A9EC46A9994C`. Tokens include `PrismMaterial-###` and `MaterialInv_###`. Four same-segment references follow the token. Each reference uses the eleven-byte or inline-typed spelling from §3.1: the owning Form scope, a `Body` container of type `CD57BC48-50EC-47DC-975A-FB6DEA72F4DA`, the cage surface of type `22709494-9149-4A70-A829-7D748A7B5DB1`, and the Scene node of type `702B9CD2-537C-429E-8CC4-22BEEEB98C37`. The members before the envelope have variable length, so the envelope sets the position of the reference run. A second envelope later in the record carries the `_physmat_aspects:Prism-###` token and closes with the appearance tail.

**Form body-record cage join.** Each Form body record binds one cage surface to its owning Form scope. The Form serializer record that names that surface has type `830A2A2B-0AA9-4D6A-ACA1-F7A2B2A06571`, version 0, with base type `98542EB9-A4F2-4137-A808-DBB5B3CD6159`, and supplies the cage's archive entry. A Form scope owns the cages of the Form body records that name it, one cage for each record.

A class-328 Form scope is 940 bytes from its primary indexed header to its class-267 paired header. The class-328 primary indexed header starts a scope whose reference table has exactly two ordered members: one class-417/267 cage group and one class-341/267 cage metadata group. The scope payload and fixed history/kind tail use the Design feature-scope grammar. All offsets are relative to the class-328 primary indexed header.

A class-417 cage group owned by a class-328 Form scope is 136 bytes from its primary indexed header to its class-267 paired header. The class-417 primary indexed header is followed by fourteen zero bytes, a marked owning class-328 scope reference, and the owning class-328 scope record index. All offsets are relative to the class-417 primary indexed header. It has fourteen zero bytes before the member count. The member count is four class-350 member references and the group has four entries of `u8 1 + u64 record index + u16 0`, repeated every 11 bytes; each entry names a class-350 primary record paired with class 351. A fixed u32 value 1 follows the member run. The tail has a marked class-272 tail reference and its class-272 tail record index, four zero bytes, a marked class-404 tail reference and its class-404 tail record index, three zero bytes, and a marked repeated class-328 scope reference carrying the repeated owning class-328 scope record index. The two terminal bytes are zero.

A class-328 Form reference entry is 11 bytes. It contains a marked record reference, its referenced record index, and two zero bytes. The same entry form is repeated in the class-417 cage run and the class-341 metadata run.

A class-341 cage metadata group owned by a class-328 Form scope is 293 bytes from its primary indexed header to its class-267 paired header. The class-341 primary indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, a marked owning class-328 scope reference, and the owning class-328 scope record index. All offsets are relative to the class-341 primary indexed header. Its fixed u32 member count is 19. The group has nineteen class-320 member references, encoded as nineteen entries of `u8 1 + u64 record index + u16 0`, repeated every 11 bytes. Its tail stores fixed u32 value 61, a finite little-endian f64, a marked class-259 tail reference with a class-259 tail record index, four zero bytes, a marked class-404 tail reference with a class-404 tail record index, three zero bytes, and a marked repeated class-328 scope reference carrying the repeated owning class-328 scope record index. The two terminal bytes are zero.

A class-350 member's class-351 paired header is preceded by a 13-byte owner backlink tail. The tail contains a marked class-417 group reference, its owning class-417 group record index, three zero bytes before the paired header, and a final paired marker `u8 1`. The class-320 metadata records are single indexed records and retain their class tag as the metadata-member discriminator.

### 1.1.2 Mesh geometry containers

A `<folder>/ParaMeshGeometry.BlobParts/ParaMeshGeometry.<uuid>.paramesh` entry holds one mesh body's geometry. A document whose bodies are all mesh bodies carries an empty `Breps.BlobParts/` directory entry and no BREP stream: the mesh containers hold the model geometry, and three Design-segment records join each container to its body (§3.1).

The container layout is:

```
0x00  89 55 44 50 4D 45 53 48 0D 0A 1A 0A   magic
0x0C  u32  2                                container version
0x10  32 zero bytes                         reserved
0x30  u64  protobuf byte count
0x38  u32  1
0x3C  protobuf message
then chunks to the end of the entry:
      u64  body byte count
      u32  chunk kind                       3 name table, 4 stream data
      body
```

The protobuf message registers the container's streams and resource GUIDs and carries a `fusion_uuid` key whose ASCII GUID equals the GUID stored by the container's Design-segment GUID record (§3.1). That GUID is independent of the `<uuid>` in the entry name.

A kind-3 body is a MessagePack map from stream name to integer stream id. A kind-4 body is a u16 descriptor byte count, a MessagePack descriptor map of that many bytes, a u32 uncompressed byte count, and a two-byte stream encoding. Encoding `5D 14` is followed by a raw LZMA1 stream with `lc` 3, `lp` 0, and `pb` 2; it decompresses to exactly the declared count. The container stores no dictionary size, and every match distance stays within the declared count. Encoding `5D FE` is followed directly by that many uncompressed bytes. The kind-4 chunks follow the name table in ascending stream-id order.

The version-2 scalar stream-descriptor grammar contains these maps: `{T: 0}`, `{T: 1, d: 1}`, `{D: 2, T: 3}`, `{D: 3, T: 3}`, `{D: 4, T: 3}`, and `{D: 3, T: 3, U: true}`. Map-entry order has no meaning. `D` is the logical component count. `T: 0` stores bytes, `T: 1` stores 32-bit terminal-delta words, and `T: 3` stores little-endian f32 components. A split stream stores `{D: N, I: true, S: lengths, T: 3}`, where `N` is 2, 3, or 4 and `lengths` holds `N` byte lengths. Each length counts one following nested kind-4 body. A packed-direction split stream stores `{D: 3, I: true, S: [A, B], T: 3, U: true}` followed by two nested kind-4 bodies of `A` and `B` bytes. Each nested body has an equal decoded length divisible by four. Its descriptor is `{T: 3}`, or `{T: 3, Z: true}` in a packed-direction split stream. A `{T: 3, Z: true}` body stores little-endian f32 values in the `{T: 3}` layout. Nested body `k` holds f32 component `k` of each element, in element order, under either descriptor. In a packed-direction split stream, the first body holds the first octahedral coordinate and the second body holds the second. Other `T` values and other key/value combinations are invalid in version 2. A stream whose descriptor omits `U` decompresses to the element count times the component count times the component width. Descriptor `{D: 3, T: 3, U: true}` stores each logical three-component direction as two f32 octahedral coordinates.

Stream names are container-local slots. Registry field 21 names the vertex-position stream, and field 22 names the triangle-corner stream. Their values are UTF-8 stream names. Fields 21 and 22 assign these roles; the literal names `v` and `t` do not. The registry binds every other stream name to its channel or property.

Registry field 9 is a u32 value associated with the face-group channel. Registry field 12 is one lowercase ASCII hyphenated version-4 UUID. It identifies the mesh container locally and is independent of the entry-name UUID, `fusion_uuid`, channel-resource GUIDs, and face-group GUIDs. The `fusion_uuid` property remains the Design-body join identity.

The position stream holds one f32 coordinate triple per vertex. Those coordinates are not model centimetres: the mesh-body Design record (§3.1) stores the affine map from container coordinates to model space. Its linear part `A` maps an oriented normal with the cofactor matrix `det(A) A^-T`; the result is normalized. The determinant sign keeps the normal aligned with the stored triangle tuple under a reflected placement. In the corner stream, the first corner is implicit. The values before the last are two's-complement differences from one corner to the next. The implicit corner is the unique starting index that keeps the complete decoded sequence inside the vertex-index domain; the last stored value does not continue the sequence.

#### Attribute channels

A `Base Mesh Feature` scope is an indexed Design operation. Its owning entity reference identifies the feature object. The mesh-body record carries a marked reference to the scope's record index; that reference is the operation-to-tessellation join. The mesh-body record also references the Design GUID record whose ASCII identity equals the container's `fusion_uuid`, joins its `.paramesh` entry, and stores the affine map that projects its vertices into model millimetres. The neutral feature definition is `MeshImport` and stores the resulting tessellation identities in reference order. A mesh import owns tessellation geometry and has no BREP `Body`; the decoder does not fabricate one.

When a document's mesh-body metadata or referenced `.paramesh` container does not satisfy the mesh-container grammar, the mesh tessellation is omitted with loss code `mesh.container-undecoded` and B-rep evaluation proceeds. A part document whose Design asset stores no binary or text BREP entry and whose mesh bodies yield no tessellation counts its `.paramesh` entries, less the decoded containers that no mesh body joins. When that count is above zero, the document reports loss code `design.mesh-only-untransferred` with the count.

Registry field 4 declares one channel whose values address vertices or triangle corners, and field 5 declares one channel whose values address triangles. A channel entry holds an optional role in field 2, an optional resource GUID in field 3, one stream entry in field 5, and zero or more face-group records in field 6. The stream entry holds the element code in field 1, the value-stream name in field 2, and the optional index-stream name in field 3. A field-6 face-group record holds its u32 key in field 1 and its GUID in field 2. Channel resource GUIDs are unique within the registry. Face-group keys and GUIDs are unique within their channel.

The element code selects the stored element:

| Code | Element                                                                      |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2    | two f32 components                                                           |
| 4    | four f32 components: red, green, blue, and alpha, in the authored sRGB scale |
| 5    | a unit direction encoded as two f32 octahedral coordinates                   |
| 7    | one terminal-delta u32 value per triangle                                    |

A field-4 channel that declares no index stream stores exactly one value per vertex, so the value stream holds the vertex count times the element width. A field-4 channel that declares an index stream stores one default value for each vertex, followed by one override value for each indexed corner position. If the value table has `E` elements and the mesh has `V` vertices, the index stream has `E - V` signed i32 values. The first `E - V - 1` values are two's-complement differences; the final value is the absolute terminal corner position. The first decoded position is the terminal minus the sum of the differences. Each next position adds the next difference. Positions are strictly increasing and address the triangle-corner sequence. A corner at a decoded position uses the corresponding override value. Every other corner uses the default value for its referenced vertex. Role 0 with code 5 supplies the corner-normal table. Roles 3 and 4 mark the texture-coordinate and colour channels.

A code-7 value stream has one 32-bit word per triangle. Every word before the last is a signed two's-complement difference from the current value to the next value. The final word is the absolute u32 value of the last triangle. The first value is the final value minus the sum of the differences. Each subsequent value adds the corresponding difference.

The role-0 code-7 channel is the face-group partition. It has no field-3 resource GUID. Its repeated field-6 records define the group keys in serialized order. Each decoded triangle value selects one field-6 key. The selected groups partition the triangle ordinals.

The role-1 code-7 channel named `tid` by the attribute-name stream assigns textures. It has one field-3 resource GUID and no field-6 records. Value `0` leaves the triangle untextured. Value `n`, for `n > 0`, selects the `n`th resource in the owning Design texture table's flags-map order (§3.1). The index is one-based and must not exceed the texture-resource count.

For a code-5 element `(u,v)`, both values are finite and in `[-1,1]`. Set `x = u`, `y = v`, and `z = 1 - |u| - |v|`. If `z < 0`, replace `x` with `(1 - |y|) sign(x)` and replace `y` with `(1 - |x_old|) sign(y)`, where `sign(0) = 1`. Normalize `(x,y,z)` to obtain the unit normal. To encode a unit normal `(nx,ny,nz)`, first divide `(nx,ny)` by `|nx| + |ny| + |nz|`. If `nz < 0`, apply the same fold to those two quotients. The resulting pair is `(u,v)`.

Registry field 7 contains one nested field 4 that names a `{T: 1, d: 1}` stream. Every value before the final value is a two's-complement difference. The final u32 is the absolute final endpoint. The first endpoint is the final endpoint minus the sum of the differences, and each next endpoint adds the next difference. Pair the resulting endpoints in order. Each pair is `(low_vertex_index, high_vertex_index)`, with `low_vertex_index < high_vertex_index`. Pairs are unique and each pair is an edge of at least one stored triangle. They classify source feature edges; ordinary triangulation edges are absent unless the source classifies them as features. An empty endpoint stream classifies no feature edges.

A registry field-8 entry pairs a property key in field 1 with either a text value in field 3 or a stream name in field 4. Key `fusion_uuid` carries the ASCII GUID the container's Design-segment GUID record repeats. Key `attname.amt.autodesk` names a `{T: 0}` UTF-8 stream. That stream starts with `<?xml version="1.0"?>` and then concatenates one or more sibling `<Attrib>` fragments. Each fragment contains exactly one `TriName` followed by one `AmtName`. `AmtName` is the authored attribute name. `TriName` is a channel-kind prefix followed immediately by the channel resource GUID: `color_tt` identifies a role-4 code-4 colour channel, `tco_tt` identifies a role-3 code-2 texture-coordinate channel, and `grp_tt` identifies a role-1 code-7 triangle channel. A `grp_tt` fragment whose `AmtName` is `tid` has the texture-selector semantics above.

### 1.1.3 Text encoding of a B-rep stream

A `Breps.BlobParts` member with the `.sat` or `.smt` extension carries the same entity model as a binary `.smb` or `.smbh` stream (§2) in the line-oriented ASCII text encoding. The header lines, record grammar, indexing, terminator, and unit rule are in [`asm.md` §7](asm.md#7-text-encoding-satsmt). The two encodings are alternatives, not layers: a document's geometry is in one of them.


### 1.1.4 Saved displayed occurrence poses

The Design asset's `OGS.BlobFolder/OGS/DefaultScene/world` stores displayed world transforms. Strings use a u32 little-endian UTF-16 code-unit count followed by UTF-16LE code units.

A transform row starts with count `26` and `OverrideTransformAttribute`. Its fixed prefix is 181 bytes: the counted attribute name, prologue `00 00 00 00 01`, sixteen little-endian f32 values, bytes `01 01`, count `25`, and `PersistentPassiveNodePath`. The matrix starts at offset 61 and is column-major. Translation is in centimetres at elements 12, 13, and 14. Its bottom row is `(0,0,0,1)`. All coefficients are finite. Rotation columns have unit squared norm and zero pairwise dot product within `1e-6`; the determinant equals one within `1e-6`.

The prefix is followed by a counted pointer string, a u32 little-endian element count, and that many 12-byte big-endian record indices. The pointer is hexadecimal text with an optional `0x` prefix and has at most 128 code units. The element count is even and below 1024. Its leading u32 is zero in an untagged element and `01 00 00 00` in a tagged element, and its remaining eight bytes give the index. A path can have all untagged elements, all tagged elements, or an untagged prefix followed by a tagged suffix. In a mixed path, the tagged suffix starts at a pair boundary after at least one untagged pair. Uniformly tagged and untagged paths carry Design record indices. A row binds the neutral occurrence whose complete chain of owning component definitions and occurrence carriers matches every path pair. A mixed path binds no neutral occurrence. For an occurrence binding, path pairs alternate the owning component-definition index and occurrence-carrier index, from the root design toward the occurrence. The final pair names the occurrence's own carrier. Each placement of a component definition has its own complete path. A descendant record index can repeat under different insertion paths; the ordered path identifies its instance. An insertion uses its placement carrier in the containing document; descendants continue with component-definition and carrier indices in the inserted document.

The exact counted attribute name and more than 100 following bytes must close as one local grammar: pinned prologue and markers, a proper rigid matrix, the exact counted path class, a bounded pointer string, and the complete counted index run. This closure identifies a transform row from its retained stream bytes.

### 1.2 Stored property and configuration entries

The following small entries are STORED:

| Entry                                           | Bytes                         | Meaning                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Properties.dat`                                | u32 byte count + JSON payload | empty document-properties slot (u32 `0`), or a `docstruct` document-type declaration |
| `.../DesignConfigurationTable.<uuid>.dsgcfg`    | JSON object                   | configuration table, including parameter and suppression overrides                   |
| `.../DesignConfigurationRule.<uuid>.dsgcfgrule` | JSON object                   | configuration activation rules                                                       |

`Properties.dat` is a u32 payload byte count followed by that many JSON bytes; count 0 (`00 00 00 00`) is the empty slot. A non-empty payload is a JSON object whose `docstruct` member declares the document type: `version` (string), `type` (`assembly-design` or `part-design`), `subtype` (`assembly-standard`, `part-standard`, `part-sheetmetal`), and an `attributes` object. An `assembly-design` document carries no B-rep streams; its model is the placement of its external-reference targets (§1.4).

Configuration tables and rules are complete JSON objects. ZIP entry name and extension select table versus rule; duplicate entry names are invalid. A rule's paired `when` and `activate` members are strings containing its activation condition and target row name. A rule object can be empty; an empty object has no members and activates nothing.

A table document is the empty object `{}` or an object with the members `asset`, `tables`, `cachedRevIds`, and `testRowData`. The empty object contains zero tables, columns, rows, and cells.

A table document is built from asset objects and typed values. An asset object has the string members `id`, `revisionId`, and `type`, an `attributes` object of strings, and a `components` array. Each component has the string members `name` and `type` and a `properties` object. Each property, and each member of a typed object value, is a typed value `{"type": T, "value": V}`. Type `String` has a string value, or an array of strings for an order list; `Bool` has a Boolean, `Int32` an integer, and `Float64` a number. Type `map<C>` has an object value whose members are typed values of type `C`, keyed by identifier. Any other type is a component type name, and its value is an object of typed members. Asset and component type names below omit the prefixes `autodesk.configuration:assets.` and `autodesk.configuration:components.`.

| Member         | Value                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `asset`        | asset of type `configuration-1.0.0` with component `tableVersion` of type `tableData-1.0.0`; its property `tableVersion` is `Int32` `1` |
| `tables`       | array of table objects                                                                                                                  |
| `cachedRevIds` | object                                                                                                                                  |
| `testRowData`  | array of strings; each string is the JSON object of one test-row cell                                                                   |

A table object has the members `asset`, `rows`, and `tableView`. Its asset has type `configurationTable-1.1.0` and the attribute `pim:configuration:tableId`, which is the table id. The asset component `tableDefinition` of type `tableDefinition-1.1.0` has the properties `id` (`String`, equal to the table id), `tableName` (`String`), `tableType` (`String`), and `columnData` (`map<columnData-1.1.0>`, keyed by column id). `rows` is an array of objects whose `asset` member is a row asset. The `asset` member of `tableView` has type `tableView-1.0.0` and the component `viewData` of type `tableViewData-1.0.0`, whose properties `columnOrder` and `rowOrder` list column ids and row ids. `rowOrder` contains each row id of the table once, in authored row order. The order of the `rows` array is independent of the authored row order.

A column value has the members `id` (`String`, equal to its map key), `isCustom` (`Bool`), `title` (`String`, the display title), and `object`, which names the configured target:

| `object` type              | Value members                                         | Configured target                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `configuredProperty-1.0.0` | `id`, `propertyKey`, `propertySet`, `type` `Property` | the document property `propertyKey` in property set `propertySet`                     |
| `configuredObject-1.0.0`   | `id`, `type` `UserParameterValue`                     | the document parameter record whose indexed-record index is `id`                      |
| `configuredObject-1.0.0`   | `id`, `type` `ParameterDoubleValue`                   | the parameter of the parameter owner record whose indexed-record index is `id` (§3.1) |
| `configuredObject-1.0.0`   | `id`, `type` `DcFeature`                              | the feature of the parameter scope record whose indexed-record index is `id`          |

A configured object `id` is a decimal ASCII indexed-record index in the Design `BulkStream` of the same asset.

A row asset has type `row-1.0.0` and the attributes `pim:configuration:rowId`, which is the row id, and `pim:configuration:rowName`, which is the row name. Its component `rowData` of type `rowData-1.0.0` has the properties `configRevisionId` (`String`), `default` (`Bool`), and `rowCells` (`map<rowCell-1.0.0>`, keyed by column id). Its component `rowDefinition` of type `rowDefinition-1.0.0` has the property `id`, equal to the row id. A row cell has the members `columnId` (`String`, equal to its map key) and `data`, whose type selects the cell value:

| `data` type                | Value members                                                                                    | Column target | Meaning                                                               |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant.expression-1.0.0` | `expression` (`String`); `value` of type `variant.float64-1.0.0` with member `value` (`Float64`) | parameter     | the row's source expression and its evaluated value in database units |
| `variant.bool-1.0.0`       | `value` (`Bool`)                                                                                 | feature       | `true` computes the feature in the row; `false` suppresses it         |
| `variant.string-1.0.0`     | `value` (`String`)                                                                               | property      | the row's property value                                              |

Each `testRowData` string is a JSON object with the members `DataType`, `ColumnUniqueID` (a column id), and the test-row value of that column. Data type `StringOptionValue` has `Value` and `Option`, `StringValue` has `Value`, `ParameterDoubleValue` has `UserName`, `Expression`, and `Value`, and `BoolValue` has `Value`. Its parameter and feature values are the values of the active row.

The `DesignConfigurationRoot` record in the Design `BulkStream` names the active row. Its indexed header is followed by a zero u32, the LP-ASCII key `DesignConfigurationRoot`, eleven zero bytes, u32 `1`, the LP-UTF16 table id, the LP-UTF16 row id of the active row, and u32 `0`. The model state stored in the document is the state of the active row. A root record can name a row of a table document that contains no rows.

The `DesignConfigurationTableSerializerTrigger` record in the Design `BulkStream` names the table blob. Its indexed header is followed by a zero u32, the LP-ASCII key `DesignConfigurationTableSerializerTrigger`, two zero bytes, and the LP-UTF16 table-entry basename. The UUID-named form has a 68-code-unit basename `DesignConfigurationTable.<uuid>.dsgcfg`, which selects the member under the asset's `DesignConfigurationTable.BlobParts/` directory. The table entry is also identified by its ZIP entry name alone; reading a configuration table does not require the trigger record.

A table lists only the features it toggles: a feature with no column keeps its current state in the active row. A suppression cell of the active row supplies the state of a feature whose records do not decide it, such as a `Sketch`.

Each row of a table supplies one neutral configuration. Its stable neutral identity is formed from the complete table-entry name and the row id as two byte-length-prefixed UTF-8 strings. Its zero-based neutral ordinal is its position in `rowOrder`, its name is the row name, and it is active when the root record names its table id and row id. A parameter cell transfers its expression as the configuration-specific source expression of the neutral parameter that its column names, and its evaluated value as that configuration's value of the parameter, in the type of the parameter's own value: a length from centimetres to millimetres, an angle in radians, and a dimensionless real unchanged. A parameter whose own value is none of these has no configuration value. A feature cell transfers a suppressed or an active feature state for the neutral feature that its column names. A property cell with an empty `propertySet` transfers its value as the configuration property `property:` followed by `propertyKey`. A parameter or feature cell whose target has no neutral entity remains a configuration-local property keyed by its column id. A paired rule transfers its `when` condition to the configuration whose row name equals its `activate` name when exactly one row across all tables has that name; the property identity includes the complete rule-entry name. One table with rows supplies the document's configuration list; independent tables with rows do not encode a shared row order. Configuration entry names and table order belong to their containing F3D document. Each F3Z member retains its document scope when the archive joins its records. Native table and rule documents remain the full-fidelity source for members without a neutral target.

### 1.3 `Manifest.dat` grammar

Both manifests use `u32`-length-prefixed strings. An ASCII field stores a byte count followed by that many bytes. A UTF-16LE field stores a code-unit count followed by twice that many bytes.

The **top-level manifest** starts with LP-ASCII `3-2-0-0`, LP-ASCII `FusionDocType`, LP-UTF16 `.f3d`, an LP-UTF16 display name, an LP-UTF16 description, a document GUID, and a document-asset GUID. Each GUID is a 36-code-unit hyphenated hexadecimal LP-UTF16 string.

Two generation-header forms follow the document-asset GUID. The current form is `u32 1234`, three generation u32 values, and a u32 capability-registry count. The legacy form is a first u32 other than `1234`, one further generation u32, and a u32 capability-registry count. The count can be zero. Each registry entry is a nonempty unique LP-ASCII name and a u32 value. A generation extension follows the registry and ends immediately before the asset-folder tail.

The asset-folder tail is the unique suffix that consumes the end of the manifest with this grammar:

```
LP-UTF16  active_asset_guid       36-code-unit hyphenated hexadecimal GUID
u32       asset_folder_count      nonzero
repeat asset_folder_count:
  LP-UTF16 asset_folder_base      one archive-path component
u32       secondary_folder_count  zero or more
repeat secondary_folder_count:
  LP-UTF16 asset_folder_base      one archive-path component
terminal:
  end of file
  or u8 0, nonempty LP-UTF16 document_display_name,
           optional (nonempty LP-UTF16 lineage_urn beginning `urn:`,
                     optional lineage_suffix
                     or LP-UTF16 `NA_EXPORT`
                     or LP-UTF16 `NA_OFFLINESAVE`), end of file
  or u8 1, end of file
  or u8 1, LP-UTF16 `NA_EXPORT`, end of file
  or u8 1, LP-UTF16 `NA_OFFLINESAVE`, end of file
  or u8 1, nonempty LP-UTF16 lineage_urn beginning `urn:`, end of file
```

The `lineage_suffix` is the fixed byte sequence `48 00 41 00 41 00 48 00 41 00`. It follows a present lineage URN in the terminal form that starts with `u8 0`. Its layout is `manifest_lineage_suffix` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

The terminal form ends at EOF. Any bytes after its final field are invalid. `NA_OFFLINESAVE` marks a document saved without cloud lineage; that manifest carries no lineage URN.

The two folder runs list distinct bases, and every listed base is an asset folder. `active_asset_guid` is the first asset GUID of the active asset. The active asset can be the Design asset, a simulation case, an animation, or another asset kind. It does not select the Design folder.

Each listed base resolves to exactly one archive folder: either `<base>` or `<base>[Active]`. That folder contains `Manifest.dat`. A **per-asset manifest** starts with its LP-UTF16 base name, a first asset GUID, a second asset GUID, and an LP-ASCII asset type. A `FusionAssetType` prefix continues with a u32 revision.

Revisions 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 19, and 20 carry a u32 capability count, repeated nonempty unique LP-ASCII capability names with u32 values, LP-ASCII `Neutron3DAssetType`, u8 zero, and an LP-ASCII subtype. The subtype is empty for the root Design asset and names a derived Fusion asset otherwise.

Revision 10 carries the same named capability registry and kind token, followed by u8 zero. Each linked document stores u32 `2`, an LP-UTF16 composite locator containing a version URN, and two LP-UTF16 GUIDs. The root tail starts with u32 values `0, root_revision, 1, 0`, or `2, 5, 1, 0`, and continues with two LP-ASCII `Design` tokens. `root_revision` is descriptive metadata and does not change the tail grammar. Revision 0 instead stores u32 values `3, 1`, LP-ASCII `Neutron3DAssetType`, u8 zero, u32 values `0, 6, 1, 0`, and two LP-ASCII `Design` tokens. These revision-0 and revision-10 root tails end the manifest.

The unique listed root `FusionAssetType` folder is the Design asset folder. Folder-run order, archive-entry order, the active-asset GUID, and B-rep presence do not select the Design asset.

After the empty subtype field, a Design per-asset manifest carries a `physicalChangeGuid` and the segment-type registry (`FusionDesignSegmentType`, `FusionACTSegmentType`, `FusionBrowserSegmentType`).

### 1.4 External references

A document that places other documents records each placement as an **XRef** keyed by an occurrence-role string (`neutronRole`). The role joins the container reference table and the Design-segment XRef record. The ACT GUID pool carries occurrence-role GUIDs. A multi-document archive stores the roles in its design description (§1.5).

**`RedirectionsStream.dat`** is a top-level JSON object: `{"name":"RedirectionsStream","schema-version":0,"designs":[...],"references":...}`. `designs` is an array; the first entry describes the document itself and each further entry one referenced document. A design entry carries `file-version` (integer), `targetFileName` (the document's `.f3d` file name), `displayName`, `lineageUrn` (`urn:adsk.wipprod:dm.lineage:<key>`), and `versionUrn` (`urn:adsk.wipprod:fs.file:vf.<key>?version=N`, same `<key>` as the lineage URN). In a document with no outgoing references, `references` is the empty object `{}`. Otherwise `references` is an array of objects `{"from","relativePath","type","properties":[...]}`. `type` is `XREF` or `DERIVED`. `from` is the document's own file name. `relativePath` is the target design entry's `targetFileName`. `properties` contains one `neutronRole` and one `neutronData` single-member object, each `{"value":"<string>","dataType":"STRING"}`. Both reference types carry these fields. `from`, `relativePath`, and `neutronRole.value` are non-empty strings; `neutronData.value` is an independent string. XREF uses `neutronRole` as its occurrence-role string. DERIVED identifies a source-document dependency; its properties retain the source role and data. XREF and DERIVED rows can share an array. The array order defines reference ordinals. DERIVED contributes zero occurrence placements.

**`ComponentReferenceData.json`** is a top-level STORED entry containing a JSON object. The object is an open document: member names and values are retained without a closed schema.

**Design-segment XRef records.** The Design BulkStream registers the record class name `DcXRefPCIFeatureMetaType`. Its dynamic three-digit ASCII class tag and record index form the indexed-record header. A standalone occurrence record carries, in order: a `u32`-count UTF-16LE record GUID; marker-tagged integer fields; a `0x01`-tagged eight-byte value, which is the presence flag and target entity ID of a cross-document reference; a `u32`-count ASCII GUID, which is that target record's type GUID and appears in the target segment's MetaStream type table; a `0x01`-tagged `u32` zero; and a `u32`-count UTF-16LE occurrence-role string equal to the reference's `neutronRole`. A grouped component-insert carrier can contain several occurrences and repeat the same occurrence-role string in metadata, placement, and construction-reference fields. Several placements may therefore carry the same role and place the same target document more than once. Each occurrence-role string is also present in the ACT-segment GUID pool.

**Placement.** An occurrence placement is a primary indexed record whose registered type-table entry has GUID `CE2913AA-CFE0-4F04-9102-24424ED3BCFA` and add-in name `Component`. Its indexed header repeats the registered entity and selects that type-table row. Primary and secondary MetaStream indices delimit its class members. An indexed-header byte pattern inside a payload does not delimit a record, and a nested base-class header does not create another placement.

A `CommonData` record of type `3B6814F4-D87B-46BD-AD9D-0BE07880F7BB`, version 0, can carry a component path and transform in this form:

```
u8   1
u32  count                       path elements
count × (reference, u32 instance discriminator)
u8   0
u8   identity_flag               omitted by forms that always store the matrix
16 × f64                         row-major 4×4, stored only when identity_flag is 0 or omitted
u32  count, count × reference
reference                        Fusion root-component aggregate
reference                        CommonData context node
```

The path integer is an instance discriminator, not the element's ordinal along the path. The counted references name local Component nodes or qualified cross-document targets. The closing local references have types `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD` and `F9CB8717-EB86-47F2-AAA7-39E142C57A09`, in that order. This component-path carrier is not an occurrence-placement record; its byte shape does not override its registered `CommonData` type.

The matrix is a proper rigid motion. Its upper-left 3×3 block is orthonormal, column 3 is the translation in centimetres, the bottom row is `(0, 0, 0, 1)`, and the determinant is `1`. An `identity_flag` of `1` states that the placement is the identity transform and stores no matrix. An inserted design's occurrence-placement record can store the identity or an earlier matrix rather than the occurrence's current pose. A component-path record of type `3B6814F4-D87B-46BD-AD9D-0BE07880F7BB` whose path is exactly two elements, one cross-document element and one local element in either order, stores the current world pose of one placed occurrence: the local element names that occurrence's occurrence-placement record, and the cross-document element's link name is that placement's occurrence role. An external occurrence at the document root takes this pose in place of its placement record's matrix, which stays in the native frame and is reported as `xref.placement-current-pose`. An external occurrence below a local owner keeps its placement matrix, which is local to the container; the carrier's world pose stays native and is reported as `xref.current-pose-native`. The cross-document element of this record can be a legacy target reference of an attributed legacy occurrence placement, which stores no link name. Such a record has exactly two path elements: the legacy target reference of the referenced design's root component, with type `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`, and then the local element. The local element names the occurrence-placement record whose own legacy target reference has the same target entity and source occurrence identity. The record stores the current world pose of that placed occurrence under the same rules.

A component-path record whose path is two cross-document elements of one role, a root component (`E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`) and then an occurrence placement (`CE2913AA-CFE0-4F04-9102-24424ED3BCFA`) in the referenced design, followed by this document's occurrence-placement record of that role and none or more of the local occurrence carriers that hold it, innermost first, stores the world pose of the occurrence inside the external occurrence. The inner occurrence's own placement below the external occurrence then gives the external occurrence's world pose. An external occurrence instance whose local owners, from the innermost, begin with the record's takes that pose, relative to its owner, when the records that list the most of its owners all give the same pose; a record that lists fewer owners can keep the pose from before an owner it leaves out moved; its placement matrix stays in the native frame and it is reported as `xref.contained-pose`. Records that give different poses for one instance leave its placement matrix and are reported as `xref.contained-pose-disagrees`; records that reach no instance stay native and are reported as `xref.contained-pose-native`.

A nested-design component-path record that holds the root component of a design the referenced design places (a cross-document element), this document's occurrence-placement record of the external occurrence (a local element), and that nested occurrence's occurrence placement in the referenced design (a cross-document element) stores the world pose of the nested occurrence. The nested occurrence placement is the last element; the root component and the local element precede it in either order. The root component and the nested placement carry different link names, and the nested placement's link name is the external occurrence's role. Local owners can follow the nested placement, innermost first. A cross-document element can state its target type inline instead of after its asset, and a local element can state the occurrence-placement type inline. The ownerless nested form uses the contained-pose relation.

A component-path record whose path is the referenced design's root component (a cross-document element), then this document's occurrence-placement record of that role and one or more of the local occurrence carriers that hold it, innermost first, stores the world pose of that external occurrence. An external occurrence instance below local owners that no record of its contained occurrences places takes the pose of its own records that list the most of its owners, when they agree, relative to its owner; its placement matrix stays in the native frame and it is reported as `xref.owned-pose`. Own records that give different poses leave its placement and are reported as `xref.owned-pose-disagrees`. An untagged contained relation without an inline-qualified own-world carrier determines the insertion pose; an own record that reaches no instance stays native under `xref.owned-pose-native`.

An inline-qualified same-role contained carrier places its exact contained occurrence. A matching own-world carrier with an inline-qualified local element places the insertion independently. A contained carrier can occur with no own-world carrier. The stored world frame is the containing Design stream's frame. An inserted Design stream maps that frame through its insertion and all outer owners. Each repeated insertion has its own expanded target scope. Each local transform is `inverse(W(parent)) * pose`, with the insertion and owner corrections composed outermost first. A contained target must resolve uniquely within the placed member, and its owner chain must select one insertion instance. Records with the longest matching owner chain select the current snapshot. Disagreeing carriers of that target retain its stored local frame. The root component and local placement can precede the contained placement in either order. In the locals-first form, the local placement and its owners precede the root component and the contained cross-document placement. An own path in this form ends with its cross-document root component. Other longer paths stay native. A local occurrence or owner element carries either its untagged reference or inline type `CE2913AA-CFE0-4F04-9102-24424ED3BCFA`. The inline identity agrees with the referenced element role.

The first counted reference run after the identity flag or matrix carries the occurrence chain, outermost first and target last. A direct contained chain has two references: the local insertion placement, then the cross-document occurrence placement in that inserted Design stream. Each reference has the occurrence-placement type when it states a type inline. The chain's local placement, target record and target role agree with the initial path elements. This chain identifies the exact contained instance within its inserted member. Ordinary contained carriers and nested-design carriers can share one insertion. Each nested carrier with this complete direct chain states the world frame of its named child.

A contained carrier can state a source insertion frame while the insertion's own current carrier states a changed frame. Let `S` be the insertion's source placement, `L` the contained occurrence's direct source pose, and `C` the contained carrier's frame in the same Design stream. The equality `C = S * L` identifies that source composition. For a direct contained chain under an insertion with its own current carrier and no owner-qualified own-world carrier, the child retains `L` under the insertion's current frame `W`; its world frame is `W * L`. An untagged contained relation determines the insertion from the contained occurrence's source placement. The resulting insertion and contained constraints precede direct operation-table compatibility.

Several component-path records can name one placement record; only a record whose path matches both the role and the placement record supplies the pose. When two or more such records exist, the occurrence keeps its placement matrix and the placement is reported as `xref.current-pose-ambiguous`.

A component-path record whose path is exactly two local elements, a Component record and a local component-occurrence carrier whose component reference is that record, stores the current pose of that local occurrence. The Component record is the first element, and neither reference carries an inline type. The any-length local form below reads a two-element path whose record-index order puts the carrier first. A component-path record whose elements are all local references and that neither form reads keeps its pose native and is reported as `assembly.local-component-path-native`. A local occurrence in the document's root component takes this pose in place of its carrier's stored placement, which stays in the native frame and is reported as `assembly.local-occurrence-current-pose`; the root occurrence is the identity, so the pose is also its world transform. A local occurrence below another component takes its pose from the longer-path form below when that form names it. Otherwise it keeps its stored placement, and the carrier's pose stays native and is reported as `assembly.local-occurrence-current-pose-native`. When two or more such records name one carrier, the occurrence keeps its stored placement and is reported as `assembly.local-occurrence-current-pose-ambiguous`. The 128-byte matrix is the only length difference between the two forms.

**Local component paths of any length.** A component-path record of type `3B6814F4-D87B-46BD-AD9D-0BE07880F7BB` whose elements are all local references without an inline type, with two or more elements, stores the world pose of one expanded instance of a local occurrence. The matrix is orthonormal with determinant `1` or `-1`; determinant `-1` states a mirrored placement. The elements form a record set stored in record-index order. Exactly one element is a Component record, the definition of the target. Exactly one other element is the target: the local component-occurrence carrier whose component reference is that Component record. The remaining elements are local component-occurrence carriers that contain the target: the path lists the target's innermost containing carriers, from the carrier in the target's definition outward, up to a count that can be less than the full chain. Each element names a distinct record. The listed containing carriers, as a set, equal the innermost containing carriers of the target instance. The initial element list can omit outer carriers.

The first counted reference run after the identity flag or matrix carries an occurrence chain when its references form the complete containing chain and end at the target occurrence carrier. A local occurrence chain uses same-segment references without inline types and lists the containing carriers from outermost to innermost, followed by the target. This complete chain identifies the expanded instance. Its target and containing carriers agree with the initial element list. The chain is scoped to the Design stream of the record.

A local component path can contain a local reference to the Design stream's `rootInstance` record in any position. That record binds the stream's unique root component and names the root frame. The remaining elements identify the target and its containing carriers.

The stored matrix is the instance's world pose in centimetres. The instance's local placement is `inverse(W(parent)) * pose`, where `W(parent)` is the world transform of the containing instance. Parent and child world poses share the same Design frame. A target in the document's root component has an identity parent frame.

**Direct operation-table poses.** A direct operation table is a Fusion record of type `549FBB80-B890-473E-A5C0-415D3D9BF4E6`, version 0 through 4, that stores a three-digit LP-ASCII class tag, a u64 indexed record identity, an LP-ASCII name, a zero run of two bytes for version 0 or six bytes for versions 1 through 4, a u32-counted dependency-reference run, an occurrence path with u32 count `1`, a local component reference, a u32 entry cursor, and a u32-counted entry run. Exactly one grammar closes a direct table. The path reference is a local occurrence-placement reference with no inline type or inline type `CE2913AA-CFE0-4F04-9102-24424ED3BCFA`. A direct table of version 4 stores a path-ordinal field between the path and the component reference: byte `02`, u32 `1`, and one u32 path ordinal. Each entry has two flag bytes, a local operation reference, and a matrix in the identity-flag form above. The flag pairs are `01 00`, `00 00`, and `01 01`. In a direct table, the entry run is nonempty, the cursor equals the entry count minus one, and the final entry ends at the record boundary. Each explicit matrix is a finite proper rigid transform. The local component reference names the source component definition selected by the source's root instance. Its inline type, when present, is `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`.

The final entry of a direct table of version 0, 1, or 4 gives the occurrence's pose in its source component frame. This pose belongs to the occurrence inside the component definition and is the same in every instance of that definition. Local owner transforms convert this pose into the occurrence's parent frame. A component-path carrier selects the contained occurrence's instance frame through the contained-pose relation above. Its selected pose has precedence over the direct table's source pose. A direct table has no unique placement when several tables name the same occurrence or its instance constraints disagree. A constraint on one occurrence leaves independent sibling tables valid. An agreeing direct table and component path retain both placement identities. Descendant paths do not give a direct occurrence pose.

The counted reference run after the matrix reaches both local and cross-document targets. The parser selects the tagged u32 run and its reference exactly when the paired Design `MetaStream.dat` header's serializer magic is `1234`; every other serializer magic selects the two-reference form without that run. The two references that close the record name the same pair of entities for every placement of one document.

A legacy typed occurrence placement uses the same type-table identity but a separate envelope. Its indexed record header is followed by:

```
u8   1
u32  1
legacy target reference
u32  instance discriminator
u32  1
u8   0
u32  1
LP-UTF16 36       source-local placement-metadata UUID
LP-UTF16 36       EntityTracking link GUID
u8   0
legacy target reference
u8   identity_flag
16 × f64          row-major 4×4, stored only when identity_flag is 0
u32  0
LP-UTF16 36       occurrence-role GUID
u8   0
u8   1
u8   4
u8[9] zero
```

Each legacy target reference is `u8 1`, `u64 target entity ID`, `u8 1`, `u64 source occurrence identity`, `u8 0`, `LP-ASCII 36 target type GUID`, and `u8 0`. The two target references are semantic duplicates. They name the target Design segment's root-component aggregate, with type `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`. The repeated u64 is a source occurrence identity, not a target record identity. The fixed reference layout is in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). The identity form is 403 bytes from its indexed header through its fixed closing tail; the matrix form is 531 bytes. `identity_flag` `1` stores no matrix, and `0` stores the rigid matrix. The dynamic class tag does not select this envelope: the occurrence-placement type-table identity and exact record closure do.

The first legacy UUID is source-local placement metadata. The second joins to an `EntityTracking` record of type `96CBEA21-17E0-4BCB-BA77-04EA87B47934`, version 4. Its five GUID fields are the tracking link, target Design asset, target root Component, source Design asset, and source root Component, in that order. An asset GUID is the first GUID of its per-asset manifest. The Component GUID is the third GUID of the root aggregate's nested Component record. The source occurrence identity and placement UUID are retained; their values are not derived from the target identities.

An attributed legacy occurrence placement with a zero control word has an empty instance name, path marker `1`, path count `1`, one legacy target reference, and a u32 path discriminator. The target entity and source occurrence identity are nonzero, and the target type is `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`. Its 88-byte prefix is followed by one of two attribute blocks. The empty block is `u8 1 + u32 0`, five bytes. The 137-byte block is `u8 1 + u32 3` followed by the ordered properties `GatedByParent = false`, `ResolutionTime = ""`, and `SelfGated = false`, with the LP-ASCII names and intrinsic types defined below.

The attribute block is followed by a 235-byte member sequence: u16 control word `0`, a positive u32 ordinal, two 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 UUIDs, a 15-byte cross-segment reference with a nonzero target and no inline type GUID, u8 separator `0`, the repeated 60-byte legacy target reference, and the identity flag. The repeated target has the same entity, source occurrence identity, and type GUID as the first target. The cross-segment reference carries its stored u32 segment index. The ordinal and path discriminator are independent integers.

The three-property identity form also carries control word `1`. This form stores identity flag `1`, the 92-byte identity tail, and a complete frame length of 552 bytes. The repeated target, occurrence-role GUID, and closing owner have the same fields as the zero-control identity form.

The empty-attribute generation can insert a source-placement flag after the positive ordinal and before the two UUIDs. Its u16 control word is `0` or `1`. Flag `1` stores source identity; flag `0` stores a proper rigid row-major matrix in centimetres. The placement after the repeated target is the owner-relative local placement. The two flags and matrices are independent. The source placement remains part of the carrier. The complete sequence closes with the occurrence role and local owner as above. Its length is 421, 549, or 677 bytes, according to the two flags. The generation is selected by complete record closure and the registered Component occurrence-placement type.

The first UUID is auxiliary placement metadata. The second UUID is the source occurrence key. It occupies a key slot in the counted occurrence-key run of same-Design records of type `96CBEA21-17E0-4BCB-BA77-04EA87B47934`, version 4. It can follow the keys of containing occurrences. The occurrence-role GUID binds the placement to the container reference; it is separate from the source occurrence key. When the placement is the carrier of a `Component Insert` scope, an Assemble operand path whose occurrence key equals the source occurrence key selects that insert's occurrence. Later keys of the path name occurrences inside the inserted document.

The attributed legacy placement tail is 92 bytes for identity flag `1` and 220 bytes for flag `0`. The matrix form starts with sixteen row-major f64 values. Both tails then store u32 `0`, a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 occurrence-role GUID, u8 `0`, and an eleven-byte local owner reference with a nonzero target. The owner reference has no inline type GUID. The complete frame is 420 or 548 bytes with the empty attribute block, and 552 or 680 bytes with the three-property block. The fixed members are in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

A Component path can replace its terminating zero byte with an inline metadata block: `u8 1`, a u32 property count, then ordered typed properties. Each property has an LP-ASCII name, an LP-ASCII intrinsic type, and the typed value. `IntrinsicMetaTypebool` stores one Boolean byte; `IntrinsicMetaTypeHString` stores an LP-UTF16 string. A block with `GatedByParent = false`, `ResolutionTime = ""`, and `SelfGated = false` serializes those three typed properties in that order. The byte after `GatedByParent`'s Boolean starts the next property; it is not a separate gate selector. The subsequent occurrence-key reference uses the standard cross-segment reference grammar. Its u32 segment index is part of the reference and is not a constant padding value. In an attributed occurrence, the byte after that reference is zero, or it begins an untyped local reference to a nonzero source record. The repeated Component reference follows in both forms. The reference does not change the placement grammar after that point. The source record is read as one registered to type `8ACBA2E5-5A4C-4438-8351-276DE96E6982` in the same Design segment. The path discriminator and the later occurrence ordinal are independent stored integers. A positive ordinal greater than one can accompany an identity marker; that form stores no matrix and retains its ordinal.

The repeated-target placement generation starts with the standard target path and its terminating u8 zero. Its generation tail is:

```
u32  stored_value                 positive, independent of the path discriminator
LP-UTF16 36       metadata GUID 1
LP-UTF16 36       metadata GUID 2
u8   0                           optional separator
reference                        repeated qualified target
u8   identity_flag
16 × f64          row-major 4×4, stored only when identity_flag is 0
u32  0
LP-UTF16           repeated occurrence role
u8   0
reference          closing local owner
```

The repeated qualified reference and the final path target have equal entity IDs, target segment IDs, asset GUIDs, target type GUIDs, link names, and optional version tails. A target entity ID and target segment ID are reference values, not framing constants. The optional zero separator precedes the reference's presence byte `1`. The repeated occurrence role equals the repeated reference's link name. Cross-document roles are LP-UTF16 values of at most 256 code units. A role can be a GUID, a GUID with a URN suffix, or a version URN. The two metadata fields are UUIDs. The second metadata UUID is the occurrence key used by assembly operand paths in the containing Design stream. It identifies the source occurrence independently of its target reference and occurrence role. Ordered containing-component occurrence keys distinguish instances below repeated local owners. The closing owner is a non-null same-segment reference, with or without an inline target type GUID. The record closes immediately after this reference. The primary indexed entity ID identifies the placement carrier; the closing reference identifies its local owner. The matrix form is exactly 128 bytes longer than the identity form.

A pathless occurrence placement has a fifteen-byte indexed header, an empty LP-ASCII name, a zero path flag, a zero separator, and u32 value `1`. Two LP-UTF16 UUIDs follow: auxiliary metadata and the source occurrence key. A zero separator precedes one cross-document root-component reference of type `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`. The identity flag, optional rigid matrix, zero u32, repeated occurrence role, zero separator, and non-null local owner reference close the record as in the repeated-target form. The role equals the cross-document reference link name. The owner can carry its inline type. The fixed prefix is in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

The transform belongs to the occurrence record rather than the referenced target. The target path is `relativePath`, and translation is in centimetres.
