The closing local owner reference names the root entity of the containing component naming space in the same Design stream. An external occurrence is a child of each occurrence of that containing component. Its stored matrix is local to the container: `W(child) = W(parent) * L(child)` for column-vector points. Each containing instance gives the external child a distinct instance path. An owner that names the component placed by `rootInstance` places the external occurrence at the document root. An absent serialized matrix is identity relative to the container. The owner component can itself have a local occurrence carrier. Its local matrix composes through the containing-component chain to the document root with the same multiplication rule.

A placement frame is valid only when its complete member sequence closes at the indexed record boundary. A truncated reference, unequal repeated target, invalid matrix, or extra tail byte does not state an identity placement. A `rootInstance` record and a record whose target path has no cross-document element are not external placements.

### 1.5 Multi-document archives (`.f3z`)

A `.f3z` is a ZIP archive holding `Manifest.json`, `DesignDescription.json`, and one member per document. A 3D design member has extension `.f3d`. A drawing member has extension `.f2d`.

`Manifest.json` is the single-member object `{"root":"<file>.f3d"}` naming the root document's member.

The root member can instead be an F2D drawing. In this form, the root design object has `contentType` `f2d` and one `DERIVED` reference to the design object whose `contentType` is `f3d`. That referenced object's `relativePath` names the archive's derived 3D model member. The drawing payload and the derived model are separate documents. The model does not contain the drawing sheets, views, dimensions, or annotations.

`DesignDescription.json` is `{"name":"Autodesk Design Description","version":"0.1","designDescription":{...}}`. The `designDescription` object carries `id`, `name`, `currentVersion`, and `designGraphs`, an array of graphs. A graph carries `creationDate`, `creatingService`, `rootIds` (the root design-object ids), `designObjectRefs`, and `designObjects`. A design object carries: `id` (integer), `version`, `about` (version URN), `lineage` (lineage URN), `from` (an `urn:adsk.objects:os.object:` URN), `relativePath` and `downloadAs` (both equal to the document's archive member name), `friendlyName`, `displayName`, `zipped`, `rootFile`, `contentType` (`f3d`), `shareInfo`, `references`, `metadata`, and `createdAt`. The `metadata.docstruct` string holds the JSON docstruct mirrored in the member's `Properties.dat` (§1.2), and `metadata.rootFileName` the document's display file name. A referencing design object's `references` is an array of groups `{"type","ids":[...],"relationships":[...]}`. A group has type `XREF` or `DERIVED`, where `ids` lists the referenced design-object ids and each relationship is `{"id":<design-object id>,"metadata":{"neutronRole":"<guid>"}}` with the same `neutronRole` as the member's `RedirectionsStream.dat` reference (§1.4). A leaf design object's `references` is the empty array.

For the `PushPullDerive` workflow, a DERIVED relationship has metadata `{"workflow":"PushPullDerive","neutronRole":"<guid>"}`. An F3D derive stores result bodies in the deriving document's model.

XREF reference resolution is member-local and recursive. Each member's `RedirectionsStream.dat` maps its occurrence-role strings to `relativePath` values naming other `.f3d` members, whose lineage and version URNs match those members' design objects. A child occurrence transform maps the child model into its containing member; ancestor occurrence transforms then map that complete result toward the root frame. A member path cannot recur in one active reference chain.

Each resolved referenced design has one product definition. Its bodies use the design frame. A body's own transform maps its carrier into that frame. Bodies and sketches owned by local component definitions retain those owners. Sketches at the referenced design root belong to the referenced design definition. Every occurrence that places the referenced design has a local prototype reference to its definition. Repeated placements share the definition, its bodies, and its sketches. The document path, lineage, version, and source placement remain in the native xref records.

Nested member occurrences form a separate tree below each placing occurrence. Their identities include the instance path, and each matrix maps into the direct parent's frame. For a definition body, `W(body) = W(occurrence path) * body-in-definition`. Occurrence placement does not change a definition body's own transform. The root document's bodies retain their existing frames and ownership.

## 2. B-rep streams

Both `.smb` and `.smbh` entries carry an ASM `BinaryFile` token stream. The stream encoding — binary header, record framing, unit rules, topology records, geometry carriers, and the construction-history partition — is specified in [`asm.md`](asm.md).

An active face identity includes its BREP member namespace. A historical face identity includes its feature-input state and belongs to that state's emitted face set. A stable ASM slot number alone does not join a face across BREP members or history states. A native selection identity remains distinct from either neutral identity.

An exact intcurve cache and the point records of its incident edge vertices use the same model coordinate frame. The body transform applies to both. A tolerant vertex point represents the endpoints of all incident edge curves within its vertex tolerance. The endpoint allowance is the maximum of the document linear tolerance, the 0.01 mm coincidence allowance, and the declared edge, vertex, and cache-fit tolerances. For neutral admission, an exact-cache endpoint miss above this allowance permits a derived vertex tolerance equal to the largest incident endpoint miss. Every incident edge must have an evaluable curve endpoint. The derived tolerance must be no more than one percent of the diagonal of each owning body's axis-aligned vertex-point bounds in the shared model frame. A body with no finite positive diagonal supplies no bound. An unowned vertex supplies no bound. A miss above the bound leaves the stored tolerance unchanged. Curve caches, parameters, vertex points, and existing larger tolerances retain their values. The derived tolerance carries the loss code `geometry.vertex-tolerance-widened`, the vertex count, and the maximum tolerance increase in millimetres. A disagreement supplies no additional translation, scale, parameter map, or replacement point. The two spring support slots and their pcurves remain ordered and independent of the solved 3D cache.

The Design body-map carriers classify binary BREP entries by complete basename. Each archive basename identifies exactly one archive entry and occurs in exactly one carrier record. A populated carrier resolves to exactly one archive entry. A zero-pair snapshot carrier can name an absent blob; that carrier contributes an empty body set. A zero-pair snapshot carrier whose blob exists classifies that archive entry. In each Design stream, one or more modern body-map records select the model `.smbh` set. When that stream has no modern map record, its snapshot body-map records select the model `.smb` set. Modern maps with zero pairs and empty basenames select an empty physical model-body set. Snapshot maps do not add physical bodies when modern maps exist. If all selected modern maps are empty and no physical body members are declared, the local physical-body set is final and empty. A part document with this empty set, no sketch entity or reference-image timeline object, and no mesh geometry container that transferred no mesh body is an empty design; the decoder reports it with the loss code `design.empty` in place of the geometry and topology transfer losses. Outgoing document references make such a document an assembly; optional document-type metadata is not required. A profile that registers neither body-map family has no Design-level partition; every binary BREP in the manifest-selected Design asset contributes to the model. History streams are selected independently by the header flag ([`asm.md`](asm.md) §1) and every selected history graph is decoded.

An `int_int_cur` support slot names its own surface and parameter curve. The two slots retain their serialized order. A `rot_spl_sur` or `rotsur` support uses the profile parameter as U and the rotation angle as V. Its solved surface cache uses its stored B-spline parameterization. Angular knot values delimit spans; a rational circular span is not linear in the rotation angle. The support pcurve is in the construction chart and does not assert an identity map to the cache chart.

---

## 3. Materials and appearance (non-B-rep)

### 3.1 Design metadata

The counted `DerivedInstance` prefix has an eleven-byte indexed header, ten zero bytes, and a marked prologue reference at offset 21. Each plain local reference consists of byte `1`, a little-endian u64 target, and two zero segment flags. A typed local reference inserts an LP-ASCII type GUID of 36 bytes between the target and the flags; it spans 51 bytes. The source-placement count follows the prologue reference: at offset 32 with plain references and offset 72 with typed references. The first source entry starts at offset 36 or 76, respectively. Each source entry stores one local relation reference, one matrix flag, and its optional matrix. Flag `1` encodes identity; flag `0` introduces sixteen little-endian f64 values. The matrices use row-major order and centimetre translations.

A u32 auxiliary-pair count follows the source placements. Each pair lists an auxiliary reference and its source relation reference, in two consecutive marked fields. A second u32 count and a run of marked relation references follow. This count equals the pair count, and these references repeat the pairs' second members in an independently stored order. Four zero bytes, one marked primary relation reference, byte `1`, and a second transform slot follow. The second transform uses the same matrix-flag grammar. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID and three zero bytes close this prefix at the generic ordered-reference table. The source placement run and the ordered-reference table can list their relations in different orders. An empty source-placement run retains its primary relation and the second transform slot. Native construction fields retain every reference's target and inline type GUID.

The 57-byte and 58-byte derived-instance relations have an eleven-byte indexed header and ten zero bytes. The marked carrier reference starts at offset 21. In the 57-byte form, two zero bytes follow that reference, the middle reference starts at offset 34, one zero byte follows it, and the scope reference starts at offset 46. In the 58-byte form, bytes `01 00 00` follow the carrier reference, the middle reference starts at offset 35, one zero byte follows it, and the scope reference starts at offset 47. The scope reference names the owning scope, and the carrier reference names its component occurrence in the same Design stream. A relation can precede or follow its owning scope in stream order. Its class tag is local to that stream.

The 177-byte typed relation uses the same three references and zero separators as the 57-byte form. Its carrier reference starts at offset 21, two zero bytes occupy offsets 72 and 73, the middle reference starts at offset 74, one zero byte occupies offset 125, and the scope reference starts at offset 126. The typed prologue reference carries type GUID `71BBEDD5-81F8-4585-816B-05908C207204`. Source relation references carry `2D6E13A1-BBEF-4FB3-9277-00D99F634136`. The auxiliary reference carries the operand-path-locator type GUID `2E3AC990-483D-4A55-8662-C064B976A957`. The relation's carrier, middle and scope references carry `CE2913AA-CFE0-4F04-9102-24424ED3BCFA`, `6CCF41D5-40BE-48ED-A834-18F3EAED6C57` and `66E375EA-40F1-4115-8D83-0F23DD30593E`, respectively.

A class-`279` / class-`261` `DerivedInstance` scope is a 443-byte frame. `byte_offset` anchors its primary indexed header and the paired class-261 header begins at `byte_offset + 443`. Ten zero bytes occupy offsets 11 through 20. A marked reference at offset 21 carries `reference_record_index` at offset 22 and has six zero trailing bytes. The scope stores u32 `1` at offset 32, a marked relation reference at offset 36, one zero byte at offset 47, and a row-major rigid transform of sixteen little-endian f64 values at offset 48. The transform has an orthonormal three-column basis and homogeneous final row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`; translation is in centimetres. The relation reference is the scope's sole ordered reference. Its class-`310` relation is a 57-byte three-reference frame. Ten zero bytes follow its indexed header; its marked fields start at offsets 21, 34, and 46, with zero tails of eight, seven, and six bytes. The first relation member names the earlier class-`380` component-occurrence carrier, and the third names the DerivedInstance scope. The carrier's occurrence GUID and explicit rigid transform identify the local occurrence; its transform equals the scope transform. The occurrence GUID is the neutral occurrence identity.

A `Shell` scope stores its walls in a pair of optional slots. The form has no class or frame-length requirement: class tags are local to a stream, and the frame length follows the wall, face, and auxiliary-reference counts. The inside wall slot comes first and the outside wall slot follows it. An absent slot is one zero byte. A present slot is a marked reference of eleven bytes to the wall's thickness scalar in centimetres. At least one slot is present. A present inside slot grows the wall inside the original boundary, and a present outside slot grows it outside. Both slots together make a wall on both sides of the original boundary, and the two thicknesses add up to the wall thickness. A neutral `Shell` with two different wall offsets has `BothSides` mode and an unset single thickness; its source retains both offsets.

One of four prefixes precedes the slots. Offsets are relative to the primary indexed header.

- In the cornered prefix, offsets 11 through 20 are zero, offset 21 is the tangent-chain Boolean, and offset 22 is the corner Boolean, with `0` for sharp corners and `1` for rounded corners. The slots start at offset 23, and twelve zero bytes follow them.
- In the compact prefix, offsets 11 through 20 are zero and offset 21 is a Boolean. The slots start at offset 22, and eight zero bytes follow them.
- In the marked prefix, offsets 11 through 19 are zero, offset 20 is `1`, offset 21 is a Boolean, offsets 22 through 24 are zero, and offset 25 is `1`. The slots start at offset 26, and eight zero bytes follow them.
- In the counted prefix, offsets 11 through 25 are those of the marked prefix. The counted prefix stores one prefix byte at offset 26. The slots start at offset 27. The zero-byte form uses the inside-first slot ordering. Four zero bytes, a u32 count `N`, `N` marked auxiliary references of eleven bytes each, and four zero bytes follow them. The auxiliary references are outside the ordered reference table.

A u32 group count, that many marked group references, a counted GUID, and three zero bytes follow, and the ordered reference table starts there. The face group is a construction group. Its role `0x0000001000000000` selects the faces that the shell removes, and its role `0x0000000400000000` selects the target bodies of a closed shell. In the cornered prefix, the first ordered reference is the first group, the table retains the groups and their members, and the table ends with the wall scalars in slot order. In the other prefixes, exactly one slot is present, the table has at least three references, the face group and the wall scalar are two different ordered references, and the remaining ordered references are the members of the face group.

Same-index scope envelopes with the same logical payload are equivalent generation forms. Scope byte offsets, scope IDs, frame lengths, primary and paired class tags, and the current and effective preceding history-state identities do not participate in that equivalence; all other logical fields, including the feature-family token, family ordinal, and ordered reference indices, must match. When exactly one envelope's current and effective preceding history-state identities resolve to one ASM transition, that envelope is authoritative. When none resolves to an ASM transition and all logical payloads are equivalent, the later equivalent envelope in stream order is authoritative. When none resolves to an ASM transition, or more than one does, and exactly one envelope begins at a primary record frame of its stream's MetaStream record index, that envelope is authoritative; a stream can retain an older typed-reference envelope after the live plain-reference one. Every other duplicate group is malformed.

The last edge-recipe member of a counted construction-operand group ends at the immediately following indexed record. Its terminal record index need not continue the consecutive indices of the member's four-record envelope.

A body-map entity suffix between a history-bearing parameter scope and the next parameter scope is the result body of the first scope. Its BREP basename selects that scope's ASM history when the scope's state pair occurs in multiple histories. A whole-body recipe whose solved candidate faces name exactly one candidate BREP supplies the same history selection. An edge-selection recipe of the scope supplies it too: its Design reference tags faces of the BREP that the recipe was evaluated against. A candidate BREP selects the history when the faces of those tags, the faces of the recipe selector tags, the candidate faces of each recipe reference and the candidate faces of the scope's edge operands all lie in that BREP's blob.

History-state identities and body slots are local to one ASM history. A construction recipe state resolves by Design stream, bound ASM history, and state identity; the same numeric state identity in another history does not name the recipe's topology state or its producing feature.

A scope's preceding and current history-state identities delimit its ASM transition interval. The interval follows the current state's `next` links back to the preceding state and can contain intermediate states. Each link names one state in the same history. The bound transition predecessor equals that linked state's identity. The interval contains every transition after the preceding state through the current state. Its affected body slots are the union of the bodies touched by those transitions, including bodies touched through topology incidence. A body slot whose first change in the interval is an insertion and whose last change is a deletion is transient: neither endpoint state holds it, and it is excluded from the affected slots. An empty transition contributes an empty set. Repeated body slots contribute one identity. A complete interval requires unique endpoint and intermediate identities, consistent links, and complete body incidence for every transition. The scope-to-history binding selects the interval namespace. An affected slot joins an active body in that history's BREP basename. A saved free-edge body uses the saved edge's stable slot for this join. An affected saved free edge is a touched entity and not a result body of the scope. A slot with several active identities remains unresolved.

`MetaStream.dat` is a segment header, a type table, two record indexes, and an optional property block. It is not a sequence of independent object records.

The header is the LP-ASCII segment type name, the u32 segment ID, an LP-UTF16 asset GUID, a u32 serializer magic, three further u32 when that magic is `1234` and one otherwise, a second LP-ASCII segment type name, an LP-ASCII add-in name, and two u32. The two type names need not be equal: the first is the segment's short name and the second its full type name.

The type table is `u32 count` and that many entries. An entry is an LP-ASCII type GUID, an LP-ASCII base type GUID, a u32 type version, an LP-ASCII add-in name, a u32 id count, and that many little-endian u64 design-entity IDs. The base type GUID is empty for a root type. The ID count is a count rather than a flag; an entry carries any number of IDs, including none.

A type GUID is an opaque length-prefixed string, not a parsable GUID. The field holds 36 or 37 characters, and its hyphens do not always fall at the canonical positions; a reader that validates hyphen placement or fixes the width at 36 rejects real files. Compare and store the string whole. The inline type GUID a generation-3 reference carries is always 36 characters.

The add-in name names the owning module and is shared by every type that module registers, so it classifies a type's module and does not identify the type. The registered modules are `ACT`, `Animation`, `Body`, `BrowserAddInIdentifier`, `CommonData`, `Component`, `DataModel`, `Dimension`, `EntityTracking`, `Fusion`, `Geometry`, `MSketch`, `ParaMesh`, `Scene`, `SimBase`, `SimCommon`, `SimFEACSObjects`, `SimPostProcessing`, and `SimStructuralAttributes`. The name is also empty, on entries no module claims, so it does not partition the table: the type GUID is the only stable identity a type carries across files.

The type table is followed by `u32 count` and that many u64 named-entity IDs, then the primary record index as `u32 count` and that many `(u64 entity ID, u64 BulkStream offset)` pairs, then a secondary index in the same form. A u64 next-entity-ID counter follows. A segment can end at the secondary index or after this counter. The live extent of a Design `BulkStream` ends at the first eleven-byte Design record header after the greatest BulkStream offset in either index if and only if that header's record index is strictly less than the record index of the header at that indexed offset.

When bytes remain after the counter, a u32 version-context count follows. Exactly that many complete contexts follow. The count is bounded by the remaining byte extent at the minimum context length.

Each context starts with an opaque u64 token and an LP-UTF16 asset identity. The identity is a GUID, or a GUID, an underscore, and a version URN in one LP-UTF16 string. A zero u32 can precede each GUID. A short context then carries an LP-UTF16 revision GUID and a u32 revision. A full context can carry an LP-UTF16 revision GUID after the asset GUID. Its remaining fields are an LP-UTF16 version URN, an LP-UTF16 asset-revision GUID, and a u32 revision. The GUIDs are canonical 36-character hyphenated GUIDs. A short context without zero prefixes occupies 164 bytes, the minimum context length. The version URN is a nonempty ASCII URN.

The stream can end after the context list. Otherwise a property block follows: `u32 count` and that many `(LP-ASCII key, u32 value)` pairs. These fields close the stream exactly.

Offsets increase strictly within each record index, and entity IDs are unique within each index. The primary index covers every sibling record in the `BulkStream`. Its entry for an entity names that entity's sole live sibling record. An indexed-record-shaped byte run at another offset is contained payload and does not replace or add a sibling record. The named-entity ID list is exactly the set of entity IDs whose bulk record carries a nonempty name. Every secondary-index entity ID is also a primary-index entity ID, and its offset lies strictly inside that entity's primary record, locating a nested record header carried within that record's own payload. The secondary offset bounds one class-member level; it does not end the primary record.

The segment ID is unique within its asset folder, not within the archive, so a cross-segment reference resolves against the segments of its own asset. It is not a fixed enum and it is not positional: a Design segment is not always `0`. The two u32 after the add-in name are a segment _type_ code — `1` Design, `5` ACT, `6` Browser — and are the same in every archive; they are not the segment ID.

**References.** Every reference member of every record in every Fusion segment uses one encoding:

```
u8   present               0 ends the reference; nothing follows
u64  target entity ID
LP-ASCII 36 target type GUID        present in the inline-typed form
u8   cross_document
if cross_document == 0:
    u8   different_segment
    if different_segment == 1: u32 target segment ID
if cross_document == 1:
    u32  target segment ID          a segment of the TARGET document
    LP-UTF16 asset GUID
    u8   same_document
    if same_document == 0:
        LP-ASCII 36 target type GUID    required without an inline type; otherwise omitted or equal
        LP-UTF16 link name          equals a `RedirectionsStream.dat` `neutronRole`
        u8   versioned
        if versioned == 1:
            LP-UTF16 36 property-key GUID
            LP-UTF16 version URN    an `urn:adsk.wipprod:fs.file:vf.…?version=n`
```

The LP-UTF16 asset GUID in a cross-document reference is the primary GUID of the target document's root Design asset. It is the first GUID after the base name in that asset's per-asset `Manifest.dat`. Select the unique asset listed by the target top-level manifest whose asset type is `FusionAssetType` and whose Fusion subtype is empty. The source top-level manifest labels this value `linkedAssetGUID`. The target top-level active-asset GUID can name an Animation or Simulation Case asset and does not define this reference value. The member-name UUID, document GUID, second per-asset GUID, and Design MetaStream header GUID are separate identities. An absent or ambiguous root Design asset does not establish a reference asset GUID.

`cross_document`, `different_segment`, `same_document`, and `versioned` are booleans. A cross-document reference does not always end after the link name: `versioned` of `1` appends the property-key GUID that names the version property and the target document's version URN, and the property-key GUID is one value per document. So a null reference is one byte, a same-segment reference is eleven, and a cross-segment reference is fifteen: length arithmetic that uses one reference width fails on a record that reaches another segment. The recurring idiom `0x01`, a u32 record index, and six zero bytes elsewhere in this document is this encoding read with a 32-bit id — the six bytes are the id's high half, which is zero while entity IDs stay small, followed by the two flag bytes.

The inline-typed reference form places an LP-ASCII 36 target type GUID between the target entity ID and `cross_document`. Its local form is 51 bytes. A qualified reference uses this inline target type in place of the separate type after `same_document`. If both type fields are present, their GUIDs are equal. The UTF-16 link name follows the type fields; its code-unit count does not state that a separate ASCII type field is present. The ASCII type field has length prefix `0x24`; the `cross_document` flag is `0` or `1`. An LP-ASCII GUID inside a reference names the target record's type.

Within the payload, members are written one class level at a time, most-derived level first, and within a level in **case-sensitive lexicographic order of the member name**, so an uppercase initial sorts before a lowercase one. Declaration order does not reach the stream. A member added at a later record version takes its place in that ordering rather than at the end, so a version gate moves a member into the middle of a level, not onto its tail.

Every payload opens with a presence byte for a class-defined leading block. The byte is `00` or `01` and never anything else. When it is `00` the property-block presence byte follows immediately, which is the common two-byte prologue. When it is `01` the class writes its leading block first and the property-block presence byte follows that block; a sketch relation's pair list is such a block. So the second payload byte is the property-block presence byte only on records whose first byte is `00`, and a reader that takes it unconditionally misframes every record carrying a leading block.

When the property-block presence byte is `01`, a u32 property count and that many `(LP-ASCII key, LP-ASCII type name, value)` triples follow before the first member. `EntityGenesis`, `pt_tag`, `crv_primary_id`, `crv_secondary_id`, `crv_tag_id_idx`, `DcFeatureOperationIdFlag`, and the sketch-text tags are keys of this block, not members of any class; the type name `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64` selects a u64 value. Any reader that addresses members by fixed offset therefore misframes exactly those records that happen to carry a property.

A record's payload may also carry a nested record header for its own entity, located by the segment's secondary index. It bounds the member sequence: the class levels end where that header begins.

A `BulkStream` record begins with an LP-ASCII decimal class tag, the u64 entity ID, and an LP-ASCII record name, then the member payload. The entity ID repeats the record-index key. The class tag is segment-local: its value is `256` plus the index of the type in that segment's type table, so one number names different types in different segments and the type GUID is the only stable discriminator. The type selected by a record's class tag is the type whose ID list contains that record's entity ID.

The Fusion feature-timeline record has type GUID `2F4C1849-1A5A-4F6C-A086-8DD445CBF94B`, base-type GUID `98542EB9-A4F2-4137-A808-DBB5B3CD6159`, type version `2` or `3`, and add-in name `Fusion`. Both versions use the same record grammar. Its type-table entity-ID run is the ordered list of timeline-record identities. Each record has the common `BulkStream` prefix, the two-byte absent-leading-block and absent-property-block prologue, one non-null same-segment context reference, a u32 item count, and that many item references. An item reference is a same-segment reference or a null reference. A null reference is a single zero byte and can precede a non-null reference. A trailing null item names no record and has no item position. A reference can carry its target type GUID inline; that GUID equals the target entity's type-table registration. The non-null item references are distinct within the Design stream, and the record ends after the final reference. An empty item run is valid. More than one timeline record can belong to one Design stream, but the records carry separate context references and do not encode an order between two nonempty item runs. Besides a parameter scope, an item can name a paste or body-to-component object that owns a `Base Feature` scope (below), a new component's group scope (type GUID `54F9ACE8-B5B8-4A6E-B582-64F629511DE4`, whose members are the component's creation scope and its occurrence step), or an occurrence's grounding (type GUID `21E03EC1-0E53-406D-A852-6D088D4D1E95`).

The item run gives authored construction order. An item can name any typed Design record and need not name a parameter scope. A parameter scope named by the item run represents a top-level feature. An unlisted parameter scope is an internal operation operand or history carrier and remains native. Its current and preceding history-state identities can bridge two listed scopes. A history-state dependency follows a unique state chain in one component naming space, one Design stream, and one bound ASM history through zero or more unlisted scopes to the preceding listed scope. Equal state numbers in different component clusters do not identify one state. A Design stream with no component naming-space registrations uses one aggregate state namespace. An absent or non-unique state chain creates no neutral dependency. Equal current and preceding state identities on the same scope do not create a dependency. A listed scope's neutral feature ordinal is its item position; items without a projected scope retain their positions as gaps. An `Assemble` datum envelope bound to a `JointOrigin` scope contributes one `JointOrigin` feature and no `Assemble` feature. The `JointOrigin` uses its own item position when the run lists it and otherwise uses the datum envelope's item position. A timeline-less Design stream contains scopes from one feature family, and its complete one-based family-local ordinal sequence gives their authored order. Independent nonempty timelines and independent scope-bearing Design streams do not encode a shared total construction order.

The design `BulkStream` caches each body's axis-aligned bounding box in the three indexed records whose identities are the body entity suffix plus one, two, and three. Each record contains a `u8 1` marker followed by the same six contiguous f64 values in centimetres, ordered `(xmax, ymax, zmax, xmin, ymin, zmin)`. Every maximum is greater than or equal to its corresponding minimum, and a body has positive extent on at least one axis. The three marker-and-sextuple frames are byte-identical despite the records' different dynamic class tags and prefix lengths. Model-space bounds convert each coordinate to millimetres. The body entity suffix joins the cache to every BREP body-map pair carrying that suffix in the same Design stream.

The design BulkStream BREP body map belongs to the type family with GUID `74CA4562-59F8-4C97-8AD1-F8297C21F9AA`, base-type GUID `E8DCB040-6A0E-4AD1-BCF3-1E1AEDD35EE4`, type version `0`, and add-in name `Body`. The sibling MetaStream type entry lists the family's entity IDs. The primary record index gives each entity's BulkStream offset, and the next primary offset gives the record end. This type family also contains non-map record frames. A body-map frame has an eleven-byte indexed header followed by either ten or eleven reserved zero bytes and a `u32 count`. Exactly `count` ordered pairs of `u64 body_selector, u64 entity_suffix` follow. The tail is either a bare u64 record reference plus a zero u32, or a local reference to a Body container with type GUID `CD57BC48-50EC-47DC-975A-FB6DEA72F4DA`. The typed-reference form can carry one additional reserved zero after its ordinary two-zero envelope. A `u32 char_count` and UTF-16LE basename code units follow the tail and end at the primary-record boundary. A positive-count record stores a `BREP.<uuid>.smbh` basename. A zero-count record stores no pairs and a zero character count. The pair count has no format bound below `u32::MAX`; the record extent imposes the physical bound. `entity_suffix` is the numeric suffix of the design entity ID. The basename qualifies the selector namespace and selects the BREP blob contributing the mapped bodies to the document model. `body_selector` first matches an equal nonnegative ASM body key. If that key is absent from the blob, the selector matches the zero-based ordinal among the blob's body records that are not sketch regions. A blob that stores a nonnegative key on no body record can store sketch-region body records. A sketch-region body has at least one edge, every edge stores a `sketch_attrib_def` record, no face stores an attribute, and no shell owns a wire edge. It holds the planar regions of one Sketch and is not a model body. The blob's body-map selectors then name exactly the remaining body records. A planar surface body made from a Sketch has `sketch_attrib_def` records on its edges and a face attribute, so it is a model body. Every ordered pair resolves to exactly one solved body under its blob's selector namespace. Multiple referenced blobs contribute independent topology graphs to one document model. A retained nonnegative body-key edit updates Design selectors that matched the old key; ordinal selectors remain unchanged.

The sibling snapshot body-map family has type GUID `40DCC3F41D-E94F-B3B1-3E95-9B6ABE572C`, the same base-type GUID, type version `0` or `1`, and add-in name `Body`. This family also contains non-map frames. A map frame uses the bare entity header `u32 3`, the three-byte dynamic class tag, the u64 entity ID, and six zero bytes. A local reference to the entity ID plus one follows; its target has type GUID `E55D0457-898F-4A8E-B1A5-C85BDBA8794F`. Two or three zero bytes in total after the target and a u32 pair count precede that many ordered `(u64 body_selector, u64 entity_suffix)` pairs. The three-zero form inserts one additional reserved zero after the ordinary or doubled-presence envelope. Each entity suffix has type GUID `D3937028-C20C-4E65-B010-94AD418A5C20`. A local reference to a Body container with type GUID `CD57BC48-50EC-47DC-975A-FB6DEA72F4DA`, three zero bytes in total after its target, and a length-prefixed UTF-16LE basename complete the primary-record extent. The ordinary same-segment and inline-typed envelopes own the first two trailing zeros; the doubled-presence envelope owns none. The basename is empty or a `BREP.<uuid>.smb` name. An empty basename requires zero pairs. Named zero-pair records use the archive resolution rule in §2. In the ordinary same-segment reference form with two trailing companion zeros, the entity header occupies 21 bytes, the companion reference starts at offset 21, the pair count is at offset 32, and the pairs start at offset 36. The ordinary container reference and its additional zero occupy 12 bytes; the basename character count follows at tail offset 12. Local references use the same-segment, inline-typed, or doubled-presence envelope; an inline type GUID equals the target entity's type-table registration.

The direct join from a mesh geometry container (§1.1.2) to its Design body uses three record classes whose type-table add-in name is `ParaMesh`. The entry-name class has type GUID `A1BAA3F6-4B67-4A0D-BACC-75F38A2230F3`, base-type GUID `130A0711-4E92-4FCD-AADE-B9C82238BB27`, and type version `0`. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, a marked same-segment reference to the GUID record at offset 21, and the u32-count UTF-16LE blob-part entry name `ParaMeshGeometry.<uuid>.paramesh` at offset 32. The entry name ends at the primary-record boundary. The GUID class has type GUID `A8338A26-5436-433C-8BAC-C3CF024AD595`, base-type GUID `98542EB9-A4F2-4137-A808-DBB5B3CD6159`, and type version `1`. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, eleven bytes at offset 21, the 36-byte LP-ASCII `fusion_uuid` at offset 32, and a marked same-segment backlink to the entry-name record at offset 72. The two records reference each other. The stored `fusion_uuid` equals the container field and is independent of the entry-name `<uuid>`.

The mesh-body class has type GUID `EA90DA22-556C-4C61-89BB-20C2681B7A9D`, base-type GUID `CB844AB6-240D-4FC9-9C9F-3679DC896D6F`, and type version `6` or `7`. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes. It stores a u32 at offset 21. It carries two equal row-major 4×4 f64 affine matrices at record-relative offsets 42 and 171. Unequal matrices make the body record invalid. Marked same-segment references at offsets 508, 519, 530, 541, and 553 name the owning feature scope, the reciprocal body wrapper, a `Body` owner, the GUID record, and a Scene node. A mesh body can instead store byte `01` at offset 20, in place of the last of the ten zero bytes, and a u32 at offset 21. It stores another u32 at offset 25. In this flagged form, the fields after offset 21 start four bytes later: the matrices start at offsets 46 and 175, and the five references start at offsets 512, 523, 534, 545, and 557. A version-6 body can store byte `01` at offset 20 while its matrices and references use the unshifted positions. A u32-count UTF-16LE display name follows its Scene-node reference. The first matrix presence byte is at offset 41 in the unshifted form and offset 45 in the shifted form. A compact version-6 body stores its first matrix presence byte at offset 37; its first matrix starts at offset 38 and its second matrix starts at offset 167 when both presence bytes are zero. A zero presence byte is followed by one 4×4 f64 matrix. A presence byte `01` has no matrix payload. The second presence byte follows the first presence byte and its payload. Fifteen bytes follow the second presence byte and its payload, and the first presentation envelope follows them. Six reference slots follow its two length-prefixed GUIDs and preset name: the five references in their stated order, with a further slot between the GUID and Scene-node references. The wrapper, owner, GUID, and Scene-node slots each hold a marked same-segment reference. The feature-scope slot holds a marked same-segment reference or one zero byte; the further slot before the Scene-node reference is open item DR-373. A zero byte in the feature-scope slot states a mesh body that no feature scope owns. Its mesh represents no body and no mesh feature; the neutral model lists it among the tessellations of the root product definition, or, in an inserted `.f3z` member, of the member definition that the inserting occurrence instances. The final eleven bytes of the primary record are a marked same-segment backlink to the owning mesh collection. The `Body` owner class has type GUID `CD57BC48-50EC-47DC-975A-FB6DEA72F4DA`, base-type GUID `A7AEA631-985B-4DD1-8CE2-DE2C-14B54081`, type version `4`, and add-in name `Body`. An alternate `Body` owner has type GUID `3A8E00DC-E342-4C03-8521-846BD9F7513E`, base-type GUID `A193F53F-86D7-4F45-A01C-51F5ECEEFC0E`, type version `3`, and add-in name `Body`. Multiple mesh bodies in one feature can reference the same `Body` owner. Each container joins through one mutually referencing entry-name and GUID pair. Multiple mesh-body records can reference the same GUID record. A join is valid only when exactly one entry-name and GUID pair across the Design streams carries the container entry name and `fusion_uuid`; every mesh body that references that GUID record joins the container. The matrix maps container vertex coordinates to model centimetres: its upper-left 3×3 block is nonsingular and carries axis scale and orientation, column 3 carries translation, and its bottom row is `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. The determinant can have either sign. The matrix changes vertex coordinates and transforms oriented normals with its cofactor matrix; triangle tuples and attribute selectors remain in container order. A negative determinant reverses model-space geometric winding relative to container-space winding. An untransformed millimetre mesh stores the f64 nearest float `0.1` on the first three diagonal cells and zero translation. The matrices are followed by two presentation envelopes with the body display name between them. An envelope is a length-prefixed UTF-16LE GUID, the physical-material library id `C1EEA57C-3F56-45FC-B8CB-A9EC46A9994C`, a zero u32, and a length-prefixed UTF-16LE preset name; the first name is the physical material `PrismMaterial-` followed by decimal digits, and the second is that name followed by `_physmat_aspects:Prism-` and decimal digits. The fixed offsets of the five references hold when both presence bytes are zero, the first preset name has 17 code units, and the feature-scope slot holds a reference; otherwise the references follow the first envelope as the presence bytes and the preset-name length place them. The display-name count is zero on a body that carries no name.

The mesh-collection class has type GUID `443807AD-8025-41A3-8A50-5157579C3D78`, base-type GUID `A7AEA631-985B-4DD1-8CE2-DE2C-14B54081`, type version `0`, and add-in name `ParaMesh`. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, a u32 body count at offset 21, bytes `01 01` at offset 25, a marked same-segment texture-table reference at offset 27, and a nested same-index record at offset 38. The nested record has type GUID `A7AEA631-985B-4DD1-8CE2-DE2C-14B54081`, base-type GUID `834C9DEF-4C39-4587-A08D-A5BD1267B7B4`, type version `0`, and add-in name `CommonData`. Its indexed header is followed by nine zero bytes, a second u32 body count at collection offset 58, that many ordered marked same-segment body references at offset 62, and one marked same-segment owner reference. The two counts are equal. The collection ends after the owner reference and has length `73 + 11 × body_count` bytes. A collection with body count zero is an empty ParaMesh registry and has no mesh-body or `Base Mesh Feature` graph. An empty collection can also store a zero u32 between its second count and its owner reference; it then has length 77 bytes. A collection can instead store byte `01` at offset 20, in place of the last of the ten zero bytes, and a u32 at offset 25 after its first body count. In this flagged form, the first body count is zero, and bytes `01 01`, the texture-table reference, and the nested record start at offsets 29, 31, and 42. The second body count `N` at collection offset 62 counts the ordered body references that follow it. When `N` is nonzero, the owner reference can follow the body references directly. The counted-entry form inserts a u32 entry count `M` that is zero or `N`, and `M` entries that each store a marked same-segment reference to one of the collection's bodies and u32 `1`, before the owner reference. An empty flagged collection stores its owner reference at offset 66 and has length 77 bytes, or stores a zero u32 at offset 66 and its owner reference at offset 70 and has length 81 bytes. The owner has type GUID `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`, base-type GUID `42054630-20A0-40E1-B969-CFE9E742F5C9`, type version `15`, `17`, `19`, `20`, `21`, `22`, or `23`, and add-in name `Fusion`. The named-entry form stores one length-prefixed UTF-16LE entry name `netfabb.mesh_body` followed by a marked same-segment reference to the collection. This form applies to each listed owner version. In versions 22 and 23, the fixed-prefix form stores its marked same-segment reference at offset 262. This reference points back to the collection. Version 21 stores a u32-count UTF-16LE name at offset 25, and the fields after the name start at the version-22 offsets plus the name length of `4 + 2 × count` bytes, so its collection backlink is at offset `266 + 2 × count`. Version 17 stores its collection backlink at offset 241. Both fixed-offset records can continue after the backlink prefix. Version 15 stores the backlink in the final eleven bytes of its variable-length owner frame. A nonempty mesh collection can hold bodies from multiple mesh feature scopes and bodies that no feature scope owns. A collection whose bodies all lack a feature scope has no `Base Mesh Feature` scope.

A mesh operation member has type GUID `1AA9CC7B-5C34-45DA-AE14-0444E7F966F2`, base-type GUID `6144EA59-3ACA-4172-9F14-A6531E94D69B`, type version `0`, and add-in name `Fusion`. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes and a marked same-segment mesh-body reference at offset 21. A mesh operation scope has type GUID `E3EB3760-4362-48D6-ABF3-698B0C12C5A9`, base-type GUID `90B8D2C6-05BB-4D0F-89EF-83AAC46CA1FF`, type version `1`, and add-in name `Fusion`, and is a parameter scope. A mesh operation group has type GUID `22975A91-16AD-4CC9-A5E4-B4F8B4C27881`, base-type GUID `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841`, type version `0`, and add-in name `Fusion`, and is a construction-operand group. The reference table of the operation scope lists the group, and the group members include the operation member. The mesh body references the operation scope and its mesh collection.

The mesh face-group parameter scopes use type GUID `CA2AE956-FD81-4EBD-A601-F93A0F335722`, version `3`, for `GenerateFaceGroups`, and `8136D47E-3955-4682-8BD7-B353B7B45624`, version `1`, for `CombineFaceGroups`. Both have base GUID `90B8D2C6-05BB-4D0F-89EF-83AAC46CA1FF` and add-in `Fusion`. The primary index selects each live scope frame. A face-group scope prefix stores ten zero bytes after its eleven-byte indexed header; its family members start at offset 21. Generate stores three nullable parameter-owner references in angle, boundary-tolerance, and minimum-size order, then a u32 method code. Combine starts with one LP-ASCII 36-character UUID token. Both forms then store two mesh-GUID references, a u32 group count, and that many LP-ASCII 36-character UUID tokens in source order. A face-group UUID token occupies 40 bytes: its u32 character count is 36 and its 36 ASCII bytes start at token offset 4. The common scope envelope follows this run. The referenced mesh-GUID records have type `A8338A26-5436-433C-8BAC-C3CF024AD595`. The construction group and member use the mesh operation registrations above. A member can reference a mesh body owned by an earlier scope.

A Generate parameter has source kind `Angle Threshold`, `Boundary Tolerance`, or `Minimum Face Group Size`. Its owner names the same scope and is present in the scope reference table. The angle scalar is in radians. The boundary-tolerance scalar uses the Design length convention of centimetres. The minimum-size scalar is dimensionless. The owner-local ordinal is independent of the setting role; an absent setting has a null owner reference. The face-group construction group stores operand role `0x0000_0004_0000_0000`.

The texture-table class has type GUID `6FC173DC-C7E3-402C-A8C0-891A26DADF8D`, base-type GUID `98542EB9-A4F2-4137-A808-DBB5B3CD6159`, type version `0`, and add-in name `ParaMesh`. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes and a u32 flags-map count at offset 21. Each flags-map entry is a 36-byte LP-ASCII resource GUID followed by an opaque u32 flags value. A u32 filename-map count follows the flags map. Each filename-map entry is a 36-byte LP-ASCII resource GUID followed by a marked same-segment filename-record reference. Keys are unique within each map, both maps have the same key set, and their serialized key orders are independent. Multiple resource keys can reference the same filename record. Both maps end at the primary-record boundary. An empty table is exactly 29 bytes. A filename record has type GUID `830A2A2B-0AA9-4D6A-ACA1-F7A2B2A06573`, base-type GUID `98542EB9-A4F2-4137-A808-DBB5B3CD6159`, type version `0`, and an empty add-in name. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes and one nonempty u32-count UTF-16LE archive-entry basename. The basename ends at the primary-record boundary and resolves to exactly one entry in `Images.BlobParts`.

The mesh wrapper has type GUID `E5B3F49A-D8D0-4EEF-BC2B-FCDDAEF9745E`, base-type GUID `98542EB9-A4F2-4137-A808-DBB5B3CD6159`, type version `0`, and add-in name `ParaMesh`. Its 40-byte prefix holds its indexed header, ten zero bytes, a marked same-segment body reference at offset 21, and eight zero bytes. The primary record can continue after the prefix. The wrapper reference of the body names the same wrapper. Each body has one wrapper.

A mesh operation scope is a parameter scope with base-type GUID `90B8D2C6-05BB-4D0F-89EF-83AAC46CA1FF` and add-in name `Fusion`. Its indexed header is followed by nine zero bytes and a flag byte at offset 20. Flag `01` inserts a u32 at offset 21 and moves every later field four bytes higher; the offsets in this paragraph group are those of the flag-`00` form. The fixed fields of the scope end with the 38-byte geometry tail: the output-geometry reference, the input-geometry reference, a u32 `0`, the source-group reference, and a zero byte. A geometry reference is a same-segment reference to the Design GUID record of one mesh geometry state; a null output-geometry reference is one byte and identifies an operation that keeps the mesh geometry. The source group is a mesh operation group. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, a u32 member count at offset 21, and that many same-segment references to mesh operation members; each member names one mesh body. An owner reference is a same-segment reference to a parameter owner of the scope. Lengths are centimetres.

| Kind | Type GUID | Type version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MeshSection` | `8FFFCBD2-7102-4A62-BCA0-8229A3C3B9DB` | `1` |
| `MeshReduce` | `BE693D4C-741E-4794-A93E-5BFED71E9E13` | `2` |
| `MeshRepair` | `68691143-5EE3-428E-9CD3-F728E4718559` | `4` |
| `MeshRemesh` | `828DDA62-2750-447D-8728-06C9B7C2B117` | `2` |
| `MeshSmooth` | `F84CD988-9696-458D-8AF3-795D12E6B9EF` | `2` |
| `MeshShell` | `1514CDB8-BB81-4895-A953-7B12F4504F99` | `2` |
| `MeshReverseNormals` | `4AB7A6BD-C40C-4C44-B7CA-0D415B6E4412` | `0` |

A `MeshSeparate` scope has type GUID `6B6FDE2E-D9B9-4866-9D07-3123C919B0D2`, base GUID `90B8D2C6-05BB-4D0F-89EF-83AAC46CA1FF`, version `2`, and add-in name `Fusion`. Its primary and paired indexed headers delimit the scope. The [Separate prefix](../layouts/f3d.md) contains the indexed header, nine zero bytes, flag byte `0`, a u32 reference count at offset 21, and counted ordered body references starting at offset 25. The [Separate post-run fields](../layouts/f3d.md) start immediately after that complete reference run. They contain a u32 selector at relative offset 0, an eight-byte raw lane at relative offset 4, a source-group reference at relative offset 12, and a zero separator. With an eleven-byte source-group reference, the separator is at relative offset 23. The [Separate common envelope](../layouts/f3d.md) follows the separator and contains a u32 character count of 36, 36 UTF-16LE GUID code units, and three zero bytes. The common counted reference table follows this envelope. Its first entry repeats the source-group reference; its next entry names a mesh operation member. The counted body-reference run and common reference table retain their independent order.

The Separate source group uses the mesh operation group registration. After its member-reference run, a two-null-reference tail stores two zero reference slots, one u32 word, a local auxiliary reference, and a u64 role. The [Separate group tail](../layouts/f3d.md) uses the first byte after the member run as its relative origin. In the ordinary local-reference form the word is at relative offset 2, the auxiliary reference at relative offset 6, and the role at relative offset 17. A Separate source member uses the mesh operation member registration. Its body reference is followed by an auxiliary reference, one u32 word, two counted UTF-16LE identifiers, and two further u32 words. In the ordinary local-reference form the auxiliary reference starts at member offset 32, the first word at offset 43, and the first identifier's count at offset 47. Each native identifier has 36 code units. The [Separate member words](../layouts/f3d.md) use the end of the second identifier as their relative origin; the two words are at relative offsets 0 and 4.

A `MeshReverseNormals` scope stores its geometry tail at offset 21. A `MeshSmooth` scope stores the smoothness owner reference at offset 21 and its geometry tail at offset 32; the smoothness is a fraction from zero to one. A `MeshShell` scope stores the thickness owner reference at offset 21 and its geometry tail at offset 32.

A `MeshCombine` scope has type GUID `EE0E56E8-5894-4D65-BAF4-9DAAF811307F`, base-type GUID `90B8D2C6-05BB-4D0F-89EF-83AAC46CA1FF`, type version `1` or `2`, and add-in name `Fusion`. The version-1 scope prefix contains the mesh scope prefix, the operation selector, a control byte, and the tool-group count. The version-2 scope prefix inserts an additional control word after the operation selector. The operation selector and the tool-group count are u32 values. For version `2`, operation selectors `0`, `1`, and `2` select join, cut, and intersection. The counted tool-group references follow in source order. The following fields are the output-geometry reference, the input-geometry reference, a zero u32, and the target-group reference. Each group contains ordered mesh-operation member references.

A `MeshPlaneCut` scope has type GUID `E3EB3760-4362-48D6-ABF3-698B0C12C5A9`, base-type GUID `90B8D2C6-05BB-4D0F-89EF-83AAC46CA1FF`, type version `1`, and add-in name `Fusion`. It uses the mesh scope prefix. The u32 cut selector is followed by a u32 matrix count of `16`, sixteen f64 matrix components in serialized order, a u32 fill selector, and a control byte. Cut selector `0` trims the mesh and `1` splits it into bodies. Fill selector `0` leaves the cut open and `1` fills it with a minimal number of faces. The following reference slots identify the source mesh group, optional output mesh group, construction group, output geometry, and input geometry. A zero u32, repeated source-group reference, and zero byte follow. A null output group occupies one byte. The source group supplies the operation input; the optional output group identifies the additional result body. The fixed prefix layout is in [the record table](../layouts/f3d.md#mesh_plane_cut_scope_prefix).

A `MeshRemove` scope has type GUID `57A2E341-A23A-469D-B41D-59B57A9AD8B8`, base-type GUID `63A5A106-D239-4D6B-A96B-319CA9B9BA6A`, type version `0`, and add-in name `Fusion`. It uses the mesh scope prefix. Its flag-`00` form stores a marked source-group reference at offset 21, a u32 scope-GUID length of `36` at offset 32, and the 36 UTF-16LE scope-GUID code units at offset 36. The source group contains the mesh bodies removed by the feature.

A `MeshReduce` scope stores the tolerance owner reference at offset 21, a u32 distribution selector at offset 32, a zero byte at offset 36, the proportion owner reference at offset 37, a u32 target selector at offset 48, the face-count owner reference at offset 52, and its geometry tail at offset 63. Distribution `0` is adaptive and `1` is uniform. Target `0` bounds the reduction by the tolerance, the largest deviation from the source; target `1` by the proportion, the percentage of source faces that the result keeps; target `2` by the face count of the result.

A `MeshRepair` scope stores the density owner reference at offset 21, the offset owner reference at offset 32, a u32 rebuild selector at offset 43, a u32 method selector at offset 47, and its geometry tail at offset 51. Method `0` closes holes, `1` stitches and removes, and `3` rebuilds the mesh with the density and the offset. Rebuild selector `0` is fast and `2` is accurate.

A `MeshRemesh` scope stores two zero bytes at offset 21, a u32 distribution selector at offset 23 with the `MeshReduce` values, and the shape-preservation owner reference at offset 27. After a non-null shape-preservation reference the scope stores a zero byte at offset 38, the edge-length owner reference at offset 39, a u32 `1` at offset 50, and its geometry tail at offset 54. A uniform distribution stores a null shape-preservation reference, and each later field is ten bytes lower. The shape preservation is a fraction from zero to one.

A `MeshSection` scope stores the section-group reference at offset 21, the reference to the `Sketch` scope that receives the section curves at offset 32, and its geometry tail at offset 43 with a null output-geometry reference. The section group is the source group.

A `Convert Mesh` scope has type GUID `62B85DC3-27B5-47BA-9F13-B2527B72EE49`, base-type GUID `2EDC2536-D95B-4469-8ACA-DC07124D9C43`, type version `4`, and add-in name `Fusion`. It uses the mesh scope prefix. In its flag-`01` form, the u32 conversion control is at offset 25, the u32 input count is at offset 29, and the ordered input-wrapper references start at offset 33. Conversion control `1` selects the prismatic method and `3` selects the faceted method. Each list reference uses the marked same-segment envelope or a null byte. The input list is followed by u32 `0xFFFFFFFF`, two zero bytes, an optional four-byte control, a u32 output count, and the ordered output-wrapper references. Eight zero bytes and a length-prefixed UTF-16LE scope GUID follow the output list.

A conversion input wrapper has type GUID `D6FB6F05-98CD-4BFF-BF90-594F77725DC1`, base-type GUID `D0D7E795-ECF7-48A8-A7A3-F983C5A29F8B`, type version `1`, and add-in name `Fusion`. Its indexed header is followed by eleven zero bytes and a marked same-segment reference to a mesh operation group at offset 22. Each wrapper defines one input context. The groups and their body members retain their serialized order.

A conversion output wrapper has type GUID `D26351F0-5940-4D23-AA20-2C35475A6D9E`, base-type GUID `CB844AB6-240D-4FC9-9C9F-3679DC896D6F`, type version `2`, and add-in name `Fusion`. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes and a u32-count UTF-16LE body GUID at offset 21. The GUID has 36 code units. A control byte, byte `01`, and a marked same-segment body reference follow it. The control byte is at offset 97, byte `01` is at offset 98, and the body reference starts at offset 99. The output list defines the order of these wrappers.

The `Base Mesh Feature` scope has type GUID `99F6967E-ED35-4222-B906-5CCF0AC70B53`, base-type GUID `2FCB0587-233E-449B-9724-9AAE5AA23647`, type version `0`, and add-in name `Fusion`. Its unflagged indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, a u32 body count at offset 21, and that many ordered marked same-segment body references at offset 25. A flagged scope stores byte `01` at offset 20 and a u32 at offset 21; its body count is at offset 25 and its body references start at offset 29. Bytes 11 through 19 are zero. The parameter-scope payload follows this list. The scope closes with a nested same-index record whose type GUID is `CB844AB6-240D-4FC9-9C9F-3679DC896D6F`, base-type GUID is `98542EB9-A4F2-4137-A808-DBB5B3CD6159`, type version is `1`, and add-in name is `DataModel` or `CommonData`. This closing record is exactly 30 bytes: its indexed header, eight zero bytes, and a marked same-segment owner reference at offset 19. Each collection body points to its collection, and each scoped collection body points to its owning scope. The scopes that its scoped bodies name partition its scoped bodies, and a body that stores no feature-scope reference belongs to no scope. Each scope lists its bodies in scope order.

The fixed mesh Scene-state record has type GUID `F85F2E62-7627-4922-A16D-53E1275D2AAC`, base-type GUID `D0EDEF7C-5879-45A4-9651-900659CC4FDD`, type version `0`, and add-in name `Scene`. It is exactly 95 bytes: its indexed header, 34 zero bytes, and the 50-byte Scene footer. The footer starts with byte `01`. Its remaining 49 bytes are either the unset-bounds sentinel or six f64 values followed by byte `01`. The finite values are the component-wise maximum corner followed by the component-wise minimum corner; every minimum component is less than or equal to its corresponding maximum. In the unset sentinel, bytes 6, 14, 22, 30, 38, and 46 are `EF`; bytes 31, 39, and 47 are `7F`; byte 48 is `01`; all other bytes are `FF`.

The Scene node has type GUID `702B9CD2-537C-429E-8CC4-22BEEEB98C37`, base-type GUID `EB7847AF-E60D-4AB0-A736-4AC00C1F1D21`, type version `1`, and add-in name `Scene`. Both forms share the indexed header, 14 zero bytes, u32 values `2` at offsets 25 and 29, a marked same-segment Scene-state reference at offset 33, u32 value `3` at offset 44, and a marked same-segment auxiliary-record reference at offset 48. The compact form is exactly 133 bytes. Its indexed header is followed by 14 zero bytes; it stores 24 zero bytes at offset 59 and the same 50-byte Scene footer at offset 83. The placed form is exactly 261 bytes. The placed form shares that header, constants, and references through offset 58. It stores 25 zero bytes at offset 59, a row-major 4×4 f64 affine transform at offset 84, and the 49-byte bounds payload at offset 212 without the compact form's leading footer marker. The transform is finite, nonsingular, and has final row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. The auxiliary record has type GUID `2343B7AB-A2E0-4C66-8B74-99A05E4C670B`, base-type GUID `74D7FEF9-44E9-494D-A25D-81EC33D2841E`, type version `1`, and add-in name `Scene`. Each mesh body has one Scene node, state, and auxiliary record.

The design BulkStream carries the document's unit settings in a `UnitSystems` collection. The collection is the LP-ASCII name `UnitSystems`, two zero bytes, `u32 6`, and six `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes` references. The six referenced records are the unit systems `CmMKS`, `MmMKS`, `MMKS`, `InchImperial`, `Imperial`, and `Custom`, in that order. A unit-system record stores an LP-ASCII key, an LP-ASCII label, byte `01`, the LP-ASCII name `<key>UnitSystemName`, the LP-ASCII namespace `NaFusion`, four zero bytes, `u32 19`, and nineteen `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes` references to its unit entries. A unit entry stores an LP-ASCII key, an LP-ASCII label, byte `01`, an LP-ASCII property name, the LP-ASCII namespace `NsCommonData`, four zero bytes, a `u32` UTF-16 code-unit count, and that many code units holding the unit name. Seventeen entries are the quantity families `Length`, `Mass`, `Time`, `Temperature`, `Speed`, `Volume`, `Pressure`, `Force`, `Power`, `Energy`, `Current`, `Substance`, `Luminosity`, `Angle`, `Currency`, `Percentage`, and `Pieces`; the remaining two are `ModelingLength` and `ModelingMass`.

The five preset systems hold fixed `ModelingLength` names: `centimeter` for `CmMKS`, `millimeter` for `MmMKS`, `meter` for `MMKS`, `inch` for `InchImperial`, and `foot` for `Imperial`. The `Custom` system holds the document's active settings; its `ModelingLength` entry, whose property name is `modelingLengthName`, holds the document display length unit as one of `millimeter`, `centimeter`, `meter`, `inch`, or `foot`. The display unit is a presentation setting and is the sole carrier of that setting. No stored quantity depends on it: model-space coordinates remain centimetres under every value, the BREP streams are independent of it, and every material-asset value carries its own unit tag.

A construction-recipe record stores its Design selector in one of two fixed frames. The prefix frame places the positive u32 selector at 20 bytes before the recipe-family name, its i32 record index at `name−16`, eight zero bytes at `name−12`, and the u32 byte length of the ASCII family name at `name−4`. The body-recipe suffix frame places the length-prefixed ASCII Design entity id at `name+24` and the selector immediately after the id; that selector names the indexed record that closes the enclosing whole-body operand. In both frames, the selector immediately follows the ASCII Design entity id. The family name selects `body_recipe_data`, `face_recipe_data`, `bounded_face_recipe_data`, `edge_recipe_data`, or `vertex_recipe_data`; the preceding record index is not a family discriminator. The common payload begins with an i64 `−1` null sentinel followed by the five i32 values `[2, 0, −1, 1, −1]`. An edge-recipe operand opens with four consecutively indexed records `N` through `N+3`; record `N+3` contains the recipe prefix, family name, and i32 program. The indexed record `N+4` terminates the ordinary edge-feature program. A `Sweep` path or guide-rail edge recipe terminates at indexed record `N+7`. Header-shaped scalar bytes inside the prefix do not terminate the operand.

An unresolved edge-selection record consists of its eleven-byte indexed header, fourteen zero bytes, `u32 19`, and ASCII `EDGE_REFERENCE_LOST`. The indexed header immediately following the marker terminates the record. Consecutive unresolved selections share that boundary: the following header of one record is the owning header of the next. An unresolved run belongs to the counted edge group whose first identity-wrapper header is the run's final following header. A run whose cardinality equals the group's operand count carries one record per operand. A run can also be shorter than the group's operand list. A complete independent recipe/history proof resolves the group's historical edges despite the unresolved run. Without such a proof, a group belonging to a scope with a preceding history state retains that state and the ordered unresolved-record identities with no resolved edges.

A fixed-radius Fillet scope with exactly one counted construction-operand group uses that group as its edge selection when every member is a compact persistent edge identity and either the group has one member with a nonempty transition-derived radius chain or every member has an exact predecessor-edge proof. A transition-derived radius-candidate set describes the complete state transition and does not assign a candidate subset to each member. The selected chain is the increasing stable-slot-order union of the qualifying predecessor edges. With multiple construction-operand groups, compact identity prefixes do not distinguish edge selections from support-face groups; only a complete edge-recipe carrier assigns the selected-edge role.

An executed `Fillet` or `Chamfer` edge group may use one nonempty transition chain when every compact persistent identity in the group carries the same chain. Without recipe evidence, the chain is complete only when its cardinality equals the member count. When the cardinalities differ, every chain edge must occur in the union of the selected recipe-reference edge sets and the members' changed or deleted boundary sets. Every member with deleted boundary edges must share one with the chain, and a resolved deleted edge must belong to the chain. The admitted chain is ordered by increasing stable edge slot.

A legacy executed `Fillet` or `Chamfer` group may use the union of deleted predecessor-boundary edges when at least one member carries such edges, the union cardinality equals the member count, every member has a complete recipe-reference context, and the contextual changed-reference candidates have exactly one perfect one-to-one assignment to that union. Each deleted edge must occur in both the preceding and changed boundary sets. The admitted union is ordered by increasing stable edge slot.

An executed `Fillet` or `Chamfer` group whose member recipes each reference exactly two faces may use the predecessor edges that its operation transition deletes. Each reference of such a member resolves to one preceding face, and the two faces differ. A member's candidates are the changed edges that both faces hold. The group selects the deleted set when the transition deletes exactly as many edges as the group has members, each resolved member edge belongs to the deleted set, every member's candidates are nonempty and deleted, the candidates together cover the deleted set, and at least one assignment pairs each member with a distinct deleted edge among its candidates. Members whose candidates coincide stay unassigned; the selected set is the same under every assignment. The selected set is ordered by increasing stable edge slot.

A legacy single-member `Fillet` or `Chamfer` group with a zero-payload two-side recipe may use a result-boundary edge when no operand boundary delta exists, that edge is named by at least two changed-reference contexts, it is the sole changed-reference edge in the result boundary, and it is absent from the preceding candidate boundary.

Standalone persistent-reference properties named `pt_tag`, `crv_primary_id`, and `crv_secondary_id` store the u32 pair `(2, 14)`, a 14-byte property slot, LP-ASCII `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64`, and the referenced u64. The compact properties embedded in sketch point and curve records omit the `(2, 14)` pair and property slot.

A generic face or edge tag group may carry a zero Design-reference count. Its selector and token remain native attribute data, but the group has no Design join and does not supply a recipe candidate. The group is retained and can be written with an empty reference run.

After the `generic_tag_attrib_def` family name, a generic-tag attribute stores two equal envelope-version integers, integer `−1`, the marker `generic_tag_attrib_def `, and a nonnegative group count. Envelope version `2` stores each body group as four values: entity kind, decimal Design id, Design reference, and integer `0`; its face and edge groups are a selector, a nonempty token, a u32 token integer, a nonnegative Design-reference count, and that many signed Design references. Version `3` adds one integer `0` to each body group and one integer `0` terminator to each face or edge group. The pair (token, token integer) identifies the group. A mixed or unsupported envelope-version pair invalidates the generic-tag payload.

Each materialized BREP history state retains the generic face and edge tag groups attached to the record revisions present in that state. Multiple face or edge revisions can carry the same token, token integer, and Design-reference set; those records are distinct fragments of one persistent selection and are not duplicates.

A face or edge recipe reference resolves in the feature-input history state. Its identity key is the token, token integer, and Design reference. Every live face or edge carrying that key belongs to the candidate set, including all fragments that inherited the same tag group. The recipe selector is structured positional data and is not compared with the tag-group selector as an integer identity. A historical candidate set supersedes candidates from the projected active BREP. A candidate already present in the feature-input state takes its surface carrier from that state; numeric entity slots in another BREP history or another state do not qualify that carrier. An active candidate absent from the feature-input state maps through a surface carrier that is invariant across the selected history. For `face_recipe_data`, references carrying the recipe's own indexed-record identity directly select the complete ordered live-face set. Transition-change cardinality does not narrow that set.

When the final eleven bytes of a sketch point or curve primary record are a marked reference, that reference is the geometry record's direct owner backlink: `0x01 + u32 sketch_container_index + six zero bytes`. It is independent of constraint membership and resolves to the record with the same index in the Design stream: a sketch entity container of type `44A64366-4BD3-4B24-881A-F94C206E8F2D` or a sketch geometry group. A group target assigns the record to the sketch container that the group names. Point class versions 0 and 8, the same-segment form of point class version 10, point class version 11, and line class version 2 carry this final backlink. In the compact NURBS form, the backlink follows the complete knot, weight, and three-coordinate control-point arrays; the indexed NURBS subtype header is nested within the curve record and does not terminate it. A point or curve without this final backlink has no direct owner. A typed sketch relation or the sketch entity container's counted member run can independently assign that record to a Sketch. Other marked references inside an extended geometry payload do not assign an owner. A record with none of these three joins is an unowned Geometry carrier.

A sketch-point geometry payload has type GUID `C2CEDAE7-1716-47C1-B7B1-07B70081D0FB`, add-in name `Geometry`, and class version 0, 8, 10, or 11. Class version 0 has no `pt_tag` property. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, a marked same-segment `paired_reference`, one flag byte, and two contiguous f64 coordinates `(u,v)`. It has no persistent point identity and no serialized `w`; its neutral depth is zero.

Class versions 8, 10, and 11 carry a `pt_tag` u64 property. An optional `EntityGenesis` u64 precedes `pt_tag` in class version 11. The property block is followed by `paired_reference`. Class versions 8 and 10 then carry seven one-byte flags. Class version 11 carries eight one-byte flags. Three contiguous f64 coordinates `(u,v,w)` follow the flags. Each flag is zero or one. All coordinates use the record form's standard length conversion. A planar Sketch uses `(u,v)` and requires `w = 0`. A spatial Sketch transforms `(u,v,w)` through the owning placement into model space. Point and curve records with the same owner belong to one neutral Sketch domain; an owner with any non-planar curve is spatial and does not also form a planar Sketch.

A derived sketch-point record has type GUID `00D157C2-2332-4BD5-BB53-048C4081D1C3`, base type GUID `C2CEDAE7-1716-47C1-B7B1-07B70081D0FB`, add-in name `MSketch`, and class version 0. Its primary frame stores the indexed header, nine zero bytes, and a non-empty property block with the class-version-11 point properties. A nested frame with the same record index follows the property block, and its class tag selects the sketch-point type with class version 11. The nested frame stores eight zero bytes at offsets 11 through 18 and the marked `paired_reference` at offset 19: `u8 1` and its u32 record index at offset 20. It stores no property-presence byte. The class-version-11 members after `paired_reference` follow. The point takes `pt_tag` and the optional `EntityGenesis` from the primary frame; every other field has its class-version-11 meaning.

The class-version-0 tail follows `(u,v)` with twenty zero bytes, f32 one, twelve zero bytes, two f32 values equal to one, bytes `01 01 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00`, a repeated marked same-segment `paired_reference`, and the direct owner backlink.

The class-version-8 closure follows `(u,v,w)` with a u64 selector, a state byte, eight zero bytes, two f32 values equal to one, bytes `00 01 00 00 00`, a repeated marked same-segment `paired_reference`, and the direct owner backlink. The only selector-state pair is `(0,0)`. The class-version-10 and class-version-11 closures use twelve zero bytes in place of the class-version-8 eight-zero lane. The same-segment class-version-10 sequence uses `(0,0)` or `(0,1)`. The inline-typed class-version-10 sequence uses those pairs or `(2,1)`. Class version 11 uses `(0,0)`, `(0,1)`, `(1,0)`, `(1,1)`, `(2,1)`, `(4,0)`, or `(4,1)`. A class-version-11 repeated `paired_reference` can be followed by four additional zero bytes before the direct owner backlink.

The point selector, point state, and versioned point flags do not select the neutral construction Boolean. A point projects as a non-construction point. A curve becomes construction geometry through a valid `TextFrame` relation or when its trailing construction flag byte equals `1` (`TextFrame` relation takes precedence); its endpoint point records do not inherit that status. In particular, `(4,0)` point endpoints can belong to a bounded line used by a midpoint relation or to a bounded line with no sketch relation, and neither the points nor that line become construction geometry from the pair alone. Profile admission therefore remains based on the resolved curve graph, explicit `TextFrame` exclusion, and the curve construction flag, not on point closure values.

The selector-state pair is native record state, not a complete geometric role code. Pair `(2,1)` permits both an empty incident-curve run and an explicit line incidence. The companion run determines incidence independently of the pair. The point remains non-construction.

Flag lanes are zero-based. In modern point forms lane 2 is zero. Lane 5 requires lane 3 and positive-zero bit patterns for all three coordinates. A zero coordinate triple does not require lane 5. Lane 7 requires class version 11, closure `(0,1)`, and one incident circular curve whose center is the point position. The remaining lanes retain independent opaque Boolean state; their values do not derive from coordinate equality or the neutral construction Boolean.

The point-tail layouts in [the fixed-layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md) start at the first flag byte. The legacy tail contains the flag, coordinates, zero lanes, f32 constants, marker, repeated paired reference, and owner reference. Each modern fixed prefix contains the flags, coordinates, selector, state, zero lane, f32 constants, and marker. Repeated paired and final owner references follow the modern prefix; their widths depend on the same-segment or inline-typed form.

Class version 10 has a second member sequence.
