Its first and repeated `paired_reference` members serialize the target type GUID `362B7EC3-0F09-47C8-A3BE-DC066715CDAE` inline between the u64 entity ID and the two same-segment flag bytes. The final member is an inline-typed reference whose target type GUID is `44A64366-4BD3-4B24-881A-F94C206E8F2D`. That final member is not a direct owner backlink.

Class version 11 also has an inline-typed member sequence. Its first and repeated `paired_reference` members serialize the target type GUID `362B7EC3-0F09-47C8-A3BE-DC066715CDAE` inline, and its final member serializes the target type GUID `44A64366-4BD3-4B24-881A-F94C206E8F2D` inline. The final member is not a direct owner backlink.

`paired_reference` resolves to a class-version-0 `Geometry` record of type `362B7EC3-0F09-47C8-A3BE-DC066715CDAE`. The companion has an eleven-byte indexed header followed by one of two prefixes. The fixed prefix is ten zero bytes. The class-version-11 present-zero prefix is nine zero bytes and bytes `01 00 00 00 00`. A u32 incident-curve count follows the prefix, followed by that many ordered sketch-curve references, one zero byte, and a final inverse reference to the point record. The inverse reference ends the companion. A same-segment point form uses marked same-segment references throughout its companion. An inline-typed class-version-10 or class-version-11 point form serializes each incident target's registered type GUID and the point type GUID inline in the inverse reference. The compact 37-byte form uses the fixed prefix, same-segment references, and an incident-curve count of zero.

A sketch-line geometry payload begins with three contiguous f64 triples: start point, displacement from start to end, and unit direction. Coordinates and displacement use the standard centimetre-to-millimetre length conversion; direction is unscaled. The full form appends a unit auxiliary normal as a fourth f64 triple. The compact planar form ends the scalar payload after the direction and immediately stores a marked record reference; its start, displacement, and direction have zero `w` components, and its omitted normal is the sketch-local `+w` axis. A referenced analytic wrapper inserts `0x01 + u32 reference + six zero bytes` before either line form. The bounded endpoints are the start point and start plus displacement. The neutral tangent is the normalized displacement. The auxiliary normal is projected onto the plane perpendicular to that tangent and normalized; when the stored unit auxiliary vector is parallel to the tangent, the first canonical coordinate axis least aligned with the tangent supplies a perpendicular normal.

A legacy inline sketch NURBS begins at curve payload offset 133. It stores an eight-byte nullable carrier reference, `u32 3`, a three-byte decimal subtype class tag, the subtype record index, eight zero bytes, and `0x01 + u32 reference + ten zero bytes`. The f64 fit tolerance, `u32 0`, and one zero pad byte follow. Three contiguous marked references use `0x01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`. Two Boolean state bytes, the u32 degree, and the eight-byte token `95 D6 26 E8 0B 2E 11 3E` follow. Knots, weights, and control points are three consecutive counted arrays. Each array header is `u32 count, u32 capacity, u32 8`; capacity is greater than or equal to count, knots and weights contain `count` f64 scalars, and control points contain three f64 coordinates per count. The knot count equals the control-point count plus degree plus one. The weights are positive, the knots are nondecreasing, and all scalar values are finite. Fit tolerance and control-point coordinates use the standard centimetre-to-millimetre length conversion; knots and weights are unscaled.

A typed form of the same record spells each of the four references as a 51-byte typed local reference (`01`, u64 target, LP-ASCII 36 type GUID, `00 00`). The four bytes after the first reference are zero. The f64 fit tolerance follows, then four zero bytes and `01` where the plain form stores five zero bytes, then the second to fourth references contiguously. The Boolean state bytes follow the fourth reference at 160 bytes beyond their plain-form offset. The four references are all plain or all typed.

A body-visibility browser-node member has type GUID `D26351F0-5940-4D23-AA20-2C35475A6D9E`, base-type GUID `CB844AB6-240D-4fc9-9C9F-3679DC896D6F`, type version `2`, and add-in name `Fusion`. The type-table entry and primary record index select its exact frame. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, an LP-UTF16 36-character node GUID, a one-byte hidden flag, `0x01 0x01`, and the node's u64 Design entity suffix. Flag `1` hides the entity in the document display; `0` shows it. Only this `0x01 0x01` member form carries body visibility; other frames registered to the same type do not. **Body visibility join:** BREP-qualified body selector → BREP body-map `entity_suffix` → typed browser-node hidden flag.

A body-presentation owner has type GUID `D3937028-C20C-4E65-B010-94AD418A5C20`, base-type GUID `63D6AD42-466A-40B7-9CCD-EB21BC500EF6`, type version `19`, and add-in name `Body`. If its type-table ordinal is `k`, its stream-local three-digit class tag is `256 + k`. The type entry lists the owner's entity, and the matching primary-index offset starts the owner frame. The next primary offset ends it; the end of the BulkStream ends the last frame.

The named-owner form uses a fixed or `EntityGenesis` entity header that identifies body entity suffix `E`. After the class-prefix members, its material member sequence is an LP-UTF16 browser-node GUID, the eleven bytes `01 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00`, an LP-UTF16 physical-material asset GUID, LP-UTF16 physical-material library id `C1EEA57C-3F56-45FC-B8CB-A9EC46A9994C`, an LP-UTF16 `PrismMaterial-###` token, a non-null same-segment reference, a null reference, a second non-null same-segment reference, an LP-UTF16 body display name, class padding ending in f32 opacity `1`, `01 01`, class padding, and an LP-UTF16 visual token. A visual token is a 36-character GUID followed by zero or more literal `_Post2015` suffixes. Equal GUID prefixes with different suffix counts identify different appearance records. The first non-null reference resolves to type GUID `CD57BC48-50EC-47DC-975A-FB6DEA72F4DA`, version `4`. The second resolves to body cache record `E + 1` or `B + 1` of type GUID `702b9cd2-537c-429e-8cc4-22beeeb98c37`, version `1`, add-in name `Scene`. The visual tail is either LP-UTF16 appearance library id `BA5EE55E-9982-449B-9D66-9F036540E140` followed by an optional LP-UTF16 `Prism-###` preset, or the LP-UTF16 identifier pair `08861000-1D69-CF2A-C082-CBD98E7E5D7F`, `005E1000-55CE-AFB6-81A1-36E3EF077C5F`. The browser-node GUID equals one typed body-visibility browser-node GUID with entity suffix `E` and primary record index `B`; neither reference in the three-reference run identifies that browser node.

The bare-owner form stores u64 body entity suffix `E` immediately after its stream-local class tag and stores no component-qualified entity ID. A header-shaped byte run in the frame payload does not replace this primary owner. The material envelope contains adjacent LP-UTF16 identifiers `D87FBE62-3B12-4CA8-9014-BAD31ABDB101` and `C1EEA57C-3F56-45FC-B8CB-A9EC46A9994C`, an LP-UTF16 `PrismMaterial-###` token, one non-null same-segment reference, an LP-UTF16 browser-node GUID, a non-null same-segment reference to node entity `E + 1` or `B + 1`, an optional LP-UTF16 body display name, optional f32 opacity `1`, bytes `01 01`, an LP-UTF16 visual token, and the LP-UTF16 identifier pair `08861000-1D69-CF2A-C082-CBD98E7E5D7F`, `005E1000-55CE-AFB6-81A1-36E3EF077C5F`. The envelope belongs to `E` only when it is unique within the exact owner frame and its browser-node GUID resolves to one typed body-visibility browser node with entity suffix `E` and primary record index `B`. Class tag `299` has no fixed body-presentation meaning.

A paired-library envelope is face-scoped only when two lower-case canonical GUID members and the fixed face-presentation carriers precede its visual token in one primary-index owner frame. The second GUID is the B-rep face-attribute identity. The first GUID does not participate in the face join. A paired-library tail without this two-GUID carrier form is not a face assignment. **Body appearance join:** named or bare body-presentation owner → Design entity suffix → the sole body-map pair with that suffix in the same Design stream → the pair's BREP basename and body selector. The basename is part of the body identity; equal selectors in different BREP basenames do not alias. More than one pair with the owner suffix, more than one body with the selector in the named BREP blob, or more than one appearance with the complete visual token makes the join invalid. **Body display name join:** named or bare body-presentation owner → Design entity suffix → the sole body-map pair with that suffix in the same Design stream → the pair's BREP basename and body selector. A non-blank LP-UTF16 body display name without control characters other than `Body` or `Body<digits>` assigns the display name of the bound model body. More than one pair with the owner suffix, more than one body with the selector in the named BREP blob, or conflicting body display names bound to one model body makes the name join invalid.

A Design component naming-space type has add-in name `Component` and base-type GUID `21F379C8-CAFD-4985-B461-767673A4C502`. Each entity registered to this type is the target of one context binding, except that a component definition stored as revisions binds one in each: records with different offsets that repeat one record index and each carry the component's name. The direct form is byte `01`, the u64 component entity id, two or three zero bytes, and a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 UUID. Its marker is not the second byte of an `01 01 + u64 component entity id` reference. The typed form is a local reference to the component entity with an inline type GUID equal to that entity's naming-space type registration, followed by zero or one zero byte and the 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 UUID; with the reference's two-byte local tail, these are the direct form's two or three zero bytes. The linked form is byte `01`, the u64 component entity id, two zero bytes, byte `01`, the u64 id of a link entity, two zero bytes, and the 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 UUID. The link entity is registered to type GUID `8ACBA2E5-5A4C-4438-8351-276DE96E6982` with add-in name `Fusion`, or the stream registers it to no type and indexes no record for it. Component roots partition each Design stream into ascending entity-id clusters: a cluster starts at its root entity id and ends before the next root entity id. A body-map entity belongs to the cluster containing its Design entity suffix, and its BREP basename adds that BREP to the component's history set. A component can own zero, one, or several BREP histories. In a component definition record, the binding's UUID is followed by the component's name: an LP-UTF16 string and two zero bytes that end the indexed record. Bindings outside a definition record store no name. Each bound UUID selects that complete component-local Design and history naming space. Persistent identities resolve their local entity ids only in the component selected by their context UUID.

A design entity header opens with an indexed record header. The fixed form stores the u64 entity suffix, five zero bytes, an optional slot (`0x00`, or `0x01` and four zero bytes), and the LP-UTF16 entity ID whose numeric suffix equals the entity suffix. The `EntityGenesis` form stores a zero run, `0x01 + u32 key_count`, `key_count` property entries, and the LP-UTF16 entity ID; its record index is the entity suffix. A property entry is an LP-ASCII key, an LP-ASCII type name, and a value. The type name `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64` selects a u64 value. The type name `IntrinsicMetaTypeHString` selects a zero u32, an empty string. Exactly one entry has the key `EntityGenesis` and a u64 value, the origin bitfield. A sketch container entity header can store the `HString` entries `AutoConstrainCompleteJobRequestId`, `AutoConstrainCompleteRequestId`, `AutoConstrainMLJobId`, and `AutoConstraintUniqueSketchId` before the `EntityGenesis` entry, with `key_count` 5. An `EntityGenesis`-form sketch entity header is followed by a paired record carrying the same record index. That record is the sketch's Geometry member ("Records of a Sketch item"): its display name, a zero byte, and the u32 member count are followed by `count` entries of `0x01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`. The first entry references the sketch's base-point record, and the other entries name the sketch's owned records. A point or curve record without relation membership joins its owning sketch through the base-point reference or the member run.

In the legacy sketch form, an `MSketch` metadata object names candidate indexed-record identities. A sketch container is the candidate whose primary indexed record is immediately followed by a second indexed record with the same record index. The paired record stores eight zero bytes after its header and a marked u32 head-placement reference. A member-owning tail continues with six zero bytes, a u32 sketch ordinal, seven state bytes, and a u32 member count at record offset 41. The count is followed by exactly that many `0x01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes` entries naming every record owned by the sketch. A localized tail omits the counted member run; its existence is closed by the referenced head-placement frame and its geometry ownership is supplied by relation owner references. The compact head-placement record is 34 bytes long. It stores ten zero bytes, `01 00`, a marked u32 reference, and six zero bytes after its indexed header and denotes the identity transform. The container record index is the sketch identity and owner reference.

A typed-reference sketch member-run record, written by the container generation whose references carry inline type GUIDs, stores each reference as a 51-byte typed reference: the head-placement reference at offset 19 ends at offset 70, a u32 sketch ordinal, two state bytes, and a u32 count of name code units follow it at offsets 70, 74, and 76, the UTF-16LE sketch name starts at offset 80, one zero byte follows the name, and the u32 member count follows that byte. A record with an empty name has its member count at offset 81. The counted entries are 51 bytes apart. The typed compact head record is 74 bytes. It stores ten zero bytes after the indexed header, `01 00` at offsets 21 and 22, and a 51-byte typed reference at offset 23. It denotes the identity transform, as does the 34-byte compact head.

An explicit head's closing reference selects its encoded width independently of the reference that names the head. A Sketch scope's local references to its sketch container and its scope placement frame each use either the plain or typed reference form.

A sketch entity container follows its self-validating entity header and UTF-16LE entity ID with an eight-byte base-record slot, `0x01`, `u32 reference_count`, then `reference_count` entries of `0x01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`. The base-record slot is either `u32 record_reference` followed by `u32 zero`, or the sentinel `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` when the sketch has no base record; the list grammar is identical in both forms. In a stream with serializer magic `1234`, the run lists the sketch's relations, a second counted run of its dimension frames follows, and the same-index Geometry member lists its points, curves, text records, and dimension frames ("Records of a Sketch item").

The current sketch entity container has type GUID `44A64366-4BD3-4B24-881A-F94C206E8F2D`, base-type GUID `37AD519C-AFB3-4CE2-9E6D-E3269FC6CDB9`, type version `18`, and add-in name `MSketch`. Its entity header is followed by a same-index Geometry member. The member has type GUID `37AD519C-AFB3-4CE2-9E6D-E3269FC6CDB9`, base-type GUID `A7AEA631-985B-4DD1-8CE2-DE2C-14B54081`, type version `4`, and add-in name `Geometry`. The member starts with `u32 3`, its three-digit dynamic class tag, and the owning u64 sketch entity suffix. Four zero bytes and one same-segment marked owner reference follow. The u32 at member offset 30 is the positive ordinal of the sketch Geometry member in its referenced Geometry collection. Two sketches of one collection can store the same ordinal. Entity suffix order and collection reference order can differ from ordinal order. The marked collection reference selects their namespace. A value can be absent from the sequence, including `1`. Byte 34 is a one-byte flag with value `0` or `1`. Each combination of this flag and the visibility flag at member offset 35 is valid. The one-byte sketch visibility flag is at member offset 35, and byte 36 is `01` or `00`. Visibility value `0` hides the Sketch and value `1` shows it. Byte 36 opens a same-segment marked reference. When it is `01`, its u64 target at member offset 37 names the direct container of the sketch: an ordinal collection or a sketch folder. The target is nonzero, and the reference has no inline type GUID. When byte 36 is `00`, the reference is null: the Geometry member belongs to no ordinal collection, and no collection lists the sketch. An LP-UTF16 sketch display name follows the direct container reference; a non-blank name without control characters assigns the sketch display name and the owning Sketch timeline feature name. The collection has type GUID `5275CBA4-3D7D-40DC-A651-1DFF3FC8AFBF`, base-type GUID `A7AEA631-985B-4DD1-8CE2-DE2C-14B54081`, version `3` or `4`, and module `Geometry`. Its indexed header is followed by nine zero bytes, a property block carrying `crv_tag_id_idx` as `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64`, and a counted run of same-segment marked references to its sketch members. Each run reference has a nonzero target and no inline type GUID. Each run target resolves to a sketch container whose Geometry member names this collection, or to a sketch folder whose parent reference names this collection. A sketch container or sketch folder occurs in at most one run. A run can omit a sketch container whose Geometry member names its collection or folder; that sketch belongs to the named container. A sketch folder has type GUID `45B3FDEA-5EBA-4B33-ADF8-47041CAC3602`, base-type GUID `A193F53F-86D7-4F45-A01C-51F5ECEEFC0E`, type version `1`, and module `Geometry`. Its indexed header is followed by nine zero bytes, `01`, five zero bytes, a flag byte that is `0` or `1`, and five zero bytes. An LP-UTF16 folder name starts at record offset 32. The name is followed by a positive u32 folder number, a u32 member count, and that many same-segment marked references to sketch containers. Each folder run reference has a nonzero target and no inline type GUID, and its target sketch names the folder in its Geometry member. A marked reference to the parent ordinal collection follows the run. A run of zero bytes and a closing marked reference end the frame. The ordinal namespace of a sketch in a folder is the parent collection of the folder. That namespace spans the sketches that name the collection and the sketches of its folders. Version `3` has six bytes after this property block and before the member list. Version `4` starts the counted run immediately after the property block. Bytes after the counted run form the frame tail. The collection reference and counted run define the ordinal namespace independently of component entity-id clusters.

A sketch geometry group has type GUID `67F4EECB-EB2C-48E6-8A25-1751E9924EAE`, type version `0`, and add-in name `MSketch`. Its primary frame stores the indexed header, ten zero bytes, a u32 ordinal at offset 21, u32 `1` at offset 25, and a zero byte at offset 29. A nested indexed header with the same record index starts at offset 30; its class tag selects type GUID `0F551F3B-B195-4486-93D0-711CB83482CE`, type version `0`, add-in name `Geometry`. The nested frame stores eight zero bytes at offsets 41 through 48, `01` at offset 49, twelve zero bytes at offsets 50 through 61, f32 `1.0` at offsets 62 and 66, and a zero byte at offset 70. A u32 member count `N` at offset 71 is followed by `N` same-segment marked references in strictly increasing record-index order. Four zero bytes or none follow, then a same-segment marked reference to the owning sketch container. The byte after the member run is `00` when the four zero bytes are present and `01` when the four zero bytes are absent. The frame is `90 + 11N` bytes with the zero bytes and `86 + 11N` bytes without them.

The final same-segment reference in the sketch collection frame tail ends at the frame boundary and names the component definition record that owns the collection. This local reference is either eleven bytes, with a one-byte marker, a u64 target, and two zero flag bytes, or 51 bytes, with an additional u32 length `36` and 36 ASCII type-GUID bytes between the target and the flags. The component definition record contains a reference to the collection and the context binding of its component naming space. Each sketch in the counted run belongs to that component. A sketch whose collection names no component definition belongs to the Design root. A root component without a separate product definition uses the Design root. A standalone document keeps its root sketches at document scope. The collection link defines sketch ownership independently of component entity-id clusters. The Sketch feature that binds a sketch belongs to the definition that owns the sketch collection listing it, independently of the entity-id cluster that contains the Sketch scope record. Entity ids of one component's sketches can lie in the cluster of another component, and one collection can list sketches whose Sketch features are consumed in several components. Consumption by features of another definition does not move a listed sketch or its Sketch feature out of the listing definition.

Typed non-construction sketch curves form neutral profile loops through endpoint incidence at the document linear tolerance. Curves named by a valid `TextFrame` relation are construction geometry: they remain projected for the text-frame constraint but are excluded from profile loops. A line's stored unit normal is an auxiliary orientation vector. Its component parallel to the stored unit line direction is removed and the remainder is normalized; when no remainder exists, the first canonical coordinate axis least aligned with the line direction supplies the perpendicular normal. The resulting normal is perpendicular to the line and retains the stored orientation side when the stored vector provides one. A bounded line belongs to the planar Sketch when both endpoints lie in its local plane. The auxiliary normal can lie in that plane. A full circle or full ellipse is a one-curve loop. A bounded line uses its stored endpoints, an arc uses the endpoints evaluated from its center, radius, and angles, a bounded ellipse uses its rotated parametric endpoints, and a nonperiodic NURBS curve uses the points evaluated at knots `degree` and `control_point_count`. An unbranched connected component is a profile exactly when every endpoint vertex has degree two. A connected component consisting of lines and circular arcs deduplicates coincident segments that share endpoints, center, radius, and start and end angles, and iteratively prunes vertices of degree less than two before evaluating profile cycles. An edge whose removal disconnects its endpoint vertices is a bridge. A profile boundary consists of cycle edges. Closed loops connected by a bridge keep separate boundaries, including a loop inside another loop. A branched component of lines and circular arcs uses the counterclockwise angular order of outgoing half-edges at each vertex. Outgoing half-edges with tangent directions that differ by at most `1e-9` radian form one tangent group, and a group can span the angle branch cut. A tangent group orders by ascending signed curvature at the vertex: a line has curvature `0`, and a circular arc has curvature `1 / radius` when the half-edge traverses it counterclockwise and `-1 / radius` when the half-edge traverses it clockwise. Equal curvature orders by ascending neutral sketch-entity identity. Every positive-area bounded face whose boundary walk traverses each constituent entity at most once is one profile, and the negative-area exterior walk and self-touching spur walks are excluded. When a deduplicated segment has a coincident replacement segment and an interior edge is shared by multiple bounded faces, the second traversal substitutes the duplicate segment identity. Profile order starts with the lowest neutral sketch-entity identity, and each subsequent use records whether traversal opposes the entity's stored direction. Open chains, zero-area walks, and branched components containing splines or ellipses do not form neutral profiles. Strictly nested closed line loops, mixed line-and-circular-arc loops, loops containing nonperiodic positive-weight NURBS curves, and full circles form atomic planar regions. Point containment counts analytic horizontal-ray intersections with lines and directed circular arcs using a half-open endpoint rule. Positive-weight NURBS boundaries use the homogeneous control polygon to bound curve speed over each nonzero knot span. Subspan chords carry conservative tubes whose radius bounds the complete rational curve subspan; winding is defined only when every tube excludes the projected point, and two boundaries are disjoint only when every cross-boundary tube pair is disjoint. A region's exterior is the unique strict-containment-minimal loop containing every projected selection point, and its holes are the exterior's immediate children in the strict-containment tree. Polygon-to-circle containment requires the circle center inside the polygon and every polygon edge strictly outside the circle. A mixed-loop exterior contains a circle when the circle center is inside and its radius is smaller than the minimum exact distance to every line or directed arc. Circle-to-polygon and circle-to-mixed-loop containment requires every segment's maximum distance from the center to be smaller than the circle radius. Circle-to-circle containment compares center distance plus the inner radius with the outer radius. Polygon-to-mixed-loop, mixed-loop-to-polygon, and mixed-loop-to-mixed-loop containment require one inner boundary point inside the exterior and no analytic line-line, line-circle, or circle-circle intersection between their bounded segments. Touching, intersecting, or tube-inseparable loops do not form a containment relation. A set of projected points on both the outer loop and one or more immediate child loops selects the unique atomic region whose closure contains every point. Points lying only on one loop remain ambiguous between the regions adjacent to that loop. A point carried by an edge perpendicular to the sketch plane selects the region containing the edge's coincident endpoint projections.

When a line-only branched component has one degree-four tangent junction, exactly two source-oriented cycles, opposite signed areas, and a non-junction probe of the smaller cycle inside the larger cycle, the two cycles form one connected profile boundary. The outer cycle is oriented positive and the inner cycle negative before concatenation at the shared junction. Other tangent junctions remain unresolved.

Atomic-region classification requires a supported boundary model for every profile loop in the selected Sketch and a defined strict-containment relation for every distinct boundary pair. An unclassified sibling loop or boundary-pair relation withholds the region because the relationship may be containment, intersection, or disjointness.

Intersecting and coincident profile loops form a planar arrangement when every curve intersection is represented by an endpoint-incidence node. A bounded line or circular arc splits at every incident node in its interior, and a full circle splits at every incident endpoint angle. Coincident line segments and same-circle subarcs with the same endpoint nodes collapse to one arrangement edge. Distinct analytic edges may meet only at their shared nodes; line-circle and circle-circle pairs account for every bounded intersection, including a second intersection away from a shared node. A full-domain nonperiodic positive-weight NURBS may meet a line only at its endpoint when its endpoint control point lies on the line and every other control point lies strictly in one open half-plane. It may meet a circular boundary only at its endpoint when every other control point lies strictly inside the circle or strictly beyond the circle's supporting tangent at that endpoint. Nonadjacent NURBS-bearing edges are disjoint only when their conservative curve tubes are pairwise disjoint. The counterclockwise tangent order of outgoing half-edges defines every positive-area bounded face; the exterior walk is excluded. A curve can bound a closed arrangement face through a proper subinterval while its complete stored span belongs to an open endpoint chain. Endpoint-loop membership and arrangement-face membership are independent. A selected arrangement face records each source sketch entity, the stored parameter interval used by that edge, and whether face traversal opposes the source direction.

The arrangement of a counted region selection uses only part of the Sketch. A unit is a profile loop or a non-construction curve in no loop; text is not a unit. The kept units start as the units that hold a curve the selection names. The box that holds the kept units grows over every unit whose box meets it within the document linear tolerance, until no unit is added. A profile loop whose box holds the grown box is not added in this step. After it, every profile loop whose box holds the final box is kept. A unit whose box misses the final box can neither cross nor lie inside a selected face, so the kept units have the faces of the complete arrangement that the selection can name. When a Sketch curve has no bounded box (a reference line, a bounded ellipse, or a NURBS with a weight that is not positive), the arrangement uses every unit.

Nonplanar sketch curves transfer into separate spatial-sketch arenas in model coordinates. The owning Design placement maps points by its rotation and scaled origin and maps direction vectors by its rotation. Spatial lines retain both endpoints. Spatial circles and arcs retain center, unit normal, perpendicular unit reference direction, radius, and arc angles. Spatial nonperiodic NURBS retain degree, knots, control points, and weights. A full circle forms one spatial profile with its stored center, normal, and reference direction. Bounded spatial curves form a profile when one unbranched connected component has exactly one continuation at every endpoint, closes with at least three curves, and its ordered endpoints lie in one nondegenerate plane. The plane normal follows boundary traversal, its u-axis follows the first boundary edge, and every boundary use records whether traversal opposes the stored curve direction. Spatial profile construction excludes construction geometry, open or branched components, nonplanar loops, and zero-area loops. Spatial curves do not participate in planar profile-loop construction or planar sketch constraints.

Class tag `287` can use the compact-owned parameter prefix. A class-`287` frame that does not close that form is read in the header forms of other parameter records. Its indexed header is followed by fifteen zero bytes, `u32 source_ordinal` at offset 26, `u8 1 + u32 owner_record_index` at offsets 30 and 31, six zero bytes at offsets 35 through 40, the expression at offset 41, and one of the exact five-byte expression trailers `00 00 00 00 00` or `00 00 00 01 00`. The remainder is LP-UTF16 `source_kind`, LP-UTF16 unit and name fields, an f64 evaluated scalar, and the twelve-byte parameter tail. The unit field may be an explicit zero-length LP-UTF16 field. The owner reference resolves through the indexed Design record graph when its primary frame exists; an absent primary frame leaves the parameter native without an owner binding. A class-`372` frame that closes no other parameter grammar is read in the compact null-owner form. Its indexed header is followed by fifteen zero bytes, `u32 source_ordinal` at offset 26, the null owner `u8 0` at offset 30, and the expression at offset 31. The class-287 expression trailers and remainder follow. The parameter has no owner binding.

The Design `MetaStream` primary index selects each registered record's `BulkStream` header by entity ID and byte offset. That header repeats the entity ID and selects the type-table row that registers it.

An indexed Design record header is `u32 class_tag_length`, a three-digit ASCII dynamic-class tag, then `u32 record_index`. `record_index` is a logical reference value; it is independent of the header's byte offset in the `BulkStream`. Record indices and Design entity suffixes are local to one Design `BulkStream`; indexed-record, sketch-owner, parameter-owner, and geometry joins never cross `BulkStream` boundaries.

An indexed parameter record has three fixed header forms. The discriminated form extends the indexed header with eleven zero bytes, a u64 family discriminator, one zero byte, `u32 source_ordinal`, and one of two owner forms. The wide discriminated form stores fifteen zero bytes there instead of eleven, so its family discriminator is at offset 26 and every later field is four bytes further on. In the wide form, the nine bytes from offset 26 are a u32 family discriminator, a zero byte, and the u32 code-unit count of the LP-UTF16 parameter comment at offset 31. The comment's code units follow the count, and every later field moves on by their byte length. A parameter without a comment stores count `0`. A frame is read in the eleven-byte form first and in the wide form when that reading does not close, because a wide frame with discriminator `0` has zero bytes at offsets 22 through 29. The comment discriminated form stores eleven zero bytes, a u32 family discriminator at offset 22, and the u32 code-unit count of the LP-UTF16 parameter comment at offset 26. The comment code units follow the count, then `u32 source_ordinal` and one of the two owner forms, with no zero byte between them. Its LP-UTF16 source expression is followed by the comment expression trailer. The comment expression trailer is five bytes: the driven flag, a zero byte, the favorite flag, a zero byte, and the document flag. Each flag is `0` or `1`, and the document flag is `1` exactly for a document parameter. In this form the document flag selects a document parameter. A parameter with document flag `0` is a dimensional constraint when its `source_kind` contains `Dimension`, and a feature input otherwise. The comment discriminated form stores no text value after `source_kind`. A frame is read in the comment discriminated form when neither the eleven-byte nor the wide reading closes. The family discriminator is a value from `0` through `6`, and it varies independently of `source_kind`. A document parameter stores `u8 0`. A dimension or feature parameter stores `u8 1`, `u32 owner_record_index`, and six zero bytes; the owner resolves through the indexed Design record graph. A dimension or feature parameter can instead store the null owner `u8 0`; it then has no owner binding. Both forms then store an LP-UTF16 source expression. The expression is followed by a nine-byte trailer or a ten-byte trailer. The nine-byte trailer is four zero bytes and five flag bytes. The ten-byte trailer is the text flag, four zero bytes, and five flag bytes. Each flag is `0` or `1`. The text flag is `1` exactly for a text parameter. The last flag byte is `1` exactly for a document parameter. As in the comment form, this document flag selects a document parameter whatever its `source_kind`, and a frame with an owner and document flag `1` matches no grammar. DR-144 gives the other four flag bytes. A frame is read with the nine-byte trailer first and with the ten-byte trailer when that reading does not close, because the first nine bytes of a ten-byte trailer with text flag `0` are a valid nine-byte trailer. DR-144 gives the trailer length of each Design stream against its MetaStream header word. The wide form with discriminator `0`, `4`, `5`, or `6` also has the wide expression trailer. The wide expression trailer is eleven bytes: the text flag, five zero bytes, the driven flag, a zero byte, the favorite flag, a zero byte, and the document flag. Each flag is `0` or `1`. The document flag is `1` exactly for a document parameter, and a document parameter has driven flag `0`. This document flag also selects a document parameter whatever its `source_kind`. The driven flag is `1` for the parameter of a driven dimension. A driven dimension measures its geometry and applies no constraint. Its expression is a literal length or angle, and the parameter and its owner store the value of that literal. The dimension frame stores the measurement of the geometry. The favorite flag is `1` for a parameter that the user marks as a favorite. The text flag is `1` for a text parameter. The ordinary compact owned form extends the indexed header with fifteen zero bytes, `u32 source_ordinal`, `u8 1`, `u32 owner_record_index`, and six zero bytes. Its LP-UTF16 expression is followed by the compact owned expression trailer. The compact owned expression trailer is five bytes: the opaque flag, the driven flag, and three zero bytes. The driven flag is `0` or `1`. The opaque flag is `0` or `1` (DR-251). It carries no family discriminator and no text value after `source_kind`; the discriminated form stores an LP-UTF16 text value there. A text parameter stores its text there, its expression is the quoted text, and its unit token is `Text`. Every other parameter stores an empty text value. The legacy compact owned form extends the indexed header with fourteen zero bytes, `u32 source_ordinal`, `u8 1`, `u32 owner_record_index`, and six zero bytes. Its LP-UTF16 expression is followed by five zero bytes. The remainder of each header form is LP-UTF16 `source_kind`, an optional LP-UTF16 unit token, LP-UTF16 parameter name, an f64 evaluated scalar, and the twelve-byte parameter tail. A dimensionless parameter may encode the absent unit as an explicit zero-length LP-UTF16 field. The document-parameter `source_kind` is localized. The decoder lists `User Parameter`, `Paramètre utilisateur`, and `Parâmetro do usuário`. In a form that stores no document flag, one of these values denotes a document parameter. A parameter that is not a document parameter is a dimensional constraint when its `source_kind` contains `Dimension`, and a feature input otherwise. A `source_kind` of a sketch or spatial-sketch dimension parameter that ends with a hyphen and decimal digits is the dimension's instance name: the text before that hyphen is the kind stem, such as `Linear Dimension`, `Diameter Dimension`, or `Angular Dimension`, and the digits are the instance number. The stem names the dimension kind. Design parameter values use database units independently of the declared display unit: `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, and `ft` lengths are stored in centimetres, while `deg` and `rad` angles are stored in radians. Dimensionless and Boolean parameters omit the unit token. A parameter with another unit token retains that token and its evaluated database scalar without assigning an unproved neutral quantity kind. `source_ordinal` is a native ordering value and can repeat within one Design `BulkStream`. A neutral parameter identity is the byte-length-prefixed Design stream name followed by the indexed-record index; `source_ordinal` and owner-record position do not participate in parameter identity. The first serialized parameter frame for a logical record index is canonical within its Design `BulkStream`; a later frame with the same index is not a second neutral parameter. Parameter names are case-sensitive; letters, digits, `_`, `"`, `$`, `°`, and `µ` remain part of an identifier in expression text. An identifier followed by `(` is a function-call head rather than a parameter reference. `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`, `deg`, and `rad` following a numeric or parenthesized value are unit suffixes; the same bare token in another expression position remains a parameter identifier. A document parameter expression resolves identifiers against uniquely named document parameters in the same Design `BulkStream`. A feature-owned parameter expression resolves first against a parameter of its owning feature, then document parameters, then a uniquely named parameter of a preceding feature in the same stream. Feature precedence follows authored timeline order, and uniqueness is evaluated after excluding the current and later features. An ambiguous eligible name, self-reference, or reference with no preceding owner does not form a dependency. Within each parameter scope, neutral ordinals are the stable topological order of resolved dependencies; native ordinal values provide the tie-break order. A dependency cycle is broken at its lowest native ordinal, after which topological ordering continues.

The twelve-byte parameter tail is `u8 0` and a marked reference without an inline type GUID: `u8 1`, `u32 collection_record_index`, and six zero bytes. It names the parameter collection of the Design stream. A parameter collection is the record registered to type `B0556F58-EE09-46A7-B18F-E296F48E5B13`, base type `A7AEA631-985B-4DD1-8CE2-DE2C-14B54081`, module `CommonData`. In type version 3 its indexed header is followed by fifteen zero bytes, a u32 at offset 26, a marked reference at offset 30, one zero byte, and `u32 parameter_count` at offset 42. In type version 4 a prefix with three LP-ASCII GUIDs precedes the same u32, marked reference, and zero byte, and `parameter_count` is at offset 166. `parameter_count` marked references of eleven bytes each follow the count. One further marked reference ends the frame. The counted run lists exactly the parameter records whose tail names the collection. When the paired Design `MetaStream` registers a parameter collection for the stream, a parameter record's tail names a registered collection. A frame whose tail names a record registered to another type is not a parameter record.

The typed compact parameter form is the compact parameter form written by the container generation whose references carry an inline target type GUID (see "**References.**"). The frame ends with the 52-byte typed parameter tail: `u8 0` and a typed local reference whose target type GUID is `B0556F58-EE09-46A7-B18F-E296F48E5B13`. This tail replaces the twelve-byte parameter tail, whose bytes after `00` are the same reference without an inline type GUID. The typed tail selects this form independently of the dynamic class tag. The indexed header is followed by fifteen zero bytes and `u32 source_ordinal` at offset 26. The owner field at offset 30 is a reference. An owned parameter stores a typed local reference there: `u8 1`, the u64 owner record index at offset 31, the LP-ASCII 36 target type GUID with its u32 length `36` at offset 39, and the two zero flag bytes at offsets 79 and 80; the owner index fits in u32. Its LP-UTF16 expression begins at offset 81 and is followed by five zero bytes. The owner reference can instead omit its inline type GUID; it is then the eleven-byte `01 + u64 + 00 00` reference, and the expression begins at offset 41 with the same trailer. A document parameter, whose `source_kind` is exactly `User Parameter`, stores the null reference `u8 0` at offset 30, and every other source kind stores an owner reference; its LP-UTF16 expression begins at offset 31 and is followed by `00 00 00 00 01`. Both forms continue with LP-UTF16 `source_kind`, the optional LP-UTF16 unit token, the LP-UTF16 parameter name, and the f64 evaluated scalar, which ends where the typed parameter tail begins. The form has no family discriminator and no reserved u32 after `source_kind`.

A Design `BulkStream` frame whose remainder matches no parameter grammar in this section is an unparsed parameter record when its tail names a parameter collection, or when its indexed header is followed by the fifteen-byte compact zero run and it ends with the typed parameter tail. A frame that closes a parameter grammar is also an unparsed parameter record when its tail names a record outside the registered parameter collections. In a stream that registers no parameter collection, a frame is an unparsed parameter record when its indexed header is followed by at least eleven zero bytes and its twelve-byte tail names a record that is unregistered. Such a record defines no neutral parameter.

A dimension or feature-input parameter without the null owner stores `owner_record_index`. Fusion can retain that reference after omitting the primary owner frame; the parameter then has no owner binding. The paired record of an omitted owner frame can remain; a lone record with the owner's `record_index` and no other header with that index is not an owner frame. When the owner frame exists, its primary indexed header starts the frame. The next indexed header with the same `record_index` ends the frame and is not part of it. A header with another record index does not end the frame. All ordinary owner forms share an eleven-byte indexed header, eight zero bytes, `01 + u32 1`, `01 + u32 scope_record_index`, six zero bytes, `u32 local_ordinal`, a scalar envelope, `01 + u32 parameter_record_index`, six zero bytes, `u32 owned_ordinal`, four zero bytes, a repeated scope field, a companion reference with a seven-byte zero trailer, and a final scope reference with a six-byte zero trailer. The scalar envelope is `00 + f64`, `00 + 01 + u32`, `00 + 00 + u32`, `00 + u32`, or `01 + u32 0 + f64`. The owner of a text parameter stores the envelope `00` + LP-UTF16 text instead, and the text equals the parameter's text value; its evaluated scalar is the parameter's evaluated value. The repeated scope field is either `01 + u32 scope_record_index + eight zero bytes` or `01 + u32 scope_record_index + six zero bytes + 01 + u8 variant`, optionally followed by one flag byte. A compact scalar owner can instead store `01 + u32 scope_record_index + seven zero bytes + 01`; this spelling has no variant and its final byte is not interpreted. `variant` and the flag byte are zero or one. The variant form occurs with the direct f64, marked u32, marked-zero-plus-f64, and text envelopes. The compact `00 + u32` envelope has no variant. The final scope index also equals `scope_record_index`. A numeric envelope's value numerically equals the parameter record's evaluated scalar. The owner, parameter, and companion indices are consecutive in owner-parameter-companion, parameter-owner-companion, or owner-companion-parameter order. The scope record is the owning sketch or construction operation, and its ordered reference table names the owner. `(scope_record_index, local_ordinal)` is unique among the owners that their scope names. `owned_ordinal` is a native ordering value and is not unique within a Design stream.

An owner frame whose stored scope record is absent, or whose stored scope does not name it in its ordered reference table, is detached. A detached owner remains after its dimension or feature input is deleted. A later record can reuse its stored scope record index, and a later owner of the same scope can reuse its local ordinal. A detached owner binds its parameter to no scope.

An owner frame outside the defined owner grammars establishes no interpreted owner binding. The referencing parameter retains its defined fields and owner record index in native storage only. Such a frame supplies no scope, local ordinal, companion, or scalar binding. The absence of an interpreted owner binding does not invalidate other records.

In the container generation that writes typed references, every reference field of the ordinary owner forms is a 51-byte typed local reference (`u8 1`, u64 target, LP-ASCII 36 target type GUID, two zero flag bytes) in place of the eleven-byte `01 + u32 + six zero bytes` spelling; one frame uses one spelling for all of its references. Every other field, every trailer, and every scalar envelope are unchanged, so each offset after the scope reference moves forty bytes later per preceding reference. The `01 + u32 1` field at offset 19 is not a reference and has the same spelling in both generations.

The admitted legacy 68-byte owner form is a separate grammar. Its eleven-byte indexed header is followed by eight zero bytes, `u8 1`, four zero bytes, a nine-byte scalar lane, `u8 1 + u32 parameter_record_index`, six zero bytes, `u32 owned_ordinal`, five zero bytes, two flag bytes, `u8 1 + u32 companion_record_index`, and eight zero bytes. The scalar lane is nine zero bytes or the scalar envelope `00 + f64`, whose value equals the linked parameter's evaluated scalar. Each flag byte is zero or one. The form carries no scope or local-ordinal lane: `scope_record_index` and `local_ordinal` are zero sentinels, and the evaluated scalar is the linked parameter's evaluated value. The owner, parameter, and companion indices are consecutive in that order. Like every owner, the frame has the parameter-owner type `D91D429C-1BB5-4640-B49F-69AF14F463E9`; its class tag is dynamic and does not identify the form.

The admitted legacy 88-byte owner form uses the same prefix through `owned_ordinal`, then stores four zero bytes, `u8 1 + u32 scope_record_index`, eight zero bytes, `u8 1 + u32 companion_record_index`, seven zero bytes, and `u8 1 + u32 scope_record_index` with a six-byte zero trailer. It carries no scalar or local-ordinal lane: `local_ordinal` is zero, and the evaluated scalar is the linked parameter's evaluated value. The two scope references must match and be nonzero. The frame has the parameter-owner type; its class tag is dynamic and does not identify the form.

The scalar owner form is 104 bytes. It stores `u8 0 + f64` as its scalar carrier, uses a six-byte zero trailer after the repeated scope reference, and stores `u8 1 + u8 variant + u8 flag` before the companion reference. A compact scalar owner is 103 bytes. It either uses an eight-byte repeated-scope trailer and omits the variant fields, or uses a six-byte trailer and stores `u8 1 + u8 variant` without the trailing zero. The counted owner is 101 bytes and stores `u8 1 + u32 evaluated_count`; every subsequent field is three bytes earlier than in the scalar form. The compact counted owner is 99 bytes and stores the count as a bare u32 at offset 40, uses an eight-byte repeated-scope trailer, and omits the variant fields. The compact typed-counted owner is 100 bytes and stores `u8 1 + u32 evaluated_count` at offsets 40 and 41, uses an eight-byte repeated-scope trailer, and omits the variant fields. The tagged scalar owner is 107 bytes and stores `u8 1 + u32 0 + f64` beginning at offset 39, uses an eight-byte repeated-scope trailer, and omits the variant fields. The tagged scalar variant owner is 108 bytes. It has the same scalar carrier, uses a six-byte repeated-scope trailer, and stores the three-byte variant fields before the companion reference. The counted owner also permits `00 + 00 + u32 evaluated_count` as an equivalent spelling of `00 + 01 + u32 evaluated_count`; both six-byte scalar envelopes store the count at offset 41. The compact typed-counted owner uses the same marker choice at offsets 40 and 41.

The indexed companion record begins with a 58-byte common prefix. Its eleven-byte indexed header is followed by 20 zero bytes, `01 + u32 owner_record_index`, six zero bytes, a nonzero u64 Unix-epoch timestamp in microseconds, and eight zero bytes. The timestamp is a wall-clock value recorded at a parameter authoring event; it does not exceed the document's last save time and is preserved unchanged across subsequent saves. Its `record_index` equals the owner frame's `companion_record_index`. The companion-owned payload interval begins after this prefix and ends at the next indexed parameter record, parameter-owner header, parameter-scope primary header, or primary header referenced by a parameter scope other than the companion owner's scope in the same Design `BulkStream`. A terminating record immediately after the prefix denotes an empty companion payload. A primary header referenced by the owning scope remains inside the payload interval. Another indexed-record header can begin a nested companion record or the following sibling record; byte adjacency alone does not select between those roles. Construction-recipe records whose name fields begin within this interval belong to the companion and retain interval order. Every dimension parameter not used by a projected locus or construction-recipe constraint forms one native sketch constraint under the parameter owner's Sketch scope. The constraint retains the governed parameter and its companion record as a `companion_payload` operand when the payload is nonempty or a `companion` operand when it is empty. A locus frame's governing companion identity, not the companion containing that frame, selects the represented parameter. When a companion physically contains one or more typed dimension frames and no typed frame or recipe names that companion as governor, the payload is only a container for the following dimensions. Its owner remains a scalar parameter and does not form a second sketch constraint from the contained frames.

A typed-reference companion prefix, written by the container generation whose references carry inline type GUIDs, is 98 bytes: the indexed header, twenty zero bytes, a 51-byte typed owner reference at offset 31, the nonzero timestamp at offset 82, and eight zero bytes. In both spellings the companion-owned payload begins sixteen bytes after the timestamp offset.

Sketch-relation records name their sketch through `ParentNode`. A legacy counted sketch member run does not list them. Every entity registered by a sketch-relation class type in the stream's type table is a relation record whose record index equals its entity ID.

A `Radius Dimension*`, `Radial Dimension*`, or `Diameter Dimension*` parameter not consumed by a typed locus or recipe relation governs every circular entity in the parameter owner's Sketch whose measured radius or diameter equals the evaluated parameter value within the source kernel's absolute linear resolution. This rule applies when its companion payload is empty and when the payload contains only auxiliary relations or presentation data. `Radius Dimension*` and `Radial Dimension*` both govern radius. One matching entity establishes a radius or diameter constraint. Multiple matching entities establish a repeated radius or repeated diameter constraint controlled by the same parameter. No matching entity establishes a neutral radial relation.

A `Tangent Dimension*` parameter uses a length unit and stores its evaluated scalar in centimetres. Its state-zero counted-locus groups are auxiliary graph records; their owner role and solved loci determine any neutral relation, and the groups do not carry the tangent-distance parameter.

A `Linear Dimension*` parameter not consumed by a typed locus or recipe relation governs every line in the parameter owner's Sketch whose endpoint distance equals the evaluated length within the source kernel's absolute linear resolution. This rule applies when its companion payload is empty and when the payload contains only auxiliary relations or presentation data. One matching line establishes an endpoint-to-endpoint distance. Multiple matching lines establish a repeated-length constraint whose entities follow Sketch entity order. No matching line establishes a neutral line-length relation.

A `Linear Dimension*` parameter not resolved as a line length governs the unique pair of parallel line entities in the parameter owner's Sketch whose supporting-line separation equals the evaluated length. One matching pair establishes an entity distance. Zero or multiple matching pairs do not establish a neutral line-separation relation.

When multiple matching parallel-line pairs remain, a profile-local pair has exactly one intervening entity in the profile's cyclic boundary traversal. Two or more profile-local pairs establish one repeated parallel-line distance when no entity belongs to more than one pair. Pairs follow profile and boundary traversal order. An overlapping local candidate graph does not establish a neutral relation.

When the entity-pair rule does not establish a relation, collinear line entities form carriers within the source kernel's absolute linear resolution. The unique pair of parallel carriers whose perpendicular separation equals the evaluated length and whose bounded member spans overlap along their common direction establishes a parallel-line-set distance when at least one carrier contains multiple entities. Disjoint bounded segments may belong to one carrier. Carrier members follow Sketch entity order. Zero or multiple matching carrier pairs do not establish a neutral parallel-line-set relation.

A `Linear Dimension*` parameter not resolved by either line-only form governs the unique point-line pair in the parameter owner's Sketch whose perpendicular separation equals the evaluated length. Zero or multiple matching point-line pairs do not establish a neutral point-line relation.

A `Linear Dimension*` parameter not resolved by another typed relation governs the unique pair of solved point loci in the parameter owner's Sketch whose Euclidean separation equals the evaluated length within the source kernel's absolute linear resolution. Point entities coincident within that resolution form one solved locus. A horizontal or vertical pair establishes the corresponding directional distance; any other pair establishes a Euclidean locus distance. Zero or multiple matching solved-locus pairs do not establish a neutral point-distance relation.

A `Linear Dimension*` parameter not resolved by a line or point relation governs concentric full-circle pairs whose centers coincide within the source kernel's absolute linear resolution and whose absolute radius difference equals the evaluated length within that resolution. One pair forms a distance relation. Multiple pairs form a repeated-distance relation only when every circle belongs to exactly one matching pair. Overlapping candidate pairs do not establish a neutral circular-separation relation.

A linear dimension measurement matches when the absolute difference between its measured value and the absolute evaluated value is no greater than `max(T, 1e-9 * (1 + max(|measured|, |evaluated|)))`, where `T` is the document linear tolerance in millimetres. Concentricity compares the center separation with zero by this same rule; it does not use a separate coordinate-scaled bound.

An `Angular Dimension` parameter not consumed by a typed locus relation governs the common direction of the unique state-zero parallel-line group in its companion. Both group loci must be bounded lines whose undirected angles from the positive Sketch `u` axis, or their supplements, equal the evaluated radian value within relative tolerance `1e-9`. The parameter drives the first locus's axis-angle constraint; the parallel group carries that direction to the second locus. Zero or multiple matching companion-local parallel groups do not establish a neutral axis-angle relation.

An `Angular Dimension*` parameter not consumed by a typed locus relation uses a preceding incident-pair proof when it follows its two line operands in Sketch serialization order. A preceding Sketch point identifies the operands when its companion names exactly two incident curve records, both records precede the parameter, and both resolve to bounded lines in the parameter owner's Sketch. The point establishes an angle relation when the lines' undirected angle, or its supplement, equals the evaluated radian value within relative tolerance `1e-9`. Exactly one distinct matching incident pair is required. A later point or curve does not participate in this proof.

A state-zero counted-locus frame for an `Angular Dimension*` parameter can contain one bounded line locus and one point locus. The line is the explicit angular operand. The point selects the unique other bounded line in the same Sketch that has the point as an endpoint and whose undirected angle, or supplement, with the explicit line equals the evaluated radian value within relative tolerance `1e-9`. The resolved two-line pair establishes the parameterized angle relation. A missing, mismatched, or non-unique candidate retains the counted relation without an inferred angular pair.

Within a dimensional companion, every contained construction-recipe family name belongs to the immediately preceding indexed record header. The containing record ends at the next indexed record header or at the end of the companion-owned payload. A nonempty recipe-specific prefix extends from the end of the eleven-byte indexed header to the u32 length field of the recipe-family name. The standard selector-bearing prefix stores ten zero bytes, `u32 1`, `u32 3`, a nonzero u32 value, and one or more persistent Design operands. An operand stores a nonzero u32 persistent-subentity selector, then its ASCII decimal-integer tag token as either LP-ASCII or unframed ASCII, followed by a u32 token integer, then a nonzero u32 Design-reference count, that many nonzero i32 Design references, and `u32 0`. The token is one or more digits or ASCII minus `0x2D` followed by one or more digits. The first operand uses LP-ASCII. The operand sequence ends with either `u32 0` or the suffix `u32 1, u32 1, u64 0, u32 n`, `n` nonzero u32 references, and four or six zero bytes. The pair (token, token integer) identifies the persistent tag group. Every selector, tag token, token integer, Design reference, and byte offset is retained in prefix order. Each operand joins to every active solved face or edge whose persistent-subentity tag contains the same selector, token, token integer, and Design reference; the candidate face and edge sets are independently ordered by entity identity and deduplicated. Faces and edges carrying the same token, token integer, and Design reference under a different selector are retained in separate alternate-selector sets and never enter the exact candidate sets. The bytes after the family name through the containing-record boundary form a nonempty contiguous sequence of little-endian i32 values with no padding. The containing header's byte offset, dynamic class tag, record index, frame length, companion identity, recipe ordinal, complete prefix bytes and offset, program offset, and complete program are retained with the recipe identity. The indexed header, prefix, length-prefixed family name, and program partition the containing record without gaps.

A counted-name standard prefix uses the header's final u32 as its operand count. Each operand stores one or more persistent names in the standard name frame. The first name's selector field also gives the positive name count for that operand. The names of one operand share one recipe-program ordinal. A name with several Design references stores the reference list of one persistent-subentity tag. For the first-side support faces of a `Fillet` or `Chamfer` edge recipe, when the first side names at least two reference ordinals, the faces that every Design reference of each name joins take precedence when the intersection of their boundary edges with the recipe's candidate edges holds exactly one edge and the treatment transition deletes that edge: a Design reference that every fragment of the tag token carries does not widen the name. When no face is common to all references of a name, that name has the union of their faces. Otherwise, the union of each name's references selects the support faces.

A paired selector-bearing prefix stores ten zero bytes, `u32 1`, `u32 2`, a positive u32 pair count, and exactly that many adjacent operand pairs. The first operand of each pair stores a nonzero u32 selector, an unframed decimal-integer token followed by four zero bytes, a positive u32 Design-reference count, and that many nonzero i32 Design references without a terminator. The second operand stores the same selector, an LP-ASCII decimal-integer token, `u32 0`, the same count and ordered Design references, and a terminating `u32 0`. The prefix ends after the final second-operand terminator. A selector mismatch, a reference mismatch, another token frame, or trailing bytes invalidates the complete paired prefix.

A grouped selector-bearing prefix stores ten zero bytes, `u32 1`, a `u32 N` with `N >= 4`, and exactly `N` groups. Values `2` and `3` select the paired and standard prefix forms. Each group starts with a positive u32 operand count. Each operand stores a nonzero u32 selector, an unframed decimal-integer token followed by four zero bytes, a positive u32 Design-reference count, and that many nonzero i32 Design references without a local terminator. One final `u32 0` terminates the complete prefix. An empty group, a different group count, another token frame, an operand terminator, or trailing bytes invalidates the complete grouped prefix.

Complete construction-recipe records in a non-locus dimension companion are independent native witness operands for one dimensional selection. No field combines records into an aggregate operation or assigns semantic order to them. Their construction-recipe kinds and programs can differ within one companion. The neutral projection uses the owner-scoped Sketch geometry and evaluated parameter to establish the dimensional relation; the result is one measurement or a repeated relation only under the rules below, not one relation per recipe. The decoder walks records in increasing recipe-family byte offset within the companion-owned payload for deterministic retention. `recipe_ordinal` is a decoder ordinal and is not serialized.

An edge recipe's words after its complete sentinel or counted prelude may occur as a contiguous subsequence of a dimension recipe program. Every such byte-identical containment joins the dimension recipe record to that edge operand. Matching operand identities are ordered and deduplicated; repeated equivalent edge recipes remain distinct operands.

A direct presentation frame of the parameter's owner whose operand measurement equals the converted parameter takes precedence over the construction recipes. A recipe-backed linear dimension whose parameter is not already projected through a governing locus frame or such a presentation frame measures solved locus pairs in its owning Sketch at the parameter's evaluated separation. A locus frame physically contained by the same companion does not supersede the recipes when that frame projects an independent geometric relation without the dimension parameter. Candidates are axis-aligned point pairs and parallel line pairs. The construction-recipe kind does not restrict the candidate geometry family. Point pairs produce horizontal or vertical point-locus distance according to their shared sketch coordinate. A parallel line pair produces an entity distance. One candidate is a single distance constraint. Multiple candidates form one repeated-distance constraint when they partition their participating entities into disjoint pairs; the pair order is point-pair discovery order followed by line-pair discovery order. A candidate graph that shares an entity between pairs is ambiguous and retains the ordered recipe operands as a native parameter-backed constraint. Zero candidates also retain the ordered recipe operands.

When that candidate graph is ambiguous, a detached point beyond an axis-aligned bounded-line endpoint establishes an extension distance if the detached point lies on the line's infinite carrier and the endpoint pair matches the evaluated separation along the carrier axis. The detached point is not an endpoint of any bounded line in the Sketch. Exactly one matching extension pair is required. Multiple matching extension pairs retain the recipe operands as a native parameter-backed constraint.

A recipe-backed `Radius Dimension*`, `Radial Dimension*`, or `Diameter Dimension*` parameter uses the same owner-scoped circular measurement rule as an empty radial companion. One measurement-matching circle or circular arc establishes a radius or diameter constraint. Multiple matches establish the corresponding repeated constraint. The recipe records remain the retained native construction graph and do not replace the circular measurement.

A paired-locus dimension frame occurs within a dimension companion's owned record interval and is delimited by two indexed headers with the same `record_index`. It may begin immediately after the 58-byte companion prefix or follow intermediate indexed records. Its primary header is followed by eight zero bytes, `01 + u32 3`, `01 + u32 0`, six zero bytes, an opaque u32, `01 + u32 first_geometry_record_index`, six zero bytes, a u32 first-role code, `01 + u32 second_geometry_record_index`, six zero bytes, and a u32 second-role code. Both geometry indices resolve to typed sketch-point or sketch-curve records. The paired header is followed after 59 bytes by the owner of the dimension parameter governed by the frame; that owner's companion identity, rather than the companion containing the frame, selects the parameter. A neutral two-locus measurement requires two distinct neutral entity identities. A linear pair forms a neutral parameter-backed measurement only when its solved geometry equals the evaluated parameter after centimetre-to-millimetre conversion: two points form a horizontal, vertical, or Euclidean locus distance, a point and line form their perpendicular separation, and two parallel lines form their perpendicular separation unless both role codes select the symmetric line-width form below. An angular pair of two lines forms a neutral angle only when their solved angle equals the evaluated radian value. Other role-dependent pairs retain their typed geometry, role codes, and parameter through the native constraint.

A paired-locus linear frame whose two loci are parallel lines and whose two role codes are nonzero is a symmetric line-width measurement. Its converted parameter equals twice the perpendicular separation of the two infinite line carriers. The typed parameter-backed distance uses the two line entities; a zero role on either locus does not select this symmetric form.

An annotated dimension frame occurs either in the parameter-scope prefix before its governed parameter or within a parameter companion's owned payload and is delimited by same-index primary and paired headers. A containing companion may belong to a dimension or feature input. The primary header is followed by eight zero bytes, `01 + u32 operand_count`, and `operand_count` entries of `01 + u32 geometry_record_index + six zero bytes + u32 role`; zero is the null locus and every nonzero index resolves to typed sketch geometry. The operand run is followed by a metadata block and the annotation byte payload. The metadata header stores `u8 1` and a u32 entry count. A frame without a metadata block stores `u8 0` alone, and its annotation byte payload begins after that byte. A populated metadata block stores one `EntityGenesis` entry: count `1`, LP-ASCII `EntityGenesis`, LP-ASCII `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64`, and the u64 origin bitfield. A frame with one null operand followed by two non-null operands can instead store count `0`; its metadata block ends after the count. The fixed metadata layouts are `dimension_annotation_metadata_header` and `dimension_annotation_genesis_metadata` in the [layout table](../layouts/f3d.md). A marked reference to the governed dimension's parameter-owner record ends that payload. Six zero bytes, a u32 return count, and the padded marked return-reference run follow. The return run is a permutation of the non-null operand indices, and zero padding extends to the paired header. The paired record stores eight zero bytes, `01 + u32 sketch_entity_suffix`, and six zero bytes after its eleven-byte header. The suffix resolves to the owning Sketch. The referenced parameter owner's companion, rather than the frame's physical interval, selects the governed parameter. When the annotation byte payload of a two-point `Linear Dimension*` frame holds at least 48 bytes, it [begins with two xyz f64 points](../layouts/f3d.md). The annotation byte payload has the layout of the measurement, text frame, prefix, text, and kind block of "**Sketch dimensions.**" in §3.1. A segment whose MetaStream serializer magic is `1234`, or `134225558` or more, stores the 91-byte text frame in it. A segment with another serializer magic stores the first 18 bytes of the text frame: the style byte, the four style values, and the byte `1` or `0`. Such a frame whose two point loci are distinct and whose horizontal and vertical point distances both equal the converted parameter establishes horizontal distance when the two payload points have finite coordinates, equal second coordinates, and different first coordinates, and vertical distance when they have finite coordinates, equal first coordinates, and different second coordinates.

A direct dimension-presentation frame is a stream-local typed frame whose primary class is registered under type GUID `6CCF41D5-40BE-48ED-A834-18F3EAED6C57` or `8C780195-72C0-4a56-A911-E43AB14357F2`. The stream-local class tag of a registered type with type-table ordinal `k` is `256 + k`. Its indexed header is followed by eight zero bytes, `u8 1`, `u32 operand_count`, and `operand_count` entries of `u8 1 + u32 geometry_record_index + six zero bytes + u32 role`; the count is between one and 64, and every geometry index resolves to a Sketch point or curve in the same `BulkStream`. Opaque presentation bytes follow the operand run through a paired indexed header with the same `record_index`. The paired class is the stream-local class registered under type GUID `90055C05-546C-4EE7-B3C9-3DD922AD0C9C` or `855F0A64-6286-4FFC-B918-BC394F600107`; its body stores eight zero bytes, `u8 1`, `u32 owner_reference`, and six zero bytes. The first following dimension parameter-owner frame whose `scope_record_index` equals the scope record of the Sketch entity named by `owner_reference` governs the presentation frame; its parameter and companion identities are retained. The operand run is the authoritative measured-geometry selection. When the rule assigns several frames to one owner, the one frame whose operand measurement equals the converted parameter establishes the relation. A one-circle or one-arc `Tangent Dimension*` frame establishes a radius constraint only when its radius equals the converted parameter. A line plus circle or arc establishes a tangent distance only when exactly one of the centerline-distance-plus-radius or absolute centerline-distance-minus-radius values equals the converted parameter. Two circles or arcs establish a tangent distance only when exactly one of the four absolute boundary combinations `d + r1 + r2`, `d - r1 - r2`, `d + r1 - r2`, and `d - r1 + r2` equals the converted parameter, where `d` is center distance. A one-line `Linear Dimension*` frame establishes endpoint distance, and a two-point `Linear Dimension*` frame establishes horizontal, vertical, or Euclidean point distance from the solved geometry. A missing or non-unique measurement retains the native dimensional constraint.

An annotated `Linear Dimension*` offset frame has one null locus and two non-null curve operands. Its return run contains those two curve indices exactly once. The curve with a null secondary persistent identity is the source; the curve with a non-null secondary persistent identity is the generated result. Both curves belong to the frame's owning Sketch. The single-source form has one null locus and one non-null source curve, and its one-entry return run names that source; the generated result is the unique same-Sketch curve with a non-null secondary identity whose solved parallel or concentric offset matches the parameter. In either form, a zero offset is invalid, the converted parameter magnitude and measured offset agree within `max(T, 1e-9 * (1 + max(|s|, |m|)))`, and the parameter factor is `1` for a positive stored value or `-1` for a negative stored value.

A parameter companion may own one or more non-overlapping counted-locus dimension frames in stream order. Each indexed header is followed by eight zero bytes, `01 + u32 locus_count`, and `locus_count` entries of `01 + u32 geometry_record_index + six zero bytes + u32 role`. The entries are followed by `00 01 + u32 sketch_entity_suffix + six zero bytes + u32 owner_role`, a u32 constraint-state mask, a second u32 equal to `locus_count`, and that many `01 + u32 geometry_record_index + six zero bytes` return entries. One zero byte ends the frame immediately before the next indexed header. Every geometry index resolves to a typed sketch-point or sketch-curve record. The return run is a permutation of the locus geometry indices. The sketch suffix resolves to a Sketch-typed Design entity. Paired-locus and counted-locus frames may coexist in one companion-owned interval; the counted form may repeat.

In a counted-locus linear offset frame, the owner role is zero, the constraint-state mask is `0x20`, and every locus and return reference resolves to a curve. The locus count is even, and its first and second halves have equal cardinality. In the role-partitioned form, the first half contains nonzero source-role codes and the second half contains role zero. In the identity-partitioned form, role codes in both halves are nonzero, every first-half curve has a null secondary persistent identity, and every second-half curve has a nonnull secondary persistent identity. The return run alternates one source-set reference and one result-set reference, defines their pairwise correspondence, and uses every locus exactly once. The source entries form the ordered source set and the result entries form the ordered generated set. Every solved pair has one common positive offset magnitude. An arc pair has the same center, equal nonzero sweep orientation, and overlapping angular intervals; trimming against adjacent offset curves can change its start and end angles. A full-circle pair has the same center, and its signed offset is the source radius minus the result radius. The positive converted dimension magnitude is the operation-level offset distance. The dimension parameter factor is `1` for a positive stored value and `-1` for a negative stored value. The generated set identifies the realized offset branch. Offset construction can change curve carriers and topology.

The counted-locus frame's counted references also satisfy the generic sketch-relation prefix grammar. A frame reached through a Dimension parameter companion is a dimension frame only; a generic sketch relation at the same Design `BulkStream` byte offset is not a second constraint.

A null-locus dimension frame has the same companion-owned interval rule and is delimited by primary and paired indexed headers with the same `record_index`. The primary header is followed by eight zero bytes, `01 + u32 2`, `01 + u32 0`, six zero bytes, a u32 null-role code, `01 + u32 geometry_record_index`, six zero bytes, and a u32 geometry-role code. A variable annotation payload extends from that fixed operand prefix to the paired header. The nonzero geometry index resolves to a typed sketch-point or sketch-curve record owned by the governed parameter scope's sketch.
