The paired header is followed after 59 bytes by the governed dimension parameter's owner. A companion-owned interval containing a null-locus frame contains no paired-locus or counted-locus frame. For an `Angular Dimension` parameter, null role `14` followed by line role `3` measures the line from the positive sketch-u axis. The line's undirected angle or its supplement must equal the evaluated parameter within relative tolerance `1e-9`; the parameter then drives a neutral axis-angle constraint.

A null-locus frame or counted-locus frame is a radial dimension when the parameter `source_kind` begins with `Radius Dimension`, `Radial Dimension`, or `Diameter Dimension`. The first two forms govern radius. One measurement-matching full circle or circular arc among the selected loci establishes a radius or diameter constraint. Multiple distinct matching circular loci establish a repeated radius or repeated diameter constraint in locus order; other loci carry annotation geometry. When a counted-locus frame contains no circular entity, a selected point can identify the unique measurement-matching circle or arc in the same Sketch whose center equals that point. A radius parameter's centimetre scalar multiplied by ten equals the solved millimetre radius; a diameter parameter's converted scalar equals twice that radius. Converted scalar `s` and measured value `m` agree when `|s - m| <= max(T, 1e-9 * (1 + max(|s|, |m|)))`, where `T` is the document linear tolerance in millimetres. No matching circular entity, a repeated circular identity, a nonfinite scalar, or a scalar/geometry mismatch retains the native dimensional relation.

A state-zero radial counted-locus frame with one point and one bounded line can be an extension annotation. The point lies on the line's infinite carrier, and the two loci do not identify the governed circular entity. When every otherwise unresolved counted frame for the companion has this form, the parameter governs the owner Sketch's unique measurement-matching circle or circular arc. The extension frames do not form additional constraints.

When a paired-locus frame's two typed loci completely determine a linear or angular constraint, that frame is the companion's governing dimensional relation. Counted-locus frames in the same companion are auxiliary graph records for that relation, not additional dimensions; they retain their native roles and order without duplicating the parameter-backed constraint. A governing paired-locus, null-locus, or recipe-backed dimension has a neutral constraint identity formed from its stable parameter identity and frame-form discriminator. Relocating either indexed frame does not change that identity. Repeated counted-locus auxiliary relations retain distinct frame identities.

For a model-space Sketch, a linear paired-locus frame whose two loci resolve to distinct point entities measures their Euclidean model-space separation. The parameter drives a neutral spatial point-distance constraint when its absolute evaluated length equals that separation within relative tolerance `1e-9`. When the two loci of a linear paired-locus or null-locus frame resolve to one point entity and one nondegenerate bounded line entity, the frame measures the model-space distance from the point to the infinite carrier of the line, and the parameter drives a neutral spatial point-line-distance constraint under the same tolerance. Both entities must belong to the frame's owning spatial Sketch. A non-length parameter, a locus of another geometry kind, a cross-Sketch pair, or a scalar/geometry mismatch retains the native dimensional relation.

A state-zero counted-locus group owned by a spatial Sketch with owner role `0x400` is a reflection-symmetry relation. Its three loci contain exactly one nondegenerate bounded line and two distinct point entities. The infinite carrier of the line is the reflection axis: the point midpoint lies on that carrier and the point-to-point vector is perpendicular to it. The group is an auxiliary relation and does not carry the companion's dimensional parameter.

The constraint identity key contains the byte-length-prefixed key portion of the neutral parameter identity followed by the byte-length-prefixed frame-form discriminator. The parameter identity's namespace and `#` separator are not nested inside the constraint key.

Except for the angular line-and-point dimension form, state-zero counted-locus groups are first classified as auxiliary graph relations independently of the companion's dimension family. Coincident point pairs, coincident point-on-curve loci, centered circular or elliptical pairs, perpendicular or parallel line pairs, collinear line pairs, and three-locus reflection symmetry are determined by typed sketch geometry. Distinct circular or elliptical members with matching centers resolve as `Concentric`; two circular members with matching centers and radii resolve as `Coradial`. A reflection group contains one bounded-line axis and two points, bounded lines, equal-radius full circles, or equal-radius circular arcs that map onto each other across the axis carrier. Reflected arcs have equal sweep magnitude and reflected endpoint sets. Owner role `0x40` on one constant-`v` line is horizontal and owner role `0x80` on one constant-`u` line is vertical. Owner role `0x100` on one bounded line and one circular arc is tangent when they share a bounded endpoint and the line direction is perpendicular to the radius there. On two distinct circular entities, including full circles and bounded circular arcs, `0x100` is tangent when their supporting circles are externally or internally tangent and the tangent point lies in each bounded arc's angular sweep; a full circle accepts every tangent point. Owner role `0x800` on two lines, two circular entities, or two ellipses is equal when their solved nonzero lengths, radii, or pair of semiaxes agree respectively. Point-on-curve membership includes bounded lines, circular arcs, elliptic arcs, and nonperiodic NURBS curves over their knot domain; a full circle or ellipse uses its entire parameter domain. Auxiliary relations do not carry the dimensional parameter. Only a state-zero two-locus group that is not an auxiliary relation can carry a linear companion's distance parameter.

For a linear companion governed only by counted-locus frames, a two-point group is the governing directional-distance relation when exactly one of its absolute coordinate differences equals the evaluated parameter. A match on the `u` difference is horizontal distance and a match on the `v` difference is vertical distance. Matching both coordinate differences is directionally ambiguous and does not transfer as a typed dimension. The evaluated parameter is stored in centimeters and the sketch coordinates are millimeters. A remaining state-zero group with exactly two typed loci is the parameter-backed distance relation.

A counted linear frame with state mask `0x20` stores an offset graph. Its locus list uses one of the source/result partitions defined above. Every locus resolves to a bounded line or circular arc. The return run alternates one source index and one result index, uses every locus exactly once, and supplies the source/result bijection. A line pair has parallel directions and constant signed separation. An arc pair has the same center, equal nonzero sweep orientation, and overlapping angular intervals; trimming against adjacent offset curves can change its start and end angles. Its signed separation follows the sweep's left normal and is the signed difference from source radius to result radius. Every pair has the same positive separation magnitude. A pair whose result lies on the source curve's right side reverses the source traversal before applying the common distance along its left normal. When the common magnitude equals the companion parameter's magnitude after centimetre-to-millimetre conversion, the parameter drives the offset relation. The distance-to-parameter factor is `1` for a positive parameter and `-1` for a negative parameter. A null-locus frame governing that companion is the offset dimension's annotation frame and does not form a second constraint.

An angular paired- or counted-locus frame may encode one line and one point instead of two lines. The point is an endpoint indirection. Among lines owned by the same sketch and incident to that point at a stored endpoint, exactly one forms either the stored angle or its supplement with the explicit line. That unique incident line replaces the point in the parameter-backed angular constraint. No line is selected when endpoint incidence and the evaluated radian value do not determine one unique candidate.

A parameter scope is one logical indexed record delimited by two headers carrying the same `record_index`. Both three-digit class tags are per-file dynamic values. The primary header begins the scope payload. In fixed forms, an LP-UTF16 feature-family name ends exactly 72, 76, 77, 78, 87, or 88 bytes before the paired header. Immediately before the LP-UTF16 field are a u32 history-state identity and an ordered reference table. The table is `u32 reference_count` followed by `reference_count` entries of `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`; it ends at the history-state identity. The rigid `As-built` scope of an N-member rigid group stores `reference_count` 0 and no entries at offset 153 + 11(N − 2), immediately before the history-state identity; byte 142 + 11(N − 2) is not a reference marker. Every other scope stores a non-empty counted table. The fixed tail starts with a nonzero u32 ordinal among scopes of the same feature family. Its preceding history-state identity is at tail offset 30 in the 72- and 76-byte forms, tail offset 31 in the 77- and 78-byte forms. In the 87-byte form, tail byte 30 is `0x01` when it begins a second marked reference, and the identity is then at tail offset 41; otherwise tail byte 30 is zero and the identity is at tail offset 31. The 88-byte form is the 78-byte form with a second marked reference: tail byte 30 is `0x01`, a u64 record index and two zero bytes follow it, and the identity is at tail offset 41. The 82-byte tail of the 347-byte `JointOrigin` form and the 104-byte tail of the 705-byte `Assemble` form have no preceding history-state identity. A history-state identity is either `0xffffffff` for null or the `state_id` of an ASM delta-state record. A non-null current identity has a non-null preceding identity. A scope that commits no ASM state of its own stores a null current identity, and its preceding identity can still name the state it follows. When one scope's preceding identity equals another scope's current identity, the former follows and depends on the latter in the modeling history. Every member resolves to the primary header of an indexed Design record in the same stream, except that a member can name a deleted member. A deleted member's record index occurs in no indexed header of the stream, and each occurrence of its u32 encoding in the stream lies between the scope's primary and paired headers or is an entry reference of the scope's record-timestamp table. The feature-family name is localized. The stored feature-family name participates verbatim in configuration naming and in the neutral feature identity. A named parameter scope stores a custom label in its tail. After the feature-family name, the tail stores a nonzero u32 ordinal, a zero u32 and an LP-UTF16 label of `L` code units, 1 to 256, at tail offset 8. The rest of the tail is a [feature item tail](#records-of-a-sketch-and-extrude-design) with each later offset moved by `2L`: the plain 78-byte form is `78 + 2L` bytes, the plain 77-byte form `77 + 2L` bytes and the typed form `196 + 2L` bytes. The preceding history-state identity is at tail offset `31 + 2L` in the plain forms and `70 + 2L` in the typed form, and the evaluation epochs at `35 + 2L` and `47 + 2L` in the plain forms. Each plain reference of the tail is `01 + nonzero u32 record_index + six zero bytes`. A non-blank label without control characters assigns the display name of the timeline feature. The token-independent frame length of a parameter scope excludes the two serialized bytes of each UTF-16 code unit of its feature-family name and of its label. A tail whose label is empty is the fixed tail. A `Sketch` scope in a stream whose sketch entity headers use the fixed form contains exactly one `01 + u32 entity_suffix + six zero bytes` reference to its Sketch-typed Design entity header; this joins that scope form to the sketch container and its relation graph. An `Esquisse` scope, and a `Sketch` scope in a stream whose sketch entity headers use the `EntityGenesis` form, uses the generic ordered reference table. The `EntityGenesis`-form `Sketch` scope's payload before the table carries one `01 + u32 entity_suffix + six zero bytes` reference to its sketch entity header and one `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes` reference to its placement record, whose index also appears in the ordered table. Before insertion into a neutral textual key, an identity component replaces each UTF-8 byte of `#`, `%`, or a whitespace code point with uppercase `%HH`; other code points remain unchanged. A neutral feature identity consists of the encoded Design stream component and encoded feature-family component, each prefixed by its encoded UTF-8 byte length, followed by the family-local scope ordinal and the scope's indexed record identity. The indexed record identity disambiguates equal family-local ordinals carried by separate component histories in one Design stream. Its canonical configuration name is the unescaped feature-family name, one ASCII space, and the decimal family-local ordinal; the indexed record identity does not participate in configuration naming.

A record-timestamp table describes the indexed record that its owner reference names. A record has at most one record-timestamp table. The [record-timestamp table prefix](../layouts/f3d.md) holds the indexed header, fourteen zero bytes, `01 01`, and a u32 entry count. That many [record-timestamp entries](../layouts/f3d.md) follow; each entry is `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes + u64 timestamp`. The owner reference follows the entries in the same entry form and is followed by eight zero bytes. A timestamp is a Unix-epoch value in microseconds. The table of a Sketch scope lists the scope's sketch members, including its deleted members.

A named `Combine` tail also has a marked-reference form. Its [named parameter-scope tail](../layouts/f3d.md) begins with the ordinal, zero word and LP-UTF16 label, followed by a counted associated-reference list, three zero bytes, a required reference, a nullable middle reference, the preceding history-state identity, the evaluation epoch, a finite binary64 evaluation duration, the second evaluation epoch, a second required reference, byte `01` and the suppressed and rolled-back flags, a third required reference, a nullable closing reference and a final zero byte. Each required or present reference is `01 + nonzero u32 record_index + six zero bytes`; null occupies one zero byte. With an empty label, no associated references and both nullable references null, the tail is 78 bytes: the associated count is at offset 12, the required references at offsets 19, 51 and 65, the middle reference at offset 30, the preceding history-state identity at offset 31, the evaluation epochs at offsets 35 and 47, the evaluation duration at offset 39, the three flag bytes at offset 62, the closing reference at offset 76 and the final zero at offset 77. Label code units add two bytes each after offset 12; each associated reference adds eleven bytes; each present nullable reference adds ten bytes to its null spelling. These references are separate from the scope's ordered operand table and component-destination browser node.

The feature-family name is display text that varies with the application language. The scope primary class tag selects a row in the segment type table, and the stable type GUID of that row selects the feature family that the following table gives, whatever the stored name. For a class GUID not in the table, an English family name selects that family and any other stored name leaves the scope a native feature. `CopyPaste` and `CutPaste` scopes share the class GUID `D57B1A22-9D5A-4D7D-A909-E08C579612CA`, and `BaseFlange`, `EdgeFlange`, `Hem`, and `Face` scopes share `7AFA0A65-B53C-472C-ACA4-5C7C0A65001C`; the table lists neither GUID. A scope of class GUID `D57B1A22-9D5A-4D7D-A909-E08C579612CA` has the paste family whose complete prefix ends at its own reference table. The CopyPaste and CutPaste prefixes distinguish these families under any stored name. Exactly one prefix matches the scope framing.

A typed-reference parameter scope, written by the container generation that writes typed references, has a 196-byte form of the 76-byte fixed tail: the u32 ordinal, fifteen zero bytes, a 51-byte typed reference at tail offset 19, the preceding history-state identity at tail offset 70, a u32, an f64, and a u32, a typed reference at tail offset 90, two zero bytes, a typed reference at tail offset 143, and two zero bytes. Its scope's ordered reference table stores `reference_count` 51-byte typed references in place of the eleven-byte entries, and every reference of one scope frame uses the same spelling. These reference positions identify the typed spelling; the class tag does not.

A reference-prefixed typed Extrude stores a 51-byte typed construction-group reference at offset 25. The operation fields follow the reference at offset 76.

A typed-reference Extrude scope stores eleven zero bytes after its indexed header and the current operation fields at offset 22: u32 operation, u32 direction, u32 face extend, the reversed-direction, geometry-kind, and start-support bytes, three zero bytes, and the unit profile normal at offset 40. It has no prologue reference. Each of the seven extent slots after the normal is an absent `u8 0` or a 51-byte typed reference to an ordered scope member, and the side-extent fields follow the slots as in the current form. The shifted typed-reference form instead stores nine zero bytes, u32 `1` at offset 20, and two zero bytes after the indexed header, so the operation fields begin at offset 26 and the profile normal at offset 44; its slots and side-extent fields follow as in the typed form.

In a direct typed-reference solid Extrude with profile-plane start, direction and face extension `[1, 2]`, and side extents `[1, 0]`, the u32 at first-side offset `+9` is an opaque distance word.

A typed-reference Extrude selection group stores ten zero bytes after its indexed header, a typed reference to its Extrude scope at offset 21, and the u32 member count at offset 72, followed by that many 51-byte typed member references. After the members come the u32 opaque index, an f64, the repeated u32, and a typed reference to the group's record index plus two. Two zero bytes follow it, so the typed group has no variant. A plain group stores either these two zero bytes or `01 + u8 variant + 00` at this position. Then come a typed reference to the record index plus one, one zero byte, and a typed reference to the Extrude scope, which ends at the paired header. Every reference of one group uses the same spelling; the scope reference at offset 21 selects it. The two zero bytes occur with both spellings; the variant form occurs only with the plain spelling.

A typed-reference profile selection is a construction-operand group member whose primary record stores ten zero bytes, a typed reference at offset 21 to its record index plus three, u32 `1` at offset 72, an LP-UTF16 36 asset GUID, and an LP-UTF16 decimal owner text naming a Sketch entity suffix. The chain record at the selection's record index plus one stores fourteen zero bytes and `01 01 01 00 00 00` after its indexed header and a typed reference to the owning Sketch scope at offset 31. A sketchless chain record stores fourteen zero bytes and `01 01 00 00 00 00` after its indexed header and a typed reference to the selection record at offset 31. Its selection names no Sketch scope. An Extrude whose profile member has a sketchless chain record keeps its native profile and reports `feature.extrude-profile-sketch-absent`. The identity record at the record index plus three stores ten zero bytes, a typed reference to the selection record at offset 21, and at offset 72 a nonzero u32 group count and that many region groups. A group stores one region, a u32 count, and that many further regions. Each region starts with a nonzero u32 loop count. Each loop stores a nonzero u32 entry count, that many 40-byte entries, and a u8 exterior flag: `0` for a hole and `1` for the exterior. Each region has exactly one exterior loop. Each entry is u32 `2`, the u64 sketch-curve primary identity, the u64 sketch-curve secondary identity, where zero names no secondary identity, three u32 operands, and eight zero bytes. The groups end exactly at the identity record's paired header.

The compact profile-loop selection uses eleven-byte local references. Ten zero bytes follow its indexed header. The local reference at offset 21 names the selection record index plus three. U32 `1` is at offset 32. The asset GUID and decimal Sketch owner text start at offset 36. The chain record at the selection index plus one has fourteen zero bytes after its indexed header. Its six-byte marker `01 01 01 00 00 00` is at offset 25. Its local reference to the Sketch scope is at offset 31. The identity record at the selection index plus three has ten zero bytes after its indexed header. Its local reference back to the selection is at offset 21. Its nonzero u32 region-group count is at offset 32. Each group has the counted loops and further regions of the typed-reference form. Compact entries have kind `3`. They contain the same primary identity, secondary identity, three operands, and eight zero bytes. The lists end at the same-index paired identity header. A kind-`3` chain whose records also form a nested profile-region selection of the sketch-profile record, with a zero secondary identity in every member, is that nested selection and not a compact profile-loop selection.

A compact profile group's complete initial boundary can select a union of atomic sketch regions in a one-sided blind Cut from the profile plane. Every initial entry has a traversal flag and incidence words `(1, 1)`. The initial exterior and holes form one directed region in the arrangement of their own curves. Opposite uses of the same curve interval cancel on boundaries shared by selected atomic regions. The remaining directed intervals cover every initial boundary interval exactly once. The complete analytic Cut-transition certificate agrees with this union. A one-sided blind Join or NewBody from the profile plane can certify the same boundary equality through inserted analytic end caps at the signed extent. Every inserted lateral face has an analytic carrier on that boundary, and its edges and vertices stay within the sweep or within a deleted lateral face that it continues, as the complete-loop Cut certificate states. The cap union covers the complete initial boundary.

A two-sided blind Join or NewBody from the profile plane can certify atomic regions through its complete analytic transition. The geometric certificate tests two intervals from the positive side lengths: the second end opposite the extrusion direction, and both ends along that direction. Each interval is measured from the profile plane. Exactly one interval must have both ends on changed parallel planes within the linear tolerance. Both end planes gain the same nonempty set of atomic regions. On every changed parallel plane, the symmetric difference of the preceding and resulting face regions has the exact line and circular-arc outline of the changed atomic regions. Interior changed planes lose subsets of the selected regions. An updated face with unchanged analytic carrier, curve and edge definitions, loop membership, and vertex positions contributes the same region in both states. Every inserted or geometrically changed lateral face has a plane or parallel-axis cylinder carrier on the selected outline. Its boundary stays within the interval between the two signed end heights or continues a deleted or updated preceding lateral face on the same carrier. The reverse coverage holds for deleted and updated preceding lateral faces against the resulting lateral faces. The interval bounds the complete lateral ellipse where a side plane meets a transverse cylinder. The boundary and carrier joins are unique and complete.

A certificate reads each atomic region of the arrangement through one interior sample point. The sample lies inside the region's outer ring, outside each region nested directly inside it, and more than one model tolerance from each of these rings. The candidates are the interior grid points of the region's bounding box divided into 24 by 24 cells. When no grid candidate lies more than ten tolerances from every ring, the candidates also include the midpoints of the intervals that horizontal rows cut from the rings; a row runs halfway between each two adjacent vertex heights, and at most 512 rows are read. The candidate farthest from every ring is the sample. A region with no candidate more than one tolerance from every ring, or with an area not greater than the square of the tolerance, has no sample, and the certificate does not hold.

A compact complete-loop group has one exterior loop, its listed hole loops, and zero further regions. Each entry has operands `[0 or 1, 1, 1]`. Each loop's entries cover each curve of exactly one Sketch loop once. The exterior and hole loops describe a bounded candidate region. The owner text, Sketch scope, curve namespace, and unique curve identities satisfy the exact profile join. For a one-sided blind Cut from the profile plane with parallel side walls, the selected region set agrees with its ASM transition. On each changed plane parallel to the Sketch, the symmetric difference of the preceding and resulting face regions has the exact line and circular-arc outline of the selected atomic regions on that plane. The changed regions are subsets of the candidate set. Every candidate region loses material on at least one changed plane. An inserted parallel face lies within the stored travel. A plane that gains a selected region lies at the stored blind extent. Each inserted lateral face has a plane or parallel-axis cylinder carrier on the selected outline, and its boundary lies within the stored travel. A lateral face can continue a lateral face that the transition deletes. The deleted face has the same plane or cylinder carrier, and the stored travel and the height ranges of these deleted faces together cover the height range of the inserted face. A lateral boundary edge has a straight carrier through its ends, belongs to a plane parallel to the Sketch, or lies on the ellipse where a lateral plane meets a transverse cylinder. The complete ellipse stays within the stored travel and projects onto the selected outline. The selected region set follows group order. Repeated groups of the same region select it once. A selection can contain every loop in the Sketch. A Sketch with one profile uses the same complete-loop membership and analytic output certificate; its explicit selection is profile index zero.

When a counted region selection names a curve identity absent from its Sketch, the stored Cut transition determines the candidate atomic arrangement regions. The candidate set contains every atomic region that loses material on a changed parallel plane. Exactly one candidate set must pass the compact Cut certificate above. Its region count equals the stored region count. Each stored region corresponds to a distinct candidate region. Every stored member identity owned by the Sketch bounds the corresponding candidate region. This reading carries `feature.profile-region-identities-stale`. Other outcomes retain the native Sketch selection.

When the loops of a typed or compact profile group join the Sketch exactly but match no planar-arrangement face, the certified Extrude transition determines the selected atomic regions. A Cut selects the atomic regions it removed from the changed planes parallel to the Sketch and must pass the compact Cut certificate above. A one-sided blind Join or NewBody from the profile plane selects the atomic regions its inserted far end caps cover at the signed extent, with the lateral-face and cap-union conditions above. Curves outside the stored loops can divide the selected material into several atomic regions; all of them form the selection. Each selected atomic region has a hole ring for every atomic region directly inside it, selected or not, so the selected regions do not overlap. Each stored entry has a decoded curve piece that bounds at least one selected region through its identity or a shared geometric interval. An entry whose identity pair names several records names the pieces with that identity pair; the selected boundary determines the participating pieces. A line entry shares a positive-length collinear interval with the selected boundary. A circle entry shares its center and radius with a positive-length circular boundary interval. The exact reading requires every curve to bound a selected region. The transition-certified reading charges `feature.profile-coincident-boundary-assumed` when an entry joins the boundary through coincidence.

The profile join binds entries through their Sketch and curve identities. The Sketch is the one whose placement carries the Sketch scope named by the chain record; exactly one placement in the stream must carry it, and its entity suffix must equal the owner text of every member selection. When no placement in the stream carries that record, the chain record is not a Sketch scope. The Sketch is then the one placement that has no Sketch scope, whose entity suffix equals the owner text of every member selection, and whose Sketch container the frame of the chain record names through a typed local reference of type `44A64366-4BD3-4B24-881A-F94C206E8F2D`. Every listed entry resolves to at least one sketch-curve record of that Sketch with the entry's primary identity, and secondary identity when it is nonzero. An entry with several such records names the pieces of one source curve that were split. A typed Sketch-curve path resolves each entry to exactly one record and uses distinct curves across all regions. A transition-certified Extrude region retains the participating boundary pieces of a multi-record entry with `feature.profile-partial-entry-assumed`; the same code applies when a decoded piece has no identity use in a selected boundary. For a complete-loop Extrude region, each source loop names every curve of exactly one complete neutral Sketch loop, without repeated curves in that loop. An entry with several records is named by every one of its records that the loop holds, and the loop holds at least one. Its exterior flag selects the exterior-loop index; its other loops select the hole indices. No two source loops of one region can name the same neutral loop. In the typed-reference form, the regions in stored order form the selection: each group's first region precedes its further regions. Duplicate regions are removed after their first occurrence. A group's first region can be the union of its further regions. Then it resolves to exactly one face of the arrangement of the Sketch profile loops, its further regions resolve to at least two atomic faces without holes, and the directed boundary intervals of these atomic faces, after opposite uses of the same curve interval cancel, are exactly the intervals of that face. The further regions then form the group's selection, and the first region adds no region of its own, also when another member repeats that group. A region with one exterior loop can also resolve to one atomic planar-arrangement face. Its ordered curve identities must match the face boundary in cyclic order, in either direction. Adjacent pieces of the same boundary curve are one identity run, including a run across the cycle start. Exactly one face must match. A matching face that encloses an island supplies no region. A typed region whose loops match no face this way is read through directed boundary rings with an assumed traversal flag (DR-124). That reading matches each loop to a face boundary ring by its multiset of curve uses and does not check entry order. Each hole loop matches the outer walk of a distinct island directly inside the face. The face supplies a region only when every one of its islands is matched and no excluded island is present. `feature.profile-loop-flags-assumed` reports each selection that takes this reading. A loop that matches no single face is assumed to be a self-crossing loop when every loop curve is a line or circular arc, at least two atomic faces that enclose no island use only loop curves, and exactly one non-empty set of those faces uses each curve as many identity runs as the loop lists it. Faces that enclose an island are assumed not to be selected. Each face of the set then supplies one region with the arrangement's directed boundary. This selection uses the curve-use counts only; the listed curve order is not checked, and `feature.profile-crossing-loop-assumed` reports each selection that takes it. No such set, more than one set, or more than 16 atomic faces that enclose no island and use only loop curves defines no region; the last case reports `feature.profile-crossing-loop-capped`. The neutral boundary retains the arrangement's directed curve parameter ranges. A member without its selection, a missing or repeated placement, an owner-text mismatch, a missing curve identity, curves outside the Sketch, an incomplete loop match, or more than one matching neutral loop defines no complete-loop profile join.

A compact planar sketch line stores nine f64 values at its geometry offset 133: the start point, the displacement, and the unit direction, each with a zero z component, followed by one local reference in either the plain or the typed spelling. Its normal is +Z. A z component is zero when it is exactly zero or when `|z| <= 1024 * f64::EPSILON * max(|x|, |y|, 1 cm)` for the same vector's centimetre x and y; such a value is floating-point noise of at most 1024 units in the last place of the vector's own coordinates. A z component above that bound is not a compact planar line.

A `Canvas` scope names its image geometry from one of two fixed prologues. The expanded prologue has nine zero bytes at scope offsets 11 through 19, a marked null u32 at offset 20, and a marked geometry-record reference at offset 25. The compact prologue has ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20 and the marked geometry-record reference at offset 21. The referenced geometry record stores a 15-byte prologue after its eleven-byte indexed header. Its first ten bytes and bytes 11 through 13 are zero, byte 10 is zero or one, and byte 14 is the Canvas visibility Boolean. Four f64 values at record offsets 26, 34, 42, and 50 form the first plane-local boundary segment. A marked supporting-plane entity suffix occurs at offset 58 with six trailing zero bytes. The plane entity belongs to a Body or Geometry Design object. A 77-byte fixed payload occupies offsets 69 through 145. Its first four bytes are a normalized finite f32 opacity followed by one zero byte. Three consecutive f64 triples begin at payload offsets 5, 29, and 53. The first triple is the model-space plane origin in centimetres; the second and third triples are orthogonal unit directions for increasing plane-local u and v. Marked references at record offsets 146, 157, and 169 name the Canvas scope, owning component entity suffix, and image-asset record; their trailing fields contain six, seven, and six zero bytes respectively. The image-asset reference is followed by a flag byte at offset 180 and four f64 values at offsets 181, 189, 197, and 205 forming the opposite boundary segment. The two segments are ordered parallel opposite edges of a nondegenerate rectangle within floating-point roundoff. The rectangle can have any in-plane rotation. An LP-UTF16 persistent label begins at offset 213 and ends at the paired same-index geometry header. The paired header is followed by eight zero bytes and a marked reference to the same owning component with six trailing zero bytes. A standalone image-asset record follows immediately; its eleven-byte indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes and an LP-UTF16 archive-entry basename ending at the Canvas scope header. The basename uniquely identifies an entry in `Images.BlobParts`. Plane-local boundary coordinates are stored in centimetres.

Canvas geometry has eight fixed prefix layouts. The modern layout is described above. The legacy prologue has twelve zero bytes followed by the visibility Boolean. The transitional prologue has ten zero bytes, bytes `01 00 00`, and the visibility Boolean. The expanded prologue has nineteen bytes: nine zero bytes, a marked null u32 at record offset 20, a byte that is zero or one, three zero bytes, and the visibility Boolean. Each field after the expanded prologue is four bytes later than in the modern layout. The planeless expanded layout uses the expanded prologue and stores the null marker `0` in place of the plane reference at record offset 62. Its payload begins at offset 63, and each field after the payload is ten bytes earlier than in the expanded layout. The payload frame alone places a planeless Canvas in model space. The extra12 layout uses the modern prologue and inserts three u32 values `0, 1, 0` between the plane reference and the geometry payload. Typed layouts use 51-byte local references: marker `01`, a u64 target, an LP-ASCII 36-byte type GUID, and two zero bytes. The plane, scope, component, and asset type GUIDs are respectively `8D424E29-DE23-4B1F-A3AD-84C52A497D1A`, `0EE4A83E-464B-4235-A62F-984F15834C27`, `8EF00D65-F18D-4179-A644-FE0CA39943D6`, and `830A2A2B-0AA9-4D6A-ACA1-F7A2B2A06573`. Untyped references have eleven bytes. The component reference has one additional zero byte in the modern, transitional, expanded, planeless expanded, extra12, and typed transitional layouts. The flag byte before the second boundary is zero in the legacy layout and zero or one in the other layouts; DR-308 records its meaning. The paired geometry record uses the same reference encoding as its primary record, so its length is thirty or seventy bytes. The image-asset prefix is unchanged.

| Layout | Visibility | First boundary | Plane reference | Payload | Scope reference | Component reference | Asset reference | Boundary flag | Second boundary | Label count |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| modern | 25 | 26 | 58 | 69 | 146 | 157 | 169 | 180 | 181 | 213 |
| legacy | 23 | 24 | 56 | 67 | 144 | 155 | 166 | 177 | 178 | 210 |
| transitional | 24 | 25 | 57 | 68 | 145 | 156 | 168 | 179 | 180 | 212 |
| expanded | 29 | 30 | 62 | 73 | 150 | 161 | 173 | 184 | 185 | 217 |
| planeless expanded | 29 | 30 | 62 | 63 | 140 | 151 | 163 | 174 | 175 | 207 |
| extra12 | 25 | 26 | 58 | 81 | 158 | 169 | 181 | 192 | 193 | 225 |
| typed_legacy | 23 | 24 | 56 | 107 | 184 | 235 | 286 | 337 | 338 | 370 |
| typed_transitional | 24 | 25 | 57 | 108 | 185 | 236 | 288 | 339 | 340 | 372 |

A `Canvas` scope can have a 98-byte fixed tail after its LP-UTF16 kind. The ordered fields are a positive feature ordinal, eight zero bytes, member count `1`, a marked self reference, three zero bytes, a marked companion reference, a zero separator, null history-state identity `0xffffffff`, evaluation epoch, finite nonnegative evaluation duration, the repeated evaluation epoch, a second marked companion reference, two zero bytes, a third marked companion reference, a closing marked self reference, and a zero byte. Each marked reference is `01 + u32 record index + six zero bytes`; companion references have nonzero indexes and both self references name the enclosing scope. The same-index paired scope header follows the tail.

A typed Canvas scope has a 196-byte fixed tail. After the positive feature ordinal and fifteen zero bytes, it stores three 51-byte typed local companion references. Their type GUIDs in order are `B7F34D7B-DAC4-41A5-B67D-D672537C3BFA`, `5FBE538E-139B-46D4-BCAF-CC796D1E1F78`, and `6CCF41D5-40BE-48ED-A834-18F3EAED6C57`. Between the first and second references are the null history-state identity, evaluation epoch, finite nonnegative evaluation duration, and repeated epoch. Two zero bytes separate the second and third references, and two zero bytes end the tail. Its reference table before the kind has two 51-byte typed local references, of types `5A1BF548-241F-46FD-9FB5-E4B05126EB9D` and `7B6C3C2D-4096-4E6D-B225-699E8C2D9355`. The history-state u32 and LP-UTF16 kind follow that table.

Let the ordered Canvas segments be `A -> B` and `C -> D`. For normalized raster coordinates `(s,t)` in `[0,1] × [0,1]`, the plane-local image point is `A + s(B-A) + t(C-A)`, with `D = B+C-A`. The ordered vectors `B-A` and `C-A` carry image rotation and both flip states. They are perpendicular and have nonzero lengths. The complete embedded raster fills this rectangle; the record has no separate crop state. To form a neutral image frame, translate the supporting-plane origin by `A`, rotate its unit axes onto `B-A` and `C-A`, set placement bounds to `(0,0)` through `(|B-A|,|C-A|)`, and clear the separate mirror flags. Convert the origin displacement and the placement bounds from centimetres to millimetres. This frame retains each ordered raster corner, including quarter-turn and arbitrary rotations.

A `Decal` scope is a presentation timeline object and has no modeling-history state or geometry outputs. Ten zero bytes occupy scope offsets 11 through 20. A marked image-asset record reference occurs at offset 21 with six trailing zero bytes. A u8 scope code occurs at offset 32. A marked target-group reference occurs at offset 33 with six trailing zero bytes. The extended Decal prefix stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, u32 value `1` at offset 20, and a zero byte at offset 24; its image-asset reference, scope code, and target-group reference occur at offsets 25, 36, and 37. Both references keep their six trailing zero bytes. The typed Decal prefix stores each reference as a 51-byte typed local reference: the image-asset reference at offset 21 has target type GUID `9A9B75AF-D286-4548-9301-28910E24EA20`, the scope code is at offset 72, and the target-group reference at offset 73 has target type GUID `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841`. The typed extended Decal prefix has the extended header and the typed references; its image-asset reference, scope code, and target-group reference occur at offsets 25, 76, and 77. The target is a construction-operand group with role `0x0000000400000000`, and each member selects decal target faces. A member that is a whole-body recipe envelope identifies its faces through its persistent reference clauses. The member's nested `body_recipe_data` records precede its enclosing `N+4` boundary.

The image-asset record index also names a Decal placement record that precedes the image-asset record. Ten zero bytes occupy placement offsets 11 through 20, and a marked record reference occurs at offset 21. A u32 vertex count at offset 32 is followed by one f32 `(u, v)` pair for each display-mesh vertex of the target body; a pair whose magnitude exceeds `1e6` marks a vertex outside the decal. The pairs are followed by a u32 decal ordinal, the f32 vector `U`, the f32 vector `V`, and three bytes. A marked record reference, two f64 values, a zero byte, an f32 value, and two marked record references separated by one zero byte follow. After four zero bytes, the record stores the f64 unit normal `N` and the f64 centre `O`, the LP-UTF16 name of the source image, a u32 count, and that many u32 vertex indices of the covered triangles. The index run ends at the image-asset record. `U`, `V`, and `O` are in Design length units. `U` is the image width axis, `V` is the image height axis, and `N` is parallel to `U x V`. For an image of `pw` by `ph` pixels with `m = max(pw, ph)`, the image width is `sqrt(2) * |U| * pw / m` and the image height is `sqrt(2) * |V| * ph / m`, both centred at `O`.

The referenced Decal image asset has two consecutive indexed records. The primary record is 30 bytes. Eight zero bytes occupy offsets 11 through 18, followed by a marked Fusion Design entity suffix at offset 19 and six zero bytes at offsets 24 through 29. The image-name record begins at offset 30 and has the primary record index plus one. Ten zero bytes occupy its offsets 11 through 20. An LP-UTF16 archive-entry basename begins at offset 21 and ends at the next indexed-record header. The basename uniquely identifies an entry in `Images.BlobParts`. The typed Decal image-asset record is 70 bytes. Eight zero bytes occupy its offsets 11 through 18, followed by a 51-byte typed local reference at offset 19 whose target is the Fusion Design entity suffix and whose target type GUID is `878C70A7-15B8-4B0B-B1B7-C2A7A23CC45C`. Its image-name record begins at offset 70 and has the same layout.

An `Align` prefix precedes its ordered reference table. The compact and extended prefix layouts are `align_scope_prefix` and `align_scope_extended_prefix`. Both start with the indexed header and nine zero bytes. The extended form adds u32 value `1`. The common block contains a zero byte, a marked record reference with six trailing zero bytes, a u32 code, a second marked record reference with six trailing zero bytes, the LP-UTF16 zero GUID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`, and three zero bytes. The first reference is member 2 of the scope reference table; the second is member 0. Member ordinals are zero-based. The code is unsigned.

The indexed record named by the first Align prefix reference is its constructor. The `align_constructor` form contains eight marked u32 words and five unsigned u32 codes in layout order. Marked words 4 and 7 are back-references to the scope record index; word ordinals are zero-based. The matrix block has sixteen consecutive finite f64 scalars in stored order. A separate finite f64 scalar occurs between the last two codes. The remaining fixed bytes are zero. The paired indexed header repeats the constructor record index.

An Align rigid-motion constructor has type GUID `84E6245F-1CDC-4FB8-8048-163A85FAD3F0`, version `2`, and source form `4`. It uses the shared six-reference rigid-transform prefix. The second Align prefix reference selects the whole-body construction group at scope-reference ordinal zero, with role `0x0000000400000000`. The group members are whole-body recipe operands. The scope reference table can store further construction groups with role `0x0000000500000000` after the constructor reference. The constructor's paired header repeats its record index.

The `align_transform_two_reference_prefix` contains two present leading references, four absent remaining reference slots, two unsigned code words, source form four, and the matrix-presence marker. The `align_transform_four_reference_prefix` contains two absent leading references and four present remaining references. A zero matrix-presence marker precedes sixteen row-major f64 scalars. A one marker omits those scalars and precedes the common 77- or 78-byte tail.

`CopyPasteBodies` uses the same scope framing with a 110-byte tail instead of the 78-byte tail. Its family-local ordinal is at tail offset 0 and its preceding history-state identity is at tail offset 53. Two marked references name a counted body group and a source-to-copy relation record. A `CopyPasteBodies` scope that stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, prologue byte `0` at offset 20, and `u32 1` at offset 21 has the body-group reference at offset 25 and the relation reference at offset 36. Any other scope has them at primary-header offsets 29 and 40. The body group has ten zero bytes after its indexed header, followed by `u32 N` and `N` marked body-operand record indices; these are the scope reference table's members after the group record. The relation record has eight zero bytes after its indexed header, a marked u32 value `2N`, and `N` ordered source/copy body-entity-suffix pairs. Each source suffix is a marked u32 with ten trailing zero bytes. Each copied suffix is a marked u32 with six trailing zero bytes; four zero alignment bytes separate it from a following pair. Source and copied suffixes are distinct. A source suffix names a `BodiesRoot` member or a body binding of the stream; the source body need not have a binding of its own. A copied suffix has a body binding. A copied suffix joins through the active Design body map to the independent neutral body introduced by the operation.

`Component Insert` has one ordered reference and a generation-specific scope prologue. A 399-byte frame has nine zero bytes after its primary header, `01 00 00 00 00`, an eight-byte occurrence identity, four zero bytes, a marked reference at offset 37, six zero bytes, `01 00`, and a row-major rigid transform at offset 50. A 381-byte frame has the same fields through the marked reference, six zero bytes, `01`, and the transform at offset 49. A 395-byte frame has ten zero bytes after its primary header, an eight-byte occurrence identity, four zero bytes, a marked reference at offset 33, six zero bytes, `01 00`, and the transform at offset 46. A 404-byte frame has nine zero bytes after its primary header, `01 00 00 00 00`, four zero bytes, an eight-byte occurrence identity, four zero bytes, a marked reference at offset 41, six zero bytes, `01 00`, and the transform at offset 54. The marked reference equals the scope's sole ordered reference. The first three forms name a 57-byte relation record. That record has ten zero bytes after its indexed header and marked references at offsets 21, 34, and 46; their zero tails are eight, seven, and six bytes. The first names the grouped component-occurrence carrier, and the third is a back-reference to the scope. The 404-byte form names a 58-byte relation record with ten zero bytes after its indexed header and marked references at offsets 21, 35, and 47; their zero tails are six, seven, and six bytes. The first names the grouped component-occurrence carrier, and the third is a back-reference to the scope. The carrier class tag is segment-local and does not select the carrier. The exact scope frame and its relation record select it. In the first three forms, the carrier stores an LP-UTF16 occurrence-role GUID followed by two zero bytes and a rigid transform equal to the scope transform. A class-`288` carrier stores consecutive identity and occurrence-role GUIDs, a linked-asset GUID, a qualified asset identity, the equal transform, and the repeated qualified identity. The 404-byte carrier placement stores the equal transform before an LP-UTF16 occurrence-role GUID, followed by `00 01 06 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00`. When the container supplies the external-reference table, the carrier entity ID, role, and transform identify one occurrence. A scope-bound construction selects its carrier by its primary indexed entity ID in the same Design stream. Its transform takes precedence only for that carrier. The carrier contributes one occurrence, and each other placement for the same role contributes a separate occurrence. A scope-bound carrier without a matching placement contributes one occurrence. A top-level insert that no external reference selects, including every insert when the table is absent, projects one root occurrence at the scope transform with an unresolved prototype, and its inserted-component feature names that occurrence. An insert that the timeline item run does not list is an operation operand and projects no occurrence.

The compact identity form is a 261-byte frame admitted for class-`296` paired with class `263`, class-`410` paired with class `261`, class-`426` paired with class `258`, class-`434` paired with class `266`, and class-`414` paired with class `264`. Relative to its primary indexed header, it has nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, `01 00 00 00 00` at offsets 20 through 24, an occurrence identity u64 at offset 25, four zero bytes at offsets 33 through 36, a marked reference to the sole relation at offset 37, six zero bytes at offsets 42 through 47, bytes `01 01` at offsets 48 and 49, u32 code-unit count 36 at offset 50, and the 36-code-unit null GUID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` at offset 54. It stores no scope transform; its transform is the identity.

Class `414` paired with class `264` also has 257- and 267-byte shifted identity frames. Both have ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, the occurrence identity at offset 21, four zero bytes at offsets 29 through 32, the marked relation at offset 33, six zero bytes at offsets 38 through 43, bytes `01 01` at offsets 44 and 45, the null-GUID code-unit count at offset 46, and its UTF-16 payload at offset 50. Their transform is the identity. The 389-byte matrix frame uses the 261-byte prologue through the relation and six zero bytes, stores bytes `01 00` at offsets 48 and 49, a row-major rigid transform at offset 50, the null-GUID code-unit count at offset 178, and its UTF-16 payload at offset 182. Its remaining scope tail is the 261-byte tail shifted by 128 bytes. The matrix in the repeated-target carrier equals the scope matrix.

The identity form names the same 57-byte relation record as the 381-, 395-, and 399-byte forms. Its first marked reference names a grouped identity carrier and its third references the scope. A class-`382` carrier is used by the class-`296`/class-`263` form; a class-`380` carrier is used by the class-`410`/class-`261` form. The class-`426`/class-`258` form uses a 57-byte class-`345`/class-`258` relation and a following 58-byte class-`393` child record; the child is the relation's second marked member and carries an opaque u64 token. The class-`345` relation stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, the carrier reference at offset 22, eight zero bytes at offsets 26 through 33, the child reference at offset 35, and the scope back-reference at offset 47. The class-`393` child stores the relation back-reference at offset 32 and its opaque token at offset 42. The class-`382`, class-`380`, and compact class-`369` carriers share a 695-byte grouped identity envelope from their primary indexed header to the relation header. The class-`382` and class-`380` forms use `00 01 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00` after the role; the compact class-`369` form uses `00 03 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00`. An external class-`369` carrier uses the same field order with a variable LP-UTF16 role length from 36 through 256 code units; a role with suffix `_urn:` uses `00 04 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00` after the role, and the relation header begins at the closure. Each has eight zero bytes at offsets 11 through 18, byte `1` at offset 19, u32 `1` at offset 20, byte `1` at offset 24, an occurrence identity u64 at offset 25, byte `1` at offset 33, and four zero bytes at offsets 34 through 37. At offset 38 it stores an LP-UTF16 component GUID, one zero separator byte, an LP-ASCII type GUID, and an LP-UTF16 occurrence-role GUID. The class-specific role marker is followed by two LP-UTF16 metadata GUIDs and `00 01 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 00`. It then repeats the component GUID, separator byte, type GUID, and role GUID, followed by `00 01 00 00 00 00`, a final role GUID, and `00 01 04 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00`. Every GUID has 36 code units or ASCII bytes, repeated component, type, and role GUIDs are equal, and the carrier has no matrix. Its placement is the identity.
The class-`434`/class-`266` identity form uses a 57-byte class-`348`/class-`266` relation with the same three marked references and zero tails. Its first reference names a class-`341` grouped identity carrier. The carrier has the grouped prefix through the occurrence identity and the component, type, and role fields above. Its role is an LP-UTF16 value of 36 through 256 code units and is either a GUID or a GUID prefix followed by `_urn:`. The first role is followed by `00 01 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00` and two LP-UTF16 metadata GUIDs. A ten-byte member then stores byte `0`, marker `1`, and the carrier's occurrence identity u64. Five bytes `01 00 00 00 00` precede the repeated component, type, and role fields. Six bytes `00 01 00 00 00 00` precede the final role field. The twelve-byte closure `00 01 04 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` ends at the relation header. The carrier has no matrix; its placement is the identity.

The class-`283` / class-`262` generation has two exact scope frames. In both forms, `byte_offset` is the primary class-`283` indexed header and the paired class-`262` indexed header begins at `byte_offset + frame_length`. Both store ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, an occurrence identity u64 at offset 21, four zero bytes at offsets 29 through 32, a marked relation reference at offset 33 with its u32 value at offset 34, and six zero bytes at offsets 38 through 43. The 257-byte form stores `01 01` at offsets 44 and 45, an LP-UTF16 null component GUID with code-unit count 36 at offset 46 and payload at offset 50, three zero bytes at offsets 122 through 124, one ordered reference at offset 125 with marker 1 at offset 129 and the relation index at offset 130, six zero bytes at offsets 134 through 139, and the current history-state identity `0xffffffff` at offset 140. Its kind count is 16 at offset 144 and its `Component Insert` payload starts at offset 148. The feature ordinal is at offset 180 and the preceding history-state identity is at offset 211. The 385-byte form stores `01 00` at offsets 44 and 45, a row-major rigid transform of 16 little-endian f64 values at offset 46, the null component GUID count at offset 174 and payload at offset 178, three zero bytes at offsets 250 through 252, one ordered reference at offset 253 with marker 1 at offset 257 and the relation index at offset 258, six zero bytes at offsets 262 through 267, and the current history-state identity `0xffffffff` at offset 268. Its kind count is 16 at offset 272 and its `Component Insert` payload starts at offset 276. The feature ordinal is at offset 308 and the preceding history-state identity is at offset 339. The remaining fixed tail bytes occupy the spans between these typed lanes and the paired header; the frame lengths are 257 and 385 bytes.

The relation for both class-`283` forms is the 57-byte three-reference form described above. Its first reference names a class-`334` carrier. A class-`334` carrier stores a 36-code-unit component identity as an LP-UTF16 field at offset 38, then a direct UTF-16LE neutron-role payload at offset 159. The role payload ends at a ten-byte discriminator tail consisting of byte `0`, a nonzero marker byte, four zero bytes, and a nonzero u32; a second 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 identity follows that tail. The class-`334` carrier has no placement matrix. The 257-byte scope supplies the identity placement, and the 385-byte scope supplies the placement matrix at offset 46.

The 272-byte Component Insert scope stores fourteen zero bytes at offsets 11 through 24, its occurrence identity u64 at offset 25, four zero bytes at offset 33, its marked relation reference at offset 37, six zero bytes at offset 42, and identity bytes `01 01` at offset 48. The LP-UTF16 null GUID starts at offset 50. Three zero bytes follow it, then the one-member ordered reference table at offset 129. A 276-byte frame replaces the fourteen zero bytes with nine zero bytes, `01 00 00 00 00`, and four zero bytes. All subsequent fields move four bytes later. The 400-byte frame stores the fields of the 272-byte frame through offset 47, bytes `01 00` at offset 48, and a row-major rigid transform at offset 50. Its LP-UTF16 null GUID starts at offset 178, and the later fields of the 272-byte frame move 128 bytes later. Both frames have an identity placement and a 58-byte relation with marked references at offsets 21, 35, and 47. The first names the carrier; the last references the scope. The relation has ten zero bytes after the header, six zero bytes after the carrier reference, `01 00 00` at offset 32, seven zero bytes after the middle reference, and six zero bytes after the scope reference. The 272-, 276-, 400-, and 404-byte frames can name an attributed legacy occurrence placement as their carrier. Its occurrence-role GUID is the occurrence role of the insert. The identity frames name a placement with identity flag `1`. The 400- and 404-byte frames name a placement with identity flag `0` whose matrix equals the scope transform. Component Insert frame lengths count the stored feature-family name `Component Insert`. A stored name of `L` UTF-16 code units adds `2 * (L - 16)` bytes to the frame length.

The 271- and 275-byte identity scopes use the respective 272- and 276-byte prefixes and ordered reference tables. The sole reference selects a 57-byte relation. Its first marked reference selects a legacy typed occurrence placement with identity flag `1`. Its last marked reference selects the scope. The carrier ends at the relation header and its role selects the occurrence.

Shifted identity insertion scopes have a 122-byte prefix. The 256-byte form uses that prefix through its null GUID, then the sole relation table, the 16-code-unit kind name and a 76-byte scope tail. The 257- and 267-byte forms retain the same identity prefix with their respective bounded tails. The 261-byte identity form and the 385-, 389- and 399-byte matrix forms retain their documented prologues independently of the source relation and carrier. The occurrence identity and stored placement belong to the scope; the referenced carrier supplies a separate source binding. The 385-byte matrix starts immediately after the two transform markers; all sixteen matrix values belong to the transform.

The 404-byte matrix scope uses the 276-byte prologue. Its fields after that prologue follow the 400-byte matrix scope with a four-byte shift: the matrix starts at offset 54 and the null GUID starts at offset 182. The scope placement and occurrence identity are independent of the relation carrier that supplies the source occurrence role.

A 261-byte identity frame stores the fields of the 272-byte frame through its one-member ordered reference table at offset 129. The class-`296`, `410`, `414`, `426`, and `434` compact generations keep their own 261-byte frames. It names a 57-byte relation with the layout of the relation of the 399-, 381-, and 395-byte forms. The first relation reference names a legacy typed occurrence placement (§1.4) with identity flag `1` that ends where the relation record begins. The final LP-UTF16 role of that placement is the occurrence role of the insert, and the identity placement is the insertion frame.

The typed-reference Component Insert scope is written by the container generation whose references carry inline type GUIDs (see "**References.**"). Its frame is 584 bytes. It stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, the occurrence identity u64 at offset 21, four zero bytes at offsets 29 through 32, and a 51-byte typed relation reference at offset 33 with inline type `2D6E13A1-BBEF-4FB3-9277-00D99F634136`. Bytes `01 00` at offset 84 precede a row-major rigid transform at offset 86. The LP-UTF16 null GUID starts at offset 214. Three zero bytes, the u32 reference count `1` at offset 293, and the typed ordered reference at offset 297 follow it. The current history-state identity `0xffffffff` is at offset 348, the kind count is at offset 352, and the feature ordinal is at offset 388. The typed relation is 177 bytes. It stores ten zero bytes after its indexed header and typed references at offsets 21, 74, and 126. Two zero bytes follow the first reference, and one zero byte follows the second. The first reference has inline type `CE2913AA-CFE0-4F04-9102-24424ED3BCFA` and names the carrier. The third reference names the scope with the inline type GUID of the Component Insert family. The carrier is a repeated-target occurrence placement (§1.4) with identity flag `0` whose matrix equals the scope transform. Its final role is the occurrence role of the insert and selects the external-reference entry.

The 420-byte identity insertion carrier has the legacy typed occurrence-placement envelope with two changes before its repeated target: a Boolean byte and a zero byte precede the count before the metadata GUID pair, and a 16-byte metadata member replaces the zero byte after that pair. The member stores marker `1`, a nonzero opaque u64 token, and seven bytes `00 01 01 00 00 00 00`. The indexed entity identity is followed by an empty LP-ASCII record name. Both legacy target references are equal. The identity flag is `1`, the following u32 is zero, and the final LP-UTF16 GUID is the occurrence role. The closure is `00 01 06 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00`. The role selects the external-reference entry and its design path. The EntityTracking link selects the inserted design asset and root Component. The scope occurrence identity and the target reference's source occurrence identity are separate identity domains. The insertion feature names the projected external occurrence. An XREF target is an external design reference; absence of an XREF match does not state that the insertion is an independent copy. The identity placement states the insertion frame. Component-path carriers state its current pose, and assembly joints can define a solved pose.

The Component Insert generation map is:

| Primary / paired class | Scope length | Scope transform | Relation length | Carrier placement |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| dynamic / 259 | 399 | matrix at +50 | 57 | role GUID, zero separator, equal matrix |
| dynamic / 261 | 381 | matrix at +49 | 57 | role GUID, zero separator, equal matrix; class 288 also supplies the legacy carrier |
| dynamic / 258 | 395 | matrix at +46 | 57 | role GUID, zero separator, equal matrix |
| dynamic / any | 404 | matrix at +54 | 58 | equal matrix, role GUID, placement marker |
| 296 / 263 | 261 | implicit identity | 57 | grouped class 382 identity carrier |
| 410 / 261 | 261 | implicit identity | 57 | grouped class 380 identity carrier |
| 426 / 258 | 261 | implicit identity | 57 (class 345 / 258 relation plus 58-byte class 393 child) | grouped class 369 identity carrier |
| 434 / 266 | 261 | implicit identity | 57 (class 348 / 266 relation) | class 341 grouped identity carrier; identity transform |
| 414 / 264 | 257 or 267 | implicit identity | 57 (class 261 relation) | repeated-target identity carrier; repeated role selects the occurrence |
| 414 / 264 | 261 | implicit identity | 57 (class 261 relation) | repeated-target identity carrier; repeated role selects the occurrence |
| 414 / 264 | 389 | matrix at +50 | 57 (class 261 relation) | repeated-target carrier with equal matrix; repeated role selects the occurrence |
| 283 / 262 | 257 | implicit identity | 57 | class 334 carrier: direct role UTF-16, no matrix |
| 283 / 262 | 385 | matrix at +46 | 57 | class 334 carrier: direct role UTF-16, no matrix |
| dynamic / any | 272 | implicit identity | 58 | 420-byte identity insertion carrier or attributed legacy placement |
| dynamic / any | 276 | implicit identity | 58 | 420-byte identity insertion carrier or attributed legacy placement |
| dynamic / any | 400 | matrix at +50 | 58 | attributed legacy placement with equal matrix |
| dynamic / any | 271 or 275 | implicit identity | 57 | legacy typed identity placement |
| dynamic / any | 261 (272-byte prefix) | implicit identity | 57 | legacy typed identity placement; its role selects the occurrence |
| dynamic / any | 584 (typed references) | matrix at +86 | 177 (typed) | repeated-target carrier with equal matrix; repeated role selects the occurrence |


A local component occurrence uses the one-element path grammar of §1.4. Its untyped form has a 229-byte identity frame or a 357-byte matrix frame. The primary record index selects the carrier by its entity and offset; its exact frame grammar identifies it, and its class tag is a per-file dynamic value. After the indexed header, the frame stores u32 `0` and an empty LP-ASCII instance name, `u8 1` at offset 19, and u32 path count `1` at offset 20. Marked component-record references at offsets 24 and 197 carry the same u64 value within one carrier. The u32 instance discriminator is at offset 35, and the path terminator is at offset 39. Each frame stores the one-based occurrence ordinal at offset 40, an LP-UTF16 carrier GUID at offset 44, and an LP-UTF16 occurrence GUID at offset 120. Offset 208 is the identity flag. The identity frame has flag `1`, ordinal one, and no matrix; its placement is the identity transform. The matrix frame has flag `0` and a row-major orthonormal local-to-container transform at offset 209. Every local component-occurrence matrix has an orthonormal upper-left 3×3 block, the bottom row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`, and determinant `1` or `-1`. A determinant of `-1` places a mirrored occurrence: the transform reflects the component's geometry and reverses its orientation. A class-`256` carrier uses a matrix frame only for an ordinal greater than one; any other class tag can use a matrix frame for ordinal one. Matrix translations are in centimetres. Nine zero bytes and the marker `u8 1` follow the flag or the matrix. The u64 owner entity is at offset 219 of the identity frame or offset 347 of the matrix frame, and two zero bytes close the frame. Occurrence GUIDs are unique within a Design stream. The `MetaStream` primary index selects the frame for each entity, including an entity with only one carrier frame.

An empty-attribute local component occurrence stores an empty attribute list after its path. It replaces the terminator at offset 39 with `u8 1` and u32 count `0` at offset 40. The ordinal is at offset 44, the LP-UTF16 carrier and occurrence GUIDs are at offsets 48 and 124, the repeated reference is at offset 201, and the identity flag is at offset 212. The identity frame is 233 bytes; the matrix frame is 361 bytes. All fields after the attribute count have the fixed untyped form's order and meaning. The empty list is followed directly by the ordinal and the two GUIDs. The root-instance path also permits this empty attribute list. The layouts are in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

Typed local component occurrences use local references with inline type GUIDs. The primary record index and the Component occurrence-placement type row (§1.4) select the carrier; the indexed header agrees with that registration. They use the repeated-target placement generation of §1.4, with a one-element path. Each reference contains `u8 1`, a u64 target, an LP-ASCII type GUID of 36 bytes, and two zero bytes. Both definition references carry inline type GUID `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`. The first definition reference starts at offset 24. The u32 instance discriminator at offset 75 and the path terminator at offset 79 follow it, then the one-based occurrence ordinal at offset 80, the LP-UTF16 carrier GUID at offset 84, and the LP-UTF16 occurrence GUID at offset 160. The repeated definition reference has the same target and inline type as the first. With the separator, the identity frame is 349 bytes and the matrix frame is 477 bytes. One zero byte at offset 236 precedes the repeated reference at offset 237 and the identity flag at offset 288. Flag `1` selects identity; flag `0` selects a matrix at offset 289. Without the separator, the 348-byte identity frame and 476-byte matrix frame have their repeated reference at offset 236 and identity flag at offset 287. An identity frame has ordinal one. A matrix frame has flag `0` and a row-major orthonormal local-to-container matrix immediately after the flag, with translation in centimetres. A class-`256` matrix frame requires an ordinal greater than one. After the flag or matrix, `u32 0`, an empty LP-UTF16 role, `u8 0`, and a typed local owner reference close the record. The owner reference carries inline type GUID `904F885E-D859-4755-A7EF-6EBED8732FAD`. The typed prefix and tail layouts are in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

An attributed local component occurrence carries a counted attribute run and an occurrence key. After the indexed header it stores u32 `0`, an empty LP-ASCII instance name, `u8 1`, u32 path count `1`, the marked u64 component-record reference at offset 24, two zero bytes, the u32 path discriminator at offset 35, `u8 1`, and a u32 attribute count at offset 40. The attribute count can be zero. Each attribute is an LP-ASCII name, an LP-ASCII type, and a value: type `IntrinsicMetaTypebool` stores one byte `0` or `1`, and types `IntrinsicMetaTypeHString` and `IntrinsicMetaTypeIString` store LP-UTF16 strings. Two prefix bytes, the u32 one-based occurrence ordinal, the LP-UTF16 carrier GUID, and the LP-UTF16 occurrence key follow. The path discriminator is independent of the later occurrence ordinal. The occurrence key is a 36-code-unit GUID or a positive decimal key such as `34`, and it is unique within a Design stream. A standard cross-segment reference, one zero byte, the repeated marked component-record reference, and two zero bytes follow. The reference retains its u64 key-record index and u32 segment index. The identity flag, the matrix when the flag is `0`, nine zero bytes, the marker `u8 1`, the u64 owner entity, and two zero bytes close the frame as in the fixed frames. An attributed identity frame can retain a positive occurrence ordinal greater than one without storing a matrix. The fixed attributed prefix is in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). A path record can name a local occurrence by its decimal occurrence key in place of its occurrence GUID.

A leading-flag local component occurrence stores its identity flag before its GUIDs. The primary record index selects the carrier, and the Component occurrence-placement type row (§1.4) registers its record. After the indexed header, the frame stores u32 `0`, an empty LP-ASCII instance name, `u8 1` at offset 19, u32 path count `1` at offset 20, the marked u64 component-record reference at offset 24, two zero bytes, and the u32 path discriminator at offset 35. An empty attribute list follows: `u8 1` at offset 39 and u32 count `0` at offset 40. The u16 ordinal prefix is at offset 44, the u32 one-based occurrence ordinal is at offset 46, and the identity flag is at offset 50. Flag `0` stores a row-major orthonormal local-to-container matrix at offset 51, with translation in centimetres. The leading flag and matrix store a source frame. The body follows the flag or the matrix: the LP-UTF16 carrier GUID, the LP-UTF16 occurrence GUID, a marked same-segment record reference, one zero byte, `u8 1`, u32 path count `1`, one zero byte, the repeated marked component-record reference, two zero bytes, and the local-placement identity flag. Local flag `0` stores the occurrence's current owner-relative matrix; local flag `1` stores identity. The two flags and matrices are independent. Nine zero bytes, the marker `u8 1`, the u64 owner entity, and two zero bytes close the frame. The frame is 251 bytes with two identity flags, 379 bytes with one matrix, and 507 bytes with two matrices. Local flag `1` with ordinal one is the base placement, and local flag `0` is the matrix placement. As in the fixed frames, a class-`256` carrier uses the matrix frame only for an ordinal greater than one. The prefix and body layouts are in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

A hidden-occurrence record has type GUID `2BB3BB69-B0FD-4D56-B4CD-DEBD30847BE3`, base-type GUID `CA12EC7A-FB0A-4045-A429-072D0874B557`, type version `1`, and add-in name `CommonData`. The type table lists one entity for each hidden occurrence, and the entity id is the record index. After the indexed header the record stores eight zero bytes, `u8 1`, and a u32 count. The count is followed by marked references: `u8 1`, a u32 record index, and four zero bytes. The record names the occurrence carriers of an occurrence path in order. A carrier is a local component occurrence record or the placement record of an external reference (§1.4). A reference to a component-definition record can stand between two carrier references, and a carrier reference can repeat. The final carrier reference names the hidden occurrence. Each earlier carrier reference names a containing occurrence, and the record hides the target only inside an instance of that carrier. An occurrence with no hidden-occurrence record is displayed.

The attribute run can be followed by an object prelude: one zero byte, a positive u32 count, that many LP-ASCII property names, one zero byte, an untyped local reference to the occurrence-placement entity itself, one zero byte, the component reference, and an LP-UTF16 persistent object key. The component reference agrees with both definition references in the enclosing occurrence. The property-name run is ordered. The persistent object key is separate from the following carrier GUID and occurrence key. A one-byte zero ordinal prefix follows this prelude.

A version-two attributed local occurrence also permits a one-byte zero ordinal prefix. The two-byte prefix form permits marker `u8 1` after the ordinal and before the carrier GUID. The ordinal prefix layouts start at the first prefix byte after the attribute run or object prelude and are defined in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). The complete frame and its repeated component reference select the prefix form. The identity reference after the occurrence key is either null or a cross-segment reference. A null reference is one zero byte followed directly by the repeated component reference. A cross-segment reference is followed by the zero separator or source reference defined above. Its segment index selects the segment header's ID, and its target selects a primary entity in that segment. An ACT target has type `96E1B59A-1989-4493-AA92-67E6072135F6`, version `0`, module `CommonData`; its cross-segment occurrence reference returns to the Design occurrence-placement entity. The occurrence key is scoped to the Design stream. The closing owner reference names the containing component naming space. A component-path pose supplies a world placement independently of the closing matrix. The owner reference closes the primary member extent. A frame that satisfies the complete leading-flag grammar has that form and its primary-index requirement.

An attributed local component occurrence also permits a typed component reference. Its path discriminator follows the complete reference at offset 75, the attribute marker is at offset 79, and the attribute count is at offset 80. The attribute run starts at offset 84. The repeated definition reference has the same target and inline type as the first. The closing owner reference is typed and carries inline type GUID `904F885E-D859-4755-A7EF-6EBED8732FAD`. The remaining members have the same order and meanings as in the untyped attributed form.

A named root-instance record can store an empty path. Its indexed header is followed by u32 `0`, LP-ASCII `rootInstance`, marker `u8 1` at offset 31, and u32 path count `0` at offset 32. This path has no component-definition reference. The empty-path typed identity root-instance frame is 255 bytes. It stores one zero byte at offset 36, u32 `2` at offset 37, LP-UTF16 carrier and occurrence GUIDs at offsets 41 and 117, and a typed local component-definition reference at offset 193.
