Identity flag `1` at offset 244 and ten zero bytes close the frame. The separated empty-path typed identity root-instance frame is 256 bytes. It adds a zero separator at offset 193 before the typed definition reference at offset 194; the identity flag moves to offset 245 and the ten zero bytes start at offset 246. Both forms store u32 `2` at offset 37. The typed reference after the GUIDs names the root component definition; it is separate from the empty path.

The component-record reference names the component definition record. That record stores the context binding of one component naming space within its primary record extent. The component definition is that naming space. A Body-container membership assigns body ownership; the order of entity identities does not define that membership. Entity-cluster fallback groups bodies in uninstanced definitions. A fallback-owned body with an unresolved component-definition binding belongs to an uninstanced stored-frame group in its Design stream. Each fallback-owned body keeps its stored frame and carries `assembly.component-body-owner-fallback`. When the neutral model has at least one occurrence, each body-owning definition that no occurrence instances, including a fallback group and the definition of an unplaced local occurrence, has one occurrence below the document root with the identity transform. Its bodies keep their stored frames, and the placement carries `assembly.stored-frame-occurrence`. A model without occurrences keeps every definition uninstanced. When an inserted Design member has no occurrence, its stored-frame groups are not kept as definitions; their bodies belong to the member definition that the inserting occurrence instances. A feature whose output bodies span several definitions with unadmitted membership retains all output body references. Its product owner is unresolved under `scope.output-owner-unresolved`. Occurrence placement applies to bodies with admitted component ownership. An admitted component-transfer intent retains its mode and source and target frames when its occurrence resolves. A definition can own no body and contain no occurrence. Its context binding identifies the definition independently of its instances. Its name, body membership, sketch collections, and component-local construction history belong to the definition at every instance count. Occurrence references and placement records identify its instances and their transforms. Carriers that name one component definition record can store different carrier GUIDs. The owner entity is the root entity of the component naming space that contains the occurrence. A root-instance path with one element names the root component of a Design stream through the occurrence-placement record whose instance name is `rootInstance`. After its indexed header that record stores u32 `0`, LP-ASCII `rootInstance`, `u8 1`, u32 path count `1`, and a marked u64 component-definition reference. The root component has one root occurrence with the identity transform. A CommonData component path can contain this root-instance record before, between, or after its component and occurrence references. This element selects the Design root independently of its discriminator. The path matrix gives the occurrence world pose in that root frame. A path with one component reference and one occurrence reference selects that occurrence in either reference order. An occurrence whose owner entity is the root entity of the root component's naming space is a child of the root occurrence, and its transform maps the component definition into the root component frame.

The terminal Body-container membership with inline-typed local references belongs to type `CD57BC48-50EC-47DC-975A-FB6DEA72F4DA`, base type `A7AEA631-985B-4DD1-8CE2-DE2C-14B54081`, version `4`, module `Body`. It consists of a u32 body count, that many typed same-segment references to Body entities of type `D3937028-C20C-4E65-B010-94AD418A5C20`, and one typed same-segment reference to the owning component definition of type `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`. The final reference ends at the primary record boundary. Each reference is `u8 1`, a nonzero u64 target, u32 GUID byte count `36`, the ASCII type GUID, and two zero bytes. The reference width is defined by `component_body_membership_reference` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). The terminal list can be empty. A listed body belongs to the named component definition irrespective of its entity suffix. The body-map suffix joins this membership to the solved body. Two memberships that name different component definitions do not define a unique owner.

The paired untyped Body-container membership consists of a u32 body count, that many untyped same-segment Body references, the same u32 count, the same unique Body references in an independent order with u32 `1` after each reference, and one untyped same-segment reference to the owning component definition. The owner reference ends at the primary record boundary. An untyped reference consists of `u8 1`, a nonzero u64 target, and two zero bytes. The type table registers the body and component targets under their respective type GUIDs. The reference and repeated-entry widths are defined by `component_body_membership_local_reference` and `component_body_membership_local_entry` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). Both body lists can be empty. A body-map entity can have no Body-container membership. The two lists have the same set of body identities. A body-map pair is outside the current model when its Design stream registers at least one Body container, every registered container has a membership in one of the three forms above with registered targets, no list names the pair's entity, the entity's browser node stores hidden flag `1`, and the entity's component cluster has no bound component definition. A pair that meets the membership conditions, with or without a bound cluster, is also outside the current model when a consuming scope names it. A consuming scope has type GUID `2A94257F-2020-4B19-9A68-103A2672F1B7` (`Combine`) or `4A782808-FBDD-4351-A10A-F7AE5693D330` (`RemoveBody`). It names a pair through a whole-body selection record whose final local reference is that scope and whose second reference run has a local reference to a registered browser node. A browser node named this way stores ten zero bytes after its indexed header, the counted GUID at offset 21, hidden flag `1`, a byte of zero or one, and a local reference to the pair's entity. The same join removes such a pair when the byte after the hidden flag is zero. The BREP stream and the body map retain that body, and the pair supplies no model body. A pair that a list names stays in the current model at either flag value. Repeated identities within either list are invalid.

A single untyped membership can store one zero u32 between its body-reference run and its owner reference. The zero word belongs to the membership extent. Registered Body targets select the complete terminal list when an overlapping byte reading permits an empty suffix. Its overhead is `component_body_membership_single_zero_overhead` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

The single untyped Body-container membership consists of a u32 body count, that many unique untyped same-segment Body references, and one untyped same-segment reference to the owning component definition. The final reference ends at the primary record boundary. The body references form the maximal contiguous reference run immediately before the owner; the count precedes that run. The type table registers every body and the owner under their respective type GUIDs. The container has the same version-4 registration as the other membership forms. Its overhead is defined by `component_body_membership_single_overhead` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). A zero count stores no body membership. Component membership requires the owner target to have the Component type registration. A terminal list whose owner has another registered type supplies no direct component-definition reference.


A local occurrence is a child of each occurrence of its containing component definition. The same rule applies to an external occurrence whose closing local owner names that definition's root entity in the same Design stream (§1.4). Each child retains its local-to-container matrix `L(child)`. Its document transform is `W(child) = W(parent) * L(child)`, with column-vector points. An identity frame is identity relative to the containing component. Each instance of a repeated component definition repeats its child occurrence tree with distinct instance paths and shared component definitions. An operand that selects one such instance names its outermost placed insertion occurrence and the native keys of its nested occurrences, outermost first, in `occurrence_path`. Component geometry remains in its definition frame. A component definition can own no physical bodies and contain local groups or external occurrences. When the selected modern maps and declared physical body members are empty, the component references and owner entities still define the local occurrence tree. Physical model-body ownership uses body records. Saved free-edge references identify edge records. A body emitted from a saved free-edge reference is selected by its saved-edge origin, not by the absence of a native body key; component body coverage excludes such bodies, and one that no product definition owns is reported under `assembly.saved-free-edge-body-unowned`. Sketch and profile wire bodies and unselected snapshot bodies supply no physical model-body ownership.

Legacy `CopyPaste` is a local component-occurrence operation. Its scope has one ordered reference and rigid source and copied placements 156 bytes apart. The 529-byte frame places them at offsets 38 and 194; the 525-byte frame omits one four-byte prologue field and places them at offsets 34 and 190. The ordered reference names the same 57-byte relation shape used by component insertion; its first reference names the generated class-`256` occurrence carrier and its third references the scope. The generated carrier's carrier GUID selects exactly one earlier ordinal-1 carrier for the source occurrence, and its transform equals the copied scope transform. The operation projects the copied occurrence as an inserted-component feature while retaining both source and copied placements in product structure.

`CutPaste` changes the containing component of one local component occurrence. Its single reference-table member names an occurrence relation. The relation has a 57-byte primary record: an indexed header, ten zero bytes, a marked occurrence-carrier reference, two zero bytes, a marked companion reference, one zero byte, and a marked reference to the paste scope. Its same-index paired header follows immediately. Eight zero bytes and a marked u64 owner-collection record reference with two trailing zero bytes follow that header. This collection belongs to the target containing component. The occurrence carrier has Component type GUID `CE2913AA-CFE0-4F04-9102-24424ED3BCFA`, precedes the relation, and starts with the local occurrence prefix: eight zero bytes, path marker `1`, path count `1`, and a marked component-definition record reference. The carrier reference identifies the transferred occurrence; the component-definition reference identifies its reusable component, rather than a body or a feature list.

The compact CutPaste prefix has ten zero bytes after its indexed header, a marked `RemoveInstance` reference at offset 21, a marked companion reference at offset 32, byte `1` at offset 43, a marked companion reference at offset 44, four zero bytes, the marked occurrence-relation reference at offset 59, byte `1` at offset 70, and the identity flag at offset 71. The 277-byte frame has identity flag `1` and no matrix. The 405-byte frame has identity flag `0` and a rigid row-major 4 × 4 f64 target placement at offset 72. Matrix translations are in centimetres. The 409-byte frame replaces the compact ten-zero-byte prologue with nine zero bytes, byte `1`, and four zero bytes; all later fields move four bytes forward. An LP-UTF16 occurrence key of 36 code units follows the identity flag or matrix. Three zero bytes, the single-member reference table, the history-state word, the kind, and an 87-byte or 88-byte scope tail follow. The shifted prefix with an explicit matrix and the 88-byte tail forms a 410-byte frame. The placement is the occurrence placement recorded by the target operation.

The RemoveInstance prefix has 22 zero bytes after its indexed header, a marked source-relation reference at offset 33, the same LP-UTF16 occurrence key at offset 44, seven zero bytes, the history-state word at offset 127, and LP-UTF16 `RemoveInstance` at offset 131. Its same-index paired header has eight zero bytes and a marked u64 source owner-collection record reference with two trailing zero bytes. The source relation has the occurrence-relation grammar above. Its carrier reference equals the target relation's carrier reference, and its owner-collection reference equals the removal's source owner-collection reference. The carrier precedes the source relation; the source relation precedes the target relation, which precedes the removal. The removal precedes the CutPaste scope. CutPaste retains the occurrence's component definition while it changes the occurrence owner and placement.

An owner collection has Fusion type GUID `3A6D1E62-99F8-4E32-BAAA-DBA0A2CFB27C`. Its containing context has Fusion type GUID `C3423E04-7E85-4B44-8E31-A5FA9C100052`. The context primary record ends with two marked references. The first names the owner collection and the second names a companion. The same-index context paired header follows, then eight zero bytes and a marked u64 component-aggregate reference with two trailing zero bytes. The collection header follows this 30-byte paired record immediately. Exactly one registered context has this collection reference and adjacency. The referenced aggregate has Fusion type GUID `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`. The context's aggregate is the containing component; the owner collection and the component naming-space root are distinct records. The component aggregate precedes its context. The referenced component aggregates, contexts, collections, carriers, and relations precede the paste scope. The context owner tail is 52 bytes: two eleven-byte marked references, an eleven-byte paired header, eight zero bytes, and the eleven-byte marked component-aggregate reference.

A CopyPaste scope whose occurrence relation has an owner collection uses the same relation grammar and target owner-collection reference. Its relation can also be the 58-byte relation of component insertion, which stores `01 00 00` at offset 32 and the companion and scope references at offsets 35 and 47. Its carrier's component reference identifies the reusable component definition of the copy. The compact CopyPaste prefix has eleven zero bytes after its indexed header, a marked companion reference at offset 22, a source identity flag, and an optional source placement. Source identity flag `0` places the source matrix at offset 34. A marked companion reference at offset 162, four zero bytes, the marked occurrence-relation reference at offset 177, byte `1`, and the target identity flag follow this matrix. Target identity flag `0` places the copied matrix at offset 190. Each placement matrix is a rigid row-major 4 × 4 f64 matrix with centimetre translations. Identity flag `1` represents the identity placement and omits that matrix. The copied placement is followed by LP-UTF16 `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`, three zero bytes, and the single-member scope reference table. A second form has fifteen zero bytes after the indexed header and shifts all later fields four bytes forward. The prefix and its reference table identify the form for every scope-tail length. The null key has no removal operand. CopyPaste creates another occurrence of the carrier's component definition. Its scope placements and target relation identify local placement and destination operands. The source occurrence and its containing component require a separate persistent-identity join.

A CopyPaste prefix with identity source placement omits the source matrix and places the second companion reference immediately after the source identity flag. The remaining fields retain their order. Its fixed prefix is `copy_paste_identity_source_prefix` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). Identity source and target placements with an 87-byte scope tail form a 269-byte frame. An identity source placement, an explicit target matrix, and an 88-byte scope tail form a 398-byte frame. Two explicit placement matrices with an 88-byte scope tail form a 526-byte frame.

When a one-direction `R-Pattern` repeats a local component occurrence, every generated placement after the seed is the transform of one generated class-`256` carrier. Those carriers share one carrier GUID and have consecutive one-based occurrence ordinals. The unique earlier ordinal-1 carrier with that carrier GUID is the seed occurrence; the pattern scope's first serialized instance transform supplies its placement. The neutral pattern seed is that occurrence and the remaining placements are product occurrences of the same local component.

Scope framing is independent of parameter ownership. A scope with no owned parameters has no parameter-owner backlink and is still identified by its paired indexed headers, feature-family field, reference table, state identities, and family-local ordinal.

`SpirePrimitive` selects the Coil feature family. A `SpirePrimitive` scope stores its result operation at primary-header offset 20 with values `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, `3 = intersect`, and `4 = new body`. Offset 24 is the clockwise Boolean. Offset 26 is u32 `2`. Offset 30 selects the driving dimensions: `1 = revolutions and height`, `2 = revolutions and pitch`, `3 = height and pitch`, and `4 = planar spiral by revolutions and radial pitch`. Offset 92 selects the section: `0 = circle`, `1 = square`, `2 = external triangle`, and `3 = internal triangle`. Offset 107 value `4` places the section inside the reference trajectory. Every form has exactly one `Diameter` and one `SectionSize` parameter. Axial forms additionally have exactly one `TaperAngle` and exactly the two parameters named by their extent. The spiral has exactly one `Revolutions` and one `Pitch` and no taper parameter. Join, cut, and intersect require one construction-operand group with role `0x0000000800000000`; new body has no such group.

`CoilPrimitive` is the compact Coil dialect. Its scope has seven or eight ordered references. Offset 20 value `1` creates a new body, offset 25 is the left-hand Boolean, and offset 26 is u32 `4`. A right-hand coil (`0`) travels clockwise viewed along its positive axis, and a left-hand coil (`1`) travels counterclockwise. Offset 30 selects the driving dimensions: `1 = revolutions and height`, `2 = revolutions and pitch`, `3 = height and pitch`, and `4 = planar spiral by revolutions and radial pitch`. Offset 92 selects the section position: `1 = inside`, `2 = on center`, and `3 = outside`. Offset 107 selects the section shape: `1 = circle`, `2 = square`, `3 = external triangle`, and `4 = internal triangle`. Its first two references retain the placement construction. An axial form has five parameter references for `Diameter`, `SectionSize`, `TaperAngle`, `Revolutions`, and its extent parameter, followed by a counted selection group with exactly one member. A spiral has four parameter references for `Diameter`, `SectionSize`, `Revolutions`, and `Pitch`, followed by the same selection group. The selection group member is a persistently identified entity record carrying the same asset and context GUIDs as the placement identity. The result state inserts one body without replacing or updating any preceding body.
The compact new-body form has a 411-byte, 432-byte, or 442-byte scope frame. The 411-byte form is the seven-reference spiral form and carries a preceding history-state identity. The 432-byte form has a 78-byte trailer after the feature-family string; the 442-byte form has an 88-byte trailer. The 432- and 442-byte forms carry no preceding history-state identity.

The legacy eight-reference new-body form is a class-`393` scope paired with class `258` and has a 427-byte frame. Its second placement reference is a class-`395` frame paired with class `258` and has a 186-byte span. Relative to that carrier's primary indexed header, bytes 11 through 47 are zero, offset 48 is a marked reference with index zero, bytes 53 through 58 and 59 through 75 are zero, offset 76 is u32 `2`, bytes 80 through 83 are zero, and offset 84 is u32 `1`. A marked reference at offset 88 names the first placement reference and has six zero trailing bytes; bytes 99 through 100 are zero and offset 101 is u32 `1`. A second marked reference at offset 105 is nonzero and distinct from the selection, transform, and owning-scope record indices, with six zero trailing bytes. Bytes 116 through 119 are zero, offset 120 is u32 `4`, bytes 124 through 133 are zero, offset 134 is u32 `109`, offset 138 is a positive finite f64, and offset 146 is u32 `109`. Marked references at offsets 150 and 163 name the transform record plus two and plus one, respectively; their six-byte trailing fields are zero. Byte 174 is zero, and the marked reference at offset 175 names the owning Coil scope with six zero trailing bytes. The carrier has no matrix and represents the identity transform.

The modern eight-reference new-body form is a class-`353` scope paired with class `259` and has a 427-byte frame. Its second placement reference is a class-`450` carrier paired with class `259` and has a 315-byte span. Relative to that carrier's primary indexed header, bytes 11 through 49 are zero and sixteen row-major f64 matrix values begin at offset 50. Bytes 178 through 203 are zero, offset 204 is u32 `512`, bytes 208 through 211 are zero, and offset 212 is u32 `256`. A marked reference at offset 217 names the first placement reference and has six zero trailing bytes. Bytes 228 and 229 are zero, offset 230 is u32 `1`, and a marked reference at offset 234 names the transform record plus 25 and has six zero trailing bytes. Bytes 245 through 247 are zero, offset 248 is u64 `1024`, and offset 256 is u64 `0x7000000000000000`. Bytes 264 through 267 are zero, and offset 268 is a nonzero u64 whose most-significant byte is `0x70`; bytes 276 through 278 are zero. Marked references at offsets 279, 292, and 304 name the transform record plus two, the transform record plus one, and the owning Coil scope, respectively; their six-byte trailing fields are zero, with two zero bytes at offsets 290 through 291 and one zero byte at offset 303. The matrix is finite, orthonormal, right-handed, and has final row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`; its translation column is in centimetres and its columns zero and two are the radial direction and trajectory axis. This carrier supplies the explicit Coil placement when the first selection carrier is complete.

A nested persistent entity-selection identity has a 45-byte expanded form or a 29-byte compact form from its identity header to the following indexed header. Both forms store ten zero bytes at identity offsets 11 through 20. The compact form stores one u64 identity at offset 21. The expanded form stores the selected Sketch entity suffix at offset 29 and the selected Sketch curve's primary identity at offset 37; the following indexed record has an independent record index. When the u64 at offset 21 is nonzero in the expanded form, it is the selected curve's secondary identity and zero is the null value. Thus a SplitFace path member carries `(curve secondary, Sketch suffix, curve primary)` in the three u64 slots, while a generic entity member carries the pair at offsets 29 and 37. The asset and context UUIDs qualify every identity in the frame.

A 431-byte eight-reference compact Coil scope carries a persistent support selection in its first reference and a registered version-8 placement construction in its second reference. Both references belong to the scope's Design stream. The placement construction supplies the solved rigid frame when its inferred-x, inferred-z, z-flip, and axis-flipped fields are zero. Its explicit matrix or identity marker supplies the Coil frame.

In the complete eight-reference compact form with a 432- or 442-byte scope, the first placement reference is a nested support-selection frame. Its persistent selection identity carries the asset and context UUIDs and the ordered persistent identity pair; the eighth scope reference names the same selected entity. The persistent prefix stores zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, u8 `1` at offset 21, the nested record index at offset 22, zero bytes at offsets 26 through 31, u32 `1` at offset 32, and the asset UUID's UTF-16 code-unit count at offset 36. The modern eight-reference new-body form uses a 41-byte selection prefix: bytes 11 through 21 are zero, offset 22 is u8 `1`, offset 23 is the nested record index, bytes 27 through 32 are zero, offset 33 is u32 `1`, and offset 37 is the asset UUID's UTF-16 code-unit count. The context UUID follows the asset UUID. A face-recipe selection frame uses the same asset and context UUID prefix and carries one exact face construction recipe instead of the persistent identity pair. Its prefix stores zero bytes at offsets 11 through 22, u8 `1` at offset 23, the nested record index at offset 24, zero bytes at offsets 28 through 33, u8 `1` at offset 34, zero bytes at offsets 35 through 37, and the asset UUID's UTF-16 code-unit count at offset 38. The modern prefix is also used by the modern face-recipe form. In both prefixes the context UUID is followed by u32 `2` and four zero bytes. The second placement reference is a rigid frame carrier. Its marker at offset 55 is u8 `1`. The identity carrier is 213 bytes to its same-index paired header, stores zero bytes at offsets 56 through 64, stores u8 `1` at offset 65, and omits the matrix; it represents the identity transform. The explicit carrier is 341 bytes to its same-index paired header, stores zero bytes at offsets 56 through 64, stores u8 `0` at offset 65, and stores 16 row-major f64 values at offset 66. Both forms have a finite orthonormal right-handed basis and final row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. Matrix columns zero and two are the radial direction and trajectory axis. The translation column is in centimetres. The neutral origin converts that column to millimetres; the axis and radial vectors remain unit directions. A placement is explicit only when both carriers and their selection semantics satisfy these invariants; otherwise the placement remains a native Coil construction.

The 442-byte compact scope form also has a 233-byte owner-referenced identity carrier. It has the same identity marker block as the 213-byte carrier. Its bytes 213 through 221 are zero, offset 222 is a marked reference, the u32 at offset 223 equals the owning Coil scope record index, and bytes 227 through 232 are zero. It represents the identity transform. The owner reference is part of the carrier and must resolve to the containing scope before the placement is typed.

The ten-reference `CoilPrimitive` form has a 450-byte Boolean, a 572-byte matrix Boolean, or a 578-byte matrix new-body scope frame. All forms store eleven zero bytes at offsets 11 through 21, a u32 at offset 22, and u32 `1` at offset 26. The 450-byte form maps offset 22 values `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, and `3 = intersect`. The 572-byte form stores a finite 16-value f64 matrix at offset 77 for Boolean operations, and the 578-byte form stores the same matrix for new body. The 572-byte form maps the same three operation values; the 578-byte form maps offset 22 value `2` to new body. Each matrix has final row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. Marked references at offsets 30 and 41 repeat the fifth and ninth ordered scope references. The form fixes a circular section inside the trajectory and counterclockwise angular travel; it has no fixed extent selector. The owned parameter source kinds select the extent: `Diameter`, `SectionSize`, `TaperAngle`, `Revolutions`, and `Height` select revolutions-and-height; replacing `Height` with `Pitch` selects revolutions-and-pitch; replacing `Revolutions` with `Pitch` selects height-and-pitch; and the four kinds `Diameter`, `SectionSize`, `Revolutions`, and `Pitch` select the spiral. Its first ordered reference is a role-`0x0000000400000000` construction group with one body-recipe member. Boolean forms use that group as their target; the new-body form retains it as generated-body construction and does not use it as a target.

The 466-byte ten-reference `CoilPrimitive` form uses the compact discriminator lanes. Its [prologue](../layouts/f3d.md) stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, u32 `1` at offset 20, the left-hand Boolean at offset 25, the u32 operation at offset 26, and the u32 extent selector at offset 30 with the compact values. The operation values are `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, and `3 = intersect`. A marked reference at offset 34 names a member of the ordered reference table. In the unflagged form, a second marked reference at offset 45 names a member of the table, and bytes 56 and 57 are `1` and `0`. In the flagged form, bytes 45 and 46 are `0` and `1`, and the second marked reference starts at offset 47 and names a member of the table. Both forms continue at offset 58. Offsets 92 and 107 select the section position and the section shape with the compact values. Its ordered reference table holds one construction group with one member: role `0x0000000400000000` at scope-reference ordinal zero, or role `0x0000000800000000` at scope-reference ordinal eight. The Boolean operation uses that group as its target.

The 454-byte ten-reference `CoilPrimitive` form has the compact prologue with the second marked reference at offset 45. Its control bytes at offsets 56 and 57 are `1` and `1`. The u32 reference count at offset 228 is ten; the ten marked references start at offset 232. The u32 history-state identity is at offset 342. The u32 feature-kind length at offset 346 is thirteen, followed by the UTF-16LE kind text at offset 350 and a 78-byte scope trailer at offset 376. The first table member is a role-`0x0000000400000000` body-target group whose member is the second table reference. The third table reference is the persistent support selection; the fourth is a registered version-9 solved placement construction. Five parameter owners and the selected-entity group complete the table.

A `Combine` scope stores one of four primary prologues. All offsets are relative to the primary indexed header. The standard prologue stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, the Boolean operation u32 at offset 20, zero at byte 24, the keep-tools Boolean at offset 25, and seven zero bytes at offsets 26 through 32. The compact prologue has a 314-byte token-independent frame. Its compact prologue stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, the operation at offset 21, the keep-tools Boolean at offset 25, three zero bytes, `01 00`, u32 one at offset 31, and a marked nonzero same-segment u64 reference at offset 35 with a two-byte zero trailing field. The extended-reference prologue has a 363-byte frame. Its extended-reference prologue stores eighteen zero bytes at offsets 11 through 28, byte one at offset 29, the keep-tools Boolean at offset 30, the operation at offset 31, and a marked nonzero same-segment u64 reference at offset 35 with a two-byte zero trailing field. Operation values of these three prologues are `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, and `3 = intersect`.

The operand-list prologue has no class or frame-length requirement, because class tags are local to a stream and the frame length varies with the kind spelling and the list lengths. It stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19 and the property-block presence byte at offset 20. When the presence byte is one, an empty property block, u32 zero, follows it and moves every later field four bytes on. The offsets below apply to a prologue without a property block, with an empty companion list, and with an ordinary present local reference. The prologue stores the zero-based operation u32 at offset 21 with `0 = join`, `1 = cut`, and `2 = intersect`, the companion count u32 at offset 25 and that many companion references, the keep-tools Boolean at offset 29, the new-component Boolean at offset 30, u32 one at offset 31, a marked nonzero same-segment u64 reference at offset 35 with a two-byte zero trailing field, a u64 operation-identity value at offset 46, and the tool list at offset 54. Each list, the companion list included, is a u32 count followed by that many local references. An ordinary local reference consumes eleven bytes; an inline-typed local reference consumes 51 bytes. Each companion advances the later fields by its complete reference width. The tool list names the operation-identity record of each tool in reference-table order. Three counted lists follow it. The first is empty. The created-body list names the browser node of each body that the operation creates, and each of these nodes names the `Combine` scope as its creating scope. Without a new-component request, the operation result is the target body and one created body for each further lump, so a result of `n` lumps has `n - 1` created bodies. A new-component request puts every result lump in the new component as a created body, so its list has at least one entry, and the target body stays in its component. The consumed-body list names, in tool order, the browser node of each consumed tool body that lies in the owning component of the `Combine`. The owning component is the new component for a new-component request and the component of the target body otherwise. The consumed-body list is empty when the feature keeps its tools. The target list follows and names the one target operation-identity record. A counted GUID, three zero bytes, and the reference table complete the prologue. A prologue with a companion can store two lists between the tool list and the target list; both are empty. Byte 20 is the property-block presence byte in this prologue and the low byte of the operation in the standard prologue. A frame without an expanded named tail whose lists name its operands, whose counted GUID and three zero bytes end at its reference table, and whose fields satisfy these list rules stores the operand-list prologue, also when the standard prologue reads its fixed fields.

Each companion reference names an unlisted `RemoveBody` scope, type GUID `4A782808-FBDD-4351-A10A-F7AE5693D330`. The companion scope stores the counted GUID of the `Combine` scope and three zero bytes before its own reference table, and its body selections name the browser nodes of the consumed tools that lie outside the owning component. It removes those tool bodies as part of the `Combine` timeline item, so the keep-tools Boolean of a `Combine` with a companion is zero, and the consumed-body list names fewer entries than the tool list. Every consumed tool is in the consumed-body list or in a companion selection. A `Combine` whose new-component Boolean is one places its result in a new component.

The operand-list prologue's reference after u32 one can be null. The null-reference form shares the first 35 bytes of the operand-list prologue. The null-reference form stores a zero reference marker at offset 35, the u64 operation identity at offset 36, and the tool count at offset 44. A present local reference can carry an inline type GUID. The counted operand lists, the operation-identity records, body-selection nested references, and browser-node links also admit inline-typed local references. Each reference consumes its complete stored form before the next field. With the new-component Boolean zero, a two-middle-list form without a companion stores an empty list followed by one entry per consumed tool, or two empty lists when tools are kept. The tool and target lists name the operation-identity records in their source order.

A body-selection record of the operand-list form stores ten zero bytes after its indexed header, the u32 clause count at offset 21, and clauses of twelve bytes each from offset 25. A marked nested reference, u32 one, the asset and context GUIDs, u32 two, u32 zero, the occurrence list, and the body-node list follow. The body-node list has one entry, which names a browser node. A browser node stores ten zero bytes after its indexed header, the counted GUID at offset 21, the hidden flag, a byte of zero or one, a marked reference to the Design entity suffix of the body, and a marked reference to the feature scope that creates the body. The second reference ends the record. The transition into the current history state of the creating scope inserts exactly one body in the history that holds the `Combine` state. That body slot identifies the operand in the preceding history state of the `Combine`. A `Combine` in this form binds its target and tools through these slots. The target binds when its slot is in the preceding state. The tools bind when every tool slot is in the preceding state and the tool slots are distinct. A tool slot that equals the target slot leaves both selections native. An operand that its slots leave unbound binds through the body-recipe rules of the other prologues. When these rules name model bodies for the tools, those model bodies replace the tools that the slots bind, and the decoder reports `feature.combine-tool-recipe-replacement-assumed` (DR-921). A recipe binding that overlaps the other operand does not apply.

A tool of the operand-list form can be a body that another component builds in its own BREP history. The browser node of such a tool names a body entity suffix, and the Design body map stores one history-only pair for that suffix. The pair names the BREP blob and body selector of the tool. The creating scope of the browser node creates that body. The history that holds the `Combine` state does not contain the body, so the slot rule above does not apply, and a `Combine` scope without a preceding history-state identity cannot use it either. When the creating scope is a timeline feature that precedes the `Combine`, the tool is the generated body of that feature, identified by its body-map pair, and the `Combine` depends on that feature. The tools are a generated-body set only when every tool resolves this way and no two tools name the same pair. A tool that has no browser node, whose pair is absent, repeated or not history-only, or whose creating scope is not a preceding timeline feature does not bind through this rule.

The ordered reference table of a `Combine` scope has an even count of at least four. Each selected body occupies two consecutive references: an operation-identity record containing a marked reference to the following body-selection record, followed by that body-selection record containing two consecutive GUID strings and one bounded whole-body recipe. Exactly one operation-identity record uses the compact form with ten zero bytes, u32 one, and the marked selection reference after its indexed header; that pair selects the target body. Every other operation-identity record uses the expanded metadata form containing `DcFeatureOperationIdFlag` and `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64`; those pairs select the tools in source-table order. The neutral operation stores the target before the ordered tools independently of their serialized scope positions. When a `Combine` feature in the standard, class-387, or class-329 prologue keeps its tool bodies (`keep_tools = true`), its scope operation encodes `Join`, and no solid body is deleted across its history transition, the resolved operation is `Cut`. The operand-list prologue stores the applied operation, so the same state stays `Join`.

A tool body-selection record with primary index `N` can carry a cross-document body-selector path. Its indexed header is followed by fourteen zero bytes, a same-segment reference to `N+3`, u32 one, consecutive LP-UTF16 asset and context GUIDs, and u32 values `2`, `0`, and `1`. A nonzero same-segment occurrence reference and u32 one follow. The cross-document body reference is byte one, a nonzero u64 body reference, byte one, a u32 segment, an LP-UTF16 asset GUID equal to the selector asset GUID, byte zero, and a nonempty LP-UTF16 link name. Its optional-tail byte is zero for no tail. Value one adds an LP-UTF16 property GUID and a nonempty LP-UTF16 version URN. The selector tail is u32 `9`, u16 `2`, a u64 selection-payload stamp, a u32 evaluation epoch, a finite nonnegative f64 evaluation scalar, a same-segment reference to `N+2`, two zero bytes, a same-segment reference to `N+1`, one zero byte, and a same-segment reference to the owning scope. The same-index paired header starts immediately after the scope reference. The persistent external body identity contains the selector asset and context GUIDs, occurrence reference, external body reference and segment, external asset GUID, link name, and optional property and version strings. The stamp and scalar bit pattern are not external body identities. The epoch is evaluation state, not a fixed selector constant. A matching visible external envelope does not determine the stamp. A native-preserving writer retains the complete selector, including the exact stamp, epoch, and scalar bits; no general zero default or GUID-derived stamp rule is defined.

A legacy `Face` scope with type GUID `7AFA0A65-B53C-472C-ACA4-5C7C0A65001C`, version 3 or 4, and module `Fusion` is a sheet-metal Base Face operation. It constructs a base flange from selected sketch regions. The ordered source pair is a version-1 `Fusion` group of type `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841` followed by a version-0 `Fusion` sketch-profile member of type `4BD53E5A-0B3E-45E5-AE8B-02044306485A`. Source pairs retain their relative scope-reference order even when other members precede them.

The source-region identity carrier has type GUID `CAA55628-037B-4D01-9C74-26118F70B63E`, version 0, and module `Fusion`. The following scope reference is sheet-metal settings of type `E75C86D6-76D8-4F1F-BC16-AB8CB74958B0`, version 2 or 3, and module `Fusion`; it is not an identity object. Both records reference the owning scope. Their indexed headers bound the carrier frame. Dynamic class tags identify registrations within one stream and do not select source semantics.

The [source-region carrier prefix](../layouts/f3d.md) contains the indexed header, ten zero bytes, a marked owning-scope reference with six zero trailer bytes, and a nonzero u32 identity count. The ordered identity-reference run follows the prefix. Each entry is a marker byte `1`, a u32 record index, and six zero bytes. A u32 discriminator, a finite f64 scalar, and an equal repeated u32 discriminator follow the run. The remaining carrier suffix is opaque. Neither the discriminator nor the scalar has a decoded material-side or result-choice meaning.

Each identity reference names a version-1 `EntityTracking` record of type `C46D3EEB-40E1-43FA-83DC-9CB204335417` with the fixed persistent identity frame: ten zero bytes, a local identity u64, asset and context LP-UTF16 GUIDs, and the optional tail slot. Identity ordinal `i` corresponds to source-pair ordinal `i`. These identities name selected source regions, not result faces or Sketch curves. A source region retains its complete ordered profile program, including context and partition curves; a recipe curve need not become a result boundary. A material side and a body or component result require independent operation data or exact geometry; unresolved choices do not follow from the opaque carrier lane.

A `ContourFlange` scope uses type GUID `7AFA0A65-B53C-472C-ACA4-5C7C0A65001C`, version 3, 4 or 6. The stored scope kind distinguishes it from a planar `Face` scope of the same type GUID. Its prefix has the indexed header, nine zero bytes, an extension marker, a present marker and an operation u32. Extension zero has no payload; extension one has a zero u32. The present marker is one. A registered `E75C86D6-76D8-4F1F-BC16-AB8CB74958B0` settings reference precedes a registered `CAA55628-037B-4D01-9C74-26118F70B63E` source-region carrier reference. Both references occur in the ordered scope reference table. Immediately before the carrier reference are an unassigned u32 and a zero byte. Immediately after its complete compact or typed local reference is a positive finite f64 thickness copy in database centimetres. The profile program uses the ordered source-group/profile-member pairs and persistent region identities defined above.

The ContourFlange vector-owner lane contains three finite f64 components, a zero byte and a complete local parameter-owner reference. The vector has unit squared norm within floating-point precision. The owner names the `AlongDistance` parameter. Its signed evaluated distance is in database centimetres. The linked rule uses the common version-zero consumer-reference prefix or version-one direct entry payload, followed by expression/value entries. Its material trailer contains a finite scalar, a nonempty LP-UTF16 material name, the LP-UTF16 expression `Thickness` and a positive f64 thickness in database centimetres. The first expression/value entry and the material trailer retain separate values.

A form-three body-recipe reference with Design reference `r` and recipe selector `s` selects persistent tags whose Design references contain `r` and whose native selector is `s`. Active-BREP face identities use either the history-source-qualified namespace or the source-less default active-BREP namespace. A form-33 operand's complete persistent identity is its stream, asset and context GUIDs, ordered `(Design reference, form)` clauses, recipe Design id, and recipe selector. Repeated occurrences of that identity select the same stable history body when every resolved occurrence agrees. A tool resolves in the target history when every clause selects the same input-state body. Otherwise, target-history candidates are discarded and every clause must select the same model body. Displayed bodies supersede cache bodies when at least one displayed candidate exists. A complete homogeneous tool list transfers as an ordered historical or model-body selection set only when every native member resolves to a distinct body. An unresolved direct-tool family with one body-recipe reference per member has one stream, asset GUID, context GUID, Design-reference form, and recipe Design id. Its selectors are the integers one through the family member count exactly once. Every nonempty archived member candidate set is identical, contains exactly the family member count of input-state bodies, contains every individually resolved family member, and excludes the Combine target. Such a family supplies that complete unordered body set. Multiple exact or family sets must be disjoint, and their union cardinality must equal the native tool count. When a Combine has exactly one circular body-pattern dependency, that pattern has one resolved historical body seed, and the number of distinct stable output-body identities plus the seed equals the circular instance count, the seed and outputs form the complete pattern body set. If the resolved Combine target is a member and removing it leaves exactly as many distinct bodies as native tools, the remainder is the historical unordered tool set. These collective proofs do not assign individual native tool members to bodies. No clause or member arbitrates when a form-33 identity has no unique body proof: zero or multiple body candidates leave the native selection unresolved, and a writer rejects the selection instead of choosing a body.

A `Draft` scope whose prologue names both angle lanes stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, u32 three at offset 21, the anchor-kind u32 at offset 25, the flipped Boolean at offset 29, the tangent-chain Boolean at offset 30, the mode u32 at offset 31, a marked reference to the first angle lane at offset 35, and a marked reference to the second angle lane at offset 46. Anchor kind `1` defines the neutral-plane form, with mode `1` for a single angle, `2` for two angles, and `3` for a symmetric draft. In modes 2 and 3 the neutral plane splits each drafted face. The portion on the side into which the neutral-plane normal points drafts by the first angle relative to the pull direction. The other portion drafts relative to the reversed pull direction, by the second angle in mode 2 and by the first angle in mode 3. The flipped Boolean reverses the pull direction: the pull direction is the negated plane normal, and the signed angle stays relative to that direction. When the source states no pull direction, `outward` is relative to the plane normal and the flipped Boolean inverts it.

Draft anchor kinds `2` and `3` have a parting prefix. The two finite auxiliary f64 scalars start at offsets 57 and 65. A Boolean boundary flag is at offset 73 and a Boolean fixed-edge-reference-present marker is at offset 74. A present fixed-edge reference starts at its marker and occupies eleven bytes. The zero marker occupies one byte. The parting group suffix follows that optional reference. Relative to the suffix in the explicit-role form, the marked pull-group reference is at offset 0, the marked tool-group reference at offset 11, and the marked drafted-face-group reference at offset 26. Both forms store u32 one at offset 22. Each reference belongs to the scope's ordered reference table, and the group identities are distinct. The explicit pull group has role `0x0000002100000000`, the tool and fixed-edge groups have role `0x0000000800000000`, and the drafted-face group has role `0x0000001000000000`. Both signed angle lanes store independent values. A parting prefix carries the legacy operand layout when the scope has exactly two nonempty role-`0x0000002100000000` groups, the pull and tool references name those groups in either order, and the target types identify one work-plane pull and one face tool. This rule applies to both parting anchor kinds, every mode, both fixed-edge marker values, and all second-angle values. Other parting prefixes use the explicit-role form.

The `MetaStream` type table identifies Design Geometry origin entities. Type `19031004-3AB6-4D13-ABBF-C51EE214688D` lists axis entities and type `8D424E29-DE23-4B1F-A3AD-84C52A497D1A` lists plane entities. One origin stores six consecutive entity identities `a` through `a + 5`: `a`, `a + 1`, and `a + 2` are the X, Y, and Z axes, and `a + 3`, `a + 4`, and `a + 5` are the XY, XZ, and YZ planes. The value of `a` is local to the Design stream, and a stream stores one origin per component. A member of a complete run is an origin entity. A stream lists every origin when its complete runs equal in number the distinct entities registered to its component naming-space type. An identity is not an origin entity when the table lists it as another type, or when the stream has a complete run, the identity is in no complete run, and either the stream lists every origin or no partial run can hold the identity; an axis-type or plane-type identity in this state names a constructed entity. A partial run can hold an identity when one of its six positions is listed and no listed position contradicts the run. The table leaves an identity unclassified when the stream has no complete run, when a partial run can hold the identity in a stream that does not list every origin, or when its registrations disagree on its origin role. Historical resolution applies only to an identity that is not an origin entity, so a selection of an unclassified identity stays unresolved.

A plane entity record has type GUID `8D424E29-DE23-4B1F-A3AD-84C52A497D1A`, base-type GUID `1E5F6CE7-7544-4DE1-8C7B-6BACF6DC8E40`, version `1`, and module `Geometry`. A constructed plane entity stores the property-block presence byte at offset 20 and the property block that "When the property-block presence byte is `01`" gives ([constructed-plane entity prefix](../layouts/f3d.md#constructed_plane_entity_prefix)). The u32 plane kind, the lower display corner, `u8 0`, the f64 origin, the f64 unit u direction, the f64 unit v direction, the upper display corner, and an LP-UTF16 Design entity ID follow the property block ([constructed-plane entity body](../layouts/f3d.md#constructed_plane_entity_body)). The numeric suffix of the entity ID equals the entity identity. A non-null same-segment marked collection reference, a u32 ordinal, five zero bytes, a non-null same-segment marked `WorkPlane` scope reference, bytes `00 01`, and an LP-UTF16 display name follow the entity ID. A non-blank display name without control characters assigns the display name of the referenced `WorkPlane` feature. Conflicting display names targeting one `WorkPlane` scope invalidate the assignment.

A `Draft` neutral-plane member whose primary identity is an origin plane in that table selects it. Its pull direction is that plane's canonical normal, and any historical candidate for the same number describes unrelated ASM topology. A member whose primary identity is an origin axis or unclassified stays unresolved.

A `Draft` scope has a variable-length frame and six or more ordered references. The ordered reference table is in record-index order, so no role holds a fixed position in it: the two scalar lanes precede the operand groups in one document and follow them in another. Two references are fixed scalar records owned by the scope, at local ordinals zero and one, and those ordinals order them. The first scalar is the finite signed first angle in radians, including zero. The second scalar is the finite signed second angle in radians. In the neutral-plane form, it is zero in single-angle mode and equals the first scalar in mode 3. One counted construction-operand group with role `0x0000001000000000` selects the drafted faces. A neutral-plane draft has one counted construction-operand group with role `0x0000002100000000`; its face-recipe members select the neutral plane. A WorkPlane-neutral form has one role-`0x0000002100000000` group with one entity-selection member whose primary identity `p` names the WorkPlane scope at record index `p + 1`; the WorkPlane matrix's third column is the pull direction, and the WorkPlane feature is the pull-plane dependency. A parting-line draft with the legacy operand layout has exactly two role-`0x0000002100000000` groups. One group has exactly one entity-selection member naming the WorkPlane in the same way, and the other group has the face-recipe members that select the parting tool. Every group record and every group member is a reference of the owning scope. Face-recipe members resolve against the preceding history state. A bounded-face Draft member without `resolved_face_slots` is selected directly only when its structured counted program is complete, its historical-support and alternate-selector lanes are empty, and either its nonempty `candidate_faces` lane has no unreferenced candidate or its exact recipe-reference lanes have one unique largest face set after lanes with alternate selectors are excluded. If that direct admission does not resolve the member, a counted bounded-face member is resolved from the Draft transition. When alternate-selector candidates are present, exactly one such candidate must exist in both the preceding and result topologies and its actual surface geometry must change between them; surface-carrier record identity alone is not sufficient. When no alternate-selector candidate is present, the exact recipe-reference candidate lane must contain exactly one candidate and that face must exist in both topologies. Missing, ambiguous, unchanged, or unsupported surface geometry does not resolve the member. The group selection is the union of the selected lane. A member with `resolved_face_slots` uses those slots.

An entity-selection member in a neutral-plane group can carry a persistent topology identity instead of a WorkPlane reference. Its `historical_face_candidates` list gives the face incident to that identity in each named history state. When the group has one member and exactly one candidate face slot contains the scope's effective preceding history state, that slot is the neutral face selection. This form has no WorkPlane transform and no pull-plane dependency. No neutral face is selected when the state has no candidate or when candidates for that state name different face slots.

When that identity is a coedge, the neutral plane is resolved from its complete radial cycle. Every cycle member must name the same edge, belong to one loop, and map through one face relation to one incident face. The exact plane carriers among the incident faces must form exactly one coincident set. An open cycle, an ambiguous relation, a missing carrier, or non-coincident plane carriers leaves the neutral plane unresolved.

F3D stores no independent material-side bit for Draft. The pull direction is the signed-angle sign composed with the oriented neutral carrier: a face uses its surface normal adjusted by face sense, and a WorkPlane uses its transform's third column. The neutral `outward` value is true exactly when the signed angle is negative; a zero angle therefore has `outward=false`.

Draft scope frame layouts are keyed by the primary and paired class tags. Each `byte_offset` is the start of the primary 11-byte indexed header. The paired header starts at `byte_offset + frame_length` and is not part of the frame. A reference entry is `u8 1 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`; the table below gives the entry start and the value offset. `kind_offset` names the first UTF-16LE code unit, so its u32 code-unit count is four bytes earlier. The current and preceding history values are u32 state identities; `0xffffffff` is null. The six ordered references in the four primary generation forms below include the two scalar owners, one drafted-face group, and the neutral-plane or parting-tool groups according to the Draft form.

| Primary / paired class | Frame length | Relative offset/type/discriminant table | Anchor and variant |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `318 / 260` | 336 | `+171: u32 reference_count=6`; `+175 + 11i: reference entry`, `i=0..5`, value at `+176 + 11i`; `+241: u32 current_history_state`; `+245: u32 code_unit_count=5`; `+249: UTF-16LE Draft`; `+259: u32 feature_ordinal`; `+290: u32 previous_history_state`; `+336: paired header` | `byte_offset` anchors the compact form. There is no reserved u32 before the count. |
| `318 / 260` | 340 | `+171: u32 0`; `+175: u32 reference_count=6`; `+179 + 11i: reference entry`, `i=0..5`, value at `+180 + 11i`; `+245: u32 current_history_state`; `+249: u32 code_unit_count=5`; `+253: UTF-16LE Draft`; `+263: u32 feature_ordinal`; `+294: u32 previous_history_state`; `+340: paired header` | `byte_offset` anchors the shifted form. The reserved zero u32 shifts the reference table and every following field by four bytes. |
| `318 / 258` | 373 | `+171..+174: u32 0`; `+175: u32 reference_count=9`; `+179 + 11i: reference entry`, `i=0..8`, value at `+180 + 11i`; `+278: u32 current_history_state`; `+282: u32 code_unit_count=5`; `+286: UTF-16LE Draft`; `+296: u32 feature_ordinal`; `+327: u32 previous_history_state`; `+373: paired header` | The paired class and nine-reference count discriminate this legacy envelope from `318 / 260`. `byte_offset` remains the primary-header anchor. |
| `372 / 259` | 340 | `+171: u32 0`; `+175: u32 reference_count=6`; `+179 + 11i: reference entry`, `i=0..5`, value at `+180 + 11i`; `+245: u32 current_history_state`; `+249: u32 code_unit_count=5`; `+253: UTF-16LE Draft`; `+263: u32 feature_ordinal`; `+294: u32 previous_history_state`; `+340: paired header` | The paired class `259` discriminates this generation. `byte_offset` anchors the primary header, not the kind string. |
| `393 / 261` | 339 | `+171: u32 0`; `+175: u32 reference_count=6`; `+179 + 11i: reference entry`, `i=0..5`, value at `+180 + 11i`; `+245: u32 current_history_state`; `+249: u32 code_unit_count=5`; `+253: UTF-16LE Draft`; `+263: u32 feature_ordinal`; `+293: u32 previous_history_state`; `+339: paired header` | The 76-byte tail and paired class `261` discriminate this form. `byte_offset` anchors the primary header. |
| `448 / 263` | 340 | `+171: u32 0`; `+175: u32 reference_count=6`; `+179 + 11i: reference entry`, `i=0..5`, value at `+180 + 11i`; `+245: u32 current_history_state`; `+249: u32 code_unit_count=5`; `+253: UTF-16LE Draft`; `+263: u32 feature_ordinal`; `+294: u32 previous_history_state`; `+340: paired header` | The paired class `263` discriminates this generation. `byte_offset` anchors the primary header. |

The Draft scalar-owner generation mapping is one tuple. The owner column names the primary owner class and frame length; the parameter and companion columns name the primary parameter class and the companion indexed-header class. A row is selected by the scope primary/paired class pair and its frame length, not by a class tag in isolation. The owner tuple applies to the two scalar owners at local ordinals zero and one; other parameters in the same stream can use the separately specified 68- or 88-byte owner grammar.

| Scope primary / paired class | Draft scope frame lengths | Owner class / length | Parameter class | Companion class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `318 / 260` | 336, 340 | `291 / 103` | `358` | `296` |
| `372 / 259` | 340 | `335 / 103` | `317` | `268` |
| `393 / 261` | 339 | `319 / 103` | `341` | `364` |
| `448 / 263` | 340 | `317 / 103` | `320` | `268` |
| `414 / 258` | 361, 383 | `441 / 103` | `260` | `315` |
| `467 / 259` | 361 | `406 / 103` | `328` | `306` |
| `318 / 258` | 373 | `284 / 103` | `379` | `393` |
| `290 / 262` | 336, 340, 373, 395 | `336 / 103` | `348` | `278` |
| `367 / 261` | 336, 340, 351, 358, 362 | `325 / 103` | `378` | `321` |
| `346 / 262` | 336, 340 | `297 / 103` | `281` | `300` |
| `381 / 262` | 340 | `313 / 103` | `353` | `317` |
| `438 / 266` | 340, 351 | `282 / 103` | `323` | `290` |

`Hole` scopes own one point-and-direction carrier and the direct support-face selections that their records reference. A Hole whose point record names a reconstructed plane references two: the sole input of the point record, and the selection that the carrier input names. A Hole scope can also own a role-`0x0000002100000000` construction group with the standard counted members, trailing reference, and entity-tracking flag carrier. The point carrier has type GUID `F2A7590D-6654-4674-B393-A2AEF4FEC48A`, with type version `1`, `2`, or `4`; its dynamic class tag does not select the grammar. Relative to the point-data primary indexed header, the fixed prefix has an indexed header at offset `0`, eight zero bytes at offsets `11` through `18`, a leading-block presence byte at offset `19`, a property-block presence byte at offset `20`, and a bounding-box index at offset `21`. The position triple is at offset `25`, the model-space direction triple at offset `49`, the two construction parameters at offset `73`, and `refType` at offset `89`. Position and construction coordinates are centimetres; the direction is a finite unit vector and is not scaled. Version `1` stores the counted input-reference count at offset `93` and omits tangent-point data. Version `2` stores a tangent triple at offset `93` and the counted input-reference count at offset `117`. Version `4` stores a tangent-data prefix byte at offset `93`, a tangent triple at offset `94`, and the counted input-reference count at offset `118`. The count is positive and each reference is non-null with a target entity index representable as `u32`. A frame of each version permits a class-level tail after the counted reference run and ends at the next indexed header, which is its paired same-index header. The direction triple is the carrier normal.

The carrier `refType` states how the point-data records that the Hole scope references place the Hole. These records have type GUID `69EE2FA7-BCC7-449E-9CA9-976CEFDFED44`, and each stores `point3d` in centimetres and its own `refType`. Carrier `refType` `13` has a zero carrier position and one or more records with `refType` `10`. Each such record gives the entry point of one Hole, in scope-reference order. Its one input is a vertex-rule input. When that input is the direct sketch-point selection envelope of §3.1 "A vertex-rule input can instead use", the sketch point it names lies at the entry point. When every entry names one point and all the points belong to one planar Sketch, those points in entry order are the Hole's sketch profile, and points generate its holes. Carrier `refType` `19` places one Hole at the carrier position, and the `point3d` of each record equals that position, unless a `refType` `17` record names a reconstructed plane as stated below. Carrier `refType` `14` places one Hole at a point on a construction plane: the carrier position is zero, the carrier direction is the plane normal, and the Hole references one record with `refType` `12`, whose `point3d` is the entry point. A carrier with no point-data record, or a Hole with no direction control, defines no placement.

A point-data record with `refType` `17` can name a reconstructed plane. Its sole input is a direct support-face selection record of the Hole scope, with the type GUID and version of the direct support-face selection below. That selection owns the reconstructed plane record that has type GUID `8D424E29-DE23-4B1F-A3AD-84C52A497D1A` and type version `0`, at a record index after the selection and before the next direct support-face selection. At most one such record lies between them. The reconstructed plane record has one indexed header and no paired header. Relative to that header, it stores a zero u32 name length at offset `15`, a leading-block presence byte at offset `19`, a property-block presence byte at offset `20`, two f64 minimum extents at offset `21`, a zero byte at offset `37`, the plane origin at offset `38`, the unit in-plane u axis at offset `62`, the unit in-plane v axis at offset `86`, and two f64 maximum extents at offset `110`. Each of the three vectors is three f64 values; the origin is in centimetres. The plane normal is the cross product of the u axis and the v axis. A carrier with `refType` `19` and one such point record at a position that differs from the carrier position places one Hole at the position of the point record when that position lies on the plane and the carrier direction is parallel to the plane normal. The entry point of that Hole is the point-record position. The transition that drills such a Hole inserts a cylinder on the axis through the point-record position along the carrier direction.

The direct support-face selection has type GUID `5A1BF548-241F-46FD-9FB5-E4B05126EB9D` and type version `1`. Its compact persistent-selection prefix is forty bytes through the asset UUID code-unit count: ten zero bytes at offsets `11` through `20`, `u8 1` at offset `21`, nested record index at offset `22`, six zero bytes at offsets `26` through `31`, `u32 1` at offset `32`, and the asset UUID code-unit count at offset `36`. The asset and context values are LP-UTF16 identifiers; the context is followed by `u32 2` and four zero bytes. The selection envelope is followed by paired and nested indexed records with indices `N`, `N+1`, `N+2`, and `N+3`; the `N+3` identity record stores ten zero bytes and the primary persistent identity at identity-relative offset `21`, and the next indexed record is `N+4`. The selection belongs directly to the Hole scope and is not a construction-operand group member. When its identity has exactly one history-qualified face candidate, the support-face selection uses the Hole feature input topology. A candidate of the Hole's own history must name a face of the state before the Hole. A candidate of that history in another state leaves the selection native. A non-unique or missing candidate leaves the selection native.

The transition that drills a Hole states its support faces. Every cylinder on a face that the transition inserts lies on the axis of an entry point, and every entry point has such a cylinder. Each entry point lies on exactly one plane of a preceding face that the transition updates. That plane is normal to the axis, and the transition rows give that face an edge on a circle centred on the entry point along the axis. The Hole selects each such face in its input topology. A plane normal of either sign along the axis satisfies this, because historical topology stores no face sense. An entry point can instead lie on the cylinder of exactly one preceding face that the transition updates. The Hole axis is then a radial line of that cylinder: it is normal to the cylinder axis and passes through the entry point on the cylinder surface. That face shares an edge with an inserted face whose cylinder lies on the axis of the entry point. The Hole selects that face in its input topology. A transition that does not satisfy these conditions states no support face. A Hole has no support face when every face of the state before it has one carrier, that carrier is one plane or one cylinder, and no entry point lies on it.

`SpherePrimitive` and `TorusPrimitive` scopes store the result-operation u32 at primary-header offset 25 with the same `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, `3 = intersect`, and `4 = new body` values, followed by byte `0x01` at offset 29. The marked inline sphere form is 462 bytes to its paired same-index header. Marked references begin at offsets 30, 41, and 52 for the placement, diameter, and result records; its row-major rigid placement matrix begins at offset 64. A torus scope is 486 bytes. Marked references begin at offsets 30, 41, 52, and 63 for the major diameter, placement, minor diameter, and result records; its matrix begins at offset 75. Matrix column 2 is the primitive axis and column 3 is its centre in centimetres. Each diameter reference names a 104-byte same-index paired scalar frame whose positive finite f64 at primary-record offset 40 is a diameter in centimetres. Sphere radius is half its diameter. Torus major radius and tube radius are half the major and minor diameters respectively.

The reference-placed `SpherePrimitive` forms store three prefix references in placement, diameter-owner, and result order. These targets are the last three members of the ordered scope reference table. The compact prefix has operation offset 25, marker offset 29, and eleven-byte marked references at offsets 30, 41, and 52. The shifted prefix has operation offset 21, marker offset 25, and eleven-byte marked references at offsets 26, 37, and 48. The typed prefix has operation offset 21, marker offset 25, and 51-byte typed references at offsets 26, 77, and 128. Their type GUIDs are `7B6C3C2D-4096-4E6D-B225-699E8C2D9355`, `D91D429C-1BB5-4640-B49F-69AF14F463E9`, and `B556C40D-B680-4BD8-9623-028CD43307EC`. The operation values are `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, `3 = intersect`, and `4 = new body`. Each marker is byte `0x01`.

The scope-local frame follows the third prefix reference. The unmarked local frame stores sixteen row-major f64 values at offset zero relative to that position. The marked local frame starts with a one-byte identity flag. Flag `0` stores the same matrix at relative offset one; flag `1` supplies identity. Each matrix is a finite rigid transform. A valid unmarked matrix and a valid marked matrix select their corresponding framing. The solved sphere frame is the referenced placement frame composed on the left of this scope-local frame. Matrix column 3 gives the centre in centimetres.

The diameter owner has local ordinal zero and retains its evaluated diameter in centimetres. Its parameter source can hold an expression. The referenced placement construction supplies the support frame through its explicit matrix or identity marker. The sphere radius is half the evaluated diameter. A sphere is invariant under rotation of its placement axes.

`BoxPrimitive` and the named `CylinderPrimitive` form use the named parameter-scope prologue. Bytes 11 through 19 are zero, the result-operation u32 is at primary-header offset 20 with values `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, `3 = intersect`, and `4 = new body`, byte 24 is zero, and byte 25 is `0x01`. Box scopes whose reference count is at offset 335, 339, 343, or 655 use the framed prefix layouts below. The ordered parameter owners are joined to the scope by native stream, scope record index, reference membership, and local ordinal. A box has five owners in ordinal order: `DistanceX`, `DistanceY`, `DistanceZ`, `OffsetDistanceX`, and `OffsetDistanceY`; the first three are positive lengths in centimetres and the last two are signed translations along the source x and y axes. A cylinder has two owners in ordinal order: `Height` and `Diameter`; both are positive centimetre lengths and the result is a full-turn cylinder. The box and named-cylinder result operation is the value at offset 20. A named cylinder references a version-8, version-9, or version-16 placement construction in the same Design stream. Exactly one referenced registered placement record supplies its solved frame. Its solved frame is a proper rigid transform with zero inferred-x, inferred-z, z-flip, and axis-flipped fields. Matrix column 3 is the cylinder origin in centimetres; column 2 is its positive axis and column 0 is its radial x direction. The local cylinder extends from zero to `Height` along its positive z-axis. The explicit matrix or an identity marker supplies the solved frame.

The extended `CylinderPrimitive` forms use the same four ordered prefix references as the shifted form. The fourth reference names the support placement. The [prefixed Cylinder header](../layouts/f3d.md#prefixed_cylinder_header) has nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, u32 `1` at offset 20, zero at offset 24, and `0x01` at offset 25. It shifts the result operation and each subsequent prefix field by four bytes.

The [counted Cylinder reference](../layouts/f3d.md#counted_cylinder_reference) is 15 bytes. The count is u32 `1`, followed by one marked reference. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID and three zero bytes precede the ordered scope reference table. The frame layouts give the following offsets relative to the primary indexed header.

| Frame length | Ordered references | Operation | Matrix | Counted reference | GUID | Ordered reference count |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 356 | 5 | 26 | | 76 | 99 | 178 |
| 479 | 5 | 22 | 72 | 200 | 223 | 302 |
| 501 or 502 | 7 | 22 | 72 | 200 | 223 | 302 |
| 506 | 7 | 26 | 76 | 212 | 227 | 306 |
| 507 | 7 | 22 | 72 | 212 | 227 | 306 |

The 356-byte form stores the compact tail marker `0x01` at offset 75. The 479-, 501-, and 502-byte forms in the table store eight zero bytes between the counted reference and the GUID. In the 506-byte form, eight zero bytes follow the matrix. In the 507-byte form, twelve zero bytes follow it. At offset 200, the counted 502-byte form stores u32 `1` and the shifted 502-byte form stores eight zero bytes.

The [typed Cylinder prefix](../layouts/f3d.md#typed_cylinder_prefix) has a byte `0x01` after the shifted operation. Four 51-byte typed references follow in reverse order of the last four ordered references. A zero byte precedes the rigid matrix. The matrix is followed by u32 `1`, a typed reference, eight zero bytes, a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID, and three zero bytes. The ordered reference count is `5`. The first ordered reference has type GUID `5A1BF548-241F-46FD-9FB5-E4B05126EB9D`. The remaining types are `7B6C3C2D-4096-4E6D-B225-699E8C2D9355`, two `D91D429C-1BB5-4640-B49F-69AF14F463E9` entries, and `92112554-B316-46D1-8AFD-C49D91252558`. The reference after the matrix has type GUID `D26351F0-5940-4D23-AA20-2C35475A6D9E`.

The extended form's support construction supplies its solved frame. The expanded and typed forms store a matrix relative to that frame. The fourth column of the composed frame is the base centre. The signed `Height` extends from the base along local z. `Diameter` remains positive. Both dimensions are in centimetres.

The shifted `CylinderPrimitive` form is keyed by its primary and paired class tags and its frame length:

| Primary class | Paired class | Frame length |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `297` | `258` | `352` or `502` |
| `375` | `258` | `352` or `502` |
| `414` | `272` | `502` |

Its bytes 11 through 20 are zero, byte 21 is `0x01`, the result-operation u32 is at offset 22, and bytes 23 through 25 are zero. The first reference at offset 26 is `0x01`, `0x01`, a u32 target, and five zero bytes. Ordinary eleven-byte marked references begin at offsets 38, 49, and 60; these four targets are the last four ordered scope references in reverse order. The 352-byte form stores byte `0x01` at offset 71, u32 `1` at offset 72, one marked reference at offset 76, eight zero bytes at offsets 87 through 94, and a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID at offset 95. Its generic scope reference table begins at offset 174. The 502-byte form stores a row-major rigid 4x4 f64 frame at offset 72, eight zero bytes at offsets 200 through 207, a 15-byte construction-reference block at offset 208 (`0x01`, u32 `0x01000000`, the first ordered scope reference as u32, and six zero bytes), and a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID at offset 223; bytes 299 through 301 are zero and its generic scope reference table begins at offset 302. At offsets 174 and 302 respectively, the generic suffix stores the reference count, the ordered eleven-byte reference run, the current history state, the 17-code-unit `CylinderPrimitive` kind, the feature ordinal, and the previous history state at offsets 306 and 456 respectively. The shifted result operation uses the same four values as the named form. A cylinder frame represents a zero-origin cylinder along the positive source z-axis; its rigid frame preserves that geometry when translation is zero and its third column is the positive z-axis. The 502-byte frame is retained in the native primitive record and is the projected primitive's placement, with its translation converted to millimetres. The named form carries its placement through its referenced construction record. The 352-byte form retains its placement construction references.

The marked-reference `BoxPrimitive` form has an eight-member or ten-member ordered reference table. Its prefix layout is [marked_reference_box_prefix](../layouts/f3d.md#marked_reference_box_prefix). Bytes 11 through 20 are zero, byte 21 is `0x01`, the result-operation u32 is at offset 22 with the four values of the named form, and byte 26 is `0x01`. Seven eleven-byte marked references start at offset 27. They name the last, sixth-last, fifth-last, fourth-last, seventh-last, third-last, and second-last table members, in that order. The last member names the result. The five parameter owners occupy the sixth-last through second-last members. The seventh-last member names the placement. Byte 104 is zero. The row-major rigid right-handed 4x4 f64 matrix at offset 105 maps local box coordinates into the support-placement frame in centimetres. Columns 0, 1, and 2 are the box x, y, and z axes; column 3 is the box origin in that frame. With zero planar offsets, the local-to-model frame is the support-placement matrix multiplied on the left of this box-local matrix. The support-placement reference joins the registered placement construction in the same Design stream. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 null GUID begins at offset 256, followed by three zero bytes at offset 332 and the reference count at offset 335. The ordered eleven-byte marked reference run starts at offset 339.
