The prefixed marked-reference `BoxPrimitive` forms store nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, u32 `1` at offset 20, zero at offset 24, and `0x01` at offset 25. Their result-operation u32 is at offset 26, followed by `0x01` at offset 30 and seven eleven-byte marked references at offset 31. Byte 108 is zero and the box-local rigid matrix starts at offset 109. The ordinary prefixed form has a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 null GUID at offset 260, three zero bytes at offset 336, and the reference count at offset 339. The extended prefixed form has that GUID at offset 264, three zero bytes at offset 340, and the reference count at offset 343. The ordered reference run follows the count. Both forms use the marked-reference box reference roles and support-frame composition. Their layouts are [prefixed_marked_reference_box_prefix](../layouts/f3d.md#prefixed_marked_reference_box_prefix) and [extended_prefixed_marked_reference_box_prefix](../layouts/f3d.md#extended_prefixed_marked_reference_box_prefix).

The typed-reference `BoxPrimitive` form has a frame length of 1295 bytes and eight ordered scope references stored as 51-byte typed local references. Its bytes 11 through 20 are zero, byte 21 is `0x01`, the result-operation u32 is at offset 22 with the four values of the named form, and byte 26 is `0x01`. Seven typed local references begin at offsets 27, 78, 129, 180, 231, 282, and 333. Their targets are the eighth, third, fourth, fifth, second, sixth, and seventh ordered scope references, and each carries the type GUID of the scope reference-table entry with the same target. Byte 384 is zero. A row-major rigid right-handed 4x4 f64 frame starts at offset 385. Frame columns 0, 1, and 2 are the box x, y, and z axes, and column 3 is the box origin in centimetres. The box is the set of points of the origin plus `a` times the first length along the x axis, `b` times the second length along the y axis, and `c` times the third length along the z axis, for `a`, `b`, and `c` in the closed unit interval. The u32 `1` at offset 513 precedes one typed local reference at offset 517. Eight zero bytes at offsets 568 through 575 precede a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 null GUID at offset 576. Bytes 652 through 654 are zero and the generic scope reference table begins at offset 655. The ordered scope references are the support-face selection with type GUID `5A1BF548-241F-46FD-9FB5-E4B05126EB9D`, the placement construction with type GUID `7B6C3C2D-4096-4E6D-B225-699E8C2D9355`, the five box parameter owners with type GUID `D91D429C-1BB5-4640-B49F-69AF14F463E9`, and the result record with type GUID `CAA90BED-408E-4F03-A4E5-B1552D95C8EE`. The five owners are the `DistanceX` through `OffsetDistanceY` owners of the named form, joined by local ordinal. The generic suffix stores the reference count at offset 655, the ordered 51-byte typed reference run at offset 659, the current history state at offset 1067, the 12-code-unit `BoxPrimitive` kind at offset 1071, the feature ordinal at offset 1099, and the previous history state at offset 1169. The result operation is the value at offset 22. When both offset owners are zero, the placement-construction frame composes on the left of the stored box-local frame. The resulting translation uses centimetres. The composed frame's origin is the box corner at the minimum of each local axis.

A `Base Feature` scope records a result-body snapshot whose construction carries no parameter-history records; a closed direct-modeling session and an imported body both produce one. For `N > 0` result bodies, bytes 11 through 18 are zero, byte 19 is `0x01`, and offset 20 stores u32 `2N`. Two parallel runs start at offset 24: `N` marked u64 Design body entity suffixes followed by `N` marked u64 passive body-reference record indices; every value has a six-byte trailing field. The ordinary form then stores a marked null reference, u32 `N`, and either the passive references or the body entity suffixes repeated as marked u32 values with six-byte trailing fields. The marked null reference is `u8 1`, a zero u64, a flag byte of `0` or `1`, and a terminal byte. One zero byte and one marked u64 shared metadata-record index with a six-byte or two-byte trailing field follow, then u32 `N` and `N` marked u32 result-record indices with six-byte trailing fields. The class-384 form paired with class 264 instead stores `0x01`, six zero bytes, and u32 `N` in one eleven-byte field before the repeated passive-reference run; its shared metadata-record index has a two-byte trailing field. The class-420 form paired with class 258 stores `0x01`, five zero bytes, `0x01`, and u32 `N` in the eleven-byte count field. Its repeated u32 run contains the body entity suffixes instead of the passive references, and its shared metadata-record index has a two-byte trailing field. The class-452 form paired with class 266 uses the same compact count field, body-suffix repeat run, two-byte metadata field, and result-body ordering. The three body runs are parallel and preserve result-body order. The body entity suffixes join through the active Design BREP body map to solved bodies. The suffix result-body form with one body stores eight zero bytes at offsets 11 through 18, `u8 1` at offset 19, and u32 `1` at offset 20, and has no passive-reference run. Its marked u64 body entity suffix at offset 24 is an ordinary local 15-byte body-entity element, followed by the marked null reference at offset 39 and u32 `1` at offset 50. The body entity suffix repeats as a marked u32 value at offset 54. One zero byte at offset 65 precedes the marked u64 shared metadata-record index at offset 66, and u32 `1` at offset 81 precedes the marked u32 result-record index at offset 85. Each value has a six-byte trailing field. Offsets 96 through 103 are zero, and the LP-UTF16 scope kind payload begins at offset 206. The zero-body form omits the counted body runs and retains only its shared metadata reference. In the ordinary `N > 0` form the LP-UTF16 scope kind payload begins at offset `169 + 52N` after a six-byte metadata field and at offset `165 + 52N` after a two-byte one, and either fixed scope tail length follows the kind. The class-384 form paired with class 264, the class-420 form paired with class 258, and the class-452 form paired with class 266 have frame length `262 + 52N` bytes. The zero-body frame length is 267 bytes. The class-314 primary paired with class-259 stores a body-snapshot form. At offsets 11 through 18 it stores eight zero bytes, then `u8 1` at offset 19 and u32 `N` at offset 20. Each body entry at offset `24 + 15i` is `u8 1 + u64 body entity suffix + six-byte field`. The body run is followed by either the eight-byte sequence `01 00 00 00 01 00 00 00` or the nine-byte sequence `01 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00`, then two consecutive LP-UTF16 GUIDs of 36 code units. Let `A = 184 + 15N`, the linkage-tail anchor. In the eight-byte form, the first GUID starts at `32 + 15N` and the second ends immediately before `A`; in the nine-byte form, the first GUID starts at `33 + 15N` and its second GUID ends at `A + 1`, with its final zero byte shared by the linkage tail at `A`. The linkage tail at `A` stores two zero bytes, `01 01 00 00 00`, a marked first-body suffix at offsets `A + 7` and `A + 8`, three zero bytes, a marked linkage record at `A + 19` and `A + 20`, six zero bytes, u32 `1` at `A + 34`, a marked auxiliary record at `A + 38` and `A + 39`, six zero bytes, and four zero bytes. A third 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID starts at `A + 57`. Let `T = A + 133`. The generic scope suffix stores three zero bytes, the one-member reference table at `T + 3`, the current history-state identity at `T + 18`, and the LP-UTF16 scope kind at `T + 22`; the reference value is at `T + 8`, and the kind payload begins at `T + 26`. This form has no preceding history-state identity. If the kind has `L` UTF-16 code units, its frame length is `431 + 15N + 2L` bytes; the English `Base Feature` form has `L = 12` and therefore length `455 + 15N`. The three GUIDs and the linkage and auxiliary records are retained in the native construction record. A legacy result-body Base Feature uses current and previous ASM state identities to name the transition that installs its result bodies: the preceding identity is the state before the capture and the current identity is the state holding the captured bodies. A legacy Base Feature that installs at least one body carries two distinct identities, and the delta state named by the current identity holds the insert changes for the captured entities. The captured construction is not exposed as parametric steps, so no scope names a state between the two.

The ordinary result-body envelope is selected by its count field, parallel reference runs, and scope-kind position. Its stream-local class pair can also occur on a compact envelope in another Design stream.

In a result-body envelope, the passive body-reference run names Body presentation owners of type `D3937028-C20C-4E65-B010-94AD418A5C20`. Their `BASEFEAT_PM_BODY_REF` property has type `PassiveRefMetaType` and names the corresponding Design body entity suffix. The result-record run names body browser nodes of type `D26351F0-5940-4D23-AA20-2C35475A6D9E`; each node names the same body entity suffix. The shared metadata record has type `493A89BA-E146-498D-9033-2783FE727AF4` and links the scope to its Body presentation. These parallel references describe one stored result set.

A Base Feature result uses its current ASM state's records and transform, with subtype ordinals from the complete stream. Later changes to the body slot retain the earlier geometry and topology in the record archive.

A Base Feature scope whose stored bodies match no body of the final model stores the bodies its history state inserts, one for each stored body entity suffix. The stored bodies of such a scope are the bodies of that state alone.

A Split Body feature that selects its target bodies in its input state names state-local body slots of the preceding history state. A selected slot that a later state deletes or revises holds that body only in the preceding state. That body is the complete reference-closed body its slot has in the preceding state's record table.

A Split Body feature whose target is one body-recipe operand names its target body by the recipe Design id and selector. The target is the body slot of the input state whose body generic-tag group of entity kind `3` stores that Design id and a Design reference equal to the selector. The input state is the state that the Split state's transition names as its predecessor. A body slot that carries the group is the target only when no other body slot of the input state carries an equal pair and the Split transition updates or deletes the slot.

A solid cut `Extrude` that changes the sole body of its preceding ASM state and retains its slot in the same BREP history cuts that body. The preceding state's records and transform give the body before the cut. Subtype ordinals come from the complete BREP stream.

The ordered body entity suffixes define the stored result-body set. A body reference retains its role in the result set when its target is unresolved. This set defines the Base Feature results independently of the historical affected-body set. Each suffix belongs to the Design stream that contains the scope and joins that stream's active BREP body map. A zero body count defines an empty result set. It does not select all bodies in the stream. The current and previous ASM identities define the result transition independently of the specialized scope payload. Each body entity reference in the transition belongs to the BREP blob that contains the history. Equal entity references in different BREP blobs have separate identities. A unique transition identifies the bodies that it changes; a body-map entry identifies the active solved body in its BREP namespace.

In the ordinary local 15-byte Base Feature body-entity and passive-reference elements, the six-byte trailing field is `cross_document:u8 0`, `different_segment:u8 0`, and `member:u32`. The first two bytes complete the general same-segment reference. The member belongs to the enclosing element and is retained per element; two elements in one scope can have different members. An envelope member follows the complete reference in a member-bearing form. Cross-segment, cross-document, and inline-typed references use the general variable-width reference grammar before that member.

The class-290 primary paired with class-261 has a legacy compact result-body envelope. For `N > 0` it uses the count field `u8 1`, six zero bytes, `u32 N`, a passive-reference repeat run, and a two-byte shared-metadata field; its frame length is `261 + 52N`. The class-360 primary paired with class-258 has the expanded result-body envelope. For `N > 0` it uses the expanded count and passive-reference repeat form; its frame length is `262 + 52N`. The class-409 primary paired with class-262 has the same expanded result-body envelope. Its zero-body frame is 258 bytes. The class-444 primary paired with class-263 has a passive compact result-body envelope. For `N > 0` it uses a passive-reference repeat run and the count field `u8 1`, five zero bytes, `u8 0`, and u32 `N`; its frame length is `262 + 52N`.

The class-365 primary paired with class-262 and the class-377 primary paired with class-259 use the same direct body-reference envelope. Its frame length is 363 bytes. Relative to the primary indexed header, bytes 11 through 18 are zero, byte 19 is `u8 1`, and offset 20 stores u32 `2`. Marked 15-byte elements at offsets 24 and 39 carry the PM body-reference record and the Design body entity suffix respectively; each element has a u32 value followed by ten zero bytes. The property block at offset 54 has one entry named `TagBodyBasedOnFaces` with type `IntrinsicMetaTypebool` and u16 value `1`. The parameter-reference group at offset 109 has count `1` and repeats the PM body-reference record at offset 115; seven bytes after that member are zero. The scope-reference member at offset 126 repeats the generic scope reference and has six zero trailing bytes. The auxiliary group starts at offset 137 with three zero bytes, then a marked auxiliary record at offset 141 and fourteen zero trailing bytes. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 envelope GUID starts at offset 160, followed by three zero bytes at offsets 236 through 238. The generic scope suffix starts with u32 `1` at offset 239, a marked copy of the scope reference at offset 243, six zero bytes, the current history-state identity at offset 254, the 12-code-unit `Base Feature` kind at offset 258, and the feature ordinal after its payload. The previous history-state identity follows the post-ordinal scope tail at offset 317. The body suffix at offset 40 joins through the active Design body map and is the body exposed by the neutral Base Feature definition. The PM record, auxiliary record, envelope GUID, and stored property are retained in the native construction record for both class pairs.

The class-452 primary paired with class-262 has two legacy body-reference envelope forms. The compact one-body form is 348 bytes. Bytes 11 through 18 are zero, byte 19 is `u8 1`, and offset 20 stores u32 `1`. A marked 15-byte body entity element at offset 24 carries one u64 Design body entity suffix and a six-byte source field. The property block at offset 39 has one `TagBodyBasedOnFaces` entry with type `IntrinsicMetaTypebool` and u16 value `1`. The compact lane stores a mode byte at offset 94 with value `0` or `1`, a u8 count `1` at offset 95, three zero bytes, a marked u64 PM body-reference record at offset 99, and three zero bytes. A marked u64 copy of the scope reference starts at offset 111 and has two zero bytes. The auxiliary group starts at offset 122 with a marker and three zero bytes, then a marked u64 DM body-reference record at offset 126 with ten zero bytes. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 envelope GUID starts at offset 145; three zero bytes at offsets 221 through 223 precede the generic scope suffix. Its reference count is at offset 224, its marked u32 scope reference at offset 228, the current history-state identity at offset 239, the `Base Feature` kind at offset 247, the feature ordinal at offset 271, and the previous history-state identity at offset 302. The paired class-262 header starts at offset 348. The body entity source field is retained with the suffix.

The expanded two-body form is 395 bytes. It has the same zero run, marker, and body count prefix, with u32 `2` at offset 20. Marked 15-byte body entity elements at offsets 24 and 39 carry the two ordered u64 body entity suffixes and six-byte source fields. Its property block starts at offset 54. A marked counted PM group starts at offset 109 with u32 count `2`; its eleven-byte members start at offsets 114 and 125 and contain marked u32 record identities with six zero bytes each. A zero separator is at offset 136. The marked explicit scope-reference member starts at offset 137 and carries a u32 record identity followed by six zero bytes. The counted DM group has u32 count `2` at offset 148; its eleven-byte members start at offsets 152 and 163. Eight zero bytes at offsets 174 through 181 precede a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 envelope GUID at offset 186. Three zero bytes at offsets 258 through 260 precede the generic scope suffix: its reference count is at offset 261, its marked scope reference at offset 265, the current history-state identity at offset 276, the `Base Feature` kind at offset 284, the feature ordinal at offset 308, and the previous history-state identity at offset 349. The paired class-262 header starts at offset 395. The body entity suffixes join through the active Design body map and are the bodies exposed by the neutral Base Feature definition. The body entity source fields, PM and DM record identities, explicit scope reference, mode when present, envelope GUID, and stored property are retained in the native construction record; the compact and expanded reference widths are selected by the envelope form.

The class-keyed result-body envelopes are:

| Primary class | Paired class | Count field after the two 15-byte runs | Repeated values | Metadata field | Frame length |
| ---: | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `290` | `261` | `u8 1`, six zero bytes, u32 `N` | passive-reference records | 2 bytes | `261 + 52N` |
| `360` | `258` | `u8 1`, six zero bytes, u32 `N` | passive-reference records | 2 bytes | `262 + 52N` |
| `384` | `264` | `u8 1`, six zero bytes, u32 `N` | passive-reference records | 2 bytes | `262 + 52N` |
| `409` | `262` | `u8 1`, six zero bytes, u32 `N` | passive-reference records | 2 bytes | `262 + 52N` |
| `444` | `263` | `u8 1`, five zero bytes, `u8 0`, u32 `N` | passive-reference records | 2 bytes | `262 + 52N` |
| `420` | `258` | `u8 1`, five zero bytes, `u8 1`, u32 `N` | body entity suffixes | 2 bytes | `262 + 52N` |
| `452` | `266` | `u8 1`, five zero bytes, `u8 1`, u32 `N` | body entity suffixes | 2 bytes | `262 + 52N` |
| other class pairs | — | the marked null reference, u32 `N` | passive-reference records or body entity suffixes | 6 or 2 bytes | kind payload at `169 + 52N` or `165 + 52N` |

Under a class pair without its own row, the count field selects the envelope. The count field `u8 1`, six zero bytes, u32 `N` selects the class-360/class-258 envelope, and `u8 1`, five zero bytes, `u8 1`, u32 `N` selects the class-420/class-258 envelope. The marked null reference, followed by u32 `N`, selects the last row (the decoder requires a zero terminal byte; DR-483): a 6-byte metadata field places the kind payload at `169 + 52N`, and a 2-byte metadata field places it at `165 + 52N`.

For the class-360/class-258, class-384/class-264, and class-409/class-262 rows, let `C = 24 + 30N`, the offset immediately after the two parallel runs. The discriminant layout is:

| Primary/paired class | Relative offset | Type | Value |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `360`/`258`, `384`/`264`, `409`/`262` | `C` | u8 | `1` |
| `360`/`258`, `384`/`264`, `409`/`262` | `C + 1 .. C + 7` | bytes[6] | zero |
| `360`/`258`, `384`/`264`, `409`/`262` | `C + 7` | u32 | `N` |
| `360`/`258`, `384`/`264`, `409`/`262` | `C + 11 + 11i` | `u8 1 + u32 passive-reference record + bytes[6]` | `0 <= i < N` |

For the class-444/class-263 row, let `C = 24 + 30N`, the offset immediately after the two parallel runs. Its discriminant layout is:

| Primary/paired class | Relative offset | Type | Value |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `444`/`263` | `C` | u8 | `1` |
| `444`/`263` | `C + 1 .. C + 6` | bytes[5] | zero |
| `444`/`263` | `C + 6` | u8 | `0` |
| `444`/`263` | `C + 7` | u32 | `N` |
| `444`/`263` | `C + 11 + 11i` | `u8 1 + u32 passive-reference record + bytes[6]` | `0 <= i < N` |

The class-409 zero-body form has, relative to its primary indexed header, offsets 11 through 19 zero, offset 20 `u8 1`, offsets 21 through 31 zero, offset 32 the shared-metadata marker, offset 33 its u64 record index, offset 41 the six-byte field, and offsets 47 through 54 zero before the first GUID. The metadata record is the sole retained reference in that form. A 258-byte `Base Feature` frame with this prefix is a zero-body frame under any pair of stream-local class tags. A 257-byte `Base Feature` frame with this prefix and its kind payload at offset 157 is also a zero-body frame under any pair of stream-local class tags. Its scope tail after the 12-code-unit kind is 76 bytes: the marked reference at offset 200 has six zero bytes after its u32 value, and the previous history-state identity is at offset 211. The 258-byte form has seven zero bytes after that value and its previous identity at offset 212. In the 262-byte zero-body form, offsets 11 through 19 are zero, offset 20 stores `u8 1`, offsets 21 through 35 are zero, offset 36 stores the shared-metadata marker, offset 37 its u64 record index, offset 45 the six-byte field, offsets 51 through 58 are zero, and u32 `36` at offset 59 counts the code units of the first GUID. The metadata record is its sole retained reference. The layout is `base_feature_wide_zero_body` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). A shifted wide zero-body form stores the same prefix through offset 50, twelve zero bytes at offsets 51 through 62, u32 `36` at offset 63 counts the code units of the first GUID, and the GUID follows at offset 67. Three zero bytes follow the GUID, u32 `1` at offset 142 counts the single scope reference, the marked reference at offset 146 repeats the shared metadata record with six zero bytes, the current history-state u32 at offset 157 names the committed state, and u32 kind length at offset 161 precedes the LP-UTF16 kind with the feature ordinal after its payload. The frame carries no body runs; its length follows the kind spelling, and the paired header begins at the frame end. The layout is `base_feature_wide_shifted_zero_body` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). The typed-reference zero-body form stores the same prefix with a 51-byte typed shared-metadata reference at offset 32; zero bytes follow it up to the null GUID length field, which lies 142 bytes before the scope kind.

A paste or body-to-component timeline object owns a `Base Feature` scope that stores the bodies the object places. The object has type GUID `BA3059E4-4B23-4D02-9D18-E7BB95C991F3` or `56225BC7-69B7-446A-9AEA-6AA25BC7806E`, and the timeline item names the object. Bytes 11 through 20 of its primary record are zero, and offset 21 stores u32 `N`. In the marked form, bytes 11 through 19 are zero, byte 20 is `0x01`, bytes 21 through 24 are zero, and offset 25 stores u32 `N`. `N` same-segment references follow the count, and the same-segment reference to the owned scope follows them. In an object with a later same-index paired header, these fields and the removal key precede that header. In the owned scope, bytes 11 through 18 are zero, byte 19 is `0x01`, and offset 20 stores u32 `2N`. Two runs start at offset 24: `N` parameter-body records, then `N` Design body entity suffixes. Both runs use the same reference form: marked 15-byte ordinary local references or 51-byte inline-typed local Body references. The 51-byte body reference stores marker `0x01`, a u64 record index, u32 `36`, ASCII type GUID `D3937028-C20C-4E65-B010-94AD418A5C20`, and two zero bytes. The owned scope takes the object's timeline position, also when the object record forms a parameter scope of its own; that scope then has no timeline position. The layouts are `timeline_body_owner_prefix`, `timeline_body_owner_marked_prefix`, and composite `base_feature_inline_typed_body_reference` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

The scope owned by a paired body-to-component object can instead store two runs of 55-byte typed body entries at offset 24. Each entry starts with marker 1 and a u64 target at offset 1. The u32 at offset 9 gives the 36-byte ASCII type GUID length. The GUID at offset 13 is the Body presentation type `D3937028-C20C-4E65-B010-94AD418A5C20`. The six-byte field at offset 49 has two clear reference flags followed by a u32 member. Both runs use the same entry form. The first run lists parameter-body records. The second run lists Design body entity suffixes.

In the scope that a paste object owns, the two runs are followed by byte `0x01`, four zero bytes, u32 `N`, and `N` pairs of LP-UTF16 GUIDs of 36 code units, before the scope's reference table. Each pair belongs to one pasted body, and the pairs can be in any order. The first GUID of a pair is the browser-node GUID of the source body of that pasted body. The second GUID is the scene-node GUID that the pasted body's parameter-body record stores. That record is a Body presentation, and its scene-node GUID is the LP-UTF16 GUID of 36 code units before the node tail `01 01` and nine zero bytes; the tail precedes the LP-UTF16 physical-material GUID of 36 code units and the physical material library identifier. GUIDs compare without regard to ASCII case. The browser node whose GUID equals the first GUID names the source's Design body entity suffix, and the parameter-body record of the scope whose scene-node GUID equals the second GUID names the pasted body. In a scope with one pasted body, the one pair belongs to that body. When the pairs do not read before the scope's reference table, the decoder keeps the scope's two body runs and reads no copy sources, and for a paste of copies it reports `feature.paste-sources-unresolved`. It does the same when a first GUID names no unique browser node, and, in a scope with two or more pasted bodies, when a second GUID names no unique parameter-body record of the scope or two pairs name one record. A paste object whose bytes after the reference to the owned scope are zero up to an LP-UTF16 null GUID of 36 code units that ends before the object's same-index paired header pastes copies, and its source bodies remain. When such an object stores, after the null GUID and before the paired header, three zero bytes, a u32 reference count, that many same-segment references, u32 `0xffffffff`, an LP-UTF16 kind of 1 through 64 code units, and a u32 family-local ordinal, the kind and the ordinal name the object's timeline item. The layouts are `timeline_owned_paste_source_pairs` and `timeline_paste_name_prefix` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

The class-444 primary paired with class-263 has a 258-byte zero-body frame. Relative to its primary indexed header, it stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, `u8 1` at offset 20, eleven zero bytes at offsets 21 through 31, and `u8 1` at offset 32. Its shared metadata u64 is at offset 33; bytes 41 through 54 are zero. A u32 36 at offset 55 precedes the 36-code-unit GUID at offset 59; bytes 131 through 133 are zero. The generic scope prefix stores u32 1 at offset 134, `u8 1` at offset 138, the repeated metadata u32 at offset 139, six zero bytes at offsets 143 through 148, the current history-state u32 at offset 149, and u32 12 at offset 153. The `Base Feature` kind starts at offset 157. The primary `byte_offset` anchors the indexed header, and the paired class-263 header begins at `byte_offset + 258`. The same prefix in a 257-byte frame, with the 76-byte scope tail defined for the class-409 zero-body form, is also a zero-body frame; its paired class-263 header begins at `byte_offset + 257`.

The typed-reference form of a `Derived Base Feature` or `DerivedBaseFeature` scope stores a result-body snapshot in typed-reference elements. The records `derived_base_feature_scope_711`, `derived_base_feature_scope_707`, and `derived_base_feature_scope_491` in `docs/layouts/f3d.toml` give the offsets, sizes, roles, and GUIDs of its three frame forms. Bytes 11 through 18 of a derived base frame are zero. The u32 at offset 20 of a derived base frame with result bodies is twice the body count, and byte 19 is `u8 1`. A zero-body derived base frame stores `u8 1` at offset 20 instead. A typed-reference element of a derived base frame is `u8 1`, a u64 Design record index, u32 36, and a 36-byte uppercase ASCII role GUID, followed by a trailing field. Equal roles have equal GUIDs in different documents. In the 711-byte form the second body element stores the Design body entity suffix that joins the active Design body map. The scope reference elements store the primary record index plus 4. The three trailing parameter elements store the primary record index plus 3, 2, and 1. The trailing member of the second scope reference element is the current history-state identity. The trailing member of the first trailing parameter element is the previous history-state identity. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID of zeros precedes the second scope reference element. The kind is length-prefixed UTF-16, followed by the feature ordinal. An f64 between two equal u32 values follows the previous history-state identity. The result bodies of a `Derived Base Feature` or `DerivedBaseFeature` scope form a stored snapshot, and the result transition of its history states identifies them in the same way as for a `Base Feature` scope.

A repeated-owner derived base frame uses eleven-byte `01 + u64 + 00 00` references to its timeline owner. It stores the reference `01 + u64 owner_record_index + 00 00` at offset 59 and the same eleven bytes twelve bytes before the frame end, followed by `u8 0`. The derived base scopes that name one owner belong to its derive operation. When, in record-index order, the previous history state of each scope after the first is the history state of the scope before it, and no derived base scope of the same stream without an owner reference has the previous history state of the first scope as its history state or the history state of the last scope as its previous history state, the result bodies of the operation are the outputs of the transition chain from the previous history state of the first scope to the history state of the last scope, in scope order.

A source-pair derived base frame carries one companion-body reference and one result-body reference in fifteen-byte local-reference elements. Its prefix has the layout `derived_base_source_pair_prefix` in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md). The body-reference count is two. Marker one and a zero u32 follow the two body references, then an eleven-byte local reference names the timeline owner. A u32 source-pair count of one follows the owner. The pair contains an eleven-byte source-body entity reference and an eleven-byte result-body entity reference. The result entity equals the second body-reference entity. A zero byte closes the pair. Every reference has marker one; the two body-reference elements have six zero trailing bytes, and the owner and pair references have two zero trailing bytes. The source and result entities join the Design body map in the same stream. The companion body record carries `BASEFEAT_PM_BODY_REF` naming the result body, and the result body record carries `BASEFEAT_DM_BODY_REF` naming the companion body. The owner supplies the derive operation and its source-frame interpretation. For a `MirrorComponent` owner, the source and result geometries use their respective component coordinates. Let `S` and `D` be the source and derived component placements, and let `R` be reflection in the owner's construction plane in assembly coordinates. The point relation is `p_result = inverse(D) * R * S * p_source`.

The 634-byte mirror-derived scope has type GUID `B1E5B971-C007-48C9-8FF5-F4CCD91F87A4`, version 10, and add-in `Fusion`. The body reference count at offset 20 is u32 2. Two marked 15-byte local body entries begin at offsets 24 and 39. The second names the saved result body entity. Its plain local reference at offset 59 names the `MirrorComponent` timeline item of type `71BBEDD5-81F8-4585-816B-05908C207204`, version 0, and add-in `Fusion`. A plain local companion reference begins at offset 621, two zero bytes begin at offset 632, and the 30-byte paired header begins at offset 634. The referenced 115-byte presentation record immediately follows the paired header. It has type GUID `6CCF41D5-40BE-48ED-A834-18F3EAED6C57`, version 1, and add-in `Fusion`. The presentation record repeats the plain local owner reference at offset 31 and names the scope with plain local references at offsets 69 and 88. The derived base scopes whose mirror owners agree follow the same history chain rule as owner-reference frames.

An `OffsetFaces` scope has a 264-byte token-independent frame with four references and a 253-byte token-independent frame with three references, whose marked reference at primary-header offset 25 names the last ordered reference. Other `OffsetFaces` scopes, including 253- and 264-byte frames whose offset-25 reference names another ordered reference, have at least three ordered references and a 77- or 78-byte scope tail. The prologue identifies these variable-length forms. In the marker-one prologue, offset 20 stores `1`, offset 21 stores u32 zero, the marked distance reference starts at offset 25, and the ordered-reference count is at offset 130. In the marker-zero prologue, offset 20 stores `0`, the marked distance reference starts at offset 21, and the ordered-reference count is at offset 126. In both prologues the u32 eleven bytes after the distance marker is one, and the marked reference fifteen bytes after the distance marker names the selected-face group. Either the group is the first ordered reference and the distance reference is the last, or the distance reference is the first ordered reference and the group is the second. The other ordered references name members of the selected-face group. The marked distance reference names a 103-, 104-, or 105-byte same-index paired scalar frame whose finite f64 at primary-record offset 40 is the signed face-normal distance in centimetres. §3.1 defines the `Shell` frame grammar. The thickness reference is a 103-, 104-, or 105-byte same-index paired scalar frame whose positive finite f64 at primary-record offset 40 is wall thickness in centimetres. The 103-byte scalar has class 354, stores marked references at offsets 24, 48, 67, 80, and 92, repeats its owning-scope reference in the first, third, and fifth slots, and uses two zero bytes before the fourth slot and seven before the fifth. Direct face operands use the face-recipe envelope and historical-face resolution rules below. OffsetFaces and Shell role-`0x0000001000000000` construction groups supply their complete selected face sets. The exact group identity is the native face selection of the neutral operation until its history states the faces. A Thicken bounded-face recipe can store the contiguous i32 recipe program without segmented node openers; its complete program and prefix references still identify the operand. Each Thicken role-`0x0000000500000000` whole-body construction group and role-`0x0000001200000000` bounded-face construction group supplies selected sheet faces, and the Thicken selects the union of their faces. When the only group's recipe cannot be joined to solved historical faces, the exact group identity is the native face selection of the neutral Thicken operation. When face operands resolve beside a whole-body group, the whole-body group identity is an unresolved member of the historical selection.

A `Thicken` scope primary frame stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19 after the indexed header and a prologue marker at offset 20. Marker `0` ends the prologue at offset 21. Marker `1` is followed by u32 zero and ends the prologue at offset 25. An optional prologue flag byte stores `0` or `1`. The result-operation u32 starts at offset 21, 22, 25, or 26 and stores `1` for join, `2` for cut, `3` for intersect, or `4` for a new body. A u32 group count `G` of at least one follows, then `G` group references, two flag bytes that each store `0` or `1`, and the scalar reference. All references in this prefix use one spelling: eleven-byte marked references or 51-byte inline-typed references. The first flag byte is `1` when the thickness is added on both sides of the selected faces. The second flag byte is `1` when the selection extends along tangent faces. A u32 zero can follow the scalar reference. Three counted reference runs follow. The first run contains identity references, the second run is empty, and the third run contains the Boolean target-body group for result operations `1` through `3`. The third run is empty for result operation `4`. A u32 count `36` and its 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID, followed by three zero bytes, close the prefix at the ordered reference count. The scalar reference names the first or the last ordered reference. The first group reference names the first ordered reference other than the scalar, and each further group reference names a later ordered reference. A Boolean target group is an ordered reference other than the scalar and has role `0x0000000400000000`. The scalar stores signed thickness in centimetres. In a one-sided Thicken, its magnitude is the finished thickness, a positive value adds material along the selected-face normal, and a negative value adds material opposite that normal. In a symmetric Thicken, its magnitude is the thickness added on each side.

A class-365 whole-body member starts after its indexed header with ten zero bytes, a nonnegative u32 reference count, and that many ordered `(u64 persistent Design reference, u32 form)` pairs. A legacy `Combine` tool form can store zero clauses; the marker then follows the count, and the empty identity supplies no persistent-face candidate or neutral body selection. A general Design reference to a nested indexed record, u32 one, an LP-UTF16 asset UUID, an LP-UTF16 context UUID, and `u32 2` follow the pair table. The nested reference admits compact and inline-typed local forms. The family identity is type GUID `9716F783-676D-42E0-93F9-EBF273E7C035`, base GUID `6144EA59-3ACA-4172-9F14-A6531E94D69B`, version 1, module `Fusion`; the three-digit class is local to the stream type table. After `u32 2`, the standard tail stores a u32 serialization form, u32 first-run count `F`, exactly `F` general Design references, u32 second-run count `G`, exactly `G` general Design references, and a trailing u32 form word. The serialization form is retained independently from both counts and from the class tag; forms `0` and `1` store this tail layout. The trailing word admits 8 and 9. An empty first run admits either trailing word; a writer must retain the trailing word independently from `F`. The SimGenerative tail also admits an explicit extra u32 zero between the second reference run and trailing word 9; that zero remains a separate field. A same-index paired header and nested indexed headers `N+1`, `N+2`, and `N+3` follow. Exactly one `body_recipe_data` record occurs after `N+3` and before the enclosing `N+4` header. This structural interval has no independent byte-length limit; the bounded Design `BulkStream` and the enclosing `N+4` header limit it. The recipe payload may contain its own indexed records; those records remain inside the member and do not replace the enclosing `N+4` boundary. A stream can store no record `N+4` after `N+3`. The member then has exactly one indexed recipe record after `N+3`, and that record contains the `body_recipe_data` family name. The 16-byte family name and eight trailing bytes end the recipe, and the indexed header that follows them closes the member. The record index of that header has no fixed delta from `N`. Each persistent reference joins to persistent face tags independently. A Thicken whole-body member has one form-three reference. Candidates outside the history BREP namespace are excluded; inserted result faces are excluded by intersecting the candidates with the exact feature-input topology. A single remaining face resolves as the historical sheet-face selection. Missing state links or multiple input candidates retain the native group selection. A complete counted Shell bounded-face recipe can select a face set. The set resolves when every candidate in the preceding topology has exactly one historical support context, every context maps its active face slot to the same single preceding slot, no context reports a changed predecessor, and the contexts cover the candidates exactly.
A class-367 whole-body member uses the same reference, UUID, serialization-form, nested-record, and recipe envelope. This form supplies whole-body selections for Scale and shape-target Extrude.

A modern uniform `Scale` or `Maßstab` scope has a 303-byte token-independent frame and five ordered references. Primary-header offset 20 stores u32 factor kind `1`, byte 24 is zero, and the positive finite f64 at offset 25 is the uniform scale factor. The marked references at offsets 33 and 44 name the fifth ordered reference and the first ordered reference. Offset 55 stores u32 `1`, byte 59 is zero, offsets 60 and 64 each store u32 `1`, and the marked reference at offset 68 names the second ordered reference. That second reference is a role-`0x0000000400000000` counted construction group selecting the transformed bodies. The first reference is the class-292 `ScaleFactor` owner, and the fifth reference is a point-data construction record whose finite `point3d` value is the scale center in centimetres; each coordinate is multiplied by ten for neutral millimetres. The body group first resolves against the scope's declared preceding history state when every member supplies one distinct input-body slot. If that historical proof does not resolve, each member must map through its complete body recipe to one current model body; displayed bodies take precedence over cache bodies, and duplicate member bodies leave the group unresolved. An unresolved group remains the exact native body selection.

A modern uniform Scale with more than five ordered references uses the same operation prefix. Its first two references select the factor owner and body group; the group's counted members follow in stored order. Two final references follow the members, with the last reference selecting the center. The ordered-reference count equals the member count plus four.

A matrix Scale scope has nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19 and a marker at offset 20. Marker `0` stores a prologue word at offset 21, a u32 body-group count at offset 25, and the first marked body-group reference at offset 29. Marker `1` stores u32 zero at offset 21, the prologue word at offset 25, the count at offset 29, and the first reference at offset 33. The count is positive. Each body-group reference selects a role-`0x0000000400000000` construction group. A marked point-data center reference follows the groups. Four optional reference slots follow in uniform, X, Y, Z order; each slot stores either one zero byte or an eleven-byte marked reference. One zero byte follows the slots. A row-major 4×4 f64 matrix follows that byte and ends at a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 null GUID. Its positive finite diagonal contains the axis factors; the six off-diagonal basis entries are zero. Its final row is `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. Translation component `t_i` equals `(1 - s_i) * c_i` in centimetres. A populated uniform slot with three empty axis slots selects equal diagonal factors. An empty uniform slot with three populated axis slots selects per-axis factors. Every named reference occurs in the scope's ordered-reference table. Each axis maps `p_i` to `c_i + s_i * (p_i - c_i)`.

A legacy `Scale` scope has a 297-byte payload with five ordered references or a 308-byte payload with six, after the two serialized bytes per UTF-16 kind code unit are excluded. Its fixed operation prefix has five zero bytes at primary-header offsets 16 through 20, the positive finite f64 uniform factor at offset 21, and marked references at offsets 29, 40, and 64 naming the final, first, and second ordered references. Offset 51 stores u32 `1`, byte 55 is zero, and offsets 56 and 60 each store u32 `1`. The second ordered reference is the role-`0x0000000400000000` counted construction group selecting the transformed bodies. The final ordered reference is a point-data construction record; its `point3d` value is in centimetres and is the scale center, so each coordinate is multiplied by ten for neutral millimetres. The first ordered reference is the `ScaleFactor` owner. The group-selection and native fallback rules are the same as the modern form.

A legacy uniform `Scale` scope also has a five-reference form with a 299-byte payload. It uses the same 75-byte fixed operation prefix. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 null GUID starts at offset 75, and three zero bytes follow it. The GUID text is `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`. The five-entry ordered reference table starts at offset 154. The current history-state identity is at offset 213, the kind code-unit count is at offset 217, and the LP-UTF16 kind code units start at offset 221. The 78-byte fixed tail follows the kind: the feature ordinal is at tail offset 0, the preceding history-state identity is at tail offset 31, and the paired same-index header follows the tail. The center, factor owner, and body group have the same ordered-reference roles as the other legacy form. Each marked reference is `u8 1`, a little-endian u32 target index, and six zero bytes.

A modern uniform Scale also uses a 302-byte token-independent frame with five ordered references. Its reference count is at offset 158 and its fixed tail is 77 bytes long. The 303-byte form at the same table offset has a 78-byte fixed tail.

A legacy uniform Scale with the null GUID and five ordered references also has a 77-byte fixed tail. Its token-independent frame is 298 bytes long. The preceding history state is at fixed-tail offset 31 in both the 77- and 78-byte forms. The same operation prefix also occurs with a named parameter-scope tail. A named tail contributes 78 bytes plus two bytes per label code unit. The named form stores five references for one body-group member or six for two. The group members follow the group in the ordered table, followed by a companion reference and the center.

A counted-group uniform Scale uses the legacy factor and the marked center and factor-owner references at offsets 21, 29, and 40. Byte 51 is one. The u32 group count at offset 52 is one or two. The marked group references start at offset 56. They are followed by u32 one and u32 zero. The null GUID and three zero bytes follow these words. The ordered table contains the factor owner, the group references in prefix order, one companion reference, and the center. The scope stores a named tail.

An owner-backed per-axis Scale stores zero bytes at offsets 11 through 28. The marked center reference is at offset 29. Byte 40 is zero, u32 at offset 41 is one, and offsets 45 through 46 are zero. Marked X, Y, and Z parameter-owner references start at offsets 47, 58, and 69. Offset 80 stores u32 one and offset 84 stores the marked body-group reference. The null GUID starts at offset 95, followed by three zero bytes. The seven-entry ordered table starts at offset 174. It stores the three owners, the body group, its member, a companion reference, and the center. The scope stores a named tail. Each factor is the positive evaluated value of the linked `ScaleX`, `ScaleY`, or `ScaleZ` parameter, in model-axis order. The owner has the corresponding local ordinal zero, one, or two.

In a uniform Scale, the dimensionless factor `s` applies to all three model axes: `p' = c + s * (p - c)`, where `c` is the stored center. The factor must be finite and greater than zero. The center follows the point-data grammar and its type-version rules. Each body member selects one whole body. The scope's non-null preceding and current history-state identities select the input and result topology in its bound ASM history. Result bodies follow the body-map and history-binding rules. The operation prefix has no separate result-body reference. The center and body selection are explicit operands.

`Move` scopes with a fixed transform frame reference one rigid-transform record and one role-`0x0000000400000000` whole-body construction group. A rigid-transform record has type GUID `84E6245F-1CDC-4FB8-8048-163A85FAD3F0` and type version `2` or `3`. Its frame runs from its primary indexed header to its same-index paired header. A 253- or 254-byte frame stores form word `5`. A 273- or 274-byte frame stores form word `1`. A 283- or 284-byte frame stores form word `0`. In these forms, offsets 11 through 42 are zero, offset 43 stores u32 form `0`, `1`, or `5`, offset 47 is zero, and sixteen row-major f64 values begin at offset 48. A 293-byte frame stores form word `2` and four marked references: offsets 11 through 30 are zero, marked references start at offsets 31, 42, and 53, offset 64 stores u32 zero, a marked reference starts at offset 68, offsets 79 through 82 are zero, offset 83 stores the u32 form word, offset 87 is zero, and the sixteen row-major f64 values begin at offset 88. The frame lengths above are those of type version `2`. A version-3 rigid-transform record stores the fields of its form at the same offsets in a frame three bytes longer: 256 bytes for form word `5`, 276 bytes for form word `1`, 286 bytes for form word `0`, and 296 bytes for form word `2`. In version 3, form `0` stores a translation, form `1` a rotation, form `5` a free move, and form `2` a point-to-point move. The matrix has an orthonormal three-column basis and homogeneous final row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. Translation components are centimetres. A positive basis determinant defines a model-space rotation about the origin followed by its translation; an identity rotational basis has no axis-angle component. A `Move` scope whose primary bytes 11 through 20 are zero stores a marked reference to its rigid-transform record at offset 21, u32 `1` at offset 32, and a marked reference to its whole-body construction group at offset 36. Both targets are ordered references, and the first ordered reference is the group or the transform record. The first marked reference selects the transform record, and the selected record stores the fields of its form above. In a `Move` scope without this prologue, the transform record is the one reference member of the type-version-2 rigid-transform type whose frame is 253, 254, 273, 274, 283, 284, or 293 bytes and stores the form word of its frame length and the other fields of that form. In the transform record of a form-0 `Move` scope, prefix code words `0, 1` select world translation directions and `0, 0` select the directions of the component that owns the scope; for both, the matrix stores the resulting motion in the coordinates of that component, which are model coordinates in the root component. The ordered references of a form-0 `Move` scope include its three parameter owners at local ordinals 0, 1, and 2, which store the X, Y, and Z translation distances in centimetres in the selected directions. The ordered references of a form-1 `Move` scope include its parameter owner at local ordinal 0, which stores the rotation angle in radians.

A marker-one `Move` prologue stores nine zero bytes after the indexed header, byte one at offset 20, u32 zero at offset 21, a marked transform reference at offset 25, u32 one at offset 36, and a marked reference to its whole-body construction group at offset 40. Both targets are ordered references, and the first ordered reference is the group or the transform record. Its ordered-reference count is at offset 130. Both Move prologues can carry additional ordered references after the body group, its members, and the transform record.

A `Move` prologue with inline-typed references has ten zero bytes after the indexed header, a 51-byte local transform reference at offset 21, u32 one at offset 72, and a 51-byte local group reference at offset 76. Each reference stores its u64 record index, LP-ASCII type GUID, and two zero bytes. The transform GUID is `84E6245F-1CDC-4FB8-8048-163A85FAD3F0`. The group GUID is `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841`. Its ordered-reference count is at offset 206, and the reference table uses 51-byte inline-typed local references.

The form-2 transform prefix also has an inline-typed reference spelling. Its first twenty bytes after the indexed header are zero. The four 51-byte references start at offsets 31, 82, 133, and 188. Offset 184 stores u32 zero; offsets 239 through 242 are zero; offset 243 stores u32 form two; offset 247 is zero; and the sixteen row-major matrix scalars start at offset 248. The fixed prefix through the matrix is 376 bytes. The plain and inline-typed reference spellings carry the same stored matrix motion.

A rigid-transform prefix stores ten zero bytes after its indexed header, followed by one finite f64 scalar. The fixed scalar prefix is `rigid_transform_leading_prefix`. Six nullable same-segment reference slots follow. An unsigned u32 code separates the fifth and sixth slots, and a second unsigned u32 code follows the sixth slot. The u32 form word, matrix-presence byte, and optional sixteen row-major matrix scalars follow the codes. The first two reference slots and the scalar form the leading fields.

The general rigid-transform prefix has twenty zero bytes after its indexed header and four nullable same-segment reference slots when its leading scalar and two leading reference slots are zero. The first three remaining slots begin at offset 31 and occur consecutively. An unsigned u32 code follows the third remaining slot, then the fourth remaining slot, a second unsigned u32 code, the u32 form word, the matrix-presence byte, and the optional sixteen row-major matrix scalars. A null slot occupies one zero byte; a present local reference occupies eleven bytes; an inline-typed local reference occupies 51 bytes. Each present slot shifts the following fields by its extra width. With four null slots, the two codes are at offsets 34 and 39, the form word is at offset 43, and the matrix starts at offset 48. Codes one and two at offset 39 are independent of form zero at offset 43. Forms four and six use this same prefix. A prefix with one plain reference in the first slot of its four-slot suffix has its codes at offsets 44 and 49, form at offset 53, and matrix at offset 58. Its fixed prefix through the matrix is 186 bytes. Form two has four present remaining reference slots. The byte after the form word is the matrix-presence marker: zero precedes sixteen f64 scalars, and one omits the matrix. With four null reference slots, form five, and an omitted matrix, the marker is at offset 47 and the common tail begins at offset 48. The 125- and 126-byte omitted-matrix frames have 77- and 78-byte tails, respectively, and a same-index paired header.


A `Modify` scope moves whole bodies by one rigid transform. Its primary bytes 11 through 19 are zero, and byte 20 is a prologue marker. When the marker is zero, the scope stores a marked reference to its rigid-transform record at offset 21, u32 body count `N` at offset 32, and `N` marked references to construction groups from offset 36. When the marker is `1`, offsets 21 through 24 store u32 zero, the marked transform reference is at offset 25, `N` is at offset 36, and the `N` marked group references start at offset 40. `N` is at least one. The marked record follows the rigid-transform record grammar of `Move`, and its matrix is the motion. The first ordered reference is the transform record. Then the ordered table stores `2N` role-`0x0000000400000000` single-member body groups, each followed by its member, and then zero or more further references. The `N` groups that the prologue names are the last `N` groups of this run, and they select the moved bodies. A `Modify` scope stores a null current history-state identity.

A `RemoveBody` scope references exactly one nonempty construction-operand group with role `0x0000000400000000`. The group members are the whole bodies deleted by the operation. Both features use the legacy body-group grammar below.

A whole-body recipe operand in a scope with a preceding history state can have zero candidate faces in that state. When the state holds exactly one body and the operand has a candidate face in the active model BREP or in the BREP stream of that history, the operand selects that body. A whole-body recipe operand without a scope history state takes the body slot of the whole-body recipe operands with the same recipe identity when all of them select one slot. The entity number of a model body is its ASM body slot. A `RemoveBody` whose operands resolve body slots through their recipe identity deletes the bodies of those slots, and its face match holds only when it selects model bodies with those entity numbers. The same rule applies to the seed group of a body pattern or Mirror. A selected slot that is absent from every model body names a body that the final model omits. The scope whose history state inserts that slot in its transition generated the body, when exactly one history state inserts the slot and exactly one scope has that state. For a `Move` body selection resolved in its input state, a scope generated the body of a slot when exactly one state in the feature's bound history inserts the slot and exactly one scope of that history has that state. A body-pattern seed, such a `Move` body selection, or a `RemoveBody` selection whose every slot names such a body selects the bodies as generated by those scopes, with the slot as the feature-local body identity. A body-pattern seed selects model bodies when every seed slot joins one result body in the BREP basename of its bound history. Every transition after the seed state through the terminal state preserves the seed slots and the existing topology and geometry records, including the carrier rows. The scope whose history state inserts each slot becomes a dependency of the pattern. The generating feature becomes a dependency of the selecting feature, and the result state of each generating scope lists every slot that its transition inserts. A `Reverse Normal` selection of body slots in its input state reads the slots in the feature's bound history. Each slot joins the active bodies in that history's BREP basename as an affected slot does. A slot that joins no body, or only a saved free-edge body, is absent. A scope generated the body of a slot when exactly one state in the feature's bound history inserts the slot, exactly one scope of that history has that state, and the feature of that scope precedes the `Reverse Normal`. When every slot joins one result body, the selection selects those model bodies, and the feature of each generating scope becomes a dependency of the `Reverse Normal`. When every slot is absent and has a generating scope, the selection selects the bodies as generated by those scopes, with the slot as the feature-local body identity. The generating features then become dependencies, and the result state of each generating scope lists every slot that its transition inserts. Any other `Reverse Normal` input-state selection keeps its input-state bodies, and the decoder reports `feature.reverse-normal-body-producer-unresolved`.

A `Combine` resolved in its input state reads the slots of its target and of its tools in the same way, each operand on its own. An operand whose every slot joins one result body, and that no transition after the result state of the `Combine` updates or deletes, selects those model bodies. For a live target operand, the transition into that result state updates the target, so a live target slot selects the body that the `Combine` produces. An operand whose every slot is absent and has a generating scope selects the bodies as generated by those scopes. The generating features become dependencies of the `Combine`. Any other operand keeps its input-state bodies, and the decoder reports `feature.combine-body-producer-unresolved`.

In the legacy body-group frame, `byte_offset` anchors the primary indexed header, and the paired header is outside the frame. The common prefix after the payload prologue is `u32 member_count`, the member reference run, two nullable references, `u32 trailing_count`, the trailing reference run, a u64 role with low word zero, ten zero bytes, `u32 opaque_ordinal`, and one finite f64 opaque scalar. The body-group tail then stores a second copy of `opaque_ordinal`, a reference to `N+2`, the two-byte construction-group flag block of variant byte and closing flag, a reference to `N+1`, byte `0`, a reference to the owning scope, and the same-index paired header. A same-segment reference is `u8 1`, a u64 target whose high word is zero, and two zero bytes; a null optional reference is one zero byte. The ordinary one-member, two-null-auxiliary, one-trailing-reference envelope is 123 bytes. The class-328 `Move` form is a separate 123-byte variant:

| Primary class and scope | Relative offset | Type | Value |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `328`, `Move` | `+36` | u8 | null auxiliary reference |
| `328`, `Move` | `+37` | `u8 1 + u64 + bytes[2]` | present auxiliary reference to `N+13` |
| `328`, `Move` | `+48` | u32 | trailing count `0` |
| `328`, `Move` | `+52` | u8 | retained null trailing-slot byte `0` |
| `328`, `Move` | `+53` | u64 | role; low word zero |

The class-328 `Move` form has no counted trailing-reference run.

In the one-member envelope, the primary-header-relative fixed fields are `+11..+20: zero`, `+21: u32 member_count`, `+25: member reference marker`, `+26: member reference value`, `+53: u64 role`, `+71: u32 opaque_ordinal`, `+75: f64 opaque scalar`, `+83: repeated ordinal`, `+87: reference to N+2`, `+98: two-byte tail discriminant`, `+100: reference to N+1`, `+111: zero`, `+112: owning-scope reference`, and `+123: paired header`. Member, auxiliary, and trailing reference counts extend the variable runs; the paired-header index closes the frame.

A `Reverse Normal` scope reverses the orientation of whole bodies. Its type GUID is `693D6578-4BCE-44F8-B15A-2CE5162A23EE`, base `666BFBBC-2150-4C5F-AAF7-09AB3C3D9E47`, version `0`. The compact Reverse Normal prefix stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, u32 `1` at offset 21, a marked body-group reference at offset 25, a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 link GUID at offset 36, and three zero bytes at offset 112. Its scope reference count is at offset 115. The shifted Reverse Normal prefix replaces the ten-zero-byte prologue with nine zero bytes, byte `1`, and four zero bytes; all later fields move four bytes forward, and its scope reference count is at offset 119. The marked reference is `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes` and names the first ordered scope reference. That record is a legacy body group with role `0x0000000400000000`. Its members are the remaining ordered scope references in the same order, and each member is a whole-body record of type `9716F783-676D-42E0-93F9-EBF273E7C035`, version `1`. The operation reverses the complete orientation of each member body, so every face normal of the body changes direction. The u32 at offset 21 is `1` for any number of body-group members. A Reverse Normal of bodies of one component stores the null link GUID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`. A Reverse Normal of bodies of several components is one timeline item that stores one linked scope per component. Each linked scope selects the bodies of its own component, and the linked scopes of one item store one shared non-null link GUID. The design timeline names one linked scope of the item, and the other linked scopes take the timeline positions directly after it. The history state identities of each linked scope name states of the BREP history of its own component, and two linked scopes can store the same state identities. When several histories hold the state pair of a body-recipe operand, the operand reads the one history whose BREP holds every candidate face of the operand; this reading is reported as `history.body-recipe-history-inferred`.

A `SurfaceUntrim` scope removes trim loops from surface faces and carries an exterior-boundary extension. Its type GUID is `4082E43B-D693-40D7-B44B-26800C9148DB`, base `2EDC2536-D95B-4469-8ACA-DC07124D9C43`, version `0`. The SurfaceUntrim prologue follows the indexed header with ten zero bytes and the u32 loop-group count `K`. `K` marked loop-group references follow, then the marked extension reference and the u32 loop type: `0` removes every trim loop of each selected face, `1` the interior loops, `2` the exterior loop, and `3` the loops of the loop groups. A u32 zero follows the loop type. Three counted reference runs come next: two empty runs and a run of one marked reference, the face group. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID and three zero bytes precede the ordered-reference count. Each marked reference is `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`. The ordered references are the extension record, the face group and its members, and then each loop group followed by its members. The extension record is the parameter owner of local ordinal zero in the same scope; its finite evaluated value is expressed in centimetres. Extension applies when an exterior boundary is removed. The face group and the loop groups are construction-operand groups with role `0x0000000900000000`. Face groups admit ordinary and bounded face-recipe members with exact group ownership and indexed envelopes. Manual-loop groups admit ordinary edge-recipe members.

The ordered persistent-face clauses of a body-recipe member identify its body through complete body-region-shell-face incidence. ASM state identifiers are scoped to their owning history; equal numeric identifiers in another history are unrelated. Resolve the unique history containing both the current and preceding states before walking the state chain. The `body_recipe_data` Design entity id and selector of the member also identify its body. When every persistent-face clause of the member has a candidate face in a body of the preceding state, and also when every clause has candidate faces and all of them are outside that state, the body of that state whose highest-ordinal persistent design link stores that id and that selector is the selected body when exactly one body has that link. This identity takes precedence over the face-incidence join. Prefer a unique preceding-history body slot. When that history state is not represented, a unique current model body is valid. Ambiguous or incomplete joins retain the exact construction-group identity as the native body selection.

A one-sided fixed-angle `Revolve` scope has a 372-byte token-independent frame with seven ordered references. Primary-header offset 25 stores the result operation with values `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, `3 = intersect`, and `4 = new body`; offset 29 stores extent kind `2`, and offset 33 stores direction kind `0`. References zero and two are counted construction groups. Role `0x0000004100000000` supplies the profile and role `0x0000002100000000` supplies the axis selection; each group has its following reference as sole member. A role `0x0000000400000000` or role `0x0000000800000000` group supplies existing-body operands for a Boolean operation. References four and five are 105-byte owned scalar frames with lane ordinals zero and one. Lane zero is the positive angular travel in radians and lane one is zero. The unmarked u32-one form has a 363-byte token-independent frame and eight ordered references. Offsets 11 through 20 are zero. Offset 21 stores the result operation, offset 25 stores extent kind `2`, and offset 29 stores direction kind `0`. Offset 30 stores u32 one. The marked u64 reference at offset 34 has a two-byte zero trailing field and names reference six, which is the sole indexed angle owner at local ordinal zero. This form omits the zero-valued opposite-side scalar. The marker-one form has a 345-, 355-, or 367-byte token-independent frame. Offset 20 is marker `1`, offset 21 is u32 zero, offset 25 stores the result operation, offset 29 stores extent kind `2`, offset 33 stores direction kind `0`, and offset 34 stores u32 one. It has six or eight ordered references and exactly one referenced indexed angle owner at local ordinal zero. This form also omits the zero-valued opposite-side scalar. The referenced-angle form has a 351-byte token-independent frame and six ordered references for a new-body operation, and a 373-byte token-independent frame and eight ordered references for a join, cut, or intersect operation. A join, cut, or intersect scope can also have a 384-byte token-independent frame with nine ordered references. It stores one more 11-byte marked reference in its ordered table, and its other fields are those of the 373-byte frame. It uses the marker-one prologue through offset 32, and offset 33 stores direction kind `0` or `1`. Direction kind `1` occurs with a full turn. Offset 34 stores the Project Axis flag, `0` or `1`. Offset 35 stores the solid flag: `1` creates a solid body and `0` a surface body. Offsets 36 and 37 store zero Symmetric and Two Sides flags, and offset 38 stores the null opposite-angle reference marker `0`. The marked angle-owner reference starts at offset 39 and names the sole angular owner at local ordinal zero. A new-body referenced-angle scope can also have a 361-byte token-independent frame with six ordered references. Its fixed tail is the 88-byte form, and its other fields are those of the 351-byte frame. This form also omits the zero-valued opposite-side scalar. The unmarked referenced-angle form has a 369-byte token-independent frame and eight ordered references. An unmarked referenced-angle scope can also have a 379-byte token-independent frame with eight ordered references. Its fixed tail is the 88-byte form, and its other fields are those of the 369-byte frame. Offsets 11 through 20 are zero, offset 21 stores the result operation, offset 25 stores extent kind `2`, and offset 29 stores direction kind `0`. Offset 30 stores the Project Axis flag and offset 31 stores the solid flag. Offsets 32 and 33 store zero Symmetric and Two Sides flags, and offset 34 stores the null opposite-angle reference marker `0`. The marked angle-owner reference starts at offset 35 and names the sole angular owner at local ordinal zero. This form also omits the zero-valued opposite-side scalar. The angular owner of a referenced-angle form stores a nonzero angle. All forms use the same profile, axis, and existing-body roles. New-body operations have only the profile and axis groups; Boolean operations have exactly one additional existing-body group. A profile group whose sole member is a nested entity-selection member, with no stored sketch-profile record, selects Sketch curves: the primary identity names one planar Sketch placement and the secondary identity names one curve of that Sketch. A named curve in more than one profile loop leaves the group unresolved. Otherwise, when each named curve occurs in one profile loop, the containing loops are the profile, and when a named curve occurs in no profile loop, the named curves are an open profile. The neutral revolution retains the exact profile group when its profile geometry is unresolved. An axis edge uses the edge-recipe envelope and historical-topology resolution rules below. An entity-selection axis stores either the owning Sketch entity suffix and selected curve identity or a persistent face identity. The unique matching line is transformed by that Sketch's placement and supplies the model-space axis. An entity-selection axis whose primary identity is an origin axis in the `MetaStream` type table and names no Sketch placement selects that Design Geometry origin axis, also when an ASM entity in the history carries the same persistent identity. A historical face candidate supplies the axis only for an identity that is not an origin entity. A body edge or face selected as the axis is an edge-recipe or face-recipe operand. Each origin axis has origin `(0, 0, 0)`, and its unit direction is `(+x)`, `(+y)`, or `(+z)`. A straight carrier contributes its origin and direction; a circular or elliptical carrier contributes its center and normal. A selected planar face contributes its carrier origin and normal. A selected cylindrical, conical, or toroidal face contributes its carrier axis. An axis group can instead contain one face-recipe operand. Its exact selector-reference candidate lane supplies the selected face carriers. Every candidate must have an analytic carrier, and all carrier axes must define the same model-space axis line. A one-sided angular travel of exactly `2π` is a full turn. Its swept geometry is invariant under reversal of the selected axis direction. For a partial turn, a positive angle revolves the profile toward the positive-normal side of its sketch plane, whatever the stored direction of the selected axis. A negative angle of a referenced-angle form revolves the profile by the angle's magnitude toward the negative-normal side. The neutral axis direction is the cross product of the in-plane direction from the axis to the profile and the sketch normal, so the revolution turns right-handed about it. Partial-turn axis orientation requires a placed Sketch, an axis parallel to its plane, and profile curves on one side of the axis.

A `Revolve` profile group uses the sketch-profile selection grammar in §3.1. A typed-reference selection's chain names the owning Sketch scope, and its identity record stores the selected regions. Boundary-loop entries name curve primary and secondary identities in that Sketch. Exterior flags distinguish the outer loop from its holes. A counted sketch-profile region selection names boundary curves by their primary identities.

A complete exterior line loop in a typed-reference or compact-reference selection can enclose several atomic regions separated by other Sketch lines. A compact group of this form has one exterior per region and zero further regions. These regions together have the encoded exterior boundary. Fragment ordinals and counts that agree with the participating line graph identify the admitted boundary fragments. A unique closed exterior walk of those fragments selects every atomic region inside that walk.

The direction-pair one-sided fixed-angle `Revolve` form has a 387-byte frame with the seven-code-unit `Revolve` kind, a 373-byte token-independent frame, and eight ordered references. Offsets 11 through 20 are zero. Offset 21 stores the result operation, offset 25 stores extent kind `2`, offset 29 stores direction kind `0`, and offset 30 stores marker `1`. Offsets 31 through 33 are zero. A marked angle-owner reference starts at offset 34 and names the sole positive angular owner at local ordinal zero. Four auxiliary marked references start at offsets 45, 57, 73, and 96; every inline target occurs in the ordered reference table. A 36-code-unit null GUID starts at offset 107, the ordered-reference count is `8` at offset 186, the history-state field is at offset 278, the LP-UTF16 `Revolve` kind has seven code units at offset 282, and the feature ordinal is at offset 300. The previous history-state field is at offset 341. This form omits the zero-valued opposite-side scalar.

A Symmetric or Two Sides fixed-angle `Revolve` scope has a 372-byte token-independent frame and seven ordered references. It uses the marker-one prologue through offset 33, and offset 34 stores the Project Axis flag, `0` or `1`. Offset 35 stores the solid flag: `1` creates a solid body and `0` a surface body. Offset 36 stores the Symmetric flag and offset 37 stores the Two Sides flag; exactly one of them is `1`. The marked opposite-angle reference starts at offset 38 and names the positive angular owner at local ordinal one. The marked angle-owner reference starts at offset 49 and names the positive angular owner at local ordinal zero. Each marked reference stores marker `1`, the u32 owner record index, and six zero bytes. The owner at local ordinal zero is the travel in the revolution direction, and the owner at local ordinal one is the travel opposite to it. A Symmetric scope stores the same angle in both owners. That angle applies to each side, so the neutral symmetric extent is twice the angle. The 372-byte one-sided form has the same token-independent frame length and reference count, so the frame length alone does not tell the two forms apart.

A to-object `Revolve` scope stores extent kind `1` and ends its travel at selected targets. The marked to-object form uses the marker-one prologue through offset 33, with extent kind `1` at offset 29. Offset 34 stores the Project Axis flag and offset 35 stores the solid flag. Offsets 36 through 38 are zero. The marked owner reference starts at offset 39, the marked axis-group reference starts at offset 50, and the side-two target slot starts at offset 61. The unmarked to-object form stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, the result operation at offset 21, extent kind `1` at offset 25, and direction kind `0` at offset 29. Offset 30 stores the Project Axis flag and offset 31 stores the solid flag. Offsets 32 through 34 are zero. The marked owner reference starts at offset 35, the marked axis-group reference starts at offset 46, and the side-two target slot starts at offset 57. In both forms, the side-two target slot is the null marker `0` in a one-sided scope and a marked reference to the side-two target group in a two-sided scope. A marked reference to the final scope reference follows the slot, and the marked side-one target-group reference follows it. Each marked reference stores marker `1`, the u32 record index, and six zero bytes. The owner reference names a parameter owner at local ordinal zero whose evaluated value is zero, and this owner does not state the travel. A marked one-sided new-body scope has a 383-byte token-independent frame and eight ordered references. A marked one-sided Boolean scope has a 416-byte token-independent frame and ten ordered references. A marked two-sided new-body scope has a 415-byte token-independent frame and ten ordered references. An unmarked two-sided Boolean scope has a 433-byte token-independent frame and twelve ordered references. A Boolean scope's role `0x0000000400000000` existing-body group occurs first. The profile group, the axis group, and one role `0x0000000500000000` target group for each side follow in that order, and the side-two target group precedes the side-one target group. Each group has its following reference as sole member. A target member selects a face, a construction plane, or a body. A body-recipe member selects every face of its body in the scope's preceding history state, and the travel ends at the first of those faces that the profile reaches. A face-recipe member has the layout of the role-`0x0000002100000000` face-recipe axis member and selects one face of the preceding history state; the travel ends where the profile reaches the surface of that face.
