A member with no face-recipe frame is an entity selection; when its primary identity names an origin plane in the Design type table, it selects that plane. The travel ends where the profile reaches that plane. Role `0x0000000500000000` does not occur in a scope that stores a fixed angle. A one-sided scope revolves the profile toward the positive-normal side of its sketch plane, whatever the stored direction of the selected axis, until it reaches its target. The two targets of a two-sided scope end the travel on opposite sides of the profile plane.

The reference-aware `Extrude` or `Extrusion` prologue stores its result-operation u32 at primary-header offset 28, or at primary-header offset 24 after thirteen zero bytes (`1..=4`), or at primary-header offset 23 after twelve zero bytes (`1..=4`). An indexed-reference prefix instead stores byte `01` at offset 25, the referenced record index at offset 26, and seven or eight zero bytes beginning at offset 30; the operation follows at offset 37 or 38 respectively. The offset-38 form stores either eight zero bytes or seven zero bytes followed by marker byte `01` at offset 37. The referenced record also occurs in the scope reference table. Operation values are `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, `3 = intersect`, and `4 = new body`. The two immediately following u32 values are the travel direction and the face-extend option; they are not an extent pair. Direction values are `1 = one side`, `2 = two sides`, and `3 = symmetric`. Offset `operation + 12` is the direction-reversal Boolean, offset `operation + 13` is the geometry-kind Boolean (`0 = sheet`, `1 = solid`), and offset `operation + 14` is the start-support byte: `0 = profile plane`, `1 = offset profile plane`, and `2 = selected face`. The current reference-aware layout stores three zero bytes at `operation + 15` through `operation + 17`. Its profile normal is three contiguous unit-length f64 values at `operation + 18`. Seven nullable reference slots immediately follow the profile normal. An absent slot is one zero byte. A present slot is `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`, and its record index occurs in the scope reference table. The start support determines the profile reference set exactly: a profile-plane start stores neither a `ProfileOffset` nor a profile-from-entity reference, an offset-profile-plane start stores only the `ProfileOffset`, and a selected-face start stores both.

The extent form is carried by two further u32 values, one per side, after the profile normal and seven nullable reference slots. Except in the shape-target form, the first-side value immediately follows the seventh slot. A first-side value other than `2` is followed by five zero bytes, the u32 target option at first-side offset `+9`, and the second-side value at first-side offset `+13`. A first-side value of `2` stores its target payload after the first-side value and stores a terminal extent word four bytes before the scope reference-count field. The two-sided current target payload also carries its second-side extent as defined below. In the shape-target form, the seventh nullable slot names the target group. A u32 zero-based scope-reference ordinal immediately after the seventh slot names the same target-group record, one zero byte follows the ordinal, and the first-side value `2` follows that byte. Extent values are `0 = absent`, `1 = distance`, `2 = to entity with an offset`, `3 = to next`, and `4 = through all`. The valid `(direction, first side, second side)` tuples are `(1, 1, 0)` for one-sided distance, `(1, 2, 0)` for one-sided to entity, `(1, 3, 0)` for one-sided to next, `(1, 4, 0)` for one-sided through all, `(2, 1, 1)` for two-sided distance, `(2, 1, 2)` for two-sided distance to face, `(2, 1, 4)` for two-sided distance and through all, `(2, 2, 1)` for target and distance, `(2, 2, 2)` for two targets, `(2, 4, 2)` for through all and face, `(2, 4, 4)` for the class-349/262 two-sided through-all frame, `(2, 2, 0)` for two-sided face targets, `(3, 1, 0)` for symmetric distance, `(3, 1, 1)` for symmetric distance with two distance lanes, and `(3, 4, 4)` for symmetric through all. The direction and side values are one redundant extent key. A reader admits only the listed tuple and rejects a frame whose values disagree; no member arbitrates between them. A writer emits the matching tuple for the selected extent. The face-extend option does not select the extent tuple. The first side is never absent, and the second side is absent when the direction is one-sided. A first side of `1` stores the `AlongDistance` input and no first-side termination reference. It can also store a zero `Side1Offset` default, which has no geometric effect. A first side of `2` stores one target form. A one-sided face target stores one `Side1Offset` owner. The shifted legacy profile-plane form can also store a zero `AlongDistance` owner. The face and `Side1Offset` determine its termination. The class-`330`/`258` 476-byte reference-aware form omits that owner and its parameter when the offset is zero; the absent owner is the zero offset, and this omission cannot encode a nonzero offset. A two-sided face-target form stores two termination groups in scope-reference order, the `Side1Offset`, `TaperAngle`, `Side2Offset`, and `Side2TaperAngle` indexed owners or fixed scalar lanes, and no distance owners. Its terminal extent word before the scope reference count is `0`; the two target faces and side-local offsets carry the two independent termination laws. A shape target stores one role-`0x0000000500000000` target group whose members are whole-body recipe operands, no termination face group, and no nonzero `Side1Offset`. Each member's persistent-reference candidate faces constrain the identity of one body in the effective preceding history state; they do not form the target boundary. The effective predecessor is the scope predecessor when present and otherwise the current ASM state's unique direct transition predecessor. The target face set is the union of every face in the complete body-region-shell-face closure of every member body. Within each closure, the body, regions, shells, and faces occur exactly once, each relation owner and member is unique, and every body, region, and shell has a nonempty child run. Every member uses the same effective preceding state. A through-all cut can retain one role-`0x0000000500000000` whole-body group for each active extent side. These groups repeat the affected-body selection and do not replace the through-all termination. A second side of `1` stores a distance reference and the second taper angle, and it stores no nonzero second offset. The distance reference can name an `AlongDistance` or `AgainstDistance` parameter. A symmetric direction points the `AgainstDistance` and `AlongDistance` references at one parameter record rather than at two records of equal value, does the same for the two taper angles, and leaves the second offset null. Each side travels the shared per-side distance. The whole travel is twice that distance. In the current reference-aware layout, a one-sided direction with a first-side value other than `2` stores target option `0`, and a two-sided or symmetric direction stores `0` or `1`. A two-sided or symmetric second-side value of this layout is followed by six zero bytes, the nullable side-two taper slot, one zero byte, and the u32 measurement word. The measurement word is `0` for a two-sided direction. For a symmetric direction, `2` makes the stored distance the travel on each side, and `1` makes the stored distance the whole travel. Two through-all values with a symmetric direction select through-all travel on both sides and store no distance parameter. A two-sided distance extent gives the second side its own distance and taper references. Scope-reference order and the extent form distinguish the start group from the termination group when both use role `0x0000001100000000`. The start group and each termination group are distinct indexed records. A complete counted bounded-face termination recipe can select a stable face set. It resolves under the same exact predecessor-coverage invariant as a Shell face set. Join, cut, and intersect require an existing-body operand group when the scope commits an ASM state; a scope with a null current history-state identity stores no existing-body operand group for them. New body has no existing-body operand group. In the one-sided distance and to-face forms, a present slot names an owned scalar lane by record index: slot zero names the start-offset lane of an offset-plane or face start, slot two names the first-side distance lane, and slot five names the first-side taper lane. The first marked reference of a first-side extent `2` target payload names the termination-offset lane. Distance and offset lanes are signed centimetres and the taper lane is radians.

A reference-aware two-sided distance-to-through-all form stores direction `2`, first-side extent `1`, and second-side extent `4`. The first side travels the referenced distance; the second side travels through all material.

A reference-aware two-sided distance-to-face form has first-side extent `1`, second-side extent `2`, and target option `1`. The byte immediately after the second-side extent is `0` or `1`. The second-side payload stores the offset and taper references in the same relative positions as the current two-sided face-target payload. The first side uses `AlongDistance`; the second side terminates at the selected face with `Side2Offset` and `Side2TaperAngle`.

The current face-target payload starts at the first-side extent. It stores the first-side offset reference at payload offset 4. In the standard two-sided face-target payload, the target option at offset 19 is one; the field also accepts `0` and `2`, and offset 23 stores the second-side extent. For a second-side extent `2`, offset 28 stores the second-side offset reference, and offset 43 stores the second-side taper reference. Each reference has the eleven-byte marked spelling. The second-side field in this payload is distinct from the zero word before the scope reference count. Its extent pair is `[2, 2]`. Nullable slot one names the second distance. In a two-sided distance form, the marked reference immediately after the second-side extent names the second taper. Nullable slot four can repeat that taper reference. Fixed lanes use the same reference assignments as indexed parameter owners. A selected termination can use role `0x0000000500000000` when there is no repeated target-group ordinal; the selected-face start and the termination occupy scope-reference order. Direction reversal can select the orientation of the two face-target sides.

| `+46..+69` | f64[3] | finite unit profile normal |
| `+70..+116` | bytes[47] | seven nullable slots in order: absent, present, present, present, absent, present, absent; an absent slot is `0`, and a present slot is `01 + u32 record index + six zero bytes` |

The class-keyed `415 / 265` one-sided forms use a shorter extent lane and their own frame anchors:

| Scope primary / paired class | Form | Frame length | Reference-count offset | Ordered reference count |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `415 / 265` | one-sided to face | 481 | `+278` | 9 |
| `415 / 265` | one-sided distance | 449 | `+268` | 7 |

Both forms anchor the primary header at `byte_offset`, use the operation prefix marker `1`, and store the common operation, direction-reversal, geometry-kind, start-support, and finite unit profile-normal fields at the offsets above. The one-sided forms store one-sided travel direction `1` at offset `+32`. The one-sided to-face form stores face-extend option `1` at offset `+36`, first-side extent `2` (to face) at `+107`, and a marked `Side1Offset` owner reference at `+111`. Its second-side extent `0` four bytes before the reference count is at `+274`. The distance form stores face-extend option `2` at offset `+36` and first-side extent `1` (distance) at `+107`; the distance form has no first-side owner lane. Its second-side extent `0` four bytes before the reference count is at `+264`. In both forms, scope-local reference lanes precede the first-side extent, the remaining scope envelope precedes the ordered reference-count field, and each ordered reference entry is `01 + u32 record index + six zero bytes`. The paired header begins at the frame length shown in the table. These frame lengths, reference counts, and the `415 / 265` class pair are admission keys; the side pairs `[2, 0]` and `[1, 0]` select one-sided to-face and one-sided distance respectively.

The ordered reference table is followed by the common scope tail: current history state, the LP-UTF16 feature kind `Extrude`, a nonzero feature ordinal, the preceding history state when present, and the paired indexed header. The class pair and frame length are admission keys. The direction/face-extend pair `[3, 2]` is not an extent tuple in this form; the side pair `[1, 1]` selects `SymmetricDistance`.

The shifted Extrude prologue stores u32 `1` at primary-header offset 20 and three zero bytes at offsets 24 through 26. It stores the result-operation u32 at offset 27, the travel direction at offset 31, the face-extend option at offset 35, the direction-reversal Boolean at offset 39, the geometry-kind Boolean at offset 40, and the start-support byte at offset 41. A one-sided or symmetric form uses one of three extent lanes. A scope reference-count field at primary-header offset 252, 262, or 263 selects the compact lane, whose first-side extent is at offset 106 and second-side extent is at offset 110. An offset-profile form with its reference-count field at offset 262 instead uses the widened extent lane at offsets 116 and 130. A reference-count field at offset 272 or 276 selects the same widened lane. A reference-count field at offset 283 uses the same widened extent lane for one-sided and symmetric forms. A long-reference form with its reference-count field at offset 692 uses the compact extent lane at offsets 106 and 110. A symmetric through-all form with its reference-count field at offset 294 stores the first-side extent at offset 116 and the second-side extent at offset 129. Values in the unselected lanes have no extent semantics. A to-entity first side stores its selected-entity payload after the first-side value and stores the second-side extent four bytes before the scope reference-count field in either lane. The ordinary two-sided distance form stores its first-side and second-side extent values at offsets 155 and 178. Its marked parameter references begin at offsets 139, 159, and 182; five zero bytes separate the first reference from the first-side extent, and eight zero bytes separate the second reference from the second-side extent. The offset-283 two-sided form stores the side extents at offsets 166 and 181, with marked parameter references at offsets 139 and 170, a trailing marked entity reference at offset 185, and eight zero bytes at offsets 196 through 203. Every field uses the same enum as the current prologue. Because the two u32 after the operation are the direction and the face-extend option, neither of them selects an extent form; the later per-side values select it, and the stored parameter set follows those.

The legacy class-330/262 symmetric distance Extrude has a 420-byte primary frame and five ordered references. The unmarked shifted prologue selects solid New Body, direction and face-extend values `[3, 2]`, zero reversal, and a profile-plane start. The two extent words are `[1, 0]` at offsets 106 and 110. The reference count is at offset 252. The first two ordered references name the profile group and its sole member. The scope can retain both the indexed AlongDistance and its fixed-distance carrier.

The legacy class-330/262 blind Cut Extrude has a 438-byte primary frame and seven ordered references. The operation starts at offset 23. The travel direction is one-sided, the face-extend option is two, the geometry is solid, and the start support is the profile plane. The seven nullable slots after the unit profile normal contain two nulls, marked references to members four and six, one null, a marked reference to member five, and one null. The extent words are `[1, 0]` at offsets 102 and 106. The reference count is at offset 248. Members zero and one name the body group and its sole member. Members two and three name the profile group and its sole member. The stored AlongDistance gives the blind travel.

The class-349/262 two-sided through-all Extrude frame is 496 bytes and has eleven ordered references. Its shifted prefix stores u32 `1` at offset 20, three zero bytes at offset 24, and the operation u32 at offset 27. Its operation is cut, its travel direction is two sides, its face-extend option is zero, its direction-reversal flag is zero, its geometry-kind flag is solid, and its start support is the profile plane. The profile normal is a unit vector. The seven nullable slots have presence vector `absent, absent, absent, present, present, present, present`; the four present references name ordered members 10, 7, 6, and 4. Both side-extent values are `4`. After the second extent, the frame stores six zero bytes, a marked reference to member 9, five zero bytes, u32 profile-group count `1`, a marked reference to member 2, eight zero bytes, u32 body-group count `1`, and a marked reference to member 0. The two count words have group-count semantics. A null GUID and three zero bytes precede the ordered reference count. Members 6 and 9 are the first and second taper owners. Their evaluated angles are in radians. Members 4 and 7 name the two affected-body groups. The profile group is member 2 and the existing-body group is member 0. The scope uses the common 77-byte tail. Its exact offsets are in `class_349_two_sided_through_all_extrude_frame` in the layout table.

The symmetric extent is `SymmetricThroughAll`; it has no distance owners or termination face groups. The profile construction group supplies the profile operand, and the trailing group supplies the existing-body operand when the operation is Boolean. This grammar is distinct from the 516-byte class-`323` face-target form and from the shifted prologue without reference-aware fields.

The compact legacy Extrude prologue stores u32 `1` at primary-header offset 20 and zero bytes at offsets 24 through 25. It stores the result-operation u32 at offset 26, the travel direction at offset 30, the face-extend option at offset 34, the direction-reversal Boolean at offset 38, the geometry-kind Boolean at offset 39, and the start-support byte at offset 40. For the one-sided distance and symmetric-distance forms, the scope reference-count field is at offset 251, the first-side extent is at offset 105, and the second-side extent is at offset 109. The valid tuples are `(1, 1, 0)` for one-sided distance and `(3, 1, 0)` for symmetric distance. A form with further present slots stores a unit profile normal followed by seven nullable references. Each present reference occupies eleven bytes and names an ordered scope member. The first-side extent follows the slots and the second-side extent follows it. The reference-count field moves with the extent fields. A compact or shifted prologue of any travel direction can store this slotted layout: the profile normal at operation offset 18, the seven nullable reference slots, the per-side extent values, the current face-target payload, and the current distance tail. The slotted layout also occurs after an indexed-reference prefix with six zero bytes beginning at offset 30 and the operation at offset 36. In a slotted form, the seventh slot can name a role-`0x0000001200000000` termination group of a one-sided face target. These fields use the same operation, direction, geometry-kind, start-support, and extent enums as the shifted prologue.

The compact legacy mixed two-sided Extrude form stores direction `2`, face-extend option `0`, first-side extent discriminator `1`, and second-side extent discriminator `2`. Its scope reference-count field is at offset 281, its first-side extent is at offset 124, and its second-side extent is at offset 128. Its ordered reference table has eleven members; its side-specific parameter owners are `Side2Offset` and `Side2TaperAngle`, and its face-operand group has the termination role. The neutral extent is two-sided with a blind first side from `AlongDistance` and a face-terminating second side; `Side2Offset` is the second-side termination offset and `Side2TaperAngle` is its draft.

A class-`296` primary Extrude scope paired with class `261` uses a one-sided-to-face envelope distinct from the compact distance and mixed forms. Its primary indexed header is the byte-offset anchor. It stores the common operation fields at offsets `+20`, `+24..+25`, `+26`, `+30`, `+34`, `+38`, `+39`, and `+40`; the first-side extent discriminator is `u32 2` at `+105`, the second-side discriminator is `u32 0` at `+257 = reference_count - 4`, and the ordered reference count is at `+261`. The travel direction is `1`; the face-extend option is `1` or `2`; the direction-reversal, geometry-kind, and start-support bytes use the common Extrude Boolean and start-support enums. The paired header distance and ordered reference count are fixed as `(440, 7)`, `(462, 9)`, or `(473, 10)`. These frame shapes select `OneSidedToFace`.

A class-`296` primary Extrude scope paired with class `261` uses a 450-byte symmetric-distance envelope. Its primary indexed header is the byte-offset anchor. It stores `u32 1` at `+20`, zero bytes at `+24..+25`, the result operation at `+26`, direction `3` at `+30`, face-extend option `2` at `+34`, direction reversal at `+38`, geometry kind at `+39`, and start support at `+40`. The first-side extent discriminator is `u32 1` at `+128`, the second-side discriminator is `u32 0` at `+267 = reference_count - 4`, and the ordered reference count is `7` at `+271`. The paired header begins at `+450`. This exact frame selects `SymmetricDistance` and remains separate from both the compact distance grammar and the class-296 one-sided-to-face grammar.

A class-`296` primary Extrude scope paired with class `261` uses a 536-byte two-sided-to-faces envelope. Its primary indexed header is the byte-offset anchor. It stores `u32 1` at `+20`, zero bytes at `+24..+25`, the result operation at `+26`, direction `2` at `+30`, face-extend option `1` or `2` at `+34`, direction reversal at `+38`, geometry kind at `+39`, and start support at `+40`. Three zero bytes at `+41..+43` precede a unit profile normal at `+44`; the seven nullable slots at `+68` have presence vector `absent, absent, absent, present, present, present, present`, and the slot run ends at `+115`. The first-side extent discriminator is `u32 2` at `+115`, the second-side discriminator is `u32 0` at `+287 = reference_count - 4`, and the ordered reference count is `13` at `+291`. The paired header begins at `+536`. This exact frame selects `TwoSidedToFaces` and remains separate from the other class-`296` grammars.

A reference-prefixed legacy Extrude stores its unit profile normal as three f64 values at offset 54.

The 515-byte class-`296`/`261` legacy one-sided-to-face frame stores u32 `1` at `+20`, a zero byte at `+24`, a marked reference at `+25` with six trailing zero bytes through `+35`, the result operation at `+36`, direction `1` at `+40`, face-extend option `1` at `+44`, direction reversal at `+48`, geometry kind at `+49`, start support at `+50`, and three zero bytes at `+51..+53`. Its seven nullable slots at `+78` have presence vector `present, absent, absent, present, absent, present, present`, ending at `+125`. The first-side extent discriminator is `u32 2` at `+125`, the second-side discriminator is `u32 0` at `+277 = reference_count - 4`, and the ordered reference count is `12` at `+281`. The paired header begins at `+515`. This exact frame selects `OneSidedToFace`.

The 483-byte class-`296`/`261` legacy one-sided-distance frame stores the same indexed anchor and common fields through `+53`, with face-extend option `2` at `+44`. Its seven nullable slots at `+78` have presence vector `present, absent, present, present, absent, present, absent`, ending at `+125`. The first-side extent discriminator is `u32 1` at `+125`, the second-side discriminator is `u32 0` at `+267 = reference_count - 4`, and the ordered reference count is `10` at `+271`. The paired header begins at `+483`. This exact frame selects `OneSidedDistance`; both legacy envelopes are separate from the compact class-`296` grammars.

The marked shifted Extrude prologue inserts marker byte `01` at primary-header offset 27. The result operation is at offset 28, travel direction at offset 32, face-extend option at offset 36, direction reversal at offset 40, geometry kind at offset 41, and start support at offset 42. A fully shifted symmetric distance form moves its extent fields, marked references, and scope reference-count field one byte forward: its reference-count field is at offset 284, its first-side extent `1` is at offset 117, and its second-side extent `0` is at offset 131. The marker does not change any field enum or parameter invariant.

The early distance-only Extrude prologue begins with one nullable field at primary-header offset 20. An absent field is one zero byte and places the operation u32 at offset 21. A present field is byte `01` and u32 zero and places the operation at offset 25. The extent-kind u32 value `2` follows the operation and selects one-sided fixed-distance travel. This dialect has no travel-direction field and no second-side extent lane. The direction-reversal Boolean follows the extent kind and reverses the profile-normal direction. A u32 geometry-kind discriminator follows the Boolean with `0 = sheet` and `1 = solid`. These forms use the profile plane as their start support. Their scope reference-count fields are at offsets 208 and 212 respectively.

An Extrude can own `Side1WallThickness` and `Side2WallThickness` Design parameters.

An Extrude scope can carry one or both of its distance and taper inputs as owned fixed scalar frames among its ordered references. Each plain-reference scalar frame is 100, 103, 104, or 105 bytes and stores `01 + u32 owning_scope_record_index` at primary-record offset 24, a u8 lane ordinal at offset 35, and a finite f64 value at offset 40. A 103-byte scalar frame uses either compact scalar-owner trailer: eight zero bytes after the repeated scope reference at offset 67, or six zero bytes followed by `u8 1 + u8 variant` at offsets 78 and 79. The class-`375`/`260` reference-aware Extrude forms (477 bytes with the 24-byte prologue, or 481 bytes with the 28-byte prologue) omit the `Side1Offset` owner and its parameter when the offset is zero. An unlinked fixed lane of a one-sided or symmetric distance Extrude uses ordinal zero for the nonzero signed `AlongDistance` in centimetres and ordinal one for the `TaperAngle` in radians; when an Extrude scope without an embedded distance construction frame owns exactly two unlinked fixed lanes where ordinal zero has value `0.0` and ordinal one is nonzero, ordinal zero is `TaperAngle` and ordinal one is `AlongDistance`. A two-sided distance Extrude uses the same two lanes for its first side, ordinal two for the nonzero `AgainstDistance` in centimetres, and ordinal three for the `Side2TaperAngle` in radians; it carries both distance lanes. Every fixed Extrude lane names the Extrude scope as owner, and the lane ordinals are unique. When a scalar frame is also an indexed parameter owner, its linked parameter `source_kind` selects the lane: `AlongDistance` selects the first-side distance, `TaperAngle` the first-side taper, and, in a two-sided distance Extrude, `AgainstDistance` the second-side distance and `Side2TaperAngle` the second-side taper; `ProfileOffset` selects the start offset and `Side1Offset` the first-side termination offset; another source kind does not select a fixed Extrude lane. Indexed Design parameters can supply either input that has no fixed lane. When both carriers supply one input, their values are equal.

A typed fixed Extrude scalar frame has 303 bytes. Its typed owner reference is at offset 24, its lane ordinal is at offset 75, four zero bytes follow, and its finite f64 value is at offset 80. A typed parameter reference at offset 88 and a typed presentation reference at offset 200 name the two records `N+1` and `N+2` in either order. Typed references at offsets 147 and 252 repeat the owning Extrude scope.

Another one-sided distance form stores the `AlongDistance` magnitude in a 100-byte owned construction frame. Ten zero bytes follow its indexed header. A marked reference to the owning Extrude scope occurs at offset 21, followed by six zero bytes and u32 one. Offset 36 stores a marked nonzero dimension reference, followed by six zero bytes. Offsets 47 and 59 both store u32 `210`, and the positive finite distance in centimetres begins at offset 51. Marked references at offsets 63 and 77 name records `N+2` and `N+1` for construction-frame record `N`; the first has six trailing zero bytes, and the second is preceded by bytes `01 00 00` and has six trailing zero bytes plus one zero byte. A second marked reference to the owning scope occurs at offset 89 and has six trailing zero bytes. In this form, owner-local scalar ordinal zero is the `Side1Offset` default and ordinal one is the taper angle. The distance construction frame replaces the ordinary ordinal-zero `AlongDistance` interpretation. The side-offset default is zero. The prologue direction-reversal Boolean selects the direction of this positive magnitude.

An Extrude face operand may use a 143-byte direct construction-group frame instead of the common counted-tail form. Ten zero bytes follow its primary indexed header. Offset 21 stores u32 one as the member count. Marked references at offsets 25, 36, and 47 name the sole member, the first auxiliary record, and the second auxiliary record; their indices equal the group index plus nine, three, and six respectively. Offset 58 stores u32 one. Offset 62 stores a marked nonzero persistent-selection discriminator with six trailing zero bytes. The u64 role at offset 73 is `0x0000001100000000`. The 26 bytes at offsets 81 through 106 are retained as opaque selection payload. Marked references at offsets 107 and 120 name the group index plus two and plus one; the first has six trailing zero bytes and two additional zero bytes, and the second has six trailing zero bytes followed by one zero byte. The marked reference at offset 132 names the owning Extrude scope and has six trailing zero bytes. A same-index paired header begins at offset 143. The sole member is the persistent entity-selection operand for the face.

A selected-face start group with role `0x0000000500000000` can contain a nested entity-selection operand instead of a face-recipe operand. The operand stores an asset UUID and context UUID and has same-index paired, `N+1`, `N+2`, and `N+3` indexed frames. The `N+3` identity frame has ten zero bytes followed by one u64 persistent identity and ends after 29 bytes at the next indexed header. The next record index is independent of `N`. The expanded entity-selection identity frame has eighteen zero bytes and two u64 identities after its indexed header, length 45, and an independent following record index. An Extrude that starts from a face and ends at all faces (side extents `4`, `0`) stores a second role-`0x0000000500000000` group after the start group; its members are body-recipe operands that select bodies, not termination faces.

The first identity in a selected-face entity operand is resolved independently in each ASM history namespace. A face identity supplies itself, a loop supplies its owning face, a coedge supplies the face owning its loop, a pcurve supplies the face owning each loop of a using coedge, and a surface supplies each face using that carrier. One history supplies a face proof only when every state containing the normalized identity maps it to the same single face. The operand resolves only when exactly one history supplies a face proof. Other identities in the construction path describe selection context and do not intersect the face candidate. When the selected history differs from the feature's operation history, the selected face is a history-qualified member of the feature's composite input topology.

Within a `Fillet` scope, an owned parameter whose `source_kind` is `Radius` or `radius` carries a fillet radius. One positive finite radius selects the constant-radius form. `ChordLen` instead carries the positive transverse distance between the fillet's two support boundaries and selects the chordal form. The ordered pair `EdgeOffset1` and `EdgeOffset2` selects the asymmetric form and stores the positive offset on each support-face side. A grouped Fillet assigns every owned dimensional parameter and `TangencyWeight` parameter exactly once; every tangency weight is finite and dimensionless, with no unit token. An ungrouped constant-radius Fillet has exactly one radius parameter and no `TangencyWeight`. Other parameter families or unrepresentable scalar values retain the native feature. Fillet dimensional scalars use the parameter record's centimetre storage. Within a `Chamfer` scope, `Distance` or `leftDistance` alone selects an equal-distance chamfer; `Distance 1` with `Distance 2`, or `leftDistance` with `rightDistance`, selects the two-distance form; and a single `Distance` or `leftDistance` together with `Angle`, `Rotate Angle`, or `rotateAngle` selects the distance-angle form. Each set selects one form and names every owner of its specification. Different sets in one scope can select different forms and parameter namespaces. Every distance is positive and finite; a distance-angle form's angle is finite and strictly between zero and pi radians. The distance scalars use the parameter record's centimetre storage and the angle scalar uses its radian storage.

A Fillet scope whose scalar lanes are stored as ordered fixed scalar records rather than direct scope-owned parameters carries one or more fixed scalar lanes in its reference table. One lane is one positive constant radius without an explicit tangency weight. An even lane count is one or more two-lane fillet groups in scope-reference order; each group is `(tangency_weight, constant_radius)` by default, or `(constant_radius, tangency_weight)` when each lane links to a Design parameter through an indexed owner frame and the parameters have source kinds `Radius` and `TangencyWeight` in swapped positions. A lane links to a Design parameter when an indexed parameter owner frame for the scope (`scope_record_index == scope.record_index` and `record_index == lane_record_index`) names that lane and references the parameter (`parameter_record_index == parameter.record_index`), and the parameter references that owner (`owner_record_index == owner.record_index`). When both lanes link to parameters with source kinds `TangencyWeight` and `Radius` in default positions, the default order applies. Any partial or contradictory lane linkage retains the native feature. Both values are positive, and the groups correspond in order to the scope's counted edge-operand groups. An odd lane count of at least three is one variable law: lane zero is a positive dimensionless tangency weight, lanes one and two are nonnegative start and end radii, and the remaining lanes are zero or more `(intermediate_radius, normalized_parameter)` pairs. Intermediate radii are nonnegative. Their parameters are finite, strictly increasing, and strictly between zero and one. At least one radius is positive. The neutral variable law orders the start radius at parameter zero, the intermediate pairs in lane order, and the end radius at parameter one.

A Chamfer scope without indexed Design parameters carries one or two positive fixed scalar lanes in owner-local order. One lane is an equal-distance chamfer. Two lanes are the independently oriented first-face and second-face setback distances. Both forms have one group, or one edge-role group and one or more face-role groups. The specification applies to the single group or to the edge-role group.

A `Thread` scope has a direct, owner-marked, or extended prefix. The direct prefix stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20 and the f64 thread angle at offset 21. Its five-byte form marker starts at offset 29, its four-byte form token starts at offset 34, and its three LP-UTF16 fields start at offset 38. The owner-marked prefix stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, u32 `1` at offset 20, one zero byte at offset 24, and the f64 thread angle at offset 25. Its form marker starts at offset 33, its form token starts at offset 38, and its three LP-UTF16 fields start at offset 42. The thread angle is the angle between the thread flanks in degrees, finite and strictly between `0` and `180`. In either prefix, the standard form marker is `01 02 00 00 00` and its form token is `36 00 67 00`. The compact form marker is `00 02 00 00 00` and its form token is `36 00 48 00`.

The compact owned Thread prefix has the owner-marked prologue through offset 32. A zero u32 prefix word starts at offset 33. Its compact marker `00 02 00 00 00` starts at offset 37, its token `36 00 48 00` starts at offset 42, and its designation LP-UTF16 starts at offset 46. The construction marker is `00 C 00 00 00`, where `C` is `1` or `2`. The scalar offsets are the common Thread scalar offsets. The trailer at marker-relative offset 38 stores a zero byte, a marked length-owner reference, a marked offset-owner reference, and byte `1`. Each marked reference is byte `01`, a u32 record index, and six zero bytes. For `C = 1`, the scope references start with the offset owner and length owner, then the face-selection group and member pairs. For `C = 2`, those pairs precede the offset owner and length owner. The trailer repeats those owner identities in length-then-offset order. The offset owner has local ordinal `0` and value zero; the length owner has local ordinal `1` and a positive value.

The owner-marked extended Thread prefix has the owner-marked prologue through offset 32. Its external flag is at offset 33 and its u32 entry count is at offset 34. Its counted 16-byte entries start at offset 38. The class, designation copy, designation, construction marker, scalar fields, and trailer follow the extended Thread grammar.

The extended Thread prefix stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20 and the f64 thread angle at offset 21. Offset 29 is `1` for an external thread and `0` for an internal thread. Offset 30 stores the u32 count of the 16-byte entries that follow it. A cosmetic thread stores count `0`. Each entry is two u64 values; the second values of one thread are consecutive. After the entries, the LP-UTF16 thread class, such as `6g`, `4g6g`, or `6H`, is followed by an LP-UTF16 designation copy that is empty or equal to the designation, and then by the designation. The construction marker and trailer select the extended form. A cosmetic extended compact Thread stores entry count and modeled flag `0` and uses the compact construction marker and scalar lanes. The extended compact trailer stores marked references to the Hole, length owner, and offset owner, followed by byte `1`. Each marked reference has an `01` byte, a u32 record index, and six zero bytes. Its scope references start with the offset owner and length owner, followed by ordered face-selection group and member pairs. The trailer repeats the second and first scope references after its Hole reference. The extended standard form uses construction marker `F W 00 00 00` and the common scalar offsets. `F` is `1` for a thread along the full face length and `0` for a thread of the length-owner length. `W` is `1` or `2`. Its modeled flag is `1` for a modeled thread whose scope has a result and `0` for a cosmetic thread and for a modeled thread whose scope has a null current history-state identity. Its trailer stores a zero byte, a marked length-owner reference, a marked offset-owner reference, and the right-handed flag: `1` for a right-handed thread and `0` for a left-handed thread. Forty zero bytes follow the flag, then a u32 count and that many marked references to the face-selection groups in selection order. Its scope references are one face-selection group and member pair for each selected face, the offset owner, and the length owner, in ascending record index. The owners precede or follow the pairs. The trailer references select the two owners, and the other references are the ordered pairs. Full-length flag `1` gives the `Through` extent and flag `0` gives the `Blind` extent of the length owner. In both the extended standard and extended compact forms, the offset owner has local ordinal `0`. Its evaluated value is the nonnegative distance in centimetres from the face end to the thread start. The length owner has local ordinal `1` and a positive evaluated value. A thread resizes its face: the result face of an external thread has the major diameter of the scope, and the result face of an internal thread has its minor diameter, for a cosmetic thread and for a modeled thread.

Class `334` paired with class `262` is a third wire form. It uses the direct standard prefix and the standard one-group reference table. Its construction marker is `01 01 00 00 00`; its scalar lanes use the same offsets as the compact tail; and its no-reference trailer is `00 00 00 01` at relative offset 38. No other class pair admits this combination.

Class `414` paired with class `263` is a compact-prefix legacy wire form. It uses the compact paired reference table. Its construction marker is `01 01 00 00 00`; its scalar lanes use the same offsets as the compact tail; and its no-reference trailer is `00 00 00 01` at relative offset 38. No other class pair admits this combination.

A standard-prefix Thread scope with the construction marker `01 02 00 00 00` is a fifth wire form. It uses the standard one-group reference table and the scalar offsets of the compact tail. Its trailer at relative offset 38 is a run of two or three zero bytes followed by the byte `01`, then u32 `1`, then a marked record reference of byte `01` and a u32 record index equal to the first scope reference, then four zero bytes. Any other trailer does not admit this form.

A compact Thread with length and offset owners can use a direct prefix. The [word-prefixed compact Thread](../layouts/f3d.md#thread_compact_hole_owners_prefix) inserts a zero u32 after the f64 and starts the five-byte compact marker at offset 33. The designation follows the form token in both layouts. The construction marker is `00 02 00 00 00` in the direct form and `F 02 00 00 00`, with `F` equal to `0` or `1`, in the word-prefixed form. Both use the extended compact trailer and the modeled flag in the scalar block. A modeled extended internal Thread can also use the `00 02 00 00 00` marker and extended compact trailer. It has one prefix entry per face.

The three LP-UTF16 fields are the designation, nominal-size text, and profile name. After the profile name, the five-byte construction marker is `00 01 00 00 00` in the standard form and `01 02 00 00 00` in the compact form. Major diameter is at marker-relative offset 5, minor diameter at 13, the modeled flag at 21, pitch at 22, and pitch diameter at 30. In every form without the extended prefix, the modeled flag is `1` for a modeled thread, whose body geometry contains the helical form, and `0` for a cosmetic thread and for a modeled thread whose scope has a null current history-state identity. The standard trailer at relative offset 38 is `00 01`. A compact trailer is either the four bytes `00 00 00 01` or a marked record reference: byte `01`, a nonzero u32 record index, and six zero bytes. The reference names the earlier owning `Hole` scope in the same Design stream; that record need not occur in the scope reference table. The Hole stable type is `1C037A07-4A15-43F6-ABFC-BBF61B9038D4`, base type `2EDC2536-D95B-4469-8ACA-DC07124D9C43`, version 5, module `Fusion`. The no-reference trailer carries no Hole association. The nominal-size text parses as one positive finite decimal value or as a fraction `N/D` of two positive integers. A fraction states the size in the units of the profile. The four physical scalars are finite and positive, and `minor diameter < pitch diameter < major diameter`. A Thread scope has a positive even reference count. The standard form's first reference is its face-selection group. Compact references are ordered `(face-selection group, sole group member)` pairs. Every Thread face-selection group has role `0x0000001000000000`. Each group member carries a face-recipe operand. The first persistent Design reference in that operand names the threaded-face candidate lane. Later references are construction context and do not enter that lane. The selected historical face is the sole first-reference candidate in the immediately preceding ASM topology. If several candidates occur in that topology, the selected face is the sole candidate deleted or updated across the complete state chain to the Thread result state. The lane can carry one local face candidate for each saved BREP revision. When these local indices are not stable identities in the preceding topology, exactly one candidate must belong to the BREP that carries the selected ASM history. The threaded face is then the sole deleted or updated preceding face bound to a right-circular cylinder whose radius, in millimetres, is within the inclusive interval from half the stored minor diameter through half the stored major diameter after centimetre-to-millimetre conversion. A plural Thread concatenates member selections in face-group order, removes repeated faces after their first occurrence, and requires every member to resolve against the same preceding state. The reference table contains one `(face-selection group, group member)` pair for each face group. If the table contains only these pairs and no parameter-owner entries, the Thread extent is `Through`; an owner-local ordinal `1` entry is `ThreadLength` and gives a positive `Blind` extent.

A Thread input-face identity uses the stable entity slot in its bound BREP history. Across the complete Thread transition interval, unchanged body, region, shell, face, loop, coedge, edge, and vertex membership and unchanged ordered topology relations preserve the selected face identity. Surface, curve, and point revisions can change within that interval. When the complete following interval to the active history head preserves body membership and all region, shell, face, loop, coedge, edge, vertex, point, surface, curve, and pcurve records, the selected slot identifies the active face in the same BREP member. Body-record updates can follow the Thread. When a following transition changes other records, the selected slot identifies the active face in the same BREP member if every following transition keeps that face slot, keeps its surface binding, and keeps the bound surface record and its surface rows. The face record and its loops can change, so a later join can extend the face. The active face surface is then the surface of the selected face in the Thread result state. A source-less active face belongs to the selected primary BREP member. A complete ordered selection has one active face identity for each selected stable slot when each slot names exactly one face in that member.

A Hole scope can have a reciprocal tail. Offsets are relative to the end of its LP-UTF16 `Hole` kind. It stores a positive feature ordinal, eight zero bytes, a member count `N` of `1` or `2`, and `N` marked member references. The first member is the Hole itself, and a second member is the Hole's owning Thread. Three bytes follow: zero, a suppression flag, and zero. Then come a marked first companion reference and either one zero byte or a further marked reference. The preceding Hole result history-state identity, a u32 evaluation epoch, a finite nonnegative f64 evaluation duration, and a second u32 epoch follow; the two epochs are independent values. A second companion reference, a second suppression flag and one zero byte, a third companion reference, a closing self reference, and one zero byte end the tail. The tail is `87 + 11N` bytes, or `97 + 11N` bytes with the further reference, so the preceding history-state identity is at tail offset `42` or `52` for one member and `53` or `63` for two. Each marked reference is `01 + u32 record index + six zero bytes`. The second and third companions name the records one and two before the first. With a Thread member, the first companion names the record immediately before the Thread primary record, so the three companion records are the Thread envelope records before it, in reverse order, and the Thread compact trailer points back to the Hole. Each suppression flag is `1` for a suppressed Hole and `0` otherwise. The paired same-index Hole header follows the tail. New data with an explicit Hole/Thread association use the allocated Hole, Thread, and companion identities; a Thread with no such association uses the no-reference trailer.

A named reciprocal Hole tail stores the feature ordinal, four zero bytes, and an LP-UTF16 label. The member count of two follows the label. The reciprocal member run and companion chain follow the count. Two zero bytes follow the second suppression flag.

The [88-byte Thread companion tail](../layouts/f3d.md#thread_hole_companion_tail) starts after the LP-UTF16 Thread kind. Fifteen zero bytes follow the feature ordinal. The first marked companion reference and a null reference precede the history-state identity at offset 31. An evaluation epoch, a finite nonnegative f64 duration, and a second epoch follow. The second marked companion reference is followed by a suppression flag and two zero bytes. The third marked companion reference and the marked Hole reference precede a final zero byte. The second and third companions name the records one and two before the first.

A Thread scope that references a timeline Hole through its compact trailer follows the Hole as a companion construction. The Thread preceding state is the Hole current state, and the Thread has a distinct current state. A suppressed pair carries null current and preceding states. A direct Thread timeline item gives its own authored position.

A `Loft` has at least two sections. The section list and the rail list of the scope body assign its construction-operand groups to sections and rails. A section group has role `0x0000004100000000`, `0x0000004300000000`, `0x0000000500000000`, or `0x0000002100000000`. A rail group has role `0x0000000500000000` or `0x0000000700000000`. A role-`0x0000002100000000` section group is a point section. A section group of role `0x0000004100000000`, `0x0000004300000000`, or `0x0000000500000000` is a profile section. The group that a non-null marked reference at standard-prefix offset 33 names is a rail. The existing-body group is the one group that neither list names, and it has role `0x0000000400000000` or `0x0000000800000000`. A NewBody Loft has no existing-body group, and a Boolean Loft has one. List order is section order and rail order. Fewer than two sections, a group that two entries name, an entry that names no group of the scope, or a further unnamed group does not define a complete neutral loft.

The compact fixed-prefix `Loft` scope has ten zero bytes after its indexed header, four bytes of value `1`, and the result-operation u32 at primary-header offset 25. Byte 29 is zero and offsets 30 through 33 are `ff ff ff ff`. The three-flag compact form stores bytes `01 01` and a byte `0` or `1` at offsets 21 through 23, the result-operation u32 at offset 24, a zero byte at offset 28, and `ff ff ff ff` at offsets 29 through 32. The operation values are `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, `3 = intersect`, and `4 = new body`. The standard `Loft` scope has nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, byte `01` at offset 20, four zero bytes at offsets 21 through 24, four flag bytes at offsets 25 through 28, and the result-operation u32 at offset 29. Byte 33 opens a same-segment marked reference. When it is `00`, the reference is null. When it is `01`, a nonzero u64 target at offset 34 and two zero flag bytes at offsets 42 and 43 follow. The three-flag standard form stores three flag bytes at offsets 25 through 27, the result-operation u32 at offset 28, and a null marked reference `00` at offset 32. Byte 29 is the nonzero low byte of the operation in the standard form and a zero operation byte in the three-flag standard form.

The `Loft` scope body starts after the result-operation u32 and the marked reference that follows it: at offset 30 in the compact form, 29 in the three-flag compact form, 34 or 44 in the standard form, and 33 in the three-flag standard form. In the compact forms, the zero byte at offset 29 or 28 is that null reference, and the `ff ff ff ff` bytes are the first body word. The body stores an i32 at body offset 0 and u32 values at body offsets 4 and 8, a reference, a u32 selector that one container generation omits, a second reference, the rail list, six bytes, a third reference, and the section list. The [Loft scope body head](../layouts/f3d.md#loft_scope_body_head) gives the fixed fields. A list is a u32 count followed by that many same-segment references. Each rail-list entry names a construction-operand group of the scope. Each section-list entry names a section record `N`, and construction-operand group `N+1` holds the selection of that section. In the reading of the body, the section list has at least two entries and every rail-list entry and every group `N+1` is a member of the scope's ordered reference table. Exactly one of the readings with and without the selector meets these conditions.

A role-`0x0000004100000000` or role-`0x0000004300000000` Loft section group with one member can carry the sketch-profile frame defined for Extrude. Its asset UUID and decimal Sketch entity suffix identify the section Sketch in the same Design stream. A stored selection whose regions each consist of one loop with exterior flag `1` selects those loop regions. A frame with no region selection on a planar Sketch selects every profile of the Sketch. On a spatial Sketch, such a frame selects the Sketch's one distinct profile when its profiles trace one region; with more distinct profiles, the section is retained as a native spatial-Sketch selection.

A sketch-profile record `N` can carry a nested profile-region selection after its same-index paired header. Indexed records `N+1`, `N+2`, and `N+3` occur in that order. The `N+3` selection starts with its eleven-byte indexed header, ten zero bytes, a marked reference to `N`, six zero bytes, and a nonzero u32 region count. Each selected region starts with a nonzero u32 loop count. Each loop starts with a nonzero u32 member count. Each member is 40 bytes: u32 kind `3`, the nonzero u32 primary persistent Sketch-curve identity, a zero u32, the u32 secondary persistent Sketch-curve identity, a second zero u32, three incidence values, and two zero u32 values. The member names the Sketch curve with that primary identity and, when the secondary value is nonzero, that secondary identity. The first incidence value is zero or one. The second and third incidence values are nonzero u32 words. An exterior byte ends each loop: `1` for the outer loop and `0` for a hole. After its loops, each selected region stores a u32 atomic-region count and that number of atomic regions. An atomic region has the same loop count, loops, and exterior bytes as a selected region, and ends after its last exterior byte. The atomic regions of a selected region are the faces of the Sketch curve arrangement that together make that selected region. A selected region that is one face of the arrangement has zero atomic regions. The same-index `N+3` companion header immediately follows the last selected region. Region, loop, and member order are significant. A text selection is a 29-byte record `N+3`: its eleven-byte indexed header, ten zero bytes, and the u64 record index of a Sketch text entity that the Sketch named by record `N` owns. The next indexed header immediately follows the u64. The text selection selects that text entity. A record without this nested selection selects the complete referenced Sketch, except for the Join and New Body form below.

The member rings of a nested selection are, for each selected region in order, the loops of its atomic regions or, when it has zero atomic regions, its own loops. When the atomic regions of a selected region name a set of curves that does not include every curve of that selected region, the selection keeps zero member rings and stays native.

The member list of a counted region names a neutral profile when that profile is the only one that holds the first member and it holds every member. A counted planar selection with an incidence word greater than two, or whose member lists do not name distinct neutral profiles, resolves in the planar arrangement of the kept units of that selection. Every point where two curves meet, including an end point of one curve on another curve, is a node, and the nodes split the curves into arrangement edges. Curves that run together between two nodes form one edge of coincident curves. An edge without a second path between its end nodes leaves the arrangement. A full circle with fewer than two nodes is one fragment. Each member list is one directed boundary ring. On an edge of one curve, a member's first incidence value is one when the ring traverses the curve against its stored direction. The outer ring of a positive-area face runs counterclockwise. An island of a face is an arrangement component that lies inside the face and inside no smaller face, and its outer walk runs clockwise. The curve identities and multiplicities of a walk count a curve of a coincident edge once for each fragment that holds it. A curve with tail marker `1` is not counted, and a walk fragment that holds no curve with tail marker `0` has no member list that matches it. A list matches a walk when the walk has the list's curve identities and multiplicities, and each fragment of one curve has a distinct member of that curve with its traversal direction. The curve identities and multiplicities settle a list when they match exactly one walk. Otherwise the traversal flags settle a list when its matching walks have individual curves on every edge. Such a list must match exactly one walk among the outer rings of the faces and the outer walks of their islands. A list that matches a face selects that face, and a list that matches the outer walk of an island is a hole ring of that face's region. The regions are the selected faces in list order, each with its hole rings in list order. Each ring records each curve, its parameter interval, and its traversal direction. For such lists, a list that matches no walk or several walks, a face or hole ring that two lists match, a hole ring of a face that no list selects, a selected face with an island that no list names, or an island without exactly one outer walk defines no selection.

When a counted member list matches no walk by fragment multiplicity, consecutive fragments of one curve at a pruned interior crossing can form one member use. The crossing is interior to both curves and transverse. Its node has four noncoincident incident edges before cycle retention and two edges of one curve after cycle retention. Curve endpoints retain their fragment multiplicities. Each ring first takes its exact fragment match. A ring with no exact match takes its unique match under the crossing reading. The selected boundary retains every directed parameter interval. This reading carries `feature.profile-crossing-runs-assumed`.

A curve with tail marker `1` that crosses a face splits it into several arrangement faces, and no walk of those faces has the curve identities of a list that names the unsplit face. A counted selection of that kind names the union of the atomic faces that its Extrude takes. For a Join or New Body Extrude with a blind distance, these are the atomic faces that the far cap of the extruded body covers, where the outline of those faces and the boundary of the cap cover each other exactly. For a Cut Extrude, these are the atomic faces that the planes parallel to the Sketch lose. Every curve that a member list names bounds one of those faces.

A Join or New Body Extrude can have a profile operand with no counted region selection in a parameter scope that has no operand group. When the Extrude has a blind distance and one transition leads from the preceding state to the result state, its selection is the atomic faces that the far cap of the inserted body covers, by the rule above. When those faces are exactly the filled profiles of the Sketch, or no far cap meets the rule, the selection is the complete Sketch. A Cut or Intersect Extrude without a counted region selection selects the complete Sketch: the planes that a Cut changes cannot show a profile over no material.

In the one-or-two incidence form of a spatial Sketch Loft section, a selected region with more than one loop and no atomic regions, or an atomic region with more than one loop, retains the native selection. Otherwise the first member of each selected region identifies one unique neutral profile boundary. Further members identify curves on that boundary or geometrically coincident full-circle revisions of its curves. Coincident circles have equal centers and radii within the document linear tolerance and parallel or opposite normals within the document angular tolerance. Every selected region must resolve, and different regions must resolve to different profile indices; a profile tracing the same region as an earlier resolved profile is named once. Otherwise, the section retains its native spatial-Sketch selection.

A one-member role-`0x0000000500000000` Loft section group can carry one entity-selection frame. Its first identity names the spatial Sketch entity suffix, and its second identity names one persistent curve. It selects the unique neutral profile whose boundary contains that curve. No matching profile or more than one matching profile leaves the section unresolved.

A `Pipe` constructs a solid section along a path. Its scope has type GUID `73615646-8752-4EE6-AD02-0B90804B7CD7`, base `3FED63D9-CDC5-4334-A5C5-6C10271320D5`, and version `2`. Four distinct canonical parameter-owner records carry the forward path fraction, reverse path fraction, Section Size, and Section Thickness at local ordinals zero through three in relative scope-reference order. Each scalar owner has type GUID `D91D429C-1BB5-4640-B49F-69AF14F463E9`, base `B24D5130-8751-4272-8143-D230D8757873`, and version `0`, and is a canonical record of its scope whether or not a parameter links to it. A counted path-selection group carries persistent edge selections in path order. Owner records identify the enclosing scope and their local ordinal; stream-local class tags do not assign a scalar role. A supported local owner frame is 103 bytes without a variant or 104 bytes with the variant, and stores its finite scalar at owner-relative offset 40. The complete scalar and parameter-owner grammars agree on the value, value offset, ordinal, and owning-scope references, and the owner frame's extent equals its primary-to-secondary indexed extent. In a `Pipe` without a point-selection pair, an open path stores the same value in both fractions, and a closed path stores fractions whose sum is at most one. Fractions that both equal one therefore name an open path whose sweep covers the whole path group. Other fractions retain their serialized values without an interval or orientation formula.

The compact Pipe prefix has an eleven-byte indexed header, ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, the `isHollow` Boolean at offset 21, the result-operation u32 at offset 22, and two opaque bytes at offsets 26 and 27. The legacy Pipe prefix has the same indexed header, nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, u8 `1` at offset 20, four zero bytes at offsets 21 through 24, the `isHollow` Boolean at offset 25, the result-operation u32 at offset 26, and two opaque bytes at offsets 30 and 31. The Boolean is `0` for solid and `1` for hollow. The operation values are `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, `3 = intersect`, and `4 = new body`. The two bytes after the operation are retained as opaque source fields. Offset 20 is the property-presence byte: the compact prefix stores `0`, and the legacy prefix stores `1` followed by a zero u32 property count at offsets 21 through 24. In a Pipe without a point-selection pair, the section frame follows the two opaque bytes. Its offsets are relative to the byte after them. Five marked references occupy offsets 0 through 54; each is the byte `1`, a u32 record index, and six zero bytes. Together they name the four canonical scalar owners and the settings record. A zero byte is at offset 55. The marked reference at offset 56 names the role-`0x0000000500000000` path group. The u32 section shape at offset 67 is `0 = circular`, `1 = square`, or `2 = triangular`.

Section Size and Section Thickness use centimetres. Section Size is the outside diameter of a circular section, the outside side length of a square section, or the altitude of an equilateral triangular section. A triangle of altitude `h` has side length `2h / sqrt(3)`. Section Thickness is active only when `isHollow` is true; a solid section can retain a positive inactive thickness. A hollow section offsets the inner boundary inward from the outside boundary by Section Thickness. Its circular inner radius is half the outside diameter minus the thickness. The two opaque bytes are not a section-shape enum or a solid/hollow selector.

The scope has one settings reference with type GUID `9414C87F-8EA3-465D-9F78-FF2FF5E9881F`, base `60F291CB-499B-4AB1-B0E5-340368671724`, and version `1`. Each construction group has type GUID `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841`, base `F8CD0BB3-2CE6-4236-8C1B-6D0638BF215F`, and version `1`, closes at its own indexed same-id paired header, and names the owning Pipe in its complete tail. Each nonempty group immediately precedes its complete ordered member run in the scope table. Neither prefix form has a sketch-profile operand. A new-body Pipe has one nonempty role-`0x0000000500000000` path group. Join and cut forms have one nonempty existing-body group with role `0x0000000400000000` or `0x0000000800000000`, followed by the path group. Intersect retains its generic group relations without an assigned operation-specific role sequence. Body-group members have type GUID `9716F783-676D-42E0-93F9-EBF273E7C035`, version `1`. Path-group members have persistent-selection type `5A1BF548-241F-46FD-9FB5-E4B05126EB9D`, version `1`, or recipe-selection type `5662F619-2281-4AD9-93DC-1FCFDA1062E7`, version `2` or `3`. These member types have base `6144EA59-3ACA-4172-9F14-A6531E94D69B`.

An optional point-selection pair has point-data type `69EE2FA7-BCC7-449E-9CA9-976CEFDFED44`, base `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841`, version `2` or `3`, finite coordinates, reference type `1`, and exactly one counted recipe-selection input. The other reference of the pair names that input. One fully marked reference between the operation prefix and the scope's counted table names the point-data record; its reference-value offset is retained. This relation is native selection metadata and does not establish a path origin. Every scope reference has exactly one claim as a scalar owner, settings record, group, group member, or point-selection pair member. References are duplicate-free, and every claimed record has a unique primary identity and type registration. The reference count is `4 + 1 + G + M + 2P`, where `G` is the group count, `M` is the total member count, and `P` is one when the point-selection pair is present and zero otherwise. A new-body table without the pair therefore has six more references than path members, and with the pair eight more.

A `SurfacePatch` scope in the fixed path form has `3n + 1` ordered references and length `340 + 44(n - 1)` or `354 + 44(n - 1)` bytes for positive boundary-component count `n`. Each counted construction-operand group has role `0x0000000400000000`, one member, and the member immediately follows the group. The settings record immediately follows that member. The group, member, and settings triples occur in boundary order. The one remaining reference is the tool body and occurs at the first or last scope-reference ordinal. The ordered group members together form the complete closed path boundary of the generated surface patch. This form has no support-face group.

A `SurfacePatch` scope of type version 5, 6, or 7 has a selection prefix at primary-scope offset `P + Q`. `Q` is 27 in the compact version-5 form, 31 in the regular version-5 and version-6 forms, and 32 in version 7. The u32 at `P + Q` is `4`, and the u32 at `P + Q + 4` is `1`. The u32 at `P + Q + 8` is the settings count `S`. `S` marked references follow, one for each boundary-settings record of the scope, in scope-reference order. The interior-list prefix follows the last settings reference. In version 5 it is eight zero bytes and the u32 interior count `I`, at prefix offset 8. In versions 6 and 7 it is twelve zero bytes and the u32 interior count `I`, at prefix offset 12. `I` marked references to interior groups follow. The tool-reference prefix follows the last interior reference. It is four zero bytes in version 5 and eight zero bytes in versions 6 and 7. The marked reference after it names the tool body.

A `SurfacePatch` scope in the interior-group form has a positive interior count. Each settings reference names a settings record whose `rPatchModelRef` names a role-`0x0000000400000000` construction-operand group with one member. The group, its member, and the settings record are three consecutive scope references. Each interior reference names a counted construction-operand group with role `0x0000002100000000` and a nonempty member list. The group and its ordered members are consecutive scope references. The prefix tool-body reference is one more scope reference. The table can also contain role-`0x0000002100000000` groups that the interior list does not name. These group runs, the named runs, and the tool body partition the ordered reference table. The table is in record-index order, so each run and the tool body can occur at any ordinal. The role-`0x0000000400000000` group members in settings order form the complete closed path boundary, and the settings records give the continuity of each boundary component. The interior groups carry the patch selections that have no settings record, in interior-reference order.

A `SurfacePatch` scope in the single-group path form has `R` ordered references and length `277 + 11R` bytes. Reference zero is one counted construction-operand group with role `0x0000000400000000`. Its ordered, nonempty member list equals references one through `R - 2`. Reference `R - 1` is the tool body. The group is the complete closed path boundary. This form has no boundary-settings record and no support-face group.

The single-group path form has implicit connected continuity because it has no boundary-settings record. Its neutral `FilledSurface` continuity is `Contact`, and its boundary-continuities vector is empty.

A grouped boundary member binds its source edge through the complete serialized recipe program. In the standard side grammar, the first side's nonzero header and scalar values are one-based prefix-reference numbers. Subtract one to obtain each reference ordinal, and deduplicate repeated ordinals. Exactly one named reference has a nonempty exact edge-candidate lane. That reference is the target; its exact lane contains one edge. Exact edge lanes outside the first-side role are topology context and do not compete with the target. Supporting-face boundaries do not filter the standard target edge.

In the alternate two-clause grammar, set intersection of the clauses' edge-reference pairs yields one target reference ordinal. Set intersection of their face-reference pairs yields one supporting-face reference ordinal. Repeated ordinals within a pair count once. The supporting reference has a nonempty, duplicate-free exact face-candidate lane; alternate-selector faces do not replace a missing exact lane. Its preceding boundary identities name at least one complete boundary. Each boundary's face slot belongs to the exact face set, the boundary face slots are distinct, and the boundaries belong to one predecessor state. Intersect the target reference's exact edge candidates with the edges of those matched boundaries. One remaining edge is the member identity. An absent or ambiguous role, missing exact face identity, displaced boundary face, empty intersection, or multiple remaining candidates leaves the member unresolved.

A complete grouped recipe resolves only when every ordered member resolves and the resulting source edges are distinct. An unresolved member retains the complete native group; a conflicting role does not permit generic edge reconstruction. When the scope supplies a predecessor state, an explicit recipe state must agree with it.

A surface-patch boundary-settings record has an empty display name and a class-version prologue of two zero bytes. Its class level is `u8 IsSeedSel`, `u32 PatchContinuity`, `u32 PatchFlip`, `f64 PatchScale`, and the `rPatchModelRef` reference, at payload offsets 2, 3, 7, 11, and 19; the base level's reference run closes the record. The three named settings apply to the one boundary component the record belongs to, not to the patch as a whole. `PatchContinuity` value `0` imposes positional continuity on that component, `1` imposes tangency, and `2` imposes curvature. `rPatchModelRef` names that component's model reference: it equals the construction-operand group record immediately preceding the settings record, so the settings record and the boundary group name the same component from both directions.

The boundary-settings indexed header is `u32le 3`, three ASCII class-tag bytes, `u64le record_index`, and `u32le 0` for the empty display name. Its 19 bytes are followed by the two zero prologue bytes, `IsSeedSel` at `R + 21`, and `PatchContinuity` at `R + 22`.

`PatchFlip` at indexed-record offset `R + 26` is the raw per-boundary side ordinal. Values `0` and `2` are distinct source encodings. A reader retains the ordinal without selecting an incident face from it.

`PatchScale` at `R + 30` is the dimensionless continuity weight. Positional/G0 continuity ignores it. For tangent/G1 and curvature/G2 continuity, raw `-1.0` selects effective weight `0.5`; a finite positive raw value is the effective weight itself. Effective weights are strictly positive. The raw double remains distinct from the effective weight: explicit `0.5` and sentinel `-1.0` represent the same effective weight, and ignored G0 negative zero remains negative zero in source state.

In a version-7 `SurfacePatch` type (`BF77AE1A-E8F6-43AB-A325-A2C984AF1C6B`), the byte at primary-scope offset `P + 31` reverses the whole created surface normal: `0` is forward and `1` is reversed. The following `u32le` at `P + 32` is `4`. This normal reversal is independent of the per-boundary side ordinal.

A `SurfacePatch` creates a new surface body. Its neutral `FilledSurface.merge_result` is therefore `false`; the scope has no independent merge-operation field.

The tool-body reference of a fixed-path settings-bearing `SurfacePatch` scope is the unclaimed endpoint reference. Its record's payload contains the scope's own entity id. In the single-group path form, the tool body is the last ordered reference. In the sketch-profile form, the tool body is the first or last ordered reference. In the interior-group form, the selection prefix names the tool body.

A `SurfacePatch` scope in the sketch-profile form has `2k + 1` ordered references for `k` sketch boundaries, where `k` is at least one. Remove the tool-body reference at either endpoint. Each remaining pair contains a counted construction-operand group with role `0x0000004100000000`, followed by its sole member. Each group is one complete closed sketch boundary. The form selects its boundaries in scope-reference order. This form has no settings records, so its boundary continuity is unresolved, and it has no support-face group.

A `SurfaceExtend` scope has at least three ordered references. Reference zero is the distance owner: an ordinary parameter owner of the scope with local ordinal zero. Its evaluated scalar is the finite signed extension distance in centimetres. Reference one is the boundary carrier. Every remaining scope reference is an edge-recipe operand, in boundary order. The `SurfaceExtend` scope prologue with an explicit method follows the scope's primary indexed header: nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, byte `01` at offset 20, eight zero bytes at offsets 21 through 28, the u32 extension method at offset 29, and the marked reference to the distance owner at offset 33. The extension method is `0` for a perpendicular extension, `1` for a natural extension, and `2` for a tangent extension.

For `n` edge operands, the boundary carrier is a counted construction-operand group of `113 + 11n` or `112 + 11n` bytes. Its first header is followed by ten zero bytes, a u32 count `n`, and `n` marked references of 11 bytes each. The references equal the scope references after the first two. The [88-byte tail](../layouts/f3d.md) or the [87-byte tail](../layouts/f3d.md) follows the reference run. Each tail stores two zero bytes, `u32 trailing_count` with value 1, and one marked trailing reference. A u64 role follows; it is `0x0000000800000000` in a `SurfaceExtend` boundary carrier. After ten zero bytes come the u32 group ordinal, a positive f64 modelling tolerance in centimetres, and a second copy of the ordinal. The ordinal is nonzero. Then come a marked reference to record `N + 2`, where `N` is the boundary-carrier record index, and the flag block. The 88-byte tail stores the flag block as `01 + u8 variant + u8 closing_flag`, and the 87-byte tail stores it as `u8 variant + u8 closing_flag`; each flag byte is zero or one. A marked reference to record `N + 1`, one zero byte, and a marked reference to the owning scope complete the tail. The distance owner and complete boundary carrier are one atomic construction.

A `SurfaceOffset` scope has three support forms. Its owner-local scalar stores a finite signed offset distance in centimetres and has owner-local ordinal zero. The boundary-carrier form uses the ordered distance-owner, boundary-carrier, and edge-recipe partition of `SurfaceExtend`. Its boundary carrier has the `SurfaceExtend` boundary-carrier form with role `0x0000004100000000`. The operation copies the selected support surfaces at the signed normal offset.

The grouped support form places the distance scalar at reference zero. That scalar is an owned fixed scalar frame of 100, 103, 104, or 105 bytes with the layout defined for `Extrude` scalar inputs. Every remaining scope reference is either a counted construction-operand group or a member of one of those groups. Each group has role `0x0000004100000000` and a nonempty member list. The group records and their ordered members partition the remaining scope references. Each member is a bounded-face operand. The first construction recipe after its `N+3` header has family `bounded_face_recipe_data` and precedes the member's `N+4` header when the stream stores one. The union of the group members is the selected support-face set. The operation copies those support faces at the signed normal offset.
