In the zero-distance body-carrier form, the scope references the distance owner, the role-`0x0000004100000000` carrier, and its sole member in that order. The carrier uses the boundary-carrier layout. The first construction recipe after the member's `N+3` header has family `body_recipe_data` and precedes the member's `N+4` header when the stream stores one. The operation copies the support surfaces of the selected body at zero offset. The member recipe family distinguishes the support forms.

A `BaseFlange` scope is 416 bytes with four ordered references. Reference zero is one standard counted construction group with sole member reference one and role `0x0000004100000000`; that member is the scope's sketch-profile record. Reference two is the indexed thickness-construction record and reference three is the operation-settings record. The scope repeats references three, two, and zero at primary-record offsets 82, 113, and 146. A positive finite f64 at primary-record offset 123 stores a copy of a sheet thickness in centimetres; it can differ from the governing thickness. The sheet-metal rule governs: the operation-settings record's rule reference names a record of type `B42ED662-8999-4C1B-A744-759D1D446D55`. After its indexed header the rule record stores ten zero bytes. Version 1 then stores a u32 rule word and entries of an LP-UTF16 expression and an f64 value. A first entry `Thickness` states the sheet thickness in centimetres: in version 1 its 22-byte name starts at rule-record offset 25 and its value at offset 47. The operation creates a planar sheet body from the closed sketch profile and places the thickness along the sketch plane's positive normal.

A `SurfaceStitch` scope has `2n + 2` ordered references for positive input-surface count `n`. At each even ordinal `2i`, a metadata-prefixed construction-operand group has reference `2i + 1` as its sole member and role `0x0000000500000000`. The group prefix after its indexed header is nine zero bytes, `01 + u32 1`, LP-ASCII `DcFeatureOperationIdFlag`, LP-ASCII `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64`, and a u64 metadata value; the standard counted-group member count follows that value. The penultimate scope reference is a fixed scalar record owned by the scope at ordinal zero; its positive finite f64 is the maximum stitched-boundary gap in centimetres. The final reference names the operation-settings record. The operation merges coincident entities, joins every selected surface body, and converts a closed result to a solid body. Each group member is a nested entity-selection record. When its primary identity resolves to exactly one history face candidate for the operation input, the complete ordered member set resolves to a historical face selection only when every member has one candidate and the complete group/reference grammar matches. Otherwise the native selection is retained.

After the indexed header, a `BoundaryFill` scope prefix begins with nine zero bytes. The byte at scope offset 20 selects the operation word at offset 21 when it is zero. When it is one, the u32 at offset 21 is zero and the operation word is at offset 25. Operation words 1, 2, 3, and 4 specify Join, Cut, Intersect, and New Body.

The selected-cell form stores counted body-group references, counted plane-tool references, one settings reference, and counted selected cells. The removal form puts two counted reference lists and a 0-or-1 removal control between the operation word and the body-group count. A count is a u32 followed by local references and one-byte null slots. The settings reference names type `5AC5B5CD-44C7-45B7-9CDC-F79B215A825D` version 0. A selected-cell reference names type `233D4E1B-1C2F-4622-96A0-0027622078CB` version 0. A named `BoundaryFill` tail can use the marked-reference form, with counted associated references and nullable middle and closing references.

A `BoundaryFill` scope in the two-cell body form is 413 bytes and has eight ordered references. Reference zero is a counted boundary-tool group with role `0x0000000400000000` and references one and two as its ordered body-recipe members. References three and five are counted selected-cell groups with role `0x0000000500000000`; their sole body-recipe members are references four and six respectively. Reference seven carries the operation settings. Each selected-cell group produces one solid result body. For each body-recipe reference, persistent candidate faces present in the exact preceding topology supply their owning body set through complete body-region-shell-face incidence. The intersection across every reference in one member must contain exactly one body. A complete group resolves to its member-ordered, deduplicated historical body selection; an unresolved member retains the complete native group.

A `Split` scope begins with the indexed header and eight zero bytes. The leading-block presence byte is zero. The property-block presence byte is zero for an absent block and one for a block with a u32 property count. The empty property block has count zero. The splitting-tool extension Boolean follows the empty property block. Zero disables extension and one enables extension. A u32 with value one and a nullable local record reference follow the Boolean. The extension setting applies independently of the tool and target selections.

A `Split` scope has two nonempty counted construction groups that partition its ordered references. Reference zero is the tool group. Its members follow contiguously. The next reference is the target group with role `0x0000000400000000`; every remaining reference is one of its body-recipe members. A role-`0x0000000900000000` tool group contains face recipe members. The single-face form carries the complete terminal program `[0, −1]`, no positive header value, and no topology nodes. Its unique referenced face in the exact preceding topology is the splitting tool. A role-`0x0000002100000000` tool group has one or more surface, plane, body, or Sketch entity-selection construction members. When the group has exactly one member and that member is a compact entity-selection record whose sole identity `p` names the WorkPlane scope at record index `p + 1`, that WorkPlane feature is the splitting plane and a dependency of the operation. When every member is a whole-body recipe operand whose body slot and face slots resolve in one history state under the whole-body recipe rules, the faces of those bodies, in member order and deduplicated, are the splitting tool. Any other role-`0x0000002100000000` group is retained complete as the splitting tool. The metadata-prefixed form stores `DcFeatureOperationIdFlag` before the member count for either tool role. The operation partitions every target body with the tool surfaces and retains every result body. Reference zero can instead be a face operand record with a `face_recipe_data` recipe and no enclosing group.

A compact `Split` construction group uses Fusion type `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841`, base `F8CD0BB3-2CE6-4236-8C1B-6D0638BF215F`, version 1. Ten zero bytes follow the indexed header. The u32 member count starts at offset 21. The nonempty member sequence repeats the entries immediately after the group in the ordered scope references. Both auxiliary references are null. The trailing-reference count is one. The role is `0x0000002100000000` for the tool group at reference zero and `0x0000000400000000` for the target group that follows the tool members. The repeated ordinal is followed by a marked reference to a later Fusion record of type `5FBE538E-139B-46D4-BCAF-CC796D1E1F78`, base `98542EB9-A4F2-4137-A808-DBB5B3CD6159`, version 0. Two zero flag bytes follow that reference. A marked reference to `N+1`, a zero byte, and a marked reference to the owning scope close the primary frame at the same-index paired header.

A version-0 `SilhouetteSplit` scope has four ordered plain local references: the point-direction carrier, its direction selector, the target body group, and the target body's recipe. The target group has role `0x0000000400000000` and contains the single body recipe. The version-4 point-direction carrier has the point-data layout above. Its single local input repeats the direction selector. Its position and nonzero vector define the solved direction in model space.

The Silhouette Split scope starts with the indexed header and nine zero bytes through offset `19`. A property flag at offset `20` is zero in the compact form or one followed by a zero u32 property count. Eight zero bytes follow the property block. The next plain local reference repeats the carrier, followed by the u32 result mode, a zero u32 and a u32 browser-reference count. Result mode `0` splits the faces of the input body, `1` splits a shelled body, and `2` splits a solid body. The browser references are plain local references. A zero u32 and a u32 of value one follow the run. The next plain local reference repeats the target group. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID and three zero bytes precede the ordered-reference table.

A `SplitFace` scope begins with an eleven-byte indexed header and eight zero bytes. Its common parameter-scope prologue starts at scope offset 19. After the prologue and a nullable direction reference, the method control has a little-endian u32 family, a u8 projection, and a u8 extension. A null direction reference with family 1 and projection 0 selects surface intersection; extension 0 disables tool extension and extension 1 enables it. A null direction reference with family 1, projection 1, and extension 0 selects closest point. A non-null direction reference with family 0, projection 1, and extension 0 selects along-vector projection. The extension field applies to surface intersection. A local along-vector reference registered to a point-direction carrier provides a three-component f64 vector and ordered input references. The carrier's primary-index entry selects its header and type registration; its same-entity secondary-index entry terminates the counted input-reference run. The vector and source selections are separate values.

A `SplitFace` scope stores its u32 ordered-reference count at offset `P`, which is 168, 172, or 176, followed by the table of `r` ordered references. The LP-UTF16 kind payload starts eight bytes after the table, at offset `P + 12 + 11r`. A fixed scope tail of 77, 78, or 87 bytes follows the kind and ends at the same-index paired header. The first reference is a nonempty counted splitting-tool group. Role `0x0000000900000000` names face operand members. Each member contributes a selected face when its recipe and preceding topology prove one. Grouped and direct face operands have a same-index paired header at N, followed by nested indexed headers N+1 through N+3. A registered envelope identifies these headers through four adjacent primary records and the secondary index at N. Each primary header selects the type-table row that registers its entity. The face recipe occupies N+3. Its registered secondary header, or the next registered primary header, bounds the recipe when the chain has a registered envelope. Role `0x0000002100000000` names path, plane, or face selections. A path tool has nested entity-selection members whose primary identity names one planar Sketch and whose secondary identity names one curve in that Sketch. An edge path tool instead has nested entity-selection members with no secondary or curve-secondary identity; each primary identity must resolve through history to exactly one edge in the feature's preceding topology. The ordered edge slots form a historical path in the feature input topology. A plane tool has one or more compact entity-selection members. Each member's sole identity `p` names the WorkPlane scope at record index `p + 1`. The ordered WorkPlane features are the tool dependencies. The target group immediately follows the tool group and its members, has role `0x0000001000000000`, and contains the bounded-face operands partitioned by the operation. In the along-vector form, the direction carrier and its ordered input references follow both groups. A path projects its ordered Sketch curves or historical input edges onto the selected faces; every plane extends through them. Both forms retain every resulting face region.

In a `SplitFace` target group, a complete counted bounded-face member whose effective active candidate set is wholly present in the preceding face candidates contributes that set. When the member's own candidate lanes are empty, faces named by its nested recipe references are topology supports. Stable surface-carrier identity maps each support to the preceding topology. A unique preceding support, a unique changed preceding support, or a unique complete preceding boundary set whose total edge count equals the counted recipe header contributes the mapped face set. Without one of those proofs, the member is topology context and contributes no target face. Every other member must contribute a proven face set, and at least one member must contribute. The target list follows member order and removes repeated stable face slots after its first occurrence.

When a `SplitFace` transition has an updated face set whose cardinality equals the target-group member count, that transition supplies a group proof when per-member recipe proofs are incomplete. Every member must have a nonempty preceding candidate lane, and the union of those lanes intersected with the updated face set must equal the updated face set. The projected target list is that union in first member and preceding-lane order. A member with no updated candidate is topology context. Duplicate updated slots, an uncovered updated slot, an empty preceding lane, or a cardinality mismatch rejects this proof. Inserted face slots are result geometry and do not enter the target list.

An `Extrude`, `Fillet`, `Chamfer`, `Hole`, `Thread`, or `Combine` scope with null current and preceding history-state identities is suppressed. An active scope in these families carries both identities and its current state is the operation result. Suppression preserves the scope's authored timeline position and its operand references. A suppressed `Combine` retains its target and tool selections as history operands. Its companion `RemoveBody` shares the owning feature's suppression state. A `Sketch` scope does not modify ASM topology and may carry null state identities without being suppressed. A neutral native feature fallback retains every scope-table reference as its zero-based ordinal and decimal record index; repeated indices remain repeated at distinct ordinals.

Every resolved Fillet or Chamfer edge group identifies stable edge slots in the ASM state named by the scope's preceding-state identity. The scope's history namespace and that state identity form the slot namespace. A scope can span several transitions; its named input state supplies the selected edges and their curve carriers. The neutral feature-input topology roster contains every body, face, and edge slot in that state. The group projects its ordered deduplicated slots as typed historical edge identities in that roster and retains the native group identity. Historical edge identities never address the active B-rep edge arena and require no active descendant.

A feature-input roster edge that a feature definition selects, or that a loop of a face selected by a feature definition uses, carries edge geometry when its curve carrier has a bounded solved parameter interval. The edge geometry is the carrier point and the unit carrier tangent at the midpoint of that interval, the model-space positions of the start and end vertices, and the faces of the same state whose loops use the edge. A solved line, circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola, or NURBS curve also supplies the carrier curve and the edge's parameter interval, with the lower endpoint first. The tangent follows the carrier parameter direction. A zero carrier derivative at the midpoint gives no tangent. Positions are in the frame of the body that the feature evaluates, before the feature applies. A cacheless helix with a stored edge interval wholly inside its native angular domain also carries the point at the midpoint of that interval. Its construction centre, major vector, minor vector, pitch vector, and apex factor define that point through the native angular parameterization. Any other roster edge carries no edge geometry. For each timeline feature bound to a history state transition, the transition records the resolved geometric properties in feature `source_properties`: `edge_midpoints`, `deleted_bodies`, `affected_bodies`, `affected_saved_edges`, `body_centers`, `body_centers_exact`, `body_centers_incomplete`, `split_plane`, and `transition_geometry`. The `deleted_bodies` property lists each solid body of the preceding state that the feature's own state does not hold. The `transition_geometry` property has value `unchanged` when the bound transition preserves every body, region, shell, face, loop, coedge, edge, vertex, surface, curve, pcurve, and point slot, and each updated record in these families preserves its type and payload after the attribute-chain head reference. Carrier references, topology links, senses, positions, and parameters compare exactly in stable entity-slot space. The one admitted topology insertion is a set of saved free edges. A saved free edge is an `edge` or `tedge` record whose coedge reference (chunk 7) is null, so no coedge, loop, or face uses it; the wire shell at its own slot holds it. Its wire body, region, and shell slots equal its edge slot. Each inserted vertex is a start (chunk 3) or end (chunk 5) vertex of an inserted saved free edge, each inserted curve is the curve (chunk 8) of one, and each inserted point is referenced by one of their vertex records. These insertions leave every physical body unchanged; `affected_saved_edges` lists their edge slots. A deleted saved free edge does not satisfy the property. Other inserted and deleted records outside these families must be attribute records. Other updated records must preserve the same type and payload or be attribute records. The property requires the feature's exact input and output state pair and complete decoded transition records. The `affected_saved_edges` property stores the stable slots of the saved free edges in the scope's affected slots. The `body_centers` property stores, for each solid body with edge evidence, the centre of the box over its available edge vertices, edge interior samples, and axis extremes of proven circular arcs. The `body_centers_incomplete` property lists the bodies whose centre rests on partial evidence: a missing edge sample, a missing vertex position, or incomplete solid topology. It includes bodies with a partial centre and bodies with no centre. Each id has the same spelling as in `body_centers`. The ids are in increasing order, separated by semicolons. The property is absent when every body's edge evidence is complete. The `body_centers_exact` property lists the bodies whose faces are all planes or cylinders and whose edges are all proven segments or arcs; for those bodies the box is the solid's own box. An edge is a proven circular arc when its curve has an axis and a face that uses the edge lies on a cylinder with that axis whose radius is the start vertex's distance from the axis. An edge is a proven segment when its curve has an axis line that holds both of its distinct end points.

Every `Fillet` and `Chamfer` scope has at least one edge operand in its ordered reference table. An edge operand's primary indexed header has record index `N`. It is followed by a same-index paired header and three consecutive nested indexed headers with record indices `N+1`, `N+2`, and `N+3`. Exactly one `edge_recipe_data` construction recipe occurs after the `N+3` header and before the following indexed header. When the `N+3` record of a construction-group member is a 29-, 45-, or 49-byte persistent entity-selection identity, the member is an entity-selection operand, and an `edge_recipe_data` family after the identity's following indexed header belongs to that later record. The bytes after the `N+3` header and before the family-name length field are retained as the recipe prefix; selector-bearing prefixes use the persistent Design operand grammar defined above, and every decoded selector/reference pair carries independently bound face and edge candidates. From the end of the recipe-family name to the following indexed header, the payload is a nonempty, contiguous sequence of little-endian i32 values with no padding. Its first seven words comprise an i64 null sentinel and five-i32 prologue; delimiter words in the prologue follow the side-clause delimiter form. The complete sequence and its first-byte offset are retained as the recipe program. The recipe's nonnegative record-index field is its persistent Design reference and joins to every active face tag carrying that reference; the candidate face set is ordered by face identity and deduplicated.

A standard two-side Fillet or Chamfer edge recipe whose primary operand has an empty preceding face set can identify an edge through its first side's nonzero reference ordinals. Each ordinal is one-based in the prefix-reference table. Repeated ordinals identify one reference. Every selected reference must resolve to one preceding face. The selected references must include at least two distinct ordinals and two distinct faces. Each face must have complete, nonempty loop and coedge memberships. The intersection of all referenced face boundaries identifies the selected edge. The edge is proven when exactly one edge of the intersection also bounds one of the recipe's candidate faces.

An edge-treatment group member can carry `vertex_recipe_data` in the same primary, paired, and `N+1` through `N+3` envelope; its following indexed header is `N+5`. The member is a corner reference, not an edge operand. Its prefix references resolve to face-fragment sets in the feature-input history state. For each reference, the candidate vertex set is the union of the boundary vertices of all referenced face fragments. The unique vertex in the intersection across every reference is the selected corner. The member retains its construction-group index and member ordinal, recipe state, and stable vertex slot.

A mixed edge-treatment group partitions its members by their typed recipe carrier. Only `edge_recipe_data` members contribute selected edges. Every `vertex_recipe_data` member must resolve in the same preceding history state and must be an endpoint of at least one selected edge in that group. Repeated edge-recipe members that resolve to the same stable edge are retained as native members and contribute one deduplicated historical edge identity.

Each operand retains the candidate faces and their stable boundary-edge slots present in the scope's result ASM topology. Each prefix reference uses its exact-selector face set when nonempty and otherwise uses its alternate-selector face set for historical boundary context. Exact-selector faces take precedence when both sets are nonempty. The scope's current state reaches its declared preceding state through one or more transitions in the bound ASM history. Every intermediate state and transition must be present, and a repeated state makes the chain invalid. The operand retains the candidate faces present in the declared preceding topology, the subset deleted or assigned a different revision by any transition in the complete chain, the stable edge slots on those preceding face boundaries, and the subset of boundary edges changed along the chain. Deleted boundary slots occur in the preceding topology, do not occur in the result topology, and occur in a deleted-edge delta in the chain. Updated boundary slots occur in both endpoint topologies and occur in a deleted-edge or updated-edge delta in the chain. Their ordered union is the changed boundary set. Result treatment faces occur in the result topology and not in the preceding topology. A missing or invalid chain produces no transition-derived proof. Every changed boundary edge retains each incident coedge in stable coedge-slot order with its owner loop and face, loop boundary count, zero-based coedge ordinal, and preceding and following edge slots.

A topology-entry selector is nonnegative, occurs at most once in each ordered clause, and increases strictly within a clause. Equal selector values group topology-context entries across clauses; a selector absent from a clause is one-sided. Each topology triplet is `[v, e, v]`, where `v` is a one-based loop-vertex ordinal not exceeding the entry's boundary-edge count and `e` is a signed i32. `e = v - 1` names the edge preceding that vertex, and `e = v` names the following edge. The decoded zero-based edge ordinal is `(v + boundary_edge_count - 2) mod boundary_edge_count` for the preceding form and `v - 1` for the following form. Other signed middle values retain no incident-edge derivation. When both triplets have incident-edge derivations, the ordered pair is conjunctive: the selected historical edge occurs at both named coedge ordinals among its incident loops. Each clause retains the changed historical edge slots occurring at a loop position named by a derived triplet. A selector containing an underived triplet has no incidence proof. For each selector context, the decoder also retains every changed boundary edge whose distinct incident-loop boundary counts satisfy all present clause entries. Selector contexts are ordered by selector value.

An edge operand whose program does not decode as the standard structured tail has six fallback candidate proofs. The reference proof intersects every nonempty changed reference-edge set and requires at least two such sets. The incidence proof intersects every selector's complete boundary-count-and-coedge-ordinal candidate set with every nonempty changed reference-edge set. The cardinality proof intersects every selector's boundary-count candidate set with those same changed reference-edge sets. The common-triplet proof applies when both triplets of an entry name the same incident-edge ordinal; it intersects their historical edge sets across every such entry and every nonempty changed reference-edge set, then resolves only a single common stable edge slot. The cross-clause triplet proof pairs the first triplet of one selector's first side with the first triplet of its second side and likewise pairs the two second triplets. It intersects each nonempty positional pair, every other nonempty positional pair, and every nonempty changed reference-edge set, then resolves only a single common stable edge slot. The deleted-triplet proof collects every historical edge named by every topology triplet and intersects that set with the preceding boundary edges deleted by the feature transition; it resolves only a single stable edge slot. These fallback proofs, persistent identity fields, and transition-derived group assignments never replace an unresolved standard structured recipe. A suppressed scope has no feature transition. For every prefix reference, the operand retains the boundary-edge set of its exact-selector faces, or its alternate-selector faces when the exact set is empty, in the retained recipe-state topology; these sets are indexed by zero-based prefix-reference ordinal. A structured recipe's nonzero local topology references select those sets by one-based ordinal in source-field order. The reference, incidence, cardinality, common-triplet, and cross-clause proofs use the selected boundary-edge sets in place of changed reference-edge sets. A proof resolves when its intersection contains exactly one stable edge slot. Every resolving proof must name the same slot. The proven slot is retained on the native operand independently of whether every member in its containing group resolves. A group without recipe operands uses its ordered persistent selection identities and retains unresolved identities in a partial historical selection. A group with recipe operands also resolves through those identities when every identity resolves and no member has a structured recipe, resolved recipe slot, changed recipe boundary, or treatment-radius candidate. In every other recipe group, identity fields are topology context and do not override recipe evidence. For group assignment, a selector-free operand contributes the complete intersection of its first two reference-edge sets. An operand without two reference-edge sets is topology context. Empty or disjoint leading reference sets identify an unresolved edge-bearing operand. An alternate operand with decoded selector contexts contributes its complete selector/reference candidate set. When those per-operand proofs do not resolve a group, each operand can instead contribute the intersection of all of its nonempty changed reference-edge sets. Every member must contribute a nonempty set in this group-level form. A group resolves when these edge-bearing member sets admit exactly one perfect assignment of distinct stable edge slots. Removing any assigned member-slot pair must eliminate every perfect assignment. The projected edge list follows edge-bearing member order and removes repeated proven identities after their first occurrence. A constant-radius Fillet group additionally uses inserted treatment faces adjacent to each operand's result candidate faces. The inserted face's surface carrier must be absent from the preceding topology and have a positive analytic or constant-blend characteristic radius. Every adjacent result face used as a support must map through one stable surface carrier to exactly one preceding face. A deleted preceding edge shared by two such supports is a radius-qualified candidate. When the inserted face's carrier is a cylinder, the edge is a straight edge parallel to the cylinder axis. When it is a torus, the edge is a circle whose axis is the torus axis. Radius-qualified candidates remain transition evidence when they are outside that member's changed or deleted boundary. They contribute through the constant-radius chain proof and not through the unique member assignment. A group also resolves as an unordered set when its members have distinct operand identities, every edge-bearing member carries the same nonempty set of deleted preceding boundary-edge slots, and the number of distinct slots equals the edge-bearing member count. Members without changed boundary edges are topology context. This cardinality form projects the slots in increasing stable-slot order. Edge groups in one scope also form an exact partition when every operand identity is distinct, every operand carries the same nonempty deleted-slot set, the total operand count equals that set's cardinality, exactly one group contains unresolved members, and every member of every other group resolves to a distinct member of the set. The incomplete group resolves as the increasing-slot-order complement of the sibling assignments when its member count equals the complement cardinality and each of its already resolved members belongs to the complement. When every member identity was replaced by a lost-reference record, a complete compact edge-treatment transition set whose cardinality equals the member count resolves independently of recipe-boundary context. When no complete group proof exists but at least one member has an exact proof, the neutral selection retains the ordered deduplicated proven historical edges and the stable native identities of every unresolved edge-bearing member as a partial historical selection; topology-context members are omitted from both lists. All forms retain the native group identity. A missing operand, duplicate operand identity, contradictory proof, or absent complete group proof prevents complete resolution. A lost-reference marker prevents complete resolution only when no independent complete group proof exists. For every prefix reference in source order, the operand retains its referenced faces in both the result and preceding topologies. Every referenced face retains its face slot, its loops in face-membership order, and each loop's aligned coedge and edge slots in cyclic membership order. When adjacent loop edges share exactly one vertex and its carrier bindings are unique, the loop also retains aligned stable vertex slots, point slots, and model-space point positions. A referenced result face also retains a preceding support face when the result face has exactly one surface-carrier binding and that carrier has exactly one face owner in the preceding topology. The support face retains the same ordered boundary context. A prefix reference's changed reference-edge set contains every deleted or updated boundary edge of its directly persistent preceding faces or unique preceding support faces. Each topology side separately retains the stable edge slots shared by the directly referenced face boundaries and the primary candidate-face boundaries. The recipe order follows the scope reference-table order.

Loft section, guide, and centerline groups can carry the same edge-recipe operand envelope and selector grammar. Role-`0x0000004100000000` and role-`0x0000004300000000` Loft section groups can instead carry the bounded-face recipe operand envelope. Their recipe candidates are evaluated in the Loft scope's preceding history topology.

For an edge-recipe Loft section group, each member carries one direct face context for each recipe reference. A target-face clause is a `(selector, token, Design reference)` tuple that occurs exactly once in every member and has one exact face candidate. Its candidate face, preceding face, result face, and unique preceding support face are the same stable face in every member. Exactly one common target-face clause whose complete preceding boundary has one edge for every group member resolves the section as that historical input face. A missing, competing, or contradictory clause retains the native group.

A complete Loft guide, Loft centerline, Sweep path, or SurfacePatch boundary group identifies an ordered path in the preceding history topology. A group with an unresolved member does not identify a complete path. A Sweep edge recipe resolves to the unique incidence-compatible edge carried by at least two distinct referenced face boundaries. Repeated local-reference ordinals name the same boundary set and do not add independent support.

A `SurfacePatch` edge operand uses an alternate recipe tail after the seven-word edge-recipe prologue. The tail starts with root `2` and contains exactly two clauses. Each clause has six `-1`-delimited nonnegative fields, a nonnegative topology-entry count, exactly eight words per counted topology entry, and a `-1` delimiter. The fields are, in order: one scalar or `[2, reference]`, one face-reference scalar, `[2, reference]`, `[0, 0]`, one edge-reference scalar, and `[0, 0]`. The reference is the field's final scalar. The two clauses share exactly one face-reference ordinal and exactly one edge-reference ordinal. The shared face reference supplies the supporting face; the shared edge reference supplies the target edge candidates. Exact candidate faces take precedence, and alternate-selector faces are used when the exact set is empty. The target candidates intersect the shared supporting face's boundary edges in the preceding history topology. Exactly one stable edge slot resolves the operand. An empty, disjoint, or non-unique intersection remains unresolved. The counted topology entries use the standard eight-word entry grammar. A final zero word may follow the second clause delimiter. This alternate tail is retained as `SurfacePatch` structure and is not parsed as the standard two-side tail.

In the settings-bearing fixed-path form, boundary groups resolve in scope-reference order. When every group resolves in the same preceding history state, their ordered edge identities form one historical path and retain the SurfacePatch scope selection as the native path identity. If any group is unresolved or the groups do not share one history state, the complete native boundary selection is retained.

A nested entity-selection member has primary indexed record `N`. Its header is followed by ten zero bytes, `01 + u32 N+3 + six zero bytes`, `u32 1`, an LP-UTF16 asset UUID, an LP-UTF16 context UUID, `u32 2`, and a u32 serialization form `0` or `1`. A same-index paired record and nested records `N+1`, `N+2`, and `N+3` follow in that order. The `N+3` record is 45 bytes: its eleven-byte indexed header, eighteen zero bytes, two u64 identity values, then an indexed header with an independent record index. The complete member retains its owning construction group and group-member ordinal. Each identity of an `N+3` record other than the compact sketch-point identity is normalized through the complete history entity-version map. In the feature's exact preceding topology, an edge identity supplies itself, a coedge supplies its incident edge, a pcurve supplies the edges of its using coedges, a curve supplies its using edges, and a vertex or point supplies its incident edges. Identities absent from the preceding state contribute no candidate. The member resolves when the intersection of every available identity candidate set contains exactly one edge. A complete ordered group of resolved members supplies a historical path. Loft section groups can carry this member form. In a role-`0x0000000500000000` Loft section or guide group, the first identity can name the unique owning spatial Sketch entity and the second identity names one unique persistent curve owned by that Sketch. The member then supplies a source-native profile or path selection within the neutral spatial Sketch; both ownership and curve identity are required. A member of a role-`0x0000002100000000` Loft point group can instead have a 37-byte `N+3` record with the compact sketch-point identity of a vertex-rule input: zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, the owning Sketch entity record index as a u64 at offset 21, and the sketch-point persistent id as a u64 at offset 29. That identity selects the one sketch point owned by that Sketch record with that persistent id, and the point's model-space position is the point section.

In a Loft guide or centerline group whose members use nested entity-selection frames, the group member run is an ordered curve selection. Every member has one unique operand at its group ordinal, all members share one asset UUID, context UUID, and owning Sketch identity, and each second identity names one unique curve identity owned by that Sketch. Duplicate member records or curve identities, missing neutral curve entities, multiple placements, or any other ambiguity retain the native group. A planar Sketch placement projects the ordered identities as `PathRef::SketchCurves`; a spatial Sketch placement projects the ordered neutral entities as `PathRef::SpatialSketchCurves`. The member order is preserved. A role-`0x0000000500000000` Loft section group whose member run selects curves of one planar Sketch in this way has those ordered Sketch curves as its section profile.

The same ordered-curve proof applies to a Sweep path or guide-rail group. Its ordered curves project as `PathRef::SketchCurves` or `PathRef::SpatialSketchCurves` for planar or spatial placement, respectively, even when the owning Sketch contains other geometry.

The transition-evaluated boundary-count candidates also prove an unordered edge group when every recipe member carries a structured selector and the candidate union cardinality equals the complete recipe-member count. Selectors with no boundary-count candidate contribute topology context. The projected group follows increasing stable edge-slot order. A radius-group member without a matching treatment candidate contributes topology context when its changed boundary intersects the complete set of exact and radius-qualified group edges. A changed member disjoint from that set prevents radius-group resolution.

Structured recipe selectors evaluate every deleted or updated edge present in the preceding topology. Primary candidate-face boundaries restrict separate boundary proofs but do not restrict the selector candidate universe.

The structured edge-recipe program has a sentinel prelude `[-1, -1, 2, 0, t0, 1, t1]` or a counted prelude `[0, t0, n, 1, t1, 2, t2, ..., n, tn]` with positive `n`. Each tag `t` is `-1`, `0`, or `1`. The standard tail starts immediately after the complete prelude with a positive i32 clause count followed by that many ordered side clauses. One tag follows the clause count, each side's two-word header, and each scalar field. One tag separates consecutive sides. A mandatory terminal tag ends the last side and the complete program. Header count `h` is positive, including `h = 1`, and equals the scalar count plus one. After the scalars, a side retains an exact field-program prefix followed by a nonnegative i32 entry count `n` and exactly `8n` topology-entry words. The compact prefix is one zero word. An extended prefix is one or more concatenated fields `[x1, ..., xk, field_tag, 0, 0, -1]`, with positive `k`, nonnegative `x` values, and `field_tag` equal to `-1` or `0`. Zero-leading fields and zero entry counts after either prefix form are valid. Exactly one complete division into the counted sides and terminal tag is valid. Prelude words and tags do not identify an edge. The header's second word and every side scalar are retained i32 values. Each zero value is a null reference slot. Every nonzero value is a positive one-based prefix-reference ordinal and is retained in source-field order with repetitions; another value invalidates local-reference binding. The first side identifies the selected-edge support faces. Intersecting their feature-input boundary-edge sets with the recipe's candidate-face boundary edges selects the operand edge when exactly one stable edge remains. When several edges remain, the counted entries' boundary-count and coedge-ordinal incidences restrict that same intersection and select the edge only when one stable slot remains. A complete edge-group selection has precedence over fragment-lane selection. Fragment-lane selection applies to members left unresolved by the member and group selection rules and preserves the selected edges and their order. Additional fragment-selected edges follow that retained list in member order. For a standard two-side `Fillet` or `Chamfer` edge recipe, each first-side reference lane contributes the live loop-edge sets of its support faces in the feature-input topology, whose fragments each persistent name joins by the precedence rule for counted names above. The intersection of these lane unions retains edges with at least two distinct supporting faces. The intersection with the recipe candidate-face boundary edges selects the edge when exactly one remains. When that intersection is empty and the lane intersection has exactly one edge, the owning Chamfer or Fillet transition proves the edge when it deletes that stable edge slot from the feature-input topology. The deletion replaces the common boundary of the distinct first-side support faces. This proof requires a nonempty intersection of the persistent names within each reference lane. The deletion test confirms the singleton lane intersection and preserves its cardinality. For a member left unresolved by the group selection rules, a proven recipe edge deleted by the transition has precedence over the member's persistent-identity edge binding. A singleton edge that lacks this transition proof is selected with `history.edge-selection-inferred`. References in later sides do not enter the face-boundary identity intersection. A `Revolve` axis edge recipe whose reference faces have no single common boundary edge selects its axis edge through these first-side support faces. An entry is an i32 side-local selector, a positive i32 count of edges in the referenced face loop, and two topology triplets. Each triplet retains its three words and zero-based vertex ordinal; adjacent middle-word forms additionally retain the derived incident-edge ordinal and preceding/following side. When both triplets derive the same incident-edge ordinal, the entry also retains that common ordinal. The clause count, header count, header value, every scalar word, complete field-program prefix, payload entry count, and every entry field are retained. A referenced result face whose stable slot is absent from the preceding state maps through its invariant surface carrier to the unique preceding support face. The reference edge set contains every deleted or updated boundary edge of the directly persistent reference face or that mapped support face. Every standard recipe member must resolve independently. The group projects member-order edges and removes repeated stable identities after their first occurrence; a repeated recipe in another group resolves to the same edge. An unresolved member retains the complete native group. A tail outside this grammar remains an exact unstructured program.

An `Extrude` face-group member and an edge-treatment bounded-face member have the same indexed-record envelope: primary record `N`, a same-index paired header, and consecutive nested records `N+1`, `N+2`, and `N+3`. Exactly one `face_recipe_data` or `bounded_face_recipe_data` construction recipe occurs after the `N+3` header and before the immediately following indexed header or the end of the Design stream, even when the enclosing construction group continues to a later indexed record. The exact recipe family is retained per face operand. In every feature family, when the final face member of a construction-operand group is followed by another scope-table reference whose primary header is later in the stream, that header bounds the member's recipe payload. The i32 at 16 bytes before the family-name bytes is the recipe's indexed-record identity. Several bounded-face recipes in one group can carry the same identity; this field is not a second binary design ID. The bytes after the `N+3` header and before the family-name length field are retained as the recipe prefix; selector-bearing prefixes use the persistent Design operand grammar defined above, and every decoded selector/reference pair carries independently bound face and edge candidates. From the end of the framed recipe-family name to the following indexed header, or to the end of the Design stream when no indexed header follows, the payload is a nonempty, contiguous sequence of little-endian i32 values with no padding. The complete sequence and its first-byte offset are retained as the recipe program. A counted program starts with `i32 0`, an i32 zero-or-minus-one prelude, and a positive i32 header value. It may carry a counted prelude after that header before its first node opener, and it may contain no node. When nodes are present, the first opener is at word index at least three and each node starts with `i32 -1`, `i32 -1`, `i32 2`; the next node opener, the following indexed header, or the end of the Design stream terminates it. The terminal Split form consists only of the first two words and has no nodes. The node payload is a `-1`-delimited root scalar, two one-word prelude runs, and one or two topology side clauses. The second prelude scalar is the side-clause count, `1` or `2`. Each side clause has the same counted header, two or three one-word scalars, zero-tagged counted payload, and ordered eight-word entry grammar as an edge recipe side. The root, first prelude scalar, and every side scalar are retained in source-field order with repetitions. Each node retains this structure, its complete word sequence, its opener byte offset, and its exclusive terminating byte offset. The recipe's persistent Design reference joins to every active B-rep face whose persistent-subentity tag contains that reference; the resulting candidate set is ordered by B-rep face identity and deduplicated. Prefix operands carrying the recipe's own Design reference divide those faces by selector. Faces whose tag selector equals the prefix selector are topology context. Faces carrying the same token, token integer, and Design reference under a different selector are the selected active face set; a nonempty selected set resolves as a whole in face-identity order. When no alternate-selector face exists, subtracting the topology-context faces produces the ordered unreferenced candidate set. An empty unreferenced set retains the broad candidates because the selected historical face has no active unreferenced candidate. Each effective active candidate also maps to its invariant surface-carrier slot when every historical occurrence of that face slot has exactly one binding to the same carrier. The operand retains every face in the scope's preceding topology that owns this carrier, each owner's ordered loop boundary context, and the subset deleted or updated across the complete state chain from the preceding state to the scope result state. When the preceding topology stores exactly one plane row or exactly one cylinder row for the carrier and no row of the other kind, the operand also retains that plane, as origin and normal, or that cylinder, as axis origin, axis direction, and radius. Every intermediate transition must be present and uniquely state-bound. Missing, conflicting, or multiply bound active carrier identities produce no support mapping. Without an alternate-selector proof, a face operand resolves to the sole effective candidate whose stable face slot is present in the scope's preceding ASM topology. If several candidates are present, it resolves to the sole candidate whose slot is deleted or assigned a different record revision along the scope's ASM transition chain. Inserted slots are result geometry and do not select an input face. DR-304 records when the recipe of an `Extrude` bounded-face operand contradicts the face that these rules select. For a grouped bounded-face operand outside the Thread and Split families, the intersection of its Design references, the preceding topology's stable face slots, and the transition-changed face slots selects the face only when it contains exactly one slot. When every effective active candidate has a support mapping and every mapping names the same nonempty predecessor-face set, that complete common set resolves the operand. For a fully structured bounded-face program, whose nodes each carry two side clauses, the positive header equals the node count or the total loop-edge cardinality of a complete predecessor-face boundary set. Individual complete support contexts and the unique union of consistent boundaries across all contexts are candidates; exactly one mapped set with that cardinality resolves, including a multi-face set. The first recipe reference identifies the result-face support used to select a unique preceding support face when direct stable-slot resolution fails. In an `Extrude` bounded-face operand whose first prefix reference carries the recipe's own Design reference, this support includes referenced topology-context faces excluded from the unreferenced candidate set. A selected-face start with several remaining candidates resolves to the sole planar candidate coincident with the selected Sketch plane within the document linear and angular tolerances. A face slot proven by either history or unique sketch-plane coincidence is retained on the native operand. A profile face group also resolves as an unordered historical-face set when exactly one surface carrier in the preceding topology owns a changed-face set whose cardinality equals the group member count, every changed face has one carrier binding, and no member carries contradictory direct or resolved prefix-reference candidates. Prefix-reference syntax with no face candidate is not selection evidence. The projected set follows increasing stable face-slot order. A start or termination face group resolves when every ordered member resolves. Alternate-selector members contribute their complete selected set. A fully structured bounded-face member with two side clauses per node whose positive header equals its parsed node count or a complete historical predecessor-boundary cardinality contributes its complete nonempty unreferenced candidate set. Other members contribute their single proven face. The resolved selection is the member-ordered, deduplicated face list and retains the native group identity. An operand that carries preceding candidates, transition-changed candidates, or historical support contexts does not project its broad active candidate set unless an alternate-selector lane explicitly supplies the selected active set or history has produced explicit resolved face slots or one resolved current-active face. Without that proof, the group stays native for a feature-specific geometry resolver. In an `OffsetFaces` operand of a scope without a role-`0x0000001000000000` group, prefix references with equal selector-field and token-field offsets form one selected-face clause. The intersection of every reference's effective candidates with the preceding topology and transition-changed faces must contain one face. Clauses contribute an ordered, deduplicated historical face list. When no clause resolves, the general unique preceding-candidate and unique transition-changed-candidate proofs apply. Such a scope with a known preceding state retains proven predecessor faces and unresolved operand identities as a partial historical selection when only a proper subset of its ordered face operands resolves.

For a legacy `Extrude` face-group member, let `r` be the `record_index` of its `bounded_face` construction recipe. The result-face lane is the union of effective candidates from every prefix reference whose `design_reference` is `r`; prefix position has no semantic role. A reference's exact-selector candidates are effective when nonempty; otherwise its alternate-selector candidates are effective. The lane is admitted only for a complete counted envelope and node run, with no alternate or unreferenced aggregate candidate lane, and with equality to the aggregate candidate set when that set is nonempty. Select the unique changed preceding face slot when one exists, otherwise the unique preceding face slot. If no preceding slot exists, a unique candidate in the ASM state's source-qualified active-BREP namespace is the current active face; when the result-face lane has one candidate and no source-qualified match is available, that candidate is also the current active face. A current active face is retained as an active identity, not as a historical slot. Multiple source matches or multiple candidates leave the member unresolved.

The legacy face-group envelope stores no independent current-active-face bit. The current-active result is derived from the preceding-slot and source-qualified candidate rules above; it is an active B-rep identity, not an input-state face slot.

A face-recipe continuation header carries `N+4` in the ordinary envelope. A serialized envelope can omit `N+4` and carry `N+5` instead. When neither expected continuation occurs before the enclosing boundary, the first following valid indexed-record header terminates the envelope; its record index has no fixed delta from `N`.

The root and first prelude value of a face-recipe node form an ordered pair of zero-based prefix-operand ordinals. The pair names the two face occurrences incident to one oriented boundary edge. Neither lane has a fixed target-face role. A pair `[0, 0]` can name two distinct faces supplied by operand zero. Zero is an ordinal, and repeated values retain distinct face occurrences.

Each endpoint clause stores a cyclic face fan as `[header_value, *scalars]`. Its `field_count` includes `header_value`. Every fan value is a zero-based prefix-operand ordinal. The second prelude value of a face-recipe node is its endpoint clause count, one or two. A node with two endpoint clauses binds an open boundary edge, one clause for each end vertex. A node with one endpoint clause binds a closed boundary edge, whose start and end are one vertex; its clause is the fan of the two faces that the closed edge bounds, and no other edge meets that vertex. Fan rotation, direction, field order, and multiplicity are retained. The ordinal namespace is the ordered list of prefix operands. References with equal selector-field and token-field offsets belong to one operand, and a reference whose token bytes immediately follow its u32 selector, with no length prefix, extends the preceding operand. In a standard recipe prefix whose u32 at offset 18 counts its operands, each operand opens with a u32 count of its persistent names, which the first name's frame reads as its selector; when the counted names end exactly at the reference suffix, every counted name belongs to its operand. Several Design references in one operand occupy one ordinal; one operand can supply several faces. A topology binding requires candidate face occurrences in one topology state that satisfy both the ordered incident pair and the endpoint fans. Multiple remaining bindings leave the recipe unresolved.

When no other start or termination rule resolves the operand to a historical face slot or an active face, an `Extrude` start or termination bounded-face recipe whose nodes each carry two side clauses can identify one complete loop of a face with several loops. The positive header equals the node count and that loop's edge count. Each node binds to one distinct edge through its incident face pair and both complete endpoint fans in the preceding topology. A unique face with a complete matching loop is the selected historical face.

A face recipe node may carry an optional postlude exactly `[-1, t, -1, 0, 0, -1]` after its topology side clauses. The signed scalar `t` and every postlude word are retained.

An extended topology field program is complete only when it contains one or more repetitions of a nonempty nonnegative field whose first word is positive, `-1`, the exact zero field `[0, 0]`, and a final `-1`. A prefix that merely ends with `-1` is not a complete field program. The compact form is the single word `[0]`.

Face-recipe side clauses use this same compact or extended field-program grammar before their counted topology entries.

The face-node `-1`-delimited grammar uses delimiter-tagged fields: each field delimiter is independently `i32 -1` or `i32 0`. This applies to the root, both one-word prelude fields, and each topology-side field. Delimiter value does not change the retained field value or side structure.

For a `Loft` bounded-face section, the references of the first prefix operand form the target-face clause. The counted recipe header equals both the node count and the target face's boundary-edge count. The Loft transition contains single-face construction bodies copied from its bounded-face inputs; splitting a copied boundary edge may add vertices without changing the source boundary. A unique target-clause face in the exact preceding topology whose ordered boundary vertices occur cyclically, in either sense, on a single-face construction body resolves as the historical section profile. Multi-face result bodies do not participate in this proof.

In an Extrude scope without a sketch-profile operand, profile-role construction groups whose members carry face recipes use the same member envelope. A profile-role group named by another profile-role group's member table is a child selection and is not an additional top-level profile. The member-reference relation is acyclic, every child has one parent, and a child follows its parent in scope-reference order. A root member can name a direct face operand or a child hierarchy with exactly one face-operand leaf. A grouped face operand retains both the scope-reference ordinal of its owning leaf group and its zero-based ordinal within that group's member table; a direct `OffsetFaces` operand has no group ownership. A root whose complete ordered leaf run resolves to historical face slots selects those faces in the scope's preceding input topology. When every root member is a later one-member child group whose bounded-face leaf has a valid paired selector prefix, the direct scope transition also resolves the root as an unordered historical-face set if it deletes exactly one unique preceding face per root member and each deleted face has exactly one surface-carrier binding. This paired-aggregate proof applies even when the member operands retain broader persistent candidate lanes. Increasing stable face-slot order maps that set to root-member order. Otherwise the complete root remains the native profile operand.

When an Extrude profile has one root, that root resolves directly as an active `Faces` profile when every bounded-face leaf has a counted recipe whose positive header equals its parsed node count, has one parsed node offset per node, and has a nonempty candidate-face lane, while its unreferenced, alternate-selector, preceding, changed, historical-support, resolved-slot, and resolved-active-face lanes are all empty. The result is the ordered, deduplicated candidate-face list. This direct proof does not use the profile scope's preceding history; any rejected lane returns the root to the historical proof above.

A sketch-driven `Extrude` scope references a sketch-profile operand in its ordered reference table. Its primary indexed header has record index `N` and is followed by ten zero bytes, `01 + u32 N+3`, six zero bytes, `u32 1`, the LP-UTF16 asset UUID, and an LP-UTF16 decimal Sketch entity suffix. A 94-byte tail ends at the same-index paired header. An 83-byte tail stores u32 `1`, a u32 that is `0` or `1`, eight zero bytes, and u32 `0x41`, then the marked references to `N+2` at tail offset 46, to `N+1` at 60, and to a record at 72, with a zero byte at 71. An 82-byte tail has the 83-byte fields with the references to `N+1` at tail offset 59 and to a record at 71, a zero byte at 70, and two flag bytes, each `0` or `1`, at offsets 57 and 58. The 93-byte compact tail stores the same nonzero u32 twice before its marked references to `N+2`, `N+1`, and a record. The 89-byte compact tail stores that u32 once, so its three marked references are four bytes earlier. In both compact tails, two flag bytes, each `0` or `1`, immediately precede the reference to `N+1`. The suffix resolves to a Sketch-typed Design entity in the same stream and therefore to that sketch's placement and relation graph. A `Revolve` or `Loft` profile group can use the same sketch-profile operand frame as its sole member; the member's scope-reference ordinal supplies the same profile-to-group join used by `Extrude`. A planar `Revolve` profile with this frame selects the complete referenced Sketch. An `Extrude` profile group can list several sketch-profile operands as its members, in scope-reference order.

The singleton Sketch-profile member of either legacy class-330/262 distance Extrude uses primary class 272 and paired class 262. Its marked prefix reference names `N+2`. Record `N+2` holds the counted region selection with the same layout as the ordinary `N+3` selection. Its 93-byte compact tail stores the u32 profile role `0x41` at offset 27. The first tail reference at offset 57 names a unique later empty record with the group-tail marker layout. Two zero flag bytes start at offset 68. The last reference names the owning Extrude scope.

A persistent-selection member with four consecutive nested records can have a 49-byte identity record, measured from its indexed header to the next indexed header. Relative to that identity header, offsets `11..19` are zero, offset `20` is presence byte `1`, offsets `21..32` are zero, offset `33` is a u32 Sketch entity record index, offset `37` is a zero u32, offset `41` is a u32 curve persistent identity, and offset `45` is a zero u32. The u32 at offset `33` is the owning Sketch entity suffix and the u32 at offset `41` is that Sketch curve's primary persistent identity. A complete role-`0x0000004100000000` group using these members selects its ordered non-point Sketch entities, whether or not they form a closed profile loop.

An Extrude profile without a sketch-profile operand may select faces from the scope's preceding ASM topology. Every counted selection member identifies a historical face directly or through face ownership of a loop, coedge, edge, pcurve, curve, vertex, point, or surface. The group resolves when the intersection of every member's owner-face set contains exactly one face, and that face is not on a curved carrier. A face whose one surface binding has a cylinder, axis, or radius row and no plane row is not a profile face; the group stays unresolved. The neutral profile retains that state-local face identity and the complete native selection group. Multiple groups retain first-group order and remove repeated proven faces after their first occurrence. If any group remains unresolved or resolves in a different history state, the scope identity retains the complete ordered profile construction.

Within an `Extrude` scope, `AlongDistance` is the signed first-side extent. A positive value follows the profile normal and a negative value reverses that normal. The sign remains a profile-normal direction state when the profile is retained as a native construction-operand group; it does not require resolving the Sketch placement to a model-space vector. `AgainstDistance` supplies the opposite-side extent; its magnitude is the second-side length. `TaperAngle` is the first-side draft angle and `Side2TaperAngle` is the opposite-side draft angle. Extent scalars use the parameter record's centimetre storage and draft scalars use its radian storage. Neutral Extrude promotion requires every owned parameter to belong to this extent, start-offset, or draft family; another parameter family retains the native operation.

An `Extrude` scope names zero or more counted selection groups in its ordered reference table. A group's primary indexed header has record index `N` and is followed by ten zero bytes, `01 + u32 scope_record_index`, six zero bytes, `u32 member_count`, and `member_count` entries of `01 + u32 member_record_index + six zero bytes`. The member run is followed by a nonzero u32, a finite f64, a second copy of the u32, `01 + u32 N+2 + six zero bytes`, `01 + u8 variant + u8 0`, `01 + u32 N+1 + seven zero bytes`, and `01 + u32 scope_record_index + six zero bytes`. `variant` is zero or one. The same-index paired header begins at primary-record offset `89 + 11 * member_count`. A group can store two zero bytes in place of `01 + u8 variant + u8 0`. That group has no variant, and its paired header begins at primary-record offset `88 + 11 * member_count`.

The standard `Loft` scope stores its result operation as a u32 at primary-scope offset 29, or 28 in its three-flag form. The compact fixed-prefix form stores it at offset 25, or 24 in its three-flag form. A standard `Sweep` stores the same operation enum at offset 25. The values are `1 = join`, `2 = cut`, `3 = intersect`, and `4 = new body`. New-body does not determine whether a Sweep is solid or surface; the dimensional kind of every bound output body determines the neutral result family. The section list and the rail list of the Loft scope body assign the section, rail, and existing-body groups. A fixed `Sweep` has one role-`0x0000004100000000` profile group followed by one role-`0x0000000500000000` path group. A guide-rail Sweep has a second role-`0x0000000500000000` group after the path group; it identifies the guide rail. The profile group's sole member can be the sketch-profile frame defined for Extrude. Its compact class-477 form has 93 bytes from the end of the Sketch entity suffix through the byte before the paired header. The u32 scalar index at tail offsets 41 and 53 is equal and nonzero, marked references at 57 and 70 name records `N+2` and `N+1`, and the marked owning-scope reference starts at 82. The 89-byte form omits the second scalar index; the three marked references instead start at offsets 53, 66, and 78. A role-`0x0000004100000000` group whose sole member is a nested entity-selection frame selects one exact planar Sketch entity: the first identity is the owning Sketch entity suffix and the second is the curve's primary persistent identity. The selected entity is an ordered profile and may be open for a surface Sweep. The profile group's member can instead be a topology-recipe selection of type `5662F619-2281-4AD9-93DC-1FCFDA1062E7`; that member carries the bounded-face recipe operand envelope, and its recipe candidates are evaluated in the Sweep scope's preceding history topology. The path group's sole member can use the same frame, with the first identity naming the owning planar Sketch entity suffix and the second naming the primary persistent identity of that Sketch's sole curve. A Boolean Sweep can additionally carry one existing-body group as its first construction group. The group has role `0x0000000400000000` at scope-reference ordinal zero, or role `0x0000000800000000` at scope-reference ordinal seven. A new-body Sweep carries no existing-body group. A six-lane Sweep scope owns six fixed scalar records with owner-local ordinals zero through five: `AlongDistance`, `AgainstDistance`, `AlongRailDistance`, `AgainstRailDistance`, `TwistAngle`, and `TaperAngle`. A compact Sweep scope stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, the u32 operation enum at offset 21, and byte `1` at offset 25. The [compact Sweep prologue](../layouts/f3d.md#compact_sweep_prologue) gives this layout. A compact six-lane Sweep scope owns the six fixed scalar records of the six-lane form. The compact two-lane Sweep scope uses primary class tag `372`, paired class tag `260`, payload length 423, and nine reference members. It owns two fixed scalar records with owner-local ordinals zero and one (`AlongDistance` and `AgainstDistance`); rail-distance, twist, and taper lanes are absent. Each scalar primary record is 100, 104, or 105 bytes to its same-index paired header. It stores the scope reference at offset 25, the owner-local ordinal at offset 35, and the finite f64 value at offset 40. AlongDistance and AgainstDistance are fractions in the closed interval from zero through one. When a guide rail is present, AlongRailDistance and AgainstRailDistance are the corresponding directed fractions of that rail in the same interval. An unguided single-path form stores one in both rail-distance lanes. The full-path form stores one in both path-distance lanes; a one-sided partial sweep stores zero in AgainstDistance and its terminal path fraction in AlongDistance.

Sweep scopes also carry a role-`0x0000004300000000` group followed by a path group, or a profile-carrier group followed by path and face groups without a separate profile-selection group. The compact Sweep prefix also occurs with a zero byte at the marker position in the [compact Sweep prologue](../layouts/f3d.md#compact_sweep_prologue), while the preceding u32 word is `1`.

After complete native admission, remaining Sweep definitions project as partial neutral Sweeps. Independently readable owner-local scalar lanes retain their values, including zero twist and taper. Missing or ambiguous values and selections remain unresolved. A `sweep:source` property retains the original scope candidates, construction groups, parameter owners, ordered parameter records, prefix bytes and bounded referenced record fragments. It also retains the source operation when the neutral result mode cannot carry it. Result-mode inference requires complete output binding and homogeneous known output kinds; a missing operation does not become new-body. A profile carrier without an exact neutral region binding retains its own indexed-header identity instead of selecting the whole Sketch. The assumptions and unresolved controls are recorded in [DR-620 and DR-621](f3d-open-items.md#dr-620-partial-sweep-sections-and-controls).

The legacy Boolean-Loft body carrier is 87 bytes from its primary indexed header to the same-index paired header. It starts with the indexed header at offsets 0 through 10, has ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, and uses offset 21 as a `01` presence byte. The owning scope record is the u32 at offset 22; offsets 26 through 31 are zero; u32 `member_count` is at offset 32 and its one same-segment member reference starts at offset 36. The opaque u32 index is at offset 47, the finite f64 scalar is at offset 51, and the repeated u32 index is at offset 59. A marked reference to record `N+2` starts at offset 63, flags `[00 00]` are at offset 74, and a marked reference to record `N+1` starts at offset 76. The same-index paired header starts at offset 87. The legacy body carrier with an owner tail is 99 bytes from its primary indexed header to the same-index paired header. It uses the 87-byte carrier fields through offset 86, stores a zero byte at offset 87 and a marked reference to the owning scope at offset 88, and its same-index paired header starts at offset 99. The legacy body carrier with a three-byte flag block is 100 bytes from its primary indexed header to the same-index paired header. It uses the 87-byte carrier fields through offset 73, stores flags `[01 00 00]` at offset 74, a marked reference to record `N+1` at offset 77, a zero byte at offset 88, and a marked reference to the owning scope at offset 89, and its same-index paired header starts at offset 100. These lengths are the only legacy body-carrier forms. The carrier is scope-reference ordinal zero.

The `Emboss` fixed-prefix form has nine ordered references. Its operation prefix is the `emboss_scope_prefix` record in `docs/layouts/f3d.toml`. After the indexed header, it stores nine zero bytes, two native u32 control words, the Depth-owner reference, an auxiliary selection-group reference, and the Horizontal Distance-owner reference. A u32 count of one and two native u64 values follow. The next three references name the Rotation Angle owner, the target-face group, and the Vertical Distance owner. A u32 count of one precedes the sketch-profile group reference. Twelve zero bytes, a u32 count of one, and a second reference to the same target-face group close the prefix. Every prefix reference is a present eleven-byte same-segment reference. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 null GUID and three zero bytes separate the prefix from the common ordered reference table.

An `Emboss` native pair contains two u64 values. The one-control-word head and two-control-word head use `emboss_single_control_head` and `emboss_two_control_head` in `docs/layouts/f3d.toml`. Both heads contain the indexed header, nine zero bytes, the control lane, the Depth-owner reference, the auxiliary-group reference, the Horizontal Distance-owner reference, and a u32 pair count. That many `emboss_native_pair` records follow the head.

The `emboss_counted_suffix` layout starts immediately after the native pair run. It contains the Rotation Angle-owner reference, the target-face group reference, the Vertical Distance-owner reference, a u32 count of one, the profile-group reference, twelve zero bytes, a u32 count of one, and a second reference to the same target-face group. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 null GUID and three zero bytes precede the common reference count. Every prefix and table reference is a present eleven-byte same-segment reference. The seven prefix target identities are distinct and nonzero. Each occurs once in the common table, whose record indices are in strictly increasing order. Exactly one control-lane reading closes the prefix at the common reference count. The control words and native pairs are independent native values.

The `Emboss` profile-first nine-reference table uses present eleven-byte same-segment references. It contains, in order, the sketch-profile group, its sole member, the target-face group, its sole member, the Depth owner, the Horizontal Distance owner, the Vertical Distance owner, the Rotation Angle owner, and the auxiliary group. These record identities are distinct. The sketch-profile group has role `0x0000004100000000`. The target-face group has role `0x0000001000000000`; its member uses the bounded-face recipe envelope. The auxiliary group uses the compact counted selection envelope and retains its independent member run. It is separate from the target-face group.

The `Emboss` scalar-owner references bind parameters with source kinds `Depth`, `Horizontal Distance`, `Vertical Distance`, and `Rotation Angle`, respectively. Each owner and its parameter belong to the same Design stream and the same Emboss scope. Each parameter points back to its owner, and the two evaluated values are equal. Depth and the two distances are signed finite lengths in centimetres; Rotation Angle is a finite angle in radians. The declared unit token controls expression display and does not change these stored units. Length unit tokens are `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, or `ft`; angle unit tokens are `deg` or `rad`. The two native control words and the native u64 pair are independent fields. The counted pair does not replace any reference in the ordered reference table.

An `Emboss` fixed-prefix sketch-profile group uses the sketch-profile operand frame defined above as its sole member. Its asset UUID and decimal Sketch entity suffix bind the selected Sketch in the same Design stream. The Sketch can contain curves and text. The entity link identifies the Sketch; it does not select every curve or every text contour in that Sketch.

Every `Extrude`, `Extrusion`, `Fillet`, `Chamfer`, `Draft`, `Loft`, `Sweep`, `Pipe`, `OffsetFaces`, `SurfaceOffset`, `MoveFace`, `DeleteFace`, `SurfaceDeleteFace`, and `Thicken` scope names one or more counted construction-operand groups in its ordered reference table. Counted groups referenced by the localized Fillet names `Congé`, `Abrundung`, and `Arredondamento` and the localized Chamfer name `Chanfrein` use the same group form as `Fillet` and `Chamfer`; these localized scope forms do not require every selection to use a counted group. A group's primary indexed header has record index `N`. Its payload is a zero leading-block byte, the property presence byte and the property block that byte gates, `u32 member_count` and that many references, two optional references, `u32 trailing_count` and that many references, `u32 0`, `u32 role`, ten zero bytes, `u32 ordinal`, `f64 scalar`, and a second copy of `ordinal` that one container generation omits. Every member is also present in the owning scope's ordered reference table. The member run and trailing-reference run may be empty, and the two optional references are both present or both absent. A trailing reference selects a grammar through its target record: persistent-selection groups name identity wrappers, placed-selection groups name the affine transform frame defined below, and SplitFace and SurfaceDeleteFace groups can name a compact flag record. The compact flag record is an indexed header followed by ten zero bytes, marker byte `01`, a boolean byte, and terminator byte `00`. Every member of a Fillet-family or Chamfer-family group has a complete edge-recipe operand frame or fixed persistent selection-identity frame owned by the same scope. Recipe-backed members can also expose their persistent identity. An identity proves one native selection operand but does not by itself prove one neutral topology edge. Within an `Extrude` or `Extrusion` scope, u64 role `0x0000000800000000` identifies existing-body operands, `0x0000004100000000` identifies the sketch-profile operand, and `0x0000001100000000` identifies face operands. Role `0x0000000500000000` identifies a target-shape group for a one-sided to-entity extent; its members are whole-body recipe operands. Within an `OffsetFaces`, `MoveFace`, `DeleteFace`, or `SurfaceDeleteFace` scope, role `0x0000001000000000` identifies selected-face operands.
