Within a `SurfaceOffset` scope, role `0x0000004100000000` identifies bounded-face support operands. Within a `Sweep` scope, role `0x0000004100000000` identifies the profile and ordered role-`0x0000000500000000` groups identify the path followed by the optional guide rail. Within an `EdgeFlange` scope, each role `0x0000000800000000` group has one edge-recipe member, and the role `0x0000004300000000` group has one corresponding edge-recipe member per role-`0x0000000800000000` group in the same order. A `Hem` scope has one single-member group of each of those roles. Within a `Loft` scope, the section list and the rail list of the scope body assign the section and rail groups, and the one unnamed group of a Boolean Loft is its existing-body group. The profile group's first member is the scope's sketch-profile record; subsequent members are counted profile-selection groups in source order. Face groups retain scope-reference order: a selected-face start contributes the first face group, and a one-sided to-face termination contributes the following face group. Absence of an existing-body group means the operation has no existing-body Boolean operand. The tail after the ordinal copy is a reference to record `N+2` or to the independent empty record defined below, a flag block, a reference to record `N+1`, a zero byte, a reference to the owning scope record, the same-index paired header, and one further reference. The flag block's last byte is the closing flag and the byte before it is `variant`, which is zero or one; one container generation prefixes the block with a further byte. The closing flag is zero or one. Neither the repeated ordinal nor that prefix byte is announced by another member, so the tail settles both: exactly one of the four readings ends at the next indexed header carrying record index `N`. In the non-Sketch feature families above, `ordinal` is nonzero and does not decrease with the record index, and the second copy equals the first. `scalar` is nonnegative and finite and may be zero. `role` occupies the high word of a u64 whose low word is zero, and it is not bounded to one byte. A localized edge-treatment group is complete only when the trailing-reference run's first record starts the identity chain defined below.

A `ReplaceFace` scope replaces selected target faces with replacement support. The ReplaceFace prologue contains an indexed header, nine zero bytes and a prefix flag. Flag `00` is followed by the Boolean control. Flag `01` is followed by a u32 word and the Boolean control. A u32-counted run of marked replacement-group references and a u32-counted run of marked target-group references follow the control. A 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 identifier and three zero bytes close the prefix at the ordered-reference count. Each marked reference is `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`. Replacement groups have role `0x0000000900000000` for body or face recipes, or role `0x0000002100000000` for entity support. Target groups have role `0x0000001000000000`. Group members retain their owning scope and ordered-reference positions. Whole-body replacement recipes select their complete input-state face set; face recipes select their retained historical faces.

A shifted legacy one-sided-to-face Extrude from the profile plane with direction and face-extend words `[1, 2]` and an unmarked operation prefix can use an independent empty record in the tail of its body, profile, and termination groups. These groups have roles `0x0000000400000000`, `0x0000004100000000`, and `0x0000001200000000`, respectively. The singleton profile group of the legacy class-330/262 symmetric distance Extrude and the singleton body and profile groups of the legacy class-330/262 blind Cut can also use this tail. Each such group stores the repeated ordinal, the marked empty-record reference, two zero flag bytes, the marked reference to `N+1`, a zero byte, and the marked owning-scope reference before the same-index paired header. The empty record has an index greater than `N` that occurs in exactly one indexed header in the Design stream. The empty group-tail record is its indexed header and eighteen zero bytes, followed by the next indexed header. Its header follows the paired group header.

In a one-sided-to-face `Extrude` or `Extrusion`, role `0x0000001200000000` is the legacy spelling of the face-termination group. In the exact class-`296`/`261` 536-byte two-sided-to-faces envelope, the same role identifies each face-termination group. The same role in a `Thicken` scope retains the bounded-face meaning defined above.

An `Extrude` or `Extrusion` existing-body group uses role `0x0000000400000000` or `0x0000000800000000`. Each member is a whole-body recipe operand. In the legacy class-330/262 blind Cut, its class-311/262 member stores an empty persistent-reference table and serialization form zero. The nested reference names the class-301 record `N+2` after class-328 record `N+1`. The body recipe lies in that nested record. The class-291 profile group starts at the body recipe's closing header `N+3`.

A role-`0x0000000800000000` group is the existing-body group of a Boolean Loft when neither list of the Loft scope body names it.

A Form result-owner record of type `493A89BA-E146-498D-9033-2783FE727AF4`, version 1, with base type `D0D7E795-ECF7-48A8-A7A3-F983C5A29F8B`, is 81 bytes from its indexed header to its same-index paired header. The owner frame stores fourteen zero bytes, a marked owning-scope reference, twenty-four zero bytes, a marked BodyPresentation reference, three zero bytes, a repeated marked owning-scope reference, and two zero bytes. The referenced BodyPresentation has type `6CCF41D5-40BE-48ED-A834-18F3EAED6C57`, version 1. This record contains no cage count and no serializer entry name. A result-owner reference does not establish a cage-to-archive identity join.

A compact counted selection envelope starts with an indexed header, ten zero bytes, a marked owning-scope reference, `u32 member_count`, and ordered member references. Each marked reference is `u8 1 + u64 record index + u16 0` and occupies 11 bytes. The prefix through `member_count` is 36 bytes. The tail starts at `T = 36 + 11 * member_count`. It stores `u32 ordinal`, a finite nonnegative `f64 scalar`, the same `u32 ordinal`, a marked independent record reference, a two- or three-byte flag block, a marked reference to record `N+1`, a zero byte, and a repeated marked owning-scope reference. The first tail reference need not name `N+2`. The two-byte flag block is `[variant, 0]`; the three-byte block is `[1, variant, 0]`, where `variant` is zero or one. The two-byte-flag tail is 52 bytes: its ordinal, scalar, repeated ordinal, first reference, flags, next reference, zero byte, and owner reference start at tail offsets 0, 4, 12, 16, 27, 29, 40, and 41. The three-byte-flag tail is 53 bytes: the fields after the flags start at tail offsets 30, 41, and 42. The same-index paired header starts immediately after that tail. The complete primary frame length is `88 + 11 * member_count` or `89 + 11 * member_count`. The ordinal is a full u32, not a u16 member-flag field. Form selection groups use this envelope and the typed tracking members defined in §1.1.1.

A Sketch-owned retained input group uses role `0x0000008100000000`. It has one member, one trailing reference, `variant = 0`, and either two null auxiliary references or two present auxiliary references. Its member is a topology-recipe selection of type `5662F619-2281-4AD9-93DC-1FCFDA1062E7` at version 1, 2, or 3, a direct persistent selection of type `5A1BF548-241F-46FD-9FB5-E4B05126EB9D` at version 1, or a whole-body recipe of type `9716F783-676D-42E0-93F9-EBF273E7C035` at version 1. These member types share base GUID `6144EA59-3ACA-4172-9F14-A6531E94D69B`. A Sketch can own multiple groups in scope-reference order. Their ordinal values can differ within one Sketch. The first reference after the optional ordinal copy names an independent registered record; it need not name `N+2`.

A `C-Pattern` or `R-Pattern` scope that repeats faces has a role `0x0000001000000000` group at ordered reference one. Each selected face is one member, the members follow the group in the ordered reference table, a construction-operand identity carries the group, and each member is followed by a `bounded_face_recipe_data` record.

Within `C-Pattern`, `R-Pattern`, and `PathPattern` scopes, role `0x0000010000000000` identifies a path-carried seed group. It has no ordinary member, two present ordered auxiliary references, and one trailing reference. Neither auxiliary reference contributes an ordinary member. Each auxiliary reference names an extended construction-operand path record `N`. Its indexed header is followed by 28 zero bytes, `u32 3` at offset 39 or `u32 2` in the same place, and 13 zero bytes. Byte 56 is `01`, and the u64 persistent entity reference is at offset 57. The placement starts at offset 65: three zero bytes, a rigid row-major 4×4 f64 matrix, and one zero byte form the transform placement; the bytes `00 00 01 00` form the compact placement. A marked reference to the owning scope, a marked reference to record `N+2`, six zero bytes, and the indexed header of record `N+1` follow the placement. Validation admits the seed group only when both auxiliary references decode as such paths.

A construction-operand affine transform is a 152-byte indexed record. Its header is followed by eleven zero bytes, sixteen row-major f64 values, and bytes `01 00`. The matrix is finite and rigid, and its last row is `[0, 0, 0, 1]`. The following indexed record begins at offset 152. Its stored record index is independent of the transform record index; it is greater but need not be consecutive.

The affine and compact relative-placement carriers have type GUID `2DF7DA30-A4E4-4260-AFD1-D9C7154CB44B`, base GUID `872045B4-F653-4691-9752-ABC7684834BF`, version zero, and module `EntityTracking`. A compact relative-placement carrier is a 24-byte indexed record. Its header is followed by ten zero bytes, byte `01`, one boolean, and byte `00`. Boolean `true` represents identity relative placement. When the two auxiliary paths supply rigid placements `A` and `B` in encoded order, the single-matrix carrier stores `inverse(A) * B`. Absence of the paths does not define an identity path pair.

The dual construction-operand transform is 278 bytes. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, two ordered finite rigid row-major 4×4 matrices, and one zero byte. The matrices begin at record offsets 21 and 149. Another indexed record or the end of the Design stream follows at offset 278; its record index is independent of the transform record index.

A construction-operand auxiliary selection path is an indexed record with index `N`. Its header is followed by ten zero bytes, byte `01`, and a u64 persistent entity identity. The expanded form then stores three zero bytes, a finite rigid row-major 4×4 f64 transform, one zero byte, marked references to the owning feature scope and record `N+2`, and six zero bytes. The compact form instead stores bytes `00 00 variant 00`, where `variant` is zero or one, followed by the same two marked references and six zero bytes. The indexed record immediately after either form has index `N+1`.

A construction-operand entity-tracking path starts with an indexed wrapper record `N`. Ten zero bytes follow its header. Byte `01`, the u64 value `N+1`, and three zero bytes select an adjacent carrier record `N+1`. The carrier header is followed by ten zero bytes, u32 values `1, 0, 1`, a u32 lane with value `2` or `3`, a u64 primary identity, a zero u64, u32 one, a signed i32 selector, a u32 kind, and a zero u64. Two optional u64 related identities follow in order; each uses u32 zero for absence or u32 one and the u64 value for presence. The indexed record after both optionals has index `N+2`. An affine-transform record or one or more 24-byte identity wrappers may precede the tracking path. A fixed persistent identity may follow it.

The tracking wrapper's registered type GUID is `335CC7BD-BBE5-40AA-9E8C-5EC99D427A3A`, its base GUID is `5C069ACB-169F-4555-9792-815B4671DDA0`, and its version is zero. The carrier's type GUID is `2DEE34BE-FA70-4D54-979C-164D86FDA786`, its base GUID is `70F5E801-1E8E-436E-8A09-36487F8A2859`, and its version is two. Both registrations use module `EntityTracking`. Each record's class selects its registering type-table row, and its primary-index entry supplies its exact physical header offset.

In this construction-path grammar, `kind` is the positive fragment count of the primary persistent Sketch curve, and `selector` is the one-based ordinal of its selected fragment. The signed storage lane satisfies `1 <= selector <= kind`. The primary and related persistent identities in the serialized tracking graph define the participating curves. Intersections and shared endpoints within that graph delimit fragments; curves outside the graph do not add cuts. The two optional related identities retain the ordered boundaries of the selected fragment. The same related identity can occupy both lanes. An unsplit curve can omit both and use `(selector, kind) = (1, 1)`.

Fragment numbering follows the serialized primary curve's parameter direction. An open curve with `m` distinct interior graph events has `m+1` fragments; fragment one starts at the parameter start. A closed curve with `m > 0` distinct graph events has `m` fragments; fragment one runs from the last event through the native parameter seam to the first event, and the remaining fragments follow increasing parameter between events. A closed curve without an event has one fragment. An Extrude selection member can follow a tracking path directly. The path selects one fragment of its primary Sketch curve and does not by itself select a profile region. Coincident events merge at the Sketch tolerance. A generated tracking path uses the direction, parameterization, and seam serialized with its primary curve.

The carrier immediately follows the complete wrapper. A construction chain continues only across physically adjacent pairs that each satisfy the complete wrapper and carrier grammar. A record with the inner carrier tuple alone does not extend the chain. Construction ownership also requires the construction-group reference to the chain root or its identity or affine-transform envelope.

A `DeleteFace` scope has at least two ordered references. Its u32 ordered-reference count is at offset `P`, which is 123, 127, or 131, and the table of `R` ordered references follows it. The first `DeleteFace` UTF-16LE code unit is eight bytes after the table, at offset `P + 12 + 11R`. A fixed scope tail of 76, 77, or 78 bytes follows the kind and ends at the same-index paired header. Reference zero is its sole role-`0x0000001000000000` construction-operand group; the remaining references are exactly that group's ordered, nonempty bounded-face members. The operation removes those selected faces and extends adjacent faces to heal the body. A named `DeleteFace` or `SurfaceDeleteFace` scope uses the common variable label tail; removing its serialized label code units leaves the 78-byte tail extent. The label assigns the display name and preserves the face-removal operation and its healing mode.

A `DeleteFace` bounded-face member whose nodes each carry one or two side clauses selects the unique complete face boundary in the preceding topology that binds every counted node. The positive program header equals the node count and the boundary-edge count. Each prefix operand of the ordinal namespace above is one zero-based operand ordinal; the effective face candidates of its references to positive Design references form that operand's face lane. A negative Design reference names an earlier feature that changed the face, and its tag matches every face that feature changed under the same token, so it adds no face to the lane. Each node's ordered incident pair binds the two face occurrences of one boundary edge. A node with two endpoint clauses binds an open boundary edge, one complete cyclic face fan for each end vertex, with face multiplicity and cyclic adjacency preserved. A node with one endpoint clause binds a closed boundary edge, whose start and end are one vertex; its clause is the fan of the two faces that the closed edge bounds, and no other edge meets that vertex. Cyclic rotation and reversal of the topology traversal preserve the fan match. Every node binds exactly one distinct edge, and the nodes cover the boundary exactly. The group selection is the member-ordered face list in one preceding state.

The scope's preceding and current state identities delimit the complete ASM transition interval of a healed `DeleteFace`. Each transition's predecessor agrees with the history header link. The operation deletes every selected face, and healing can delete further faces. When the group has `N` distinct members and the interval's deletion sets contain exactly `N` distinct faces, all present in the preceding topology, the selected face set is those faces. This cardinality proof requires disjoint face insertion and deletion sets across the interval. Each selected face is absent after the interval.

The compact prologue, with `P` 127, stores `1` at offset 20, a u32 zero at 21, u32 one at 33, and the marked reference to reference zero at 37. The legacy prologue, with `P` 123, stores `0` at offset 20 and has no u32 zero, so u32 one is at 29 and the marked reference to reference zero is at 33. Its ordered reference table, role-`0x0000001000000000` construction-operand group, bounded-face members, and healed-face operation are the same as the standard `DeleteFace` form. The primary and paired class tags of this layout vary between files: the pairs `264`/`262`, `383`/`263`, `373`/`266`, `399`/`257`, `442`/`257`, and `447`/`262` all occur. They do not select the layout.

A `DeleteFace` scope with typed references has the same prologue fields, ordered references and operation, with every reference stored as a 51-byte typed reference. `P` is 163 after the legacy prologue and 167 after the compact prologue. The first `DeleteFace` code unit is at offset `P + 12 + 51R`, and a fixed tail of 196 bytes follows the kind and ends at the same-index paired header.

`DéplacerFace` is the localized kind name of `MoveFace`. Its prologue carries marked references to a transform record and a face group, followed by a counted ordered-reference table. A complete face-group run consists of a role-`0x0000001000000000` construction-operand group and its ordered, nonempty members immediately after the group. The group is at reference zero, or reference one when the transform is first. The transform reference can occur before or after additional ordered references outside that run. The registered rigid-transform family has type GUID `84E6245F-1CDC-4FB8-8048-163A85FAD3F0`, version `2` or `3`. The marker-one prologue stores `1` at offset 20, a u32 zero at 21, and byte `1` at 25. The marked reference to the transform record is at 26, u32 one is at 37, the marked reference to the group is at 41, and the ordered-reference count is at 131. The marker-zero prologue stores `0` at offset 20, has no u32 zero, and places every later field four bytes earlier: byte `1` at 21, the transform reference at 22, u32 one is at 33, the reference to the group is at 37, and the ordered-reference count is at 127. The nine bytes between the indexed header and the marker are prefix fields. The selected transform record uses the form and matrix byte grammar of a `Move` rigid-transform frame. Its marked record identity is independent of its ordinal in the ordered table. The fixed prologue layouts are `move_face_marker_zero_prologue` and `move_face_marker_one_prologue`. The two marked references can also use the 51-byte inline-typed local spelling of §3.1. Both references then use that spelling: the transform reference stores type GUID `84E6245F-1CDC-4FB8-8048-163A85FAD3F0`, the group reference stores type GUID `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841`, and the ordered-reference table uses 51-byte inline-typed local references. The inline-typed marker-zero prologue stores byte `1` at offset 21, the transform reference at 22, u32 one at 73, and the group reference at 77, and the ordered-reference count is at 207. The inline-typed marker-one prologue places every field after the u32 zero four bytes later, and its ordered-reference count is at 211. Its layouts are `move_face_typed_marker_zero_prologue` and `move_face_typed_marker_one_prologue`.

The transitions of a `MoveFace` or `OffsetFaces` feature state the feature's selection. A `MoveFace` translation can span more than one transition, and the input state is the scope's preceding state. The motion moves every selected face, and a face tangent to a selected face can move with it. A surface row follows a translation when its origin shifts by the translation and its normal, axis, and radius stay; this holds when the translation lies in the plane of the surface. A plane row follows an offset distance `d` when its normal stays and its origin shifts by `|d|` along that normal. A cylinder row follows `d` when its axis line stays and its radius changes by `|d|`. When the transitions from the input state delete no face, every face they update has one plane or cylinder row in the input and output states, and the updated faces whose rows follow the motion number exactly the distinct members of the role-`0x0000001000000000` group, those faces are the selection in the input state. The faces of one surface move together. When the group has one distinct member and the faces whose rows follow the motion are two or more faces of one input surface, those faces are the selection when the member's recipes state no selection and one nonnegative Design reference of the member's recipe names exactly that face set.

The members of a `MoveFace` or `OffsetFaces` group also state the selection. Each member is a bounded-face recipe and selects the face of the input state that the `DeleteFace` bounded-face rule resolves for it. When every distinct member resolves to a face and the faces are distinct, they are the selection. When the transitions also state a selection, the two selections are equal.

The input state of a `Shell` feature is the scope's preceding state. The face recipes of the role-`0x0000001000000000` group bind their persistent Design references to tags in that input state. A bounded-face member selects an input face through a complete boundary loop that matches its counted node program. The positive header equals the node count and that loop's edge count. A complete assignment pairs every node with one distinct loop edge through its incident face pair and both complete endpoint fans in the input topology. The selected face is unique across all complete assignments. The group's distinct recipe faces are the removed faces, in the order of their first member. For a group whose recipes do not resolve, the following wall comparison applies. The shell adds a wall to each face it keeps: a face at the wall offset whose plane row is parallel to the kept face's plane row and offset by that distance along its normal, or whose cylinder row has the same axis line and a radius that differs by that distance. The wall offset is the wall thickness, or half of it for a shell on both sides. The transition updates or deletes each removed face and adds no wall for it. When every face that the transition updates or deletes has one plane or cylinder row in the input state, and the changed faces without a wall number exactly the distinct members of the role-`0x0000001000000000` group, those faces are the removed faces in the input state.

Unhealed surface-face removal serializes as `SurfaceDeleteFace`, including the [wide surface-delete prologue](../layouts/f3d.md) form. Its u32 ordered-reference count is at offset `P`, which is 123, 127, 128, 131, 134, 138, or 142. The ordered-reference table, the first `SurfaceDeleteFace` UTF-16LE code unit at offset `P + 12 + 11R`, and the 76-, 77-, or 78-byte fixed scope tail follow as in the `DeleteFace` frame. Its reference table, its sole role-`0x0000001000000000` construction-operand group, and that group's ordered bounded-face members follow the `DeleteFace` rules above. The operation removes the selected faces and leaves the adjacent faces unchanged, so the result is an open sheet rather than a healed solid.

For a `SurfaceDeleteFace` bounded-face member, the selected historical face set resolves when its counted program has one opener-framed node for each positive header count, its preceding candidate slots are unique and nonempty, its changed candidate slots equal that complete preceding set, and its historical contexts form a one-to-one cover of those slots. Each context has exactly one preceding face equal to its active slot, exactly one changed preceding face equal to that slot, and exactly one complete boundary whose face is that slot. The resolved selection is the sorted preceding slot set. A member that fails any condition retains the native construction group; changed-face cardinality alone is not selection evidence.

An `UnStitch` scope separates selected faces from their bodies, and each selected face becomes an individual surface body. Its type GUID is `8DA2F4A9-C420-419B-AD5D-9CC901DF0B78`, base `2EDC2536-D95B-4469-8ACA-DC07124D9C43`, version `0`. The compact UnStitch prologue stores ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, a selection flag byte at offset 21, and the u32 identity count `N` at offset 22. The marked UnStitch prologue stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19, u32 `1` at offset 20, a zero byte at offset 24, the selection flag byte at offset 25, and `N` at offset 26. The extended UnStitch prologue adds a zero u32 at offset 26 and stores `N` at offset 30. With `S` the offset of `N`, three counted runs of marked references follow: `N` identity references, one for each member face in order; a u32 count `B` with `B` source references; and u32 `1` with the face-group reference. Each marked reference is `01 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`. The 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` and three zero bytes follow, so the u32 ordered-reference count is at offset `S + 91 + 11(N + B + 1)`. The ordered-reference table has `N + 1` references: the face group, a role-`0x0000001000000000` construction-operand group, followed by that group's `N` ordered bounded-face members. The first `UnStitch` UTF-16LE code unit is eight bytes after the table, and the 76-, 77-, or 78-byte fixed scope tail or the common variable label tail follows as in the `DeleteFace` frame. The operation removes each member face from its body and leaves the face geometry unchanged.

A `SurfaceTrim` scope has two nonempty counted construction-operand groups that partition its ordered references. Reference zero is the target group with role `0x0000000400000000`. Its body-recipe members follow it contiguously, and each member selects a target body in the preceding body state. The next reference is the tool group, and every remaining reference is one of its members. A tool group with role `0x0000002100000000` contains entity-selection operands for trimming curves or body-recipe operands for trimming bodies. A tool group with role `0x0000000900000000` contains one face-recipe operand. Its complete terminal program `[0, −1]` selects the trimming face in the preceding topology. The scope's record-timestamp table is followed by one indexed record and then the BRep-cell table. The table's primary header and its same-index paired header bound the table payload. Ten zero bytes follow the primary header. A u32 cell count is at offset 21. The positive count opens entries at offset 25; each entry is 19 bytes: a marked indexed-record reference at entry offset 0 and a positive u64 entry value at entry offset 11. Each entry references a distinct indexed record. A u32 trailing value follows the entry run and is at least every entry value. A zero u32 follows the trailing value, then the paired header. When the entry count is less than the trailing value and the entry values are distinct, each entry is a cell selected for removal, its value is the one-based cell ordinal, and the trailing value is the total cell count of the operation's partition. The BRep-cell table is an operation carrier outside both construction-operand groups. The selected removal set is the complete trim-region semantic. A neutral `TrimSurface` retains that set as the `cells` form of its `keep` field; `Inside` and `Outside` apply to operations whose source semantics reduce to one canonical region.

The `Unfold` scope has type GUID `EC187027-FF97-48A3-8031-F923807E630B`, version 0. The `Refold` scope has type GUID `483D584F-29AA-46DA-ABA2-F139B0ED8100`, version 1. Their fold-scope prefix contains the indexed header, nine zero bytes and a nullable extension. Extension byte zero ends the extension; byte one precedes a zero u32. The Unfold prefix then stores one control byte and four local references in order: a construction group, common sheet-metal settings, a wrapper, and another construction group. The first, second and fourth targets occur in the scope's ordered reference table. The wrapper has type GUID `2E3AC990-483D-4A55-8662-C064B976A957`. Both construction groups have type GUID `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841` and role `0x10`. The Unfold body group uses role `0x04`; the Refold selection group uses role `0x08`. Local references use the compact or inline-type form from §3.1 References.

The `UnfoldRefoldGroupMode` carrier has type GUID `99F375B3-8331-47DE-9E99-9A0882F2ED29`, version 0. Its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes, the LP-UTF16 name `UnfoldRefoldGroupMode`, a u32 mode, byte one, a u32 member count, the ordered local member references and five zero bytes. Its same-index paired header bounds the primary frame. Member order is independent of numeric record-index order. The carrier can contain intermediate operations between an Unfold and a Refold.

The mask-and-slots settings prefix uses six optional references in version 1, seven in version 2 and nine in version 3. Version 1 local references can carry inline type GUIDs. After the optional references, versions 1 and 2 store the rule reference and four zero bytes. The presentation reference, zero byte and owner reference close the primary frame.

A version-0 sheet-metal rule stores a [u32 settings-reference count](../layouts/f3d.md) at offset 21, after the indexed header and ten zero bytes. That count bounds the local settings references that start at offset 25. Each compact reference is 11 bytes. A u32 rule word follows the reference run. Version 1 places the rule word directly after the ten zero bytes. The first entry is an LP-UTF16 expression and an independent finite f64. A first entry named `Thickness` stores the sheet thickness in centimetres. A material trailer contains a finite f64, an LP-UTF16 material name, LP-UTF16 `Thickness` and an explicit positive finite thickness in centimetres.

The construction groups of a `Bend` scope carry roles `0x10` and `0x21`. A `Bend` scope owns one `BendAngle` parameter for each angular input. Its evaluated angle uses radians and retains its sign. An explicit radius override has source kind `BendRadius`; its evaluated length uses centimetres. The ordered scope references carry the construction groups, selection operands, and parameter owners. The parameter owner retains the association between a value and the scope reference table.

A distance-form single-edge `EdgeFlange` scope has `8 + W` ordered references: the selection wrapper, the role-`0x08` group and its edge-recipe operand, the height and angle parameter owners, the role-`0x43` aggregate group and its aggregate edge-recipe operand, the settings record, and `W` width-distance parameter owners. The ordered reference table is in record-index order, so no role has a fixed table position. Each role is named by a marked slot in the fixed operation section instead, the recipe-backed operand of a group is the record three after that group, and the `W` entries no role claims are the width-distance owners. `W` carries the edge-width mode: zero spans the complete edge, one centres the flange on it, and two measures the flange from each end. `W` is at most two.

A single-edge to-object `EdgeFlange` scope has eleven ordered references: the eight distance-form roles with no width-distance owners, a role-`0x21` target group and its entity-selection operand, and one `ToObjectOffset` parameter owner. The target group has one member, and the member is the record three after the target-group record. The target entity-selection operand's primary identity names the indexed record immediately before the selected `WorkPlane` or `WorkPoint` scope. The target group and its member are named by the ordered table; the two further marked references in the fixed section are not ordered-table members.

A four-byte scope-header member is present in some `EdgeFlange` and `Hem` frames and absent in others. The member is not announced, so it shifts the fixed operation section by a header shift `S` of zero or four. `S` is settled by reference agreement: exactly one candidate makes every marked slot name a record the ordered reference table lists, and a frame that reads under both candidates is refused.

The `EdgeFlange` fixed operation section starts at offset `85 + S` with a u32 bend-position discriminator, the u32 edge count `1`, the marked wrapper reference, the marked settings reference, a u32 height-datum discriminator, and the marked angle-owner and height-owner references. Bend-position value `1` puts the bend outside the selected edge, `2` inside it, `3` at it, and `4` tangent to the side reference plane. Height-datum value `1` measures the height from the inner faces of the sheet and `2` from the outer faces. A u32 whose role is not settled follows the height-owner reference, and the positive f64 inside bend radius in centimetres starts 15 bytes after that u32. Fourteen bytes after the radius starts a u32 result-record count `R`. The marked aggregate-group reference starts 22 bytes after the radius plus `15R`, and the marked role-`0x08` group reference follows it 27 bytes later. The primary frame length is `493 + 15R + 11W + S`.
A class-`361`/`258` or class-`362`/`258` two-edge distance-form `EdgeFlange` has a 620-byte primary frame and twelve distinct references in increasing record-index order. The fixed fields are defined by `edge_flange_corner_operation` in `docs/layouts/f3d.toml`. The edge count and closing edge-group count are both `2`. Bend position is `2`, height datum is `2`, and reference side is `4`. The side padding, radius padding, and group padding are zero bytes. The three result references are distinct, with trailers `1`, `1`, and `0`; the result separator is `1`. A positive finite f64 scalar follows the reference-side field and its zero run. The two wrapper slots and two role-`0x08` group slots pair by ordinal. Each edge operand is the record three after its group. The fixed slots claim the wrappers, settings, height and angle owners, aggregate group, edge groups, and edge operands from the ordered table. The two remaining ordered references are the aggregate operands in edge order. Width spans each complete edge. Both edge selections use the common height, angle, datum, and bend position.

A class-`325` or class-`334` single-edge distance-form `EdgeFlange` scope uses a separate fixed layout. The class-`325` form has paired class `258`; the class-`334` form has paired class `257`. Both forms have eight ordered references, no width-distance owners, and a 494-byte primary frame. Relative to the primary scope header, the fixed fields are bend position at offset `76`, edge count `1` at `80`, the marked wrapper reference at `84`, the marked settings reference at `95`, height datum at `106`, the marked angle owner at `110`, the marked height owner at `121`, reference-side discriminator at `132`, and the positive finite f64 inside bend radius in centimetres at `138`. The result count at `146` is `2`; the two 15-byte result records start at `150` and `165`, carry marked references, and have u32 trailers `1` at `161` and `0` at `176`. A u32 value `1` at `180` precedes the marked aggregate-group reference at `184`; the marked role-`0x08` group reference starts at `207`. Each group's recipe-backed operand is the record three after the group. The bend-position and height-datum values have the meanings defined for the standard form.
A class-`325`/`258`, class-`334`/`257`, or class-`364`/`261` full-edge multi-edge `EdgeFlange` scope uses a 591-byte fixed layout with twelve ordered references and no width-distance owners. Relative to the primary scope header, the bend-position discriminator is at offset `92`, the edge count at `96`, the two marked wrapper references start at offsets `100` and `111`, the marked settings reference at `122`, height datum at `133`, the marked angle owner at `137`, the marked height owner at `148`, reference-side discriminator at `159`, and the positive finite f64 inside bend radius in centimetres at `165`. The edge count is `2`. The result count at `173` is `3`; the three 15-byte result records start at `177`, `192`, and `207`, and have u32 trailers `1` at `188`, `1` at `203`, and `0` at `218`. A u32 value `1` at `222` precedes the marked aggregate-group reference at `226`. The two marked role-`0x08` group references start at `249` and `260`, and each group's recipe-backed operand is the record three after the group. After the fixed slots claim the wrappers, settings, owners, aggregate group, and edge groups, the remaining ordered references are the two edge operands followed by the two aggregate operands in source order. The bend-position and height-datum values have the meanings defined for the standard form.
A class-`364`/`261` per-edge-width `EdgeFlange` scope uses a 643-byte primary frame with fourteen ordered references. Its fixed operation starts at primary-relative offset `92`. The bend-position discriminator is at `92`, the edge count `2` at `96`, the marked wrapper references at `100` and `111`, the marked settings reference at `122`, height datum at `133`, the marked angle owner at `137`, the marked height owner at `148`, reference-side discriminator at `159`, and the positive finite f64 inside bend radius in centimetres at `165`. The result count at `173` is `5`; the five 15-byte result records start at `177`, `192`, `207`, `222`, and `237`, and have u32 trailers `1` at `188`, `203`, `218`, `233`, and `0` at `248`. A u32 value `1` at `252` precedes the marked aggregate-group reference at `256`. The two marked role-`0x08` group references start at `279` and `290`, and each group's recipe-backed operand is the record three after the group. After the fixed slots claim the wrappers, settings, owners, aggregate group, and edge groups, the remaining ordered references are the two edge operands, two aggregate operands, and two `EdgeWidth` owners in source order. The bend-position and height-datum values have the meanings defined for the standard form.
A class-`286`/`258` single-edge distance-form `EdgeFlange` scope uses a 483-byte primary frame with eight ordered references and no width-distance owners. Relative to the primary scope header, the fixed fields are bend position at offset `80`, edge count `1` at `84`, the marked wrapper reference at `88`, the marked settings reference at `99`, height datum at `110`, the marked angle owner at `114`, the marked height owner at `125`, reference-side discriminator at `136`, and the positive finite f64 inside bend radius in centimetres at `142`. The result count at `150` is `1`; its 15-byte result record starts at `154`, carries a marked reference, and has a u32 trailer `0` at `165`. A u32 value `1` at `169` precedes the marked aggregate-group reference at `173`; the marked role-`0x08` group reference starts at `196`. Each group's recipe-backed operand is the record three after the group. The bend-position and height-datum values have the meanings defined for the standard form.

The extended class-`286`/`258` two-edge distance form uses an 801-byte primary frame with 28 ordered references. Its fixed operation has the class-`325`/`334` two-sided-per-edge offsets: bend position at `96`, edge count `2` at `100`, wrapper references at `104` and `115`, settings at `126`, height datum at `137`, angle owner at `141`, height owner at `152`, reference side at `163`, and positive finite f64 inside bend radius in centimetres at `169`. Result count `5` is at `177`; five 15-byte result records start at `181`, `196`, `211`, `226`, and `241`, with trailers `1` at `192`, `207`, `222`, `237`, and `0` at `252`. A u32 value `1` at `256` precedes the aggregate-group reference at `260`; the two role-`0x08` group references start at `283` and `294`. Each edge-group operand is the record three after its group, and the aggregate operands are the two members of the role-`0x43` group. After those fixed roles and group operands are claimed, four signed `EdgeOffset_1`/`EdgeOffset_2` owners occur in source order, followed by twelve auxiliary references. The signed offsets retain their zero and negative values. The auxiliary references remain ordered operation members.
The to-object fixed operation section uses the same common fields through the result-record count and has one result record. Five zero bytes follow the count, then the marked target-group reference starts at `94 + S`. The u32 at `105 + S` is `2`. The marked first inserted reference starts at `109 + S`; the u32 at `120 + S` is `1`; and the marked second inserted reference starts at `124 + S`. Four zero bytes follow the second inserted reference, the u32 at `139 + S` is `1`, and the marked aggregate-group reference starts at `143 + S`. Twelve zero bytes follow the aggregate-group reference, the u32 at `166 + S` is `1`, and the marked role-`0x08` group reference starts at `170 + S`. The primary frame length is `576 + S`. The two inserted marked references remain native operation references.

The reference-framed `EdgeFlange` blocks and its two-offset wrapper use the fixed fields in `docs/layouts/f3d.toml`. The operation uses registered type `7AFA0A65-B53C-472C-ACA4-5C7C0A65001C`, version 4 or 6, and the stored kind `EdgeFlange`. Its prologue contains bend position and a positive edge count. The count bounds marked wrapper references. A settings reference, height datum, angle-owner reference and height-owner reference follow. The short or wide reference-side block carries side code `4`, zero padding and a positive finite scalar. A counted result-reference run follows; each result has a u32 trailer, `1` before the last result and `0` at the last. An empty run is valid. Separator `1`, the aggregate-group reference and a short or wide group header follow. The group count equals the prologue edge count and bounds the main edge-group references in wrapper order. Every present wrapper, settings, parameter-owner, aggregate and main-group reference occurs in the ordered scope table. Null references retain independent controls.

The two-offset wrapper uses registered type `4A557CE2-375C-4F69-AA76-2403109F1491`, version 1. Its five counted references name the main group, two boundary groups and two offset owners. A nested-wrapper reference and the owning-scope backlink close the frame. The main-group reference agrees with the scope slot at the same ordinal. The source kinds `EdgeOffset_1` and `EdgeOffset_2` carry signed lengths: a negative offset narrows the flange, a positive offset extends it, and zero retains the boundary. The boundary groups retain the source reference programs. These groups can select faces, points or planes. The neutral offset law preserves each signed value and boundary reference independently.

The class-`325`/`258` and class-`334`/`257` two-sided-per-edge forms carry four `EdgeWidth_1`/`EdgeWidth_2` owners in source order. The first pair belongs to the first role-`0x08` edge group and the second pair belongs to the second role-`0x08` edge group. `EdgeWidth_1` and `EdgeWidth_2` are the first-end and second-end distances for that selected edge; they are independent between edge groups and are not one operation-wide pair. The neutral `TwoSidesPerEdge` width law preserves one pair per selected edge in edge-group order. It does not infer a cross-edge orientation from the fixed operation.

An `EdgeFlange` role-`0x0000000800000000` group can use its transition as an edge proof when every member has no recipe-reference entries, selector contexts, or local topology references. A member then contributes its updated predecessor boundary edge when exactly one updated edge is present and that edge occurs in its preceding, changed, and result boundary sets. For a group with multiple members, the contributed singleton sets must have one unique assignment of distinct stable edge slots. An extra updated edge, a missing endpoint occurrence, or a duplicate assignment leaves the group native.

Their 669-byte primary frame has sixteen ordered references. The fixed operation starts at primary-relative offset `96`: bend position at `96`, edge count `2` at `100`, wrapper references at `104` and `115`, settings at `126`, height datum at `137`, angle owner at `141`, height owner at `152`, reference side at `163`, and positive finite f64 inside bend radius in centimetres at `169`. Result count `5` is at `177`; five 15-byte result records start at `181`, `196`, `211`, `226`, and `241`, with trailers `1` at `192`, `207`, `222`, `237`, and `0` at `252`. A u32 value `1` at `256` precedes the aggregate-group reference at `260`; the two role-`0x08` group references are at `283` and `294`. Each group's recipe-backed operand is the record three after the group. After those fixed roles and group operands are identified, the aggregate operands are the aggregate-group members and the four remaining parameter owners are the width owners.

Parameter records owned by an `EdgeFlange` scope name their role in their source kind. The height owner names `FlangeHeight` and the angle owner names `FlangeAngle`. In the ordinary distance form, a symmetric width owner names `EdgeWidth`, and the two-sided owners name `EdgeWidth_1` and `EdgeWidth_2` in reference-table order. The class-`364`/`261` per-edge-width form has two `EdgeWidth` owners after the edge and aggregate operands in reference-table order; its classed fixed layout identifies that owner lane separately from the ordinary width-owner count. The extended class-`286`/`258` form uses signed `EdgeOffset_1` and `EdgeOffset_2` owners for its two-sided-per-edge distances.

A `Hem` scope names one parameter owner per input its form takes, the edge wrapper, a role-`0x08` group and its edge operand, a role-`0x43` aggregate group and its edge operand, and the settings record. The ordered reference table is in record-index order, so no role holds a fixed position in it. The header shift `S` defined for `EdgeFlange` applies here too.

The form is carried by the parameter set and the executed transition, not by a fixed-section discriminator. Each owner's parameter names its role in its source kind: a flat hem owns `HemGap` and `HemLength`, an open hem owns the same two, a rolled hem owns `HemRadius` and `HemAngle`, and a teardrop hem owns `HemGap`, `HemLength`, and `HemRadius`. A flat hem stores a `HemGap` its form does not use.

The gap-and-length frame is `494 + S` bytes. It stores the u32 edge count `1` at offset `89 + S`, the marked edge-wrapper reference at `93 + S`, the marked settings reference at `104 + S`, the marked gap-owner and length-owner references at `127 + S` and `138 + S`, and a positive f64 rule-derived inside bend radius in centimetres at `156 + S`. The marked aggregate-group reference is at `193 + S` and the marked role-`0x08` group reference at `220 + S`; each group's operand is the record three after the group.

A rolled frame has the same `494 + S` length and group-reference offsets. Its owner references start at offsets `126 + S` and `139 + S`, and its rule-derived inside bend radius remains at `156 + S`; the first owner is the angle input and the second is the radius input. A teardrop frame is `515 + S` bytes. Its marked gap-owner, length-owner, and radius-owner references start at offsets `127 + S`, `138 + S`, and `149 + S`, its rule-derived inside bend radius starts at `166 + S`, and its marked aggregate-group and role-`0x08` group references start at `203 + S` and `230 + S`. A valid frame has one of these three owner layouts, with matching marked slots, group operands, and paired-header length.

An executed gap-and-length `Hem` inserts exactly two coaxial cylinder carriers parallel to the selected source edge. Let their radii be `r0 < r1`, and let `t = r1 - r0`. The form is `Open` when `2r0 = t`, and `Flat` when `2r0 < t`. A transition that does not satisfy either invariant retains the shared gap-and-length form. The preceding state supplies the source edge.

The common Hem controls start at `C = 85 + S`. The u32 at `C+0` is the bend position; code `3` selects Adjacent. The u32 at `C+30` is the compatibility value `1`, `C+34` and `C+35` are null optional legacy references, and the u32 at `C+36` is the compatibility value `4`. The Flip byte at `C+40` is `0` for Forward and `1` for Reverse. These controls do not select the hem form. The byte at `C+41` belongs to the form-specific owner layout and is not a common null-reference lane.

The common sheet-metal settings carrier occurs in Design segments and in `FlatPatternAssetSubType/Design1`. Its type GUID is `E75C86D6-76D8-4F1F-BC16-AB8CB74958B0`. The mask-and-slots form has a primary indexed header followed by ten zero bytes and a u32 override mask. Version 2 stores seven optional local references; version 3 stores nine. Each absent reference is one zero byte. Each present reference is byte `01`, a u64 entity ID, and two zero bytes. Present references resolve in the same primary record index. After the optional run, a present reference names a rule of type `B42ED662-8999-4C1B-A744-759D1D446D55`. Version 2 then stores four zero bytes; version 3 stores either `00 00` or `01 00 00`. The version-3 suffix byte form is retained in the native settings record. A present reference names a presentation record of type `6CCF41D5-40BE-48ED-A834-18F3EAED6C57`, followed by a zero byte and a present reference to the owning feature scope. The primary class tag resolves to the settings type in the segment-local type table. The same-index paired header begins exactly at the secondary index offset; its class tag resolves to type GUID `CB844AB6-240D-4FC9-9C9F-3679DC896D6F`. Eight zero bytes and a present context reference close the primary-index extent. The context and owner references can name different records.

Mask `4` can accompany a `9C4242C5-68AE-4C93-B839-AA1989258D06` BendRadius override bundle in optional slot 1 (zero-based). Its indexed header and ten zero bytes precede a reference to the parameter owner. Mask `240` can accompany a `7C03CB51-CA81-4670-9B00-1A7C08692A8D` relief override bundle in optional slot 2. Its indexed header and ten zero bytes precede u32 count `2`, owner references for BendDepth and BendRemnant in that order, then an owner reference for BendWidth. Each owner has type `D91D429C-1BB5-4640-B49F-69AF14F463E9` and links to a parameter of type `7A6A3D31-BE74-4E19-9115-20642944C2E4`. The owner scope equals the settings owner, and the owner and parameter evaluated scalars agree. Length scalars use centimetres; parameter expressions retain their authored units.

A one-member `Extrude` termination group can select its target through a construction operand identity that the group owns instead of a face recipe. Its member then has no face-recipe frame, and the identity resolves the selection. When the member is a compact entity-selection record whose sole identity `p` names the WorkPlane scope at record index `p + 1` and the side's termination offset is zero, the side ends at that WorkPlane's plane. A selected-face start group with the same one member and a zero start offset starts the travel on that plane.

A face-recipe operand's continuation search begins after its recipe-family name. Indexed-looking type entries inside the recipe prefix do not end the operand. The expected continuation record has index `N+4` or `N+5`; otherwise the first indexed header after the family name ends the program.

A Fillet selection set can store its face selections in a group of their own. Its edge group has role `0x0000000800000000`, and its face group has role `0x0000001000000000` and bounded-face members. A selected face applies the treatment to its edges. When the two construction-operand groups of a Fillet scope are such an edge group and face group and the scope has one constant radius, both groups use that radius and its tangency weight. A fixed Fillet with one fixed radius law applies that law to both groups in the same way.

A variable-radius `Fillet` assigns one parameter run to each construction-operand group in scope-reference order. In a scope with multiple groups, owner-local order contains repeated runs of `TangencyWeight`, `StartRadius`, `EndRadius`, all `MidRadius` inputs, then all dimensionless `MidParams` inputs. All runs can omit `TangencyWeight`. Each run has one start radius, one end radius, and equal numbers of midpoint radii and positions. A scope with one group has one `StartRadius`, one `EndRadius`, zero or more paired `MidRadius` and dimensionless `MidParams` inputs, and zero or one dimensionless `TangencyWeight`. When present, `TangencyWeight` is retained as the explicit tangency weight; its omission means that no explicit weight is stored. Start and end radii occupy normalized edge-chain parameters zero and one. Each `MidParams` value is the normalized parameter of the corresponding `MidRadius`; repeated midpoint inputs pair in owner-local order. Radii are nonnegative, at least one radius is positive, and midpoint parameters are distinct values inside `(0, 1)`. The stored midpoint order can differ from edge-chain order.

A chordal `Fillet` set names one construction-operand group, one `ChordLen`, and its dimensionless `TangencyWeight` when stored. The chord length applies to every edge operand in the group. A prefix can name several independently dimensioned chordal sets.

A `Fillet` scope without a decoded radius carrier supplies no neutral radius dimension or law form. Its neutral groups retain an unresolved radius with no form and no explicit tangency weight. Decoded selection groups retain their native identities when their topology is unavailable; a missing group definition leaves a scope-native selection. The `fillet:source` source property retains the decoded scope, parameters, owner links, groups and selection operands, including source-only parameters whose owner definitions are unavailable. These source values retain their stored units and order. Existing dimensioned projections keep their source properties. A structurally identified full-round group retains an unresolved center selection when its bounded-face operand exists but its center topology is unavailable.

A fixed `Fillet` has no indexed parameter owners and exactly one construction-operand group, or the edge group and the face group of one selection set. Its fixed scalar lanes follow owner-local ordinal order. A single lane is a nonnegative constant radius with no explicit tangency weight. A multi-lane sequence starts with a positive dimensionless tangency weight. It then carries either one nonnegative constant radius or two endpoint radii followed by zero or more alternating intermediate-radius and intermediate-parameter pairs. Intermediate parameters are strictly increasing and lie in `(0, 1)`. The first and second radii apply at parameters zero and one; each following radius applies at its paired intermediate parameter. Radii use centimetre storage, and at least one radius is positive.

A parameter-owned `Fillet` scope names its fillet sets in a prefix. Offsets are relative to the primary indexed header. The prefix stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19 and a prologue byte at offset 20. Prologue byte `0` ends the prologue at offset 21; prologue byte `1` is followed by `u32 0` and ends it at offset 25. Then follow `u32 N` with `N >= 1`, `N` fillet-set references, a u32 compatibility word, a flag run, `u32 N`, and `N` edge-group references. The flag run is the current form, a rolling-ball corner byte followed by `00 01` and nine zero bytes, or the compact form `01 01` followed by nine bytes. The rolling-ball corner byte is `1` when corners where fillet edges meet are rolling-ball corners and `0` when they are setback corners. Each reference is `u8 1 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes`, and the references within each list are distinct. The `u32 36` code-unit count of the entity GUID follows the last edge-group reference. The compatibility word is `1` for the singleton asymmetric form below and `0` for the other forms. Fillet set `i` treats edge group `i`. Every edge-group reference is a construction-operand group of the scope and a member of its reference table.

A fillet set is one indexed record. Its frame ends at the next indexed header and has one of the forms below. Offsets are relative to the set's indexed header. Every byte that the form does not name is zero.

| Form | Frame length | Fields |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| constant | 97 | `+23: u8 1`; `+25: u8 curvature continuity`; `+26: u8 tangent chain`; `+29: edge-group reference`; `+63: Radius owner reference`; `+78: u32 set ordinal`; `+82: TangencyWeight owner reference` |
| chordal | 97 | `+22: u8 1`; `+26: u8 flag`; `+28: ChordLen owner reference`; `+39: edge-group reference`; `+78: u32 set ordinal`; `+82: TangencyWeight owner reference` |
| compact constant | 93 | `+22: u8 1`; `+24: u8 flag`; `+27: edge-group reference`; `+59: Radius owner reference`; `+70: four bytes`; `+74: u32 set ordinal`; `+78: TangencyWeight owner reference`; `+89: four bytes` |
| short constant | 80 | `+22: u8 1`, `+26: edge-group reference`, `+57: Radius owner reference` |
| asymmetric without weight | 97 | `+21: u8 1`; `+27: u32 1`; `+31: EdgeOffset1 owner reference`; `+42: EdgeOffset2 owner reference`; `+72: edge-group reference`; `+84: u32 2`; `+93: u32 3` |
| variable with two midpoint controls | 153 | `+29: edge-group reference`; `+47: u32 2`; `+51: first MidParams owner reference`; `+62: second MidParams owner reference`; `+77: u32 4`; `+81: StartRadius owner reference`; `+92: EndRadius owner reference`; `+103: first MidRadius owner reference`; `+114: second MidRadius owner reference`; `+138: TangencyWeight owner reference` |

The asymmetric and variable forms above each occupy a singleton set list with implicit ordinal zero. The asymmetric form stores two offsets and omits a tangency weight. In the variable form, midpoint radii and positions pair by their index in their respective lists. The two endpoint radii precede the midpoint radii.

The short constant form uses its position in the compact set list as its ordinal. Its referenced edge group starts at the next indexed header. The set applies its Radius parameter to that group. In a list of short constant sets, one unclaimed dimensionless `TangencyWeight` parameter per edge group pairs by increasing owner-local ordinal and scope-reference group order. Each weight ordinal and group reference occurs once.

For forms with a stored ordinal, the set ordinals of a prefix's `N` sets are the integers `0` through `N - 1`, each used once. List order and ordinal order can differ. The edge-group reference equals the prefix's edge-group reference at the set's list position. Each owner reference names an indexed parameter owner of the scope. That owner references exactly one Design parameter, and the parameter references the owner back. The parameter's source kind is the kind the form names. The set's radius-law and `TangencyWeight` parameters apply to its edge group. In the constant form, the tangent-chain byte is `1` when the set extends its edges along tangent edges and `0` otherwise, and the curvature-continuity byte is `1` when the set has curvature (G2) continuity and `0` for tangent continuity. The flag byte of the chordal and compact forms is `0` or `1`.

A parameter-owned `Chamfer` scope names its chamfer sets in a prefix. Offsets are relative to the primary indexed header. The prefix stores nine zero bytes at offsets 11 through 19 and a chamfer prologue byte at offset 20. Prologue byte `0` ends the prologue at offset 21; prologue byte `1` is followed by `u32 0` and ends it at offset 25. Then follow `u32 corner_type`, an entry-run marker, `u32 E` with `E >= 1`, and `E` ten-byte entries. The corner type is `1` for chamfer corners, `2` for miter corners, and `3` for blend corners. The entry-run marker is the current form `00 01` or the compact form `01`. Entry `k`, counted from one, is `u64 k`, `u8 s`, and a zero byte, where `s` is the one-based number of the chamfer set that the entry belongs to. Every set number from one to `N` occurs. Then follow `u32 N` with `N >= 1`, `N` chamfer-set references, `u32 N`, and `N` edge-group references, each a distinct `u8 1 + u32 record_index + six zero bytes` reference. The `u32 36` code-unit count of the entity GUID follows the last edge-group reference. Chamfer set `i` treats edge group `i`. Every edge-group reference is a construction-operand group of the scope and a member of its reference table.

A chamfer set is one indexed record with a primary and a paired indexed header; its frame ends at the paired header. Offsets are relative to the primary header. Every byte that the form does not name is zero.

| Form | Frame length | Fields |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| equal distance | 83 | `+21: u8 tangent chain`; `+24: distance owner reference`; `+36: u32 spec kind 1`; `+40: edge-group reference`; `+53: u32 set number`; `+57: u8 1`; `+60: auxiliary reference`; `+72: scope reference` |
| two distances | 93 | `+21: u8 flag`; `+22: u8 distance reversal`; `+24: first distance owner reference`; `+35: second distance owner reference`; `+46: u32 spec kind 2`; `+50: edge-group reference`; `+63: u32 set number`; `+67: u8 1`; `+70: auxiliary reference`; `+82: scope reference` |
| distance and angle | 93 | `+21: u8 flag`; `+22: u8 distance reversal`; `+23: angle owner reference`; `+34: distance owner reference`; `+46: u32 spec kind 3`; `+50: edge-group reference`; `+63: u32 set number`; `+67: u8 1`; `+70: auxiliary reference`; `+82: scope reference` |
| compact equal distance | 82 | `+21: u8 flag`; `+24: distance owner reference`; `+36: u32 spec kind 1`; `+40: edge-group reference`; `+53: u32 set number`; `+59: auxiliary reference`; `+71: scope reference` |

The scope reference names the Chamfer scope. The edge-group reference equals the prefix's edge-group reference at the set's position. Each owner reference names an indexed parameter owner of the scope whose Design parameter references the owner back. A distance owner's parameter has source kind `Distance` or `leftDistance`. The two distances have `Distance 1` and `Distance 2`, or `leftDistance` and `rightDistance`. An angle has `Angle`, `Rotate Angle`, or `rotateAngle`. Taken in the reference-table order of their edge groups, the sets name the owners of each specification slot in increasing owner-local order. The set number is the set's one-based position in the prefix list. The auxiliary reference names an indexed record. In the equal-distance form, the tangent-chain byte is `1` when the set extends its edges along tangent edges and `0` otherwise. The flag byte of the other forms is `0` or `1`. The distance-reversal byte of the two-distance and distance-angle forms is `0` for the stored setback-side order and `1` for its reversal. Each set carries its own reversal independently of the other sets.

A full-round `Fillet` has no indexed parameter owner or radius law. It has exactly one role-`0x0000000400000000` construction-operand group with one member. The member is the compact persistent-identity frame also retained in the edge-identity arena, but its group-linked bounded-face operand classifies it as a face selection. Its resolved preceding-state face is the full-round center face. The group has one trailing compact relative-placement carrier, its boolean is `true`, and its `variant` byte is zero. A neutral full-round group retains the center face and represents both side sets as automatic selections.

A Chamfer set's group and owner references define its dimensional pairing independently of adjacent sets. In a Chamfer scope without a set list, construction-operand groups in scope-reference order pair one-to-one with dimensional specifications in increasing owner-local order. An equal-distance chamfer has one `Distance` or `leftDistance` parameter per group. A two-distance chamfer has either one `Distance 1` and one `Distance 2`, or one `leftDistance` and one `rightDistance`, per group. A distance-angle chamfer has one `Distance` or `leftDistance` parameter and one `Angle`, `Rotate Angle`, or `rotateAngle` parameter per group. Each independently dimensioned specification applies to the ordered edge operands carried by its paired group. A scope with exactly one role-`0x0000000800000000` edge group and one or more role-`0x0000001000000000` face groups stores one specification. The edge group and the face groups all take that specification, because the face groups add selected faces to one selection and have no dimension of their own.

A fixed equal-distance `Chamfer` has no indexed parameter owner. It owns exactly one fixed scalar record with owner-local ordinal zero. That scalar is the positive `Distance` in centimetres. It applies to the scope's single construction-operand group, or to the scope's one edge-role group.

A `Hole` scope starts after its indexed header with eight zero bytes, a zero leading-block byte, and a property-presence byte. Byte `0` omits the property block; byte `1` supplies it. The property block stores a u32 count followed by each property's LP-ASCII name, LP-ASCII intrinsic type, and scalar. Count zero stores no properties. Count one stores `SavedHoleDepthInNonDistanceExtentsCase` with type `IntrinsicMetaTypedouble` and a finite f64 depth in centimetres. The Hole type version of the scope class selects the extent block that follows. Type version `3` stores `01 01` and no extent control; a type-version-3 Hole with one `HoleDepth` is Distance, and the property block of that version stores no saved depth. Type version `4` stores the extent controls `01 01 X 00` directly. Type versions `5` and `7` store a u32 tap type before the extent controls: `0` for a simple hole, `1` for a clearance hole, `2` for a tapped hole, and `3` for a taper-tapped hole. A simple or clearance hole models its stored `HoleDiameter`. A tapped hole models the bore diameter that its thread size gives, a taper-tapped hole models the tapered bore of its thread size, and the stored `HoleDiameter` of both keeps the input diameter. The extent control `X` is `0` for Distance and `1` for a non-distance extent. A Distance Hole with control `0` has one `HoleDepth`. A Hole with control `0`, the saved-depth property, and no `HoleDepth` is Extents To; its sole role-`0x0000000500000000` construction group has one member and names the face where the hole ends. The parameter table can retain `HoleDepth` when the extent control is `1`. In type versions `5` and `7` the extent controls are `01 01 X F`, and a u32 `1`, four LP-UTF16 sizing names, a u32 hole type, and a direction control byte follow them. Standard flag `F` `0` stores four empty names, so the direction control is at byte `28` from the start of the extent controls. Flag `1` stores the standard, fit, size, and fastener names of a standard-size hole, in that order. In a clearance hole, the size name designates the fastener size within the standard and the fit name is the clearance fit. The hole type is `0` for a simple hole, `1` for a counterbore, and `2` for a countersink. Direction control value `0` makes the Hole travel against the carrier normal, and value `1` makes it travel along that normal. Control `1` with the saved-depth property, no `HoleDepth`, and only start-face operands defines Through All. The start-face operands are either absent or two direct face recipes in scope-reference order: a `face` or `bounded_face` recipe, then a `bounded_face` recipe. On a face-point carrier, with `refType` `19`, they are four direct face recipes at consecutive scope-reference ordinals: a `face` or `bounded_face` recipe, then three `bounded_face` recipes. Every reference entry names its operand record. A further face reference does not define this form. A direct persistent face selection on a carrier with `refType` `13` does not change the form. The same selection on a carrier with another `refType` does not define this form.

A blind `Hole` has exactly one positive `HoleDepth`, one positive `HoleDiameter`, and one `TipAngle` parameter. Length values use centimetre storage, and the angle uses radian storage. A `TipAngle` strictly between zero and pi defines a conical drill point. `HoleDepth` measures to the shoulder; the conical tip extends beyond that depth. A `TipAngle` equal to pi defines a flat bottom. A counterbored hole additionally has one positive `CBDepth` and one positive `CBDiameter`. For Distance, `CBDepth` does not exceed `HoleDepth`. `CBDiameter` is greater than `HoleDiameter`. A countersunk hole instead has one positive `CSDiameter`, greater than `HoleDiameter`, and one `CSAngle` strictly between zero and pi, which is the included angle of the countersink in radians. A hole has at most one of the counterbore and countersink pairs. A Hole placed by reference-edge distances also has one positive `RefDim1` and optionally one positive `RefDim2`. It has one role-`0x0000002100000000` construction group for one distance and two such groups for two distances. The carrier point stores the position that these distances give. An Extents To or Through All hole has the same diameter, tip-angle and optional counterbore or countersink parameters, with no `HoleDepth`. The member of an Extents To hole's role-`0x0000000500000000` group is the record index of a direct `face` recipe operand of the scope. Its face can belong to another body, and the extent has no offset. Other parameter families or multiplicities do not define these hole forms.

A `Hole` scope's point-and-direction carrier is the indexed record whose type-table entry is `F2A7590D-6654-4674-B393-A2AEF4FEC48A` at version 4. Its base level is:

```
u32      boundingboxIndex
3 × f64  position
3 × f64  direction
2 × f64  pointParameters
u32      refType
u8       tangentPointDataPrefix
3 × f64  tangentPointData
u32 count, count × ref inputs
```

The input count frames the final reference run. It is positive, every input reference is marked, every f64 is finite, and `direction` is a unit vector. `position` and `tangentPointData` use centimetres. The two point parameters, `refType`, and the prefix byte are retained as encoded. `Hole` construction-operand groups use role `0x0000000400000000`, `0x0000000500000000`, or `0x0000000800000000` and carry no Extrude role discriminator. They are native metadata; a Hole's typed body and face operands are direct scope references. The body operand uses a whole-body recipe, and each face operand uses a face or bounded-face recipe. When more than one face operand is present, their resolved stable input-face slots must be identical; otherwise the face selection is unresolved.

The first identity-wrapper record in a construction-operand group's trailing-reference run starts a nested identity chain. Every wrapper is an indexed header followed by ten zero bytes and `01 01 00`; the next indexed header begins exactly 24 bytes after the wrapper header. Wrappers repeat while physically adjacent records carry the same wrapper grammar, and chains may share wrapper suffixes. Physical adjacency to the first non-wrapper record does not by itself assign that record to the operand. When the following record is a fixed persistent identity, it is exactly 190 bytes from its indexed header to the next indexed header. Its header is followed by ten zero bytes, a u64 local identity, an LP-UTF16 asset UUID, an LP-UTF16 context UUID, `u32 2`, and a reserved optional-slot marker followed by u32 zero. The marker is zero when the slot is absent and one when it is present. The marker and zero payload carry no selection semantics. For an `Extrude`, the asset UUID equals the owning scope's sketch-profile asset UUID. A `Fillet` or `Chamfer` replaces every selected input edge. When one group contains `n` compact persistent members and its exact operation transition deletes exactly `n` edges, the group selects the complete unordered deleted-edge set; neutral transfer does not require a per-member assignment. The value of `n` is the compact-member count of that group. The cardinality proof is evaluated independently for each group and does not apply to another feature family.

Each selection member is a 190-byte or 204-byte indexed record ending immediately before the next indexed header. The 204-byte form appends a fourteen-byte tail to the 190-byte form: byte `00`, u32 `2`, u64 `1`, and byte `00`, in that order. This tail requires a present optional slot. The tail does not change the local, asset, or context identity. Its eleven-byte header is followed by ten zero bytes, a local persistent identity, the LP-UTF16 asset UUID, an LP-UTF16 context UUID, `u32 2`, and the same optional-slot marker plus u32 zero. Every member's asset UUID equals the scope's sketch-profile asset UUID, and all members in one group carry the same context UUID. Selection-group member order is the encoded run order. A construction-operand identity chain belongs to the member when its following indexed header is the member header and its complete local, asset, and context identity equals the member identity; multiple construction groups may share one member through separate chains. A Fillet or Chamfer persistent-edge identity has an eleven-byte indexed header followed by twelve zero bytes, or eleven or ten zero bytes in the compact forms, then a marker byte `1`, a u32 local identity, six zero bytes, u32 `1`, and the two LP-UTF16 UUIDs. The local identity names either the equal stable ASM entity slot or a record revision assigned to one stable slot by the complete history archive. In a bulletin update pair `(old, new)`, `old` is the archived record revision and `new` is its stable entity slot. In a deletion pair `(old, null)`, the archived revision and stable slot are both `old`. Each archived revision has one such mapping. A value valid in both namespaces resolves only when both name the same stable slot. State identities occurring in more than one retained ASM history do not contribute to identity or position resolution. The normalized stable slot, its invariant topology or carrier family across uniquely identified states, and the ordered containing state identities form the historical selection identity. A class-297 identity whose local identity equals `N+3` and whose record contains the bounded-face envelope above is a bounded-face edge rule. Its exact preceding support face supplies ordered boundary edges; intersection with the owning feature transition's deleted treatment edges is the rule's selected edge run. Every support owner must be changed by that transition, and repeated edges contributed by later group members are removed after their first occurrence. Historical topology retains each plane and cylinder (`surface_cylinders`) surface carrier alongside each vertex-to-point binding and each point carrier's model-space position. A loop supplies its coedges, a pcurve supplies every coedge using that carrier, a coedge supplies its edge, an edge supplies its two vertices, a curve supplies every edge using that carrier, a vertex supplies itself, and a point supplies its stored position. When the local identity uniquely equals a persistent point id or a primary or nonzero secondary persistent curve id in the same stream whose owner reference names the selected Sketch or is absent, it selects that point or curve.

A selection member whose optional slot is absent can instead be a 240-byte indexed record ending immediately before the next indexed header. The scope-tail form appends a fifty-byte tail to the 190-byte frame: byte `00`, an f64, a u32 with value `0x104`, a marked same-segment chain reference, bytes `01 00 00`, a second marked chain reference, byte `00`, and a closing marked scope reference, in that order. The closing scope reference names the record index of the Extrude scope that owns the selection group. The tail does not change the local, asset, or context identity. Offsets are in the `extrude_selection_member_scope_tail` table. The f64, the u32, and the two chain references are retained as encoded.

A selection member whose 190-byte frame ends with a zero optional-slot value (the slot marker byte is zero or one) can carry an extended tail. The lengths 14 and 50 belong to the typed tails above and are not extended tails. The member ends at the next indexed record header, which is u32 `3`, three ASCII digits and a u32 record index. The first such header after the frame ends the tail, and a record that omits the u32 length of its header lies inside the tail. A tail that a header ends has 1 to 1024 bytes. When no header follows, the tail runs to the end of the stream, whatever its length, and the member is the last record of the stream; the MetaStream primary index then extends that record to the stream end. The tail is retained as encoded.

A fixed persistent identity can terminate the Design stream after its 190-byte frame. Both UUID strings use 36 UTF-16 code units. It then has no following indexed record; its native following-record index is zero and its following byte offset is the stream-end boundary. A selection member has the same terminal form. Its fourteen-byte tail, when present, precedes the stream-end boundary.

An Extrude selection resolves to neutral sketch-loop indices when every ordered member resolves to a curve and each curve occurs in exactly one neutral profile loop. A role-`0x0000004100000000` construction group can contain nested entity-selection members directly. All members have the same primary identity, asset UUID, and context UUID. The primary identity names one Sketch placement, and each member's secondary identity names one unique curve owned by that Sketch. The ordered, deduplicated profile-loop indices containing those curves are the selection. A curve in no loop leaves the group unresolved. Repeated members of one loop produce one loop index in first-member order. A Sketch with no non-construction text that contains exactly one profile loop has one possible selection and resolves to that loop independently of the member identity family. Otherwise a member in the historical body, region, shell, surface, face, loop, coedge, edge, vertex, point, curve, or pcurve family supplies its historical boundary-vertex positions. Body, region, and shell members traverse the complete body-region-shell-face ownership hierarchy. A historical state contributes positions only when the complete ownership and entity-to-edge-to-vertex-to-point chains required by every member resolve in that state. Positions from different history states are never combined. Each complete state-local member set is orthogonally projected into the selected Sketch frame, and every resolving state must select the same neutral result.
