When no history state contributes a complete member set, each persistent Sketch point supplies its projected position and each persistent Sketch curve supplies every neutral profile containing that exact curve. The collective positions select one atomic supported planar region when they lie strictly inside the same smallest containing loop or uniquely span that region's exterior and immediate-child boundary loops. If collective positions do not select one region, exact member selections form their ordered deduplicated union. One unique selected region also governs when every differing member resolves to one of that region's exterior or hole boundary loops. Each region records its exterior-loop index and immediate child-loop indices. Model-space displacement normal to the Sketch plane does not affect the result. When member identities do not resolve, the Extrude scope's current and previous history-state identities select their unique linked transition. The current state links to the previous state directly or through intermediate states whose transitions carry no history rows and neither insert nor delete any topology entity. Each inserted face with a complete face-loop-coedge-edge-vertex-point boundary is projected into the Sketch frame. A boundary has at least three distinct vertex positions, or all its edges are closed and each contributes its one vertex. A face whose points select an atomic region is a cap candidate; a side face selects no region. The transition resolves when at least one cap candidate exists and every cap candidate selects the same region. When the inserted-face selections differ, the faces whose boundary points lie at one offset along the Sketch normal are caps. When at least one cap exists, every cap selects, and all caps select the same loop or region, that selection is the proof; the other inserted faces are Boolean result context. When that inserted-face proof does not resolve, deleted faces in the state immediately before the transition supply a second transition proof. Every deleted face must have exactly one surface-carrier binding, exactly one carrier must own more than one deleted face, every other deleted carrier family must be a singleton, and deleted face identities must be unique. Every face in the multi-face family must have a complete historical boundary whose projected points select a profile. The family resolves to the ordered deduplicated union when all faces select loops or all faces select regions. When member curve identities match multiple profile loops and transition proofs yield no selection, each member selects the containing profile with the smallest entity count. Multiple groups resolve as their group-ordered, deduplicated union when every group resolves to loops or every group resolves to regions. When both explicit profile indices and member selection groups are present, the merged group selection is retained when every resolved region is an untrimmed loop included in the explicit profile indices; otherwise the explicit profile indices take precedence. When an `Extrude` profile resolves to `HistoricalFaces` and binds to a history transition, historical faces in the preceding state topology match candidate sketches in reverse stream order by circle-center alignment, vertex coincidence, adjacent cylindrical faces, or transition proof, selecting the candidate with the smallest absolute plane distance. The feature records `historical_face_sketch` and `historical_face_profiles` in feature `source_properties`, and records `historical_face_offset` when its absolute value exceeds `1.0e-4` centimetres. An incomplete member run, conflicting cap candidates, absence of a cap candidate, a boundary point that does not uniquely identify a region closure, an unsupported profile geometry family, intersecting candidate loops, an unresolved group, or a mixture of loop and region selections retains every group identity in scope-reference order as a native selection within the resolved Sketch.

An Extrude selection against a spatial Sketch resolves each complete selection group from the member local persistent identities. Every member must uniquely name a curve owned by the selected spatial Sketch, each named curve must occur in exactly one spatial profile, and all members of one group must name the same profile. Members that uniquely name different profiles contradict the group, and the history transition then selects no profile. A direct role-`0x0000004100000000` entity-selection group instead uses the common primary Sketch identity and each member's secondary curve identity; it contributes the ordered, deduplicated union of the uniquely containing spatial profiles. Multiple groups contribute profile indices in scope-reference order and remove repeated indices after their first occurrence. A spatial Sketch containing exactly one profile resolves to index zero when exact member identities are unavailable. Otherwise the scope's current and previous history-state identities select their unique linked transition. For each inserted face with a complete face-loop-coedge-edge-vertex-point boundary, the boundary points are tested against every spatial profile. A profile is a candidate when all point offsets along its normal are equal, its complete boundary consists of spatial lines, and every point projected into its profile frame lies in the polygon closure. A profile with missing or nonlinear boundary geometry prevents that face from contributing a candidate when all point offsets along the profile normal are equal. At least one inserted face must contribute a candidate, and all contributing faces must name the same profile. If the inserted faces do not resolve, the deleted faces in the state immediately before the transition use the same rule. An incomplete member run, an ambiguous curve-to-profile relation, conflicting member identities, conflicting face candidates, or unsupported candidate geometry retains every group identity in scope-reference order as a native selection within the resolved spatial Sketch. A scope with neither a selection group nor a sketch-profile frame retains the scope identity as a native selection within the resolved spatial Sketch.

An Extrude scope whose sketch-profile frame names a spatial Sketch takes candidate profiles from its selection groups when it has any, from the frame's nested region selection when it has one, and otherwise from every profile of the Sketch. In a nested selection, each selected region is its one loop, or its atomic regions of one loop each that together name every curve of the selected region. A loop names a profile when that profile is the only one whose boundary holds the curve of the first member, every member's curve is a boundary curve or traces the same geometry as one, and every boundary curve is a member's curve or traced by one. A selected region with more than one loop and no atomic regions, an atomic region with more than one loop, or a loop that names no single profile boundary names no profile. A candidate whose boundary has the same number of curves as an earlier kept candidate, each tracing a line with the same end points or a coincident full circle of the other, is the same region and is named once. Candidates from the selection groups or the nested region selection are the selection, and a Sketch with one profile selects that profile. The transition from the scope's previous to its current history state certifies a set of candidates when the inserted planar faces parallel to the profile plane that lie farthest from it are off that plane, every edge of those faces has a proven carrier, and the outline of the union of those faces and the outline of the union of the candidate profiles cover each other, carrier by carrier over their whole intervals. A frame with no selection group and no nested region selection on a Sketch with more than one profile selects every distinct profile when the transition certifies them.

Inserted Extrude side faces that all project to the same nonempty sketch-loop selection prove that selection; inserted regions are Boolean result context. When side faces project to differing loops, one inserted cap selecting a loop-defined region remains the proof only when every loop selection names exterior or hole loops of that region. A loop outside the cap region or multiple distinct cap regions contradicts the proof.

When every inserted cylindrical side face is one concentric sketch circle and every inserted plane parallel to the sketch has its outer radius on that circle and its inner radius on one cylinder of the preceding topology, the assumed selection is the smallest concentric ring set covering that cap: every concentric sketch circle strictly outside that cylinder and at most the outer radius, in increasing radius, where each circle bounds the disjoint ring outside the preceding selected circle (or outside a concentric sketch circle on the body cylinder for the innermost ring). This selection requires at least two such circles, one of them on the outer radius, and charges `feature.profile-body-circle-rings-assumed`. One ring between the preceding cylinder and the next sketch circle remains the cylindrical side-face selection.

When every inserted cylindrical side face is one concentric sketch circle and every inserted plane parallel to the sketch has its inner radius on that circle and its outer radius on one cylinder of the preceding topology, the assumed selection is the smallest concentric ring set covering that shoulder: every concentric sketch circle strictly outside that circle and at most the first sketch circle strictly outside the body cylinder, in increasing radius, where each circle bounds the disjoint ring outside the preceding selected circle (and the innermost ring has the inner sketch circle as its hole). That outer sketch circle is part of the selection only when its radius is at most the next larger cylinder of the preceding topology about the same center, and the selection charges `feature.profile-body-circle-rings-assumed`. No sketch circle strictly outside the body cylinder leaves the cylindrical side-face selection.

For a one-sided planar face termination, the resolved face of the recipe takes precedence over a derived preceding-face set. A unique recipe candidate whose offset termination plane matches a changed transition cap selects the face in the feature-input state. An `Extrude` result state can follow its preceding state through a chain of several transitions. When every link of that chain is uniquely bound, the `Extrude` face selections read the preceding state, and the changed caps are the faces that any link inserts or updates and that the result state holds. If the recipe candidates leave the selection unresolved, a unique selected or preceding candidate with stored-cap agreement supplies the face. This agreement includes a cap on the start plane when the changed parallel caps share that plane. An unresolved conflict retains the native termination group.

A native `ToFace` target selection resolves from exactly one qualifying referenced face in its termination group. The qualifying face has a planar surface whose normal is parallel to that side's oriented sweep direction and whose plane origin lies in that direction beyond the profile plane. More than one qualifying candidate, or no candidate with all three properties, retains the native selection. When an `Extrude` extent uses a `ToFace`, `ToPlane`, `ToShape`, or `ThroughNext` termination on any side and binds to a history transition, the transition chain evaluates inserted points, aligned curve axes, and aligned surface planes with signed distance magnitude above `0.1` centimetres from the start plane along the sketch normal. The signed distance of the qualifying candidate with minimum absolute value is recorded as `extrude_to_distance` in feature `source_properties` when its absolute value exceeds `1.0e-4` centimetres.

Each parameter-owning Sketch scope references exactly one paired placement record in its Design stream. Its carrier is a fixed placement frame or a registered versioned placement construction. The compact placement frame is 201 bytes from its primary indexed header to its same-index paired header and denotes the identity local-to-model transform. The explicit placement frame is 329 bytes and inserts a row-major 4×4 f64 local-to-model matrix at primary-record offset 55. The 305- and 325-byte placement frames store the same matrix at primary-record offset 48. Its bottom row is `(0, 0, 0, 1)` and its three basis columns are orthonormal. Matrix column 0 is the sketch u-axis, column 1 is the sketch v-axis, column 2 is the sketch normal, and column 3 is the model-space origin.

A planar or spatial Sketch takes the name of the Feature projected from its owning Sketch scope: the stored kind spelling plus a space and the feature ordinal. This rule applies when exactly one placement in the same stream carries that scope, exactly one Feature with a non-empty name projects from that scope, and exactly one scope selects the sketch. Each other sketch uses its entity-id name.

The versioned carrier has the placement type GUID, base type GUID `2CA5A1CD-C99B-4C9B-91AF-57989148E841`, module `Fusion`, and the registered class version. Its indexed header agrees with its record index, class tag, and primary offset. Its class members and base level end at its same-index paired header.

A `Sketch` scope joined to `EntityGenesis`-form entity headers references its placement in a wider frame. The placement type GUID is `7B6C3C2D-4096-4E6D-B225-699E8C2D9355`. With an empty display name, its class members start at primary-record offset 21. The bytes from indexed-header offset 11 through 20 are zero. Version 4 admits marked and unmarked matrix forms. The placement class holds one class level whose members are, in order:

```
u8       LinearOffsetOnPeriodicFace      v >= 14
3 × f64  alignUpDirection                v >= 4
f64      arcLengthForPeriodicFace        11 <= v <= 15
u8       periodicFaceMode                v == 16
u8       axisFlipped                     v >= 8
u8       bUseUDirection                  v >= 10
ref      definerCreator                  v >= 6
ref      extraOffset                     v >= 13
ref      globalParamU                    v >= 9
ref      globalParamV                    v >= 9
ref      globalReorientParam             v >= 9
ref      globalReorientParam1            v >= 9
u8       isInferredXAxis
u8       isInferredZAxis
u8       isZFlip
u8       identity                        absent in the unmarked version-4 form
16 × f64 matrix3d                        present without a marker, or when identity is 0
f64      oldRotation                     v >= 7
f64      pickPointParam                  v == 2
2 × f64  pickpoint                       v >= 1
u32 count, count × ref  rEdgeReferences  v >= 5
ref      rOrigin
u32 count, count × ref  rPlaneReferences
ref      rXAxis
ref      rZAxis
u32      refType
u8       resizeType                      v >= 12
u32 count, count × ref  values
```

Version 15 uses the version-14 member grammar. Version 16 replaces the eight-byte `arcLengthForPeriodicFace` member with the one-byte `periodicFaceMode` member. The remaining members keep their encoded order. The fixed prefix through `bUseUDirection` is defined in the `placement_v16_solved_prefix` layout table. The mode byte retains its encoded numeric value.

The placement `refType` has the following direct-reference shapes and scalar roles. A scalar role names the source kind of the parameter reached through its scalar owner. The `values` list preserves the order shown.

| `refType` | Direct geometry references | `values` scalar roles |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 2 | Empty | Empty or `AlongDistance` |
| 3, 4, 10 | Empty | `RotateAngle` |
| 5, 8, 11, 12 | Empty | Empty |
| 6 | Required `rOrigin`; optional `rXAxis` and `rZAxis`; empty edge and plane lists | Empty or `OffsetX`, `OffsetY`, `OffsetZ`, `AngleZ` |
| 7 | Required `rOrigin` and `rZAxis`; two `rPlaneReferences`; null `rXAxis`; empty edge list | `OffsetX`, `OffsetY`, `OffsetZ`, `AngleZ` |
| 13 | Empty | `PathDistance` |
| 15 | Empty | `RotateAngle` |
| 17 | Empty | `AlongDistance` |
| 20 | Empty | Empty or `OffsetX`, `OffsetY`, `OffsetZ`, `AngleZ` |
| 21 | Empty | `RotateAngle` |

“Empty” direct geometry means that `rOrigin`, `rXAxis`, and `rZAxis` are null and both `rEdgeReferences` and `rPlaneReferences` are empty. It does not mean that the construction has no geometry operands: the owning scope retains its separate ordered references. Code `20` has a non-null `definerCreator` of type `0F38E3C4-2E39-470B-A4FD-D3187224FB9F`, version `0`; the other listed codes have a null creator. Codes `4` and `10` retain distinct numeric values even though their scalar roles and direct geometry shapes agree. The solved matrix does not identify the construction rule or replace owner-scope operands.

In version 14, a non-null `extraOffset` names a version-0 scalar-parameter owner of type `D91D429C-1BB5-4640-B49F-69AF14F463E9`. The owner references a parameter of type `7A6A3D31-BE74-4E19-9115-20642944C2E4` whose source kind is `ExtraOffset`. The parameter retains its authored length unit and expression. This direct owner reference is independent of the trailing `values` list. It can occur with a nonempty or empty `values` list and does not replace a list member.

The unmarked version-4 form stores its matrix at primary-record offset 48, immediately after the three axis-state bytes. It has no identity marker. The marked form stores the identity marker before the matrix. The base level follows the class members. `matrix3d` is the row-major 4×4 local-to-model transform with the translation in column 3 and the bottom row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`; the origin is in centimetres. The leading identity byte is the member's presence marker read the other way round: `1` states that the transform is the identity and stores no matrix, so the two forms of one class version differ by exactly the matrix's 128 bytes. `alignUpDirection` is a unit vector or zero. `resizeType` is one byte wide; reading it as a u32 desynchronizes the `values` list that follows it. WorkPlane records of the same class are not sketch placements.

A `WorkPlane` scope's ordered member references bind its solved plane to exactly one placement construction in the same Design stream. The placement construction uses the registered type and versioned member grammar above. An explicit `matrix3d` supplies the solved frame. An identity marker of `1` supplies the identity frame and omits the matrix bytes. The frame source offset is the explicit matrix offset or the identity-marker offset. Column 0 is the plane u-axis, column 2 is its normal, and column 3 is its origin in centimetres. The stored frame is the solved plane of a placement whose `isInferredXAxis`, `isInferredZAxis`, and `isZFlip` members are zero, whose `axisFlipped` member, when present, is zero, whose `bUseUDirection` is zero or one, and whose version-16 `periodicFaceMode` is zero. The explicit matrix and the identity marker give the solved orientation for both direction values. `LinearOffsetOnPeriodicFace`, `alignUpDirection`, `arcLengthForPeriodicFace`, `oldRotation`, `pickPointParam`, `pickpoint`, and `resizeType` are construction-solver inputs whose solved result is the stored frame. The scalar parameters, `refType`, and geometry operands carry the construction definition separately from its solved frame.

A `WorkPlane` scope references one placement frame of the same indexed record class. The class-290/262 placement frame is 325 bytes: it stores 34 zero bytes after the indexed header, bytes `0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00` at offsets 45 through 48, and a row-major 4×4 f64 local-to-model matrix at offset 49. The class-308/257, class-320/258, class-364/263, class-380/262, and class-431/257 placement frames use a second 325-byte layout: they store 38 zero bytes after the indexed header and the same matrix at offset 49. One 321-byte compact form stores the same zero prefix and matrix offset. Class 364 is also paired with class 264 and stores the matrix at offset 49 in two 321-byte forms: 35 zero bytes followed by `0x01, 0x00, 0x00`, or 34 zero bytes followed by `0xcc, 0xcd, 0x00, 0x00`. The 326-byte compact form stores 39 zero bytes after the indexed header and the matrix at offset 50. Its primary and paired class pair is 279 and 266, 409 and 258, or 450 and 259. The 337-byte class-350/258 and class-409/258 placement frames use a third 337-byte layout: they store 39 zero bytes after the indexed header and a row-major 4×4 f64 local-to-model matrix at offset 50. The 352-, 363-, and 374-byte direct forms store `0x01` at offset 55, six zero bytes at offsets 56 through 61, an opaque little-endian u16 at offset 62, two zero bytes at offsets 64 and 65, and the matrix at offset 66. These layout bytes identify a direct form whatever its segment-local class tags. The 362- and 373-byte referenced forms store `0x01, 0x00, 0x01` at offsets 55 through 57, a u32 construction-record reference at offset 58, fourteen zero bytes, and the matrix at offset 76. The matrix basis, origin, rigidity, and centimetre units equal a sketch placement matrix. The matrix of a frame whose bytes 45 and 46 are zero, or whose bytes 62 and 63 are zero in a direct form, defines the constructed plane directly: column 0 is the plane u-axis, column 2 is its normal, and column 3 is its origin.
A legacy three-reference `WorkPlane` scope is a 279-byte class-359 frame paired with class 262. Its first member is a 345-byte class-400 placement frame paired with class 262; the placement frame stores 38 zero bytes after its indexed header and the row-major 4×4 f64 local-to-model matrix at offset 49. The scope's two remaining members are vertex-recipe records, and this form has no five-member `ExtraOffset` construction table. The solved placement matrix is the complete plane carrier for this form.
The class-350/262 three-reference `WorkPlane` scope is 273 bytes, or 269 bytes in its omitted-lane variant. In the 273-byte form, its reference count is at offset 133, the three marked member references are at offsets 138, 149, and 160, the current history-state identity is at offset 170, the UTF-16LE kind starts at offset 178, the feature ordinal is at offset 196, and the preceding history-state identity is at offset 227. The 269-byte form shifts these fields to 129, 134, 145, 156, 166, 174, 192, and 223. The paired header is class 262. The ordered members are not positional; one member is a class-256/262 placement frame. The class-256/262 WorkPlane placement frame is 325 bytes. That 325-byte frame has zero bytes 11 through 44; bytes 45 through 46 are an opaque little-endian u16; bytes 47 through 48 are zero; the class-256/262 placement frame stores its row-major 4×4 f64 local-to-model matrix at offset 49. The two remaining members are construction metadata. The placement matrix of a frame whose opaque u16 is zero is the complete plane carrier for this form.

The class-337/266 WorkPlane placement frame is 325 bytes and uses the same offsets: bytes 11 through 44 are zero, bytes 45 through 46 are an opaque little-endian u16, bytes 47 through 48 are zero, and the row-major 4×4 f64 local-to-model matrix starts at offset 49. The class-341/261 and class-346/262 placement frames use a 321-byte form with the same prefix and matrix offsets. These class-pair rules are separate from the zero-prefix 321-byte form.

The class-322/261 WorkPlane placement frame is 332 bytes. Bytes 11 through 48 are zero. The frame stores a row-major 4×4 f64 local-to-model matrix at offset 49; the remaining 155 bytes are the opaque placement-carrier tail.

A three-point `WorkPlane` scope has five ordered references: the solved placement frame, three `vertex_recipe_data` operands in construction-point order, and one `ExtraOffset` parameter owner. The placement frame's construction reference names the `ExtraOffset` owner. Its finite evaluated value is zero. Each vertex operand uses the five-record terminal envelope defined for a `WorkPoint` vertex input. Its persistent face references select one common vertex in the preceding history state. The three vertices are distinct and non-collinear. Their positions lie on the solved placement plane, and their cross-product normal is parallel or antiparallel to the placement normal.

A two-point `WorkAxis` scope has five ordered references. Reference zero is a 232-byte solved-axis carrier. After its indexed header it stores ten zero bytes, u32 value count 8, and eight f64 values at offset 25. The values are a three-coordinate origin and a three-component displacement in centimetres, followed by two zeros. A u32 reference count of two at offset 118 precedes two marked references. The legacy layout stores endpoint coordinates in separate records. Those records are 197-byte point carriers, and each stores 31 zero bytes after its indexed header and a three-coordinate point at offset 42. A nonzero displacement defines the axis direction.

A `WorkAxis` scope can reference a point-and-direction carrier with type GUID `F2A7590D-6654-4674-B393-A2AEF4FEC48A` and version 1 or 4. Its base level has the fields of the Hole carrier above. Version 1 omits the tangent point data prefix and tangent point data. For `refType` 12, `boundingboxIndex` 8 identifies the stored line. The `position` field gives the axis origin in centimetres. A nonzero `direction` displacement defines the axis direction.

Carrier properties are ordered occurrences. Each property has a length-prefixed ASCII key, a length-prefixed ASCII intrinsic type name, and a value. Keys can be empty or repeated. `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64` has a u64 value; `IntrinsicMetaTypedouble` has an f64 value.

Two two-reference `WorkAxis` scope forms use direct axis carriers. Their scope frames are:

| Primary class | Paired class | Frame length | Reference-count offset | Member-reference offsets | Current-state offset | Kind offset | Feature-ordinal offset |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 302 | 262 | 268 | 131 | 136, 147 | 157 | 165 | 181 |
| 361 | 258 | 254 | 127 | 132, 143 | 153 | 161 | 177 |

The first ordered member is the direct axis carrier and the second is its construction-support record. The class-297/262 carrier is 215 bytes; the class-335/258 carrier is 195 bytes. Both carriers store ten zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, u32 value count 8 at offset 21, and eight f64 values at offset 25. Values 0 through 2 are the origin in centimetres, values 3 through 5 are the displacement in centimetres, and values 6 and 7 are zero. The displacement is finite and nonzero. The carrier stores u32 reference count 6 at offset 89 and u32 value 1 at offset 93. Its remaining construction/reference tail starts at offset 97 and ends at the paired header; the tail layout is generation-specific. The support record is class 306/262 or class 349/258 and is 293 bytes. The direct carrier's origin and displacement define the axis direction.

A `JointOrigin` scope owns one coordinate frame. The 336- and 347-byte forms store 34 zero bytes after the primary indexed header, a marked construction-record reference at offset 45 with ten trailing zero bytes, and a row-major rigid 4×4 local-to-model matrix at offset 60. The 385-byte class-364 form is paired with class 264 and stores 34 zero bytes, `0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00`, and the matrix at offset 49. The 389-byte class-337 form is paired with class 266 and uses the same 34-byte zero prefix, marker, and matrix offset; its 212-byte tail is generation-specific. The 300-, 322-, and 344-byte parameter-scope envelopes store construction graphs; their solved frame is the unique matching operand frame in the consuming `Assemble` scope. An operand frame whose construction reference equals the `JointOrigin` scope record index defines that origin. The 604-byte class-276 `Assemble` form paired with class 258 stores a marked construction reference at offset 24, seven zero bytes, the origin matrix at offset 36, a marked `JointOrigin` scope reference at offset 164, six zero bytes, and u32 value 1. It has exactly eight parameter owners. Four placement owners at local ordinals zero through three precede the angle, local X offset, local Y offset, and local Z offset alignment owners at ordinals four through seven. Matrix columns 0, 1, and 2 are the coordinate-system x, y, and z axes; column 3 is its origin in centimetres.

A version-2 `JointOrigin` scope can store its solved frame in a separate placement carrier of type `7B6C3C2D-4096-4E6D-B225-699E8C2D9355`. The first scope reference names the carrier. Its index is the scope index plus one. Its indexed header starts 30 bytes after the paired scope header. The final eleven bytes of the carrier are a marked scope backlink. The paired carrier header follows it.

| Carrier version | Carrier length | Matrix offset | Scope backlink offset |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 6 | 369 | 60 | 358 |
| 6 | 391 | 60 | 380 |
| 8 | 412 | 61 | 401 |

The 369- and 391-byte carriers store 34 zero bytes after the indexed header, a marked construction-record reference at offset 45, and four zero bytes after that reference. The 412-byte carrier stores 35 zero bytes after the indexed header, a marked construction-record reference at offset 46, and the bytes `00 00 01 00` after that reference. The matrix columns give the axes and the origin in centimetres.

The marked scope reference in an `Assemble` datum envelope identifies its `JointOrigin`. For a carrier-backed `JointOrigin`, the carrier matrix is the solved frame even when the datum envelope stores a different matrix at offset 36.

A direct `WorkPoint` scope references a point-data construction record. The primary record is paired by its record index. Its class level is:

```
i32      boundingboxIndex     v >= 2
2 × f64  param
ref      pickPtParam          v >= 1
3 × f64  point3d
u32      refType
3 × f64  tangentPointData     v >= 3
```

A vertex-rule input can instead use the direct sketch-point selection envelope. It keeps the same persistent-selection prefix and four nested indexed records, with the identity record at `N+3` ending at `N+4`. From the identity record header, offsets 11 through 19 are zero, offset 20 is the presence byte `01`, offsets 21 through 24 are a zero `u32`, offsets 25 through 28 are the owning Sketch entity record index, offsets 29 through 32 are a zero `u32`, offsets 33 through 36 are the sketch-point persistent id, and offsets 37 through 40 are a zero `u32`. The identity record can instead have a 37-byte compact form: zero bytes at offsets 11 through 20, the owning Sketch entity record index as a u64 at offset 21, and the sketch-point persistent id as a u64 at offset 29. The next indexed record is `N+4` and carries the point-data record. The owning Sketch record index and sketch-point persistent id resolve to one sketch point; the point belongs to a planar or model-space sketch according to its projected sketch arena.

For `refType` 10, this direct sketch-point envelope is an alternate to the B-rep vertex recipe; the input envelope determines which semantic operand is selected.

The base level's first counted reference list holds the point's geometry inputs. `point3d` is the work point in centimetres. `refType` names the construction rule. Value `5` selects the center of one circular edge. Value `7` selects the intersection of two edges. Value `8` selects the intersection of three planes. Values `1` and `10` select one B-rep vertex. Value `1` requires one `vertex_recipe_data` input and retains its distinct serialized value; it does not select the direct sketch-point envelope. Value `14` selects the intersection of one edge and one plane. Value `20` selects a normalized position along one edge. These forms carry respectively one, two, three, one, two, and one input references. A value-`1` record with another input count or carrier has no assigned construction meaning. The u32 immediately after the optional `tangentPointData` is the input count, and that many marked references follow it; the count, rather than a fixed rule table, frames the input run. `refType` is not bounded above by the rules a given file uses. Each input names a record of class `5662F619-2281-4AD9-93DC-1FCFDA1062E7` or `5A1BF548-241F-46FD-9FB5-E4B05126EB9D`; both classes derive from `6144EA59-3ACA-4172-9F14-A6531E94D69B`. An edge-valued input uses the four-record `edge_recipe_data` envelope that starts at indexed record `N`, but the following indexed header is `N+5`; this consumer does not use the ordinary edge-feature envelope's `N+4` closing index. A vertex-valued input has the same `N` through `N+3` envelope and `N+5` closing index with family name `vertex_recipe_data`. Its persistent face references select one common vertex in the input history state, and that vertex's point position equals `point3d`. A plane-valued input uses the compact persistent entity-selection envelope. Its primary identity names the indexed record immediately before the selected `WorkPlane` scope record. Value `20` owns one `PathDistance` parameter. Its finite evaluated scalar is the path fraction in the closed interval from zero through one; it is not a centimetre length. A `refType` of `18` may include a second input naming a child point-data record and repeats that child's `point3d` unchanged. `boundingboxIndex` holds uninitialized memory where the record does not use it, so a reader takes it only from a record whose `refType` gives it a meaning. `tangentPointData` is `(-1, -1, -1)` where unused.

A member-run sketch's `EntityGenesis`-form entity header is followed by a paired same-index record whose prologue — zero bytes from record offset 11 to 19, `0x01` at offset 19, and a u64 head-record reference at offset 20 — names the head record of the sketch's member run. The explicit head record stores its u32 record index at offset 7, eleven zero bytes, the row-major 4×4 f64 local-to-model placement at offset 22, then `00` plus either a one-byte null closing reference (152 bytes) or a marked closing reference that starts with `01` (162 bytes, or 202 bytes with an inline type GUID). The matrix row and column semantics equal the explicit placement frame, and the origin is in centimetres. The entity header's reference tail carries a marked back-reference to the owning feature's entity. A Sketch scope whose sketch-entity binding names the entity owns the member-run sketch. A localized `Esquisse` scope does not repeat the sketch entity suffix in its generic reference table. Without such a binding, a Sketch scope without a sketch-entity binding owns the preceding sketch entity when it is the only such Sketch scope that follows that entity before the next sketch entity in the same Design stream. A member-run sketch without such a scope retains no parameter-scope owner.

A text-frame boundary curve has type GUID `16DEFC4D-1816-4FB0-8E39-9BDA23954248`, version `0`, and add-in `MSketch`. It uses the ordinary `EntityGenesis` curve-identity prefix followed by two point references. The first reference has seven zero bytes after its u32 record index and the second has six. An inline indexed analytic-curve record follows: its numeric LP-ASCII class tag is followed by the enclosing curve record index, eight zero bytes, and the ordinary twelve-f64 bounded-line payload. The line coordinates and displacement use centimetres.

A sketch relation is the leading-block presence byte `01`, a u32 count and that many `(reference, u32 relation ordinal)` pairs, the property-block presence byte and its block, the `ParentNode` reference naming the owning Sketch, a u64 constraint mask, a u32 count and that many bare references, and one zero byte. The leading-block presence byte is also the constraint-mask width discriminator. Value `01` selects the paired member run and the u64 mask. Value `00` selects the relation base class's version-0 form, omits the pair list, and selects a u32 mask. Another value is invalid and does not select a mask width. The mask is little-endian, so every mask above `0xff` begins with a zero byte and a reader that locates it by skipping zeros reads it shifted. The property block carries `EntityGenesis` where the relation has one. The record ends at the trailing zero byte, at the next indexed-record header. Relation kind is a property of the record class: the shared relation class, the text-path class, and the spline class are distinct classes, and no member of any of them encodes a kind.

A sketch-relation class writes its own members between the property block and `ParentNode`. The class is named by the type GUID its segment's type table carries for the record's entity; a class tag cannot name it, because a tag is `256` plus an index into that segment's own type table and one tag names different relation classes in different segments. `60403D47-0C49-49B0-BDE8-1679608164A2` is the shared relation class, `D3BD153B-EB8A-405E-9D29-69EE0C3D227C` the offset class, and `73762C3B-82DC-4632-93B0-B8FE1CC5282F` the spline-group class; none of the three writes a member of its own, so `ParentNode` follows the property block directly. `24DB790E-3DCD-4336-AFA3-6F119EF2239B` is the tangency class and writes three `u8` flags, each `0` or `1`. `8B369926-123F-4F9D-878E-6D4C076128D3` is the text-frame class and writes two references, the second of which is the sketch-text entity and repeats the relation's first member. `9D30FCDC-EA07-4141-93E2-918B1A59E962` is the text-path class and writes the text-entity reference, a u32 character count, and that many glyph blocks; from class version 1 a `u8 1` precedes the reference. `8269E861-0BB7-47E0-9911-5AE3EC475058` is the circular-pattern class and writes the optional angle-parameter reference, the optional count-parameter reference, the evaluated f64 total angle in radians, the evaluated u32 instance count, the pattern tables, and one zero byte. `40800FB9-C2BE-494E-A047-7D76E82B9F6C` is the rectangular-pattern class and writes three `u8` flags, a u32-counted run of references, the pattern tables, and its two direction clauses. The pattern tables are a u32-counted map whose entry is a u64 key, a u32 count, and that many u64 values, followed by a u32-counted run of u32; either table may be empty.

The tangency subclass flags refer to the semantic return-member order. For a bounded endpoint contact, the first two bytes select the first and second curve's contact endpoint: `1` selects the stored start and `0` selects the stored end. The third byte selects the sign of the two parameter-direction tangents at that contact: `1` means a positive dot product and `0` means a negative dot product. A full circle has no distinct start or end locus. The bytes retain solver-branch state; they do not assert that cached derivatives are exactly parallel. A shared-class relation with mask `0x100` stores tangency without these subclass bytes.

The rectangular-pattern reference run materializes ordered optional direction-entity slots, direction one before direction two. Its count is zero, one, or two; a materialized slot can hold a null reference. A non-null target is a line parallel or antiparallel to its direction clause. The first of the three rectangular flags is `uses_extent`; the second selects symmetry in direction one. The third flag retains its encoded value. The fixed class prefix is in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

The pattern map is an optional instance-identity cache. Its values are persistent `crv_primary_id` values, in the corresponding instance's curve order. A value vector can repeat the complete ordered group. A reduced evaluated count does not remove stale cache entries. Circular keys are one-based instance ordinals. For a rectangular pattern with one row, zero-based direction-one instance `i` has triangular key `(i + 1)(i + 2) / 2`. The map can be empty; its keys do not define the evaluated geometry. Retained records preserve entry order, value multiplicity, and stale entries.

The u32 run after the pattern map stores suppressed full-pattern instance ordinals. Ordinal zero is the seed. Stored ordinal `k`, with `k` at least one, corresponds to suppression-array index `k - 1`. The active instance set excludes those ordinals before the return geometry is divided into instance groups. An empty run suppresses no instance.

The text-frame class's first reference is an optional materialized center point. Its type is `00D157C2-2332-4BD5-BB53-048C4081D1C3`, derived from the ordinary sketch-point family. Its coordinates equal the arithmetic mean of the four frame boundary starts. A present center also occurs in the relation's member and return graph; a null first reference does not materialize that helper. The second class reference remains the text entity.

The two reference runs hold the same members. The integer interleaved into the first run is a relation ordinal, not a member role: it counts the relations already recorded on the member it follows, so the integers on one member are pairwise distinct across that member's relations and say nothing about the member's part in this relation. Only the second run is in semantic order, and member position below means position in the second run. A native neutral relation retains both runs and the auxiliary references in field order; repeated references remain repeated. A zero mask denotes the default coincident relation. Constraint bits are `0x1` coincident, `0x2` colinear, `0x4` concentric or operand-discriminated symmetry, `0x8` equal length, `0x10` parallel or operand-discriminated midpoint, `0x20` perpendicular or operand-discriminated offset, `0x40` horizontal, `0x80` vertical, `0x100` tangent, `0x200` curvature, `0x400` symmetry, `0x800` equal, `0x1000` midpoint, `0x2000` polygon, `0x10000000` circular pattern, `0x20000000` rectangular pattern, `0x80000000` spline group, `0x2000000000` offset, `0x10000000000` text frame, and `0x20000000000` text path. Binary neutral geometric constraints require two distinct entity identities. A single-bit `0x40` or `0x80` relation with one line constrains the line horizontally or vertically. With two point entities, `0x40` constrains equal vertical sketch coordinates and `0x80` constrains equal horizontal sketch coordinates. A single-bit polygon relation with at least three completely resolved member references transfers those members in source order as one polygon constraint. A single-bit `0x100` or `0x200` relation transfers only when both resolved members are curve-valued; `0x100` is tangency and `0x200` is equal tangent-direction and curvature continuity at contact. A single-bit `0x800` relation transfers equal size for two lines, two circular entities, or two ellipses; a circle and circular arc are compatible circular entities. Other member families retain the native relation and ordered operands. A `0x4` relation between two circular or elliptical entities is concentric. A three-member `0x4` or `0x400` relation is symmetry when all three entity identities are distinct and exactly one line member is a reflection axis that maps the other two point, line, equal-radius full-circle, or equal-radius circular-arc entities onto each other; reflected arcs also have equal sweep magnitude and reflected endpoint sets. The unique geometric relation assigns the axis independently of member order. A `0x10` relation with two line members is parallel. A `0x10` or `0x1000` relation with one bounded line and one point whose coordinates equal the arithmetic mean of the line's stored endpoints constrains that point to the line midpoint; member order does not change the roles. A `0x1000` relation with one circular arc and one point at the arc's middle angle, the arithmetic mean of its start and end angles, constrains that point to the arc midpoint; member order does not change the roles. A `0x10000000` relation's input members are the pattern center point and the seed entities; its generated members are the instance entities. Its class members carry the angle parameter, the count parameter, the evaluated total angle, and the evaluated instance count. Its return run lists the instances in instance order and ends with the center point. A `0x20000000` relation stores two direction clauses after the class's counted reference run and its pattern tables. The first clause starts at the byte after the second pattern table; its optional count-parameter reference directly follows its evaluated count. Each clause is the evaluated u32 count, the count-parameter reference, a three-component f64 unit direction, a source distance scalar, and the distance-parameter reference, in that order, so each count directly precedes its count-parameter reference. A clause parameter reference can be null. A non-null reference identifies its driving parameter; a null reference leaves the evaluated count or signed distance without a driving parameter and does not change the clause framing. The first rectangular class flag selects the distance form: `0` stores signed adjacent spacing and `1` stores the signed total seed-to-final span. For an extent with count greater than one, adjacent spacing is the scalar divided by count minus one. The counted reference run selects neither distance form. Count includes the seed instance. The member and return runs list instances in instance-major order with one fixed per-instance entity order; the first instance is the seed. The direction-one index advances fastest: with direction-one count `n`, instance position `p` has direction-one index `p mod n` and direction-two index `p div n`. The distance scalar of a direction with count one moves no instance. A `0x80000000` relation is the spline-group relation: it binds a spline's curve-identity records and its primary curve record to the owning sketch and carries no geometric constraint; a relation whose sole bit is `0x80000000` and whose complete member run resolves to distinct typed entities transfers those members in source order as one spline-group constraint. In a model-space spline group the second run ends with the NURBS and the preceding members are the consecutive control-polygon segments: member `i` joins control points `i` and `i+1`. The first run holds the same members in an unrelated order, so its last entry does not name the spline. A preceding member without an independent geometry payload inherits that exact solved segment; an independently stored segment must have the same ordered endpoints. A `0x10000000000` relation's members are the sketch-text entity followed by its frame curves; the text entity repeats as the second of the class's two references, and the return run names the frame curves. A `0x20000000000` relation occupies a record class distinct from the shared sketch-relation class. Its members are the path curve and the sketch-text entity, and its return run names the path curve. Its class members are the text-entity reference, a u32 character count, and that many blocks of `u32 16` and a row-major 4×4 f64 transform placing one character in the owning sketch frame in centimetres, in character order; `ParentNode` follows the last block directly. Pattern angle- and distance-parameter references resolve to scalar parameter owner frames and pattern count-parameter references resolve to counted parameter owner frames of the pattern's input parameters.

Sketch text occupies two record classes. `E0618268-3A06-450E-9E94-7CF4C2E66802` is the `textex_tag` class and `f0b1afa3-3baf-42d0-b2f3-94b95662f2a9` is the `txt_tag` class; both derive from `8E9D588C-28EF-43C4-B9A6-AA5430A68D4B` and both type-table entries carry the add-in name `Geometry`. A legacy record of either class carries its identity as a property-block key, not as a member: `textex_tag` in the first class and `txt_tag` in the second, with `txt_tag_base` and `EntityGenesis` optional in both. A `txt_tag` record below class version 4 writes no identity key at all and stores no persistent identity; its property block can hold `txt_tag_base` alone. Such a record uses its indexed-record index as a source-local text identity within the owning Sketch. The source-local identity is unique within the Design stream but does not claim persistence across a rewritten source document. The legacy classes share the record prefix, the leading block, and the property block, and diverge after them. The leading block takes the form a sketch relation carries: a presence byte, and, when that byte is `01`, a u32 count and that many `(reference, u32)` pairs.

The indexed Design form of `textex_tag` has the indexed header: the three-digit class tag is followed by a u32 record index at byte 7. Bytes 11 through 19 are zero, and the ordinary property block starts at byte 20. This form has no record-name string or leading relation block. Its property block contains `textex_tag` and may contain `EntityGenesis`. The byte after the property block is zero, followed by the f64 width factor, four f32 RGBA colour components, the counted UTF-16LE font-family name, a zero byte, and the f64 nominal text height in centimetres. After the common text body, its class suffix is a u32 text-type discriminator (`0` for frame text or `1` for path text), followed by u32 values `1, 256, 0, 0`, two zero bytes, two positive f32 scale values, and five zero bytes. The owning-sketch reference follows the suffix. The indexed form carries no neutral anchor or rotation.

In a `textex_tag` record the property block is followed by `u8 1`, an f64 horizontal width factor, four f32 RGBA colour components each in `[0, 1]`, a u32-count UTF-16LE font-family name, `u8 0`, and an f64 nominal text height in centimetres. The width factor precedes the font family and the height follows it; a reader that swaps them assigns every text the same height. The width factor takes `0` and `1`, so a reader that requires it positive refuses the records storing `0`; the height is always positive. A `0` does not scale glyph advance to zero, so it does not denote a zero horizontal scale, and a neutral model takes no width factor from a record storing zero.

In a `txt_tag` record the twenty-nine bytes from the end of the property block to the u32 font-family count are the f64 rotation, a style byte, four residual bytes, and the four f32 RGBA colour components each in `[0, 1]`. The class stores no width factor. Its font-family name is directly followed by the height, with no zero byte between them, and it inserts members between the height and the text string: two Boolean bytes, the f64 x and y coordinates of the text anchor point in the sketch frame in centimetres, and eleven further bytes ahead of the u32-count UTF-16LE text string. Below class version 4 that run is ten zero bytes. At class version 4 it is `00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00`. The first Boolean byte after the height selects horizontal flip. The second Boolean is independent. Bit 0 of the style byte selects bold. The remaining style bits and the four residual bytes retain their encoded values; they do not define an italic or underline assignment.

A `textex_tag` record writes two optional parameter-reference members: one after the height naming the parameter driving it, and one after the text string naming the parameter driving the content. The record either writes a member, whose own presence byte then says whether it targets a parameter, or omits it; nothing ahead of a slot distinguishes the two, so a reader frames the record by requiring the member sequence to end exactly on the owning-sketch reference. Between the two slots the record stores a u32 horizontal-alignment enum, three flag bytes, and a u32-count UTF-16LE text string; after the second slot it stores a u32 vertical-alignment enum, one flag byte, and an i32 font weight. Horizontal value `1` is left, `2` is right, and `3` is center. Vertical value `1` is top, `2` is bottom, and `3` is middle. Each alignment varies independently of the other. The font weight is a signed i32. Values `400`, `500`, and `750` map to normal, medium, and bold weight; other values retain their numeric identity without that three-value assignment.

A `textex_tag` record's class tail opens with a u32 text-type enum: `0` is frame text and stores a row-major 4×4 f64 placement transform, `1` is path text and stores none. One flag byte follows the enum, ahead of the transform slot, and repeats the enum's value. The transform is a rigid placement. Its bottom row is `(0, 0, 0, 1)`, and it carries no scale and no shear. Its third row and third column are the identity's and its 2×2 basis has determinant `+1`, or its third row is `(0, 0, -1, 0)`, its third column is `(0, 0, -1, 0)`, and its 2×2 basis has determinant `-1`. The second form turns the sketch plane over and mirrors the text in the sketch. In the first form, column 3 is the text anchor point in the sketch frame in centimetres, and the angle of basis column 0 is the text rotation counterclockwise about that anchor. A record whose text type is path text stores no anchor and no rotation. A `txt_tag` record writes neither the parameter-reference slots nor the text-type enum and its transform: its f64 text rotation in radians directly follows the property block and is followed by five bytes before the colour components. Its text string is followed by a u32-counted reference run, bytes `00 01 00`, an i32 font weight, and an f64 cached natural text width in centimetres. The cached width is independent of the frame width. Zero is an explicit unrotated value. Thirty bytes and the padded owning-sketch reference close a record of either class. A `textex_tag` record can store four zero bytes between the thirty bytes and the owning-sketch reference. Text-frame and text-path relations resolve the text record as a typed sketch entity. Text-path character transforms scale their translation column from centimetres to neutral millimetres.

The `txt_tag` leading block names four frame lines in perimeter order. Each line names the text entity and the same owning sketch. The first line starts at the text anchor and follows the rotation axis, reversed when horizontal flip is set. The second line has the nominal text height. The post-string reference run repeats these same four line references once or twice in the same order.

The legacy text presentation suffix is thirty bytes: u32 `0`, u8 `1`, five f32 values `(0, 0, 0, 1, 1)`, u32 `0`, and u8 `0`. This suffix carries inherited presentation defaults. It does not supply the glyph colour; the RGBA run before the font family supplies that colour. The fixed text-member and presentation layouts are in [the layout tables](../layouts/f3d.md).

A two-line `0x20` relation is perpendicular. An aggregate `0x20` offset relation has an even return-member run of at least four curve records. Consecutive return members form ordered `(source, result)` pairs. Each source curve has a null secondary persistent identity and each result curve has a nonzero secondary identity. Every resolved entity participates in exactly one pair. Every pair resolves to parallel bounded lines at one common positive separation magnitude. A result on the source curve's right side reverses that source traversal before applying the common distance along its left normal. The relation constrains the complete ordered pair set at that common offset distance. The `0x2000000000` offset relation stores an even member run. Its second run supplies the source/result bijection in order, as consecutive `(source, result)` pairs; source secondary identities need not be null, so one relation's results can be the next relation's sources. It stores one or more pairs. Each pair resolves to parallel bounded lines, or to a circle or arc and a circle or arc whose centers coincide, at one common positive separation magnitude. Two arcs of one pair share their traversal direction and overlap in angle. The signed distance of a line pair is measured along the source line's left normal. The signed distance of a circular pair is the source radius minus the result radius, negated for a clockwise source arc. A single-curve linear annotation frame drives an otherwise unparameterized offset relation when its curve is one of that relation's sources and its parameter magnitude uniquely equals the relation's common distance.

Each member and return-member index resolves through the indexed Design record graph. A sketch-point record contributes its persistent point identity, and a sketch-curve record contributes its primary and nullable secondary persistent curve identities. Other indices retain their generic indexed-record identity. Resolution preserves the encoded run order and cardinality. Persistent point identities and persistent curve-identity pairs are unique within one owning sketch in one Design `BulkStream`. Neutral sketch-entity identities combine the byte-length-prefixed owning sketch identity, a point-or-curve discriminator, and the corresponding persistent identity values; indexed-record position does not participate.

A relation whose sole constraint bit is coincident and whose complete member run resolves to distinct typed sketch points or curves constrains those entity loci to coincide. Repeated references to one entity retain the native relation because they do not distinguish multiple loci on that entity. A point and curve pair is a point-on-curve constraint. The encoded member run supplies the neutral coincident-locus order without an additional endpoint selector. When the solved geometry has exactly one shared point across all members and exactly one point, start, end, or center locus per member at that position, those exact loci define the neutral constraint. Multiple shared positions or multiple loci from one member at the shared position retain whole-entity coincidence.

Relations owned by a spatial Sketch use the same member and return runs. Coincident, midpoint, tangent, horizontal, vertical, and spline-group bits retain their ordinary geometric meanings in model space. A coincident relation resolves only between two distinct points at the same transformed model-space position. A midpoint relation resolves only when its point equals the transformed midpoint of its bounded line. A tangent relation resolves only between two distinct spatial curve entities. A single-line horizontal relation constrains the model-space line parallel to placement-matrix column 0; a single-line vertical relation constrains it parallel to column 1. Spatial point coordinates come from the point record's complete `(u,v,w)` payload rather than from a planar projection.

A spatial Sketch linear-dimension annotation frame can carry one null annotation locus followed by two line loci. The two line records define the measured entities; the null locus carries no geometric operand. When the transformed lines are parallel, their model-space minimum separation equals the governing length parameter.

A spatial Sketch `Linear Dimension*` parameter without a typed annotation frame first governs every bounded line in its owner whose model-space endpoint distance equals the evaluated length within the source kernel's absolute linear resolution. One matching line establishes a line-length relation. Multiple matching lines establish a repeated line-length relation in spatial-sketch entity order. With no matching line, the parameter governs a parallel-line distance only when exactly one pair of transformed lines has the evaluated model-space minimum separation. When that entity-pair rule does not establish a relation, collinear transformed lines form carriers within the same resolution. The unique pair of parallel carriers with the evaluated minimum separation and overlapping bounded member spans establishes a parallel-line-set distance when at least one carrier contains multiple entities. Carrier members follow spatial-sketch entity order. Zero or multiple matching carrier pairs do not establish a neutral relation.

The owning sketch reference is the numeric suffix of the owning sketch container's full Design entity id. It resolves through the sketch entity-header table. The reference applies to every typed sketch-point and sketch-curve record named by the relation's member and return-member runs. All relations using one typed geometry record carry the same owning sketch reference. Conflicting owner references are invalid.

A sketch-point record contains one typed property named `pt_tag`: `u32 property_count=1`, LP-ASCII `pt_tag`, LP-ASCII `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64`, and the persistent u64 point id. The record then stores `0x01`, a u32 paired record reference, a 14-byte flag area whose bytes are each `0x00` or `0x01`, and two f64 sketch coordinates at record offsets 89 and 97. The alternate form sets `property_count=2` and prefixes `pt_tag` with an `EntityGenesis` `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64` property; all subsequent fields shift by 52 bytes. The center point of a fillet arc can store the `pt_tag` of the filleted corner point. That center point has one incident curve and the corner point has other incident curves; the later of the two points takes its record index as its point identity.

A sketch-curve record contains two typed properties in order: `crv_primary_id` and `crv_secondary_id`, both `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64`. The primary id is the curve's persistent identity; zero in the secondary slot is null. The identity pair does not name one curve record: distinct curve records owned by one Sketch can carry the same primary and secondary ids, and each such record is a separate curve. The alternate form sets `property_count=3` and prefixes these properties with an `EntityGenesis` `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64` property, shifting the curve identity and geometry fields by 52 bytes. The `EntityGenesis` value on a sketch point or curve is an origin bitfield: bit `0x2` marks a user-authored entity, bit `0x4` marks SVG-imported sketch geometry, bit `0x8` marks source geometry imported from DXF, bits `0x80` and `0x100` mark rectangular- and circular-pattern membership, and bit `0x200` marks a result curve generated by a sketch offset. A generated center point of an imported circular arc and native text-generated entities carry zero. The segment type table selects the geometry family before the geometry payload is read. Type GUID `DCA267ED-D615-4934-B64F-AD805E8003E2`, version `1` or `2`, add-in `Geometry`, is the bounded-line class. Its derived bounded-line classes are `EA3B930A-3383-4AD3-BE25-4B2814EA3985`, version `0`; `AE42BAB6-643F-4169-A33C-529C8E0A4D84`, version `0`; `F279874A-17AB-43DA-BF8E-80259802D06E`, version `0`; and `58751243-FEA8-41E6-BBC9-37960EB8164B`, version `0`, all with add-in `Geometry`. Type GUID `F0130424-8B7E-4092-93C9-1CA807482534`, version `0`, add-in `Geometry`, is the full-circle and circular-arc class. Type GUID `FF23079A-D99C-47AB-940E-2F4E18F022AB`, version `2`, add-in `Geometry`, is a second circular-arc class. A full analytic payload following the identity properties is twelve f64 values. A line stores `(start point xyz, displacement xyz, auxiliary unit direction xyz, unit sketch normal xyz)`. Start plus displacement defines its bounded geometry; the neutral unit tangent is the normalized displacement. A circular arc stores `(center xyz, unit normal xyz, in-plane unit reference direction xyz, radius, start angle, end angle)`. Angles are radians. A full circle stores an angular interval spanning 2π. Point coordinates, displacements, and radii in fixed-form records are in centimetres; in `EntityGenesis`-form records they are ten times the centimetre value, and the placement frame maps `(x/10, y/10, 0)` into model space. A planar neutral projection accepts local sketch normal `(0,0,+1)` or `(0,0,-1)` and multiplies arc angles by its z sign to use the neutral positive-z angular convention. A referenced analytic wrapper prefixes this payload with `0x01 + u32 record_ref + six zero bytes`.

Immediately after the 96-byte analytic payload, a planar sketch-curve record stores `N` (`1 <= N <= 3`) contiguous 11-byte marked references (`0x01` + u32 `record_index` + six zero bytes), followed by `P` pad bytes (`P = 5` when `N = 1`, `P = 3` when `N` is `2` or `3`), three opaque bytes, a u8 tail marker, u32 `1`, and a u8 construction flag; when the u8 construction flag equals `1`, the curve is construction geometry. The tail marker is `0` or `1`. A curve with tail marker `1` is not named by a counted region member list. A planar sketch-curve record can store two opaque bytes in place of the three. In that form, one byte follows the two opaque bytes, then a u32 lane that is `0` or `1`, then a byte that is `1`.

A spatial-sketch surface record has `property_count=2`: `EntityGenesis` followed by `surface_tag`, both `IntrinsicMetaTypeuint64`. The surface tag is its persistent identity. A u32 control-point count follows the surface tag, then that many xyz f64 control points in centimetres. The tensor-product definition follows as u32 first degree, u32 second degree, u32 first knot count and its f64 knots, u32 second knot count and its f64 knots, then u32 first control count and u32 second control count. Control points are first-parameter-major. Their count equals the product of the two control counts, and each knot count equals its control count plus its degree plus one. Both knot vectors are nondecreasing. The owning spatial Sketch placement transforms every control point into model space.

A spatial-sketch `Coincident` relation between a point record and a surface record constrains the point to lie on that surface.

A sketch NURBS payload begins with either an eight-byte all-`0xff` null sentinel or a non-null u64 carrier reference, then a nested dynamic-class record header, the degree marker, f64 fit tolerance, and three arrays. Each array header is `(u32 count, u32 duplicate_count, u32 scalar_width=8)`. The arrays are the nondecreasing f64 knot vector, positive f64 weights, and xyz f64 control points. A non-rational curve stores a zero-length weight array; otherwise weight and control-point counts are equal. In both forms, `knot_count = control_point_count + degree + 1`. Fit tolerance and control points are in centimetres. Type GUID `D82E012F-6DDD-4AED-BDE1-C0F7F9100B9B`, version `3`, add-in `MSketch`, is the standalone spline-curve class. It carries this payload after its curve-identity properties, and its counted control-point array holds the curve's control points in centimetres.

The ACT `BulkStream` is framed by its sibling `MetaStream` primary index. Each primary `(u64 record index, u64 BulkStream offset)` pair starts one record. Its extent ends at the next primary offset or at the end of the stream. Offsets increase strictly, and record indexes are unique u32 values. Each record starts with an LP-ASCII class tag of exactly three decimal digits and the same u32 record index. Class tag `n` names type-table entry `n - 256`, and that entry's entity-ID list contains the record index. An `ACTTable` byte window in another indexed record's payload does not identify the table.

**The ACT segment.** An ACT segment tracks change versions per design entity. Its records key on an **entity key**, the LP-UTF16 string `<segment id>_<entity id>` naming a design entity of the same document. Where an entity key sits beside a reference to the entity it names, the segment id in the key is that reference's target segment id.

An **ACT component link** payload is ten zero bytes, `0x01 + u32 instance-root record + six zero bytes`, an entity key, `0x01 + u32 tracked-entity record + five zero bytes`, `0x01 + u32 registry flag`, an LP-UTF16 display name, zero through eight zero bytes, and `0x01 + u32 components-root record`. Zero bytes can fill the remainder of the indexed record extent. The registry flag is zero or one. There is one link per component. The tracked-entity field is a Design record reference to an entity of the component type `E03784ED-5E19-4E14-B9F2-3B07017018CD`. The entity key does not select a document root and need not end in `_3`. The document-root link tracks entity `3` of the component type. A Design whose component type has no entity `3` has a document-root link that tracks another entity of that type. An ACT stream can contain an ACT table and change groups without component links.

An **ACT change group** payload is ten zero bytes, a u32 count, that many `(LP-ASCII change kind, LP-UTF16 change version GUID)` pairs, and an optional entity key of the entity the group tracks. The semantic payload ends after the optional entity key. An all-zero remainder is padding. Nonzero bytes after the final semantic payload are opaque stream residue, including any leading zero bytes; they are not class-owned fields. A source-preserving rewrite retains this residue byte for byte. A source-less writer ends the group after the optional entity key and does not generate residue from the dynamic class tag. The change-group type GUID is `ABC8C0E3-50FB-4E8C-AFF3-116759A36073`, with base GUID `19E286C3-1C58-4F13-8050-3F00EC2F1562`, version 0, module `ACT`; its dynamic tag is a stream-local type-table ordinal. The change kinds are `Appearance`, `Geometry`, `PhysicalMaterial`, `Properties`, `StructureChange`, and `Transform`. A group holds a subset of them. The all-zero GUID is the unchanged state. The indexed record index is the change group's identity. A group without an entity key gets it from its ACT-table row. A keyed group can have no inline ACT-table row.

The ACT segment has exactly one indexed **ACT table** record. After its dynamic record header, it stores a zero u32, LP-ASCII `ACTTable`, a zero u16, a u32 row count, and that many rows. A row is `0x01 + u32 change-group record index + six zero bytes + LP-UTF16 entity key`. Its record index names one change group. When the group repeats the key, the two keys are equal. Duplicate row indexes, duplicate groups, a missing group, or a key disagreement are invalid.

An uncounted ordered GUID pool follows the rows. Each pool item is an LP-UTF16 canonical 36-character hyphenated GUID. The pool carries stream-wide change-version and occurrence-role identities. It ends at the first field that is not such a GUID; pool position does not assign a GUID to one row or channel. A u32 reference count follows, then that many `0x01 + u32 target record + six zero bytes` references. Each target is a record in the same primary index. A u32 channel-registry count follows, then that many `(LP-ASCII channel name, LP-UTF16 canonical 36-character GUID)` entries. Registry names are unique. The registry ends at the indexed table record's extent.

An **ACT instance root** opens with the prologue, a further u8, a u32 count, and that many LP-ASCII change kinds, which are the same six kinds in the same order. Two references, the entity key, and a further reference follow them.

On a body, `generic_tag_attrib_def` supplies a one-through-eight-byte ASCII design/construction ID distinct from the material-assignment suffix. This ID keys the design BulkStream body construction-recipe records and is retained without truncation. A body can have no body-keyed recipe.

A compact single-member `Fillet` or `Chamfer` scope can carry a Design lineage key instead of an ASM edge number. The lineage key is the exact pair of asset and context UUIDs. Its local Design identity is not an edge slot. Candidate histories contain the exact serialized current-to-previous state pair, including no-op histories. Each independent selector contributes only when its intersection with those candidates contains one history. All contributing selectors must agree, and at least one must contribute. Whole-body recipe operands with the same lineage key contribute their source-qualified persistent face references. A construction identity with the same persistent lineage key contributes the history of its owning scope only when that scope's exact state pair identifies one history.

The compact owner-body wrapper has EntityTracking type GUID `CB4F4CC2-9D6F-48BA-9B1F-20C1992C9C9C`, base GUID `5C069ACB-169F-4555-9792-815B4671DDA0`, version 2. Its primary indexed frame is 33 bytes: the eleven-byte indexed header, ten zero bytes, a marked u64 reference to the following indexed record, then three zero bytes. The adjacent carrier has EntityTracking type GUID `90055C05-546C-4EE7-B3C9-3DD922AD0C9C`, base GUID `70F5E801-1E8E-436E-8A09-36487F8A2859`, version 0. Its 29-byte primary indexed frame contains the eleven-byte header, ten zero bytes, and a u64 Design body suffix. Both records must match their primary indexes and dynamic type registrations. The wrapper reference names the carrier; the carrier index is the wrapper index plus one. A construction group's retained wrapper chain that ends at this owner wrapper contributes the BREP source obtained by joining the suffix to the same Design stream's body map. Physical proximity to a scope does not establish ownership.

For a lineage-bound compact scope with one group and one member, the transition rule assigns the member only when the reconstructed treatment chain contains one edge. The full deleted-edge set does not assign the member. Missing, ambiguous, or conflicting lineage selectors do not bind a history. An empty or multi-edge treatment chain does not assign a member through the transition rule. Independent operand-recipe rules can assign the member within the selected history.

An executed `Fillet` or `Chamfer` group with exactly one selection operand resolves a connected source-edge chain from its exact ASM transition. A result face is a treatment face when its sole surface carrier is absent from the preceding topology. Its support faces are the result faces adjacent across its boundary that map to one preceding face. A face that occurs in the preceding topology maps to itself when its sole surface carrier is unchanged. A result face absent from the preceding topology maps to the one preceding face on its sole surface carrier; when that carrier has no single preceding face, it maps to a removed preceding face on the same carrier that owned one of its loops. Each mapping holds only when every loop of the result face that a preceding face owned belongs to the mapped face, and no such loop had two preceding owners. Every preceding edge shared by a pair of those support faces and deleted by the transition belongs to the selected chain. The chain is the nonempty increasing stable-slot-order union across all treatment faces. Recipe evidence is the union of each operand's changed and deleted boundary edges and the changed-reference edge sets selected by its local topology references; when local topology references are absent, all reference contexts contribute. When any recipe evidence exists, every chain edge must occur in that union. A directly resolved deleted boundary edge must occur in the chain, and every operand with deleted boundary edges must share one chain edge. A transition-chain vector is scoped to the complete state transition and repeats on persistent identities that share that transition. The repeated vectors do not assign edges to individual identities. A group with multiple full-layout persistent members does not take the transition-chain vector as its selection.

An executed `Hem` group has one selectorless empty reference context for the selected edge and one or more nonempty reference contexts for its support faces. The union of those nonempty contexts contains the support-face boundary edges changed by the transition. The selected source edge is the unique changed boundary edge absent from that union. A sole candidate is a historical edge selection in the group's preceding state; no sole candidate leaves the native selection unresolved.

The deleted-triplet proof is independent of contextual reference-edge intersections. A unique deleted-triplet slot resolves when selected reference sets are empty or disjoint. Any other exact deleted-edge proof must name the same slot.

A class-413 Mirror scope has primary class `413` and paired class `262`. Its ordered reference table is variable and precedes the kind string. The fixed tail after the UTF-16LE kind has 77 bytes: offset 0 stores the feature ordinal, offset 31 stores the preceding-history state, offset 35 stores u32 marker `89`, offset 39 stores the positive stitch tolerance as an f64 in source centimetres, and offset 47 repeats marker `89`. Offset 51 stores a marked reference to scope index plus two followed by two zero bytes; offset 64 stores a marked reference to scope index plus one followed by two zero bytes. The paired indexed header begins at offset 77 of this tail. The class-413 frame has no owner-local ordinal-one tolerance record.

A class-440 Mirror scope has primary class `440` and paired class `258`. Its ordered reference table is variable and precedes the kind string. The fixed tail after the UTF-16LE kind has 77 bytes with the same field offsets and reference order as the class-413 tail, but both scalar markers are u32 `100`. The f64 at tail offset 39 is the positive stitch tolerance in source centimetres; the references at offsets 51 and 64 name scope index plus two and plus one, each followed by two zero bytes. The paired indexed header begins at tail offset 77. The class-440 frame has no owner-local ordinal-one tolerance record.

A class-441 Mirror scope has primary class `441` and paired class `267`. Its ordered reference table is variable and precedes the kind string. The fixed tail after the UTF-16LE kind has 72 bytes: offset 0 stores the feature ordinal, offset 30 stores the preceding-history state, offset 34 stores u32 marker `61`, and offset 38 stores the positive stitch tolerance as an f64 in source centimetres. Offset 46 stores a marked reference to scope index plus two followed by two zero bytes, and offset 59 stores a marked reference to scope index plus one followed by two zero bytes. The paired indexed header begins at tail offset 72. This form has no repeated scalar marker and no owner-local ordinal-one tolerance record. The scope reference at ordinal 3 names a class-426 primary frame paired with class `267`; its 99-byte frame stores the exact count `2` at offset 40, a parameter reference to count-record index plus two at offset 45, owned ordinal `1` at offset 55, scope-record index at offset 64, companion-record index plus one at offset 77, and scope-record index at offset 89. The paired class-267 header begins at offset 99.

A class-391 Mirror scope has primary class `391` and paired class `261`. Its ordered reference table is variable and precedes the kind string. The fixed tail after the UTF-16LE kind has 76 bytes: offset 0 stores the feature ordinal, offset 30 stores the preceding-history state, offset 34 stores u32 marker `94`, and offset 38 stores the positive stitch tolerance as an f64 in source centimetres. Offset 46 stores u32 marker `94`; offset 50 stores a marked reference to scope index plus two followed by two zero bytes, and offset 63 stores a marked reference to scope index plus one followed by two zero bytes. The paired indexed header begins at tail offset 76. This form has no owner-local ordinal-one tolerance record.

A class-369 Mirror scope has primary class `369` and paired class `261`. Its ordered reference table is variable and precedes the kind string. The fixed tail after the UTF-16LE kind has 77 bytes: offset 0 stores the feature ordinal, offset 31 stores the preceding-history state, offset 35 stores u32 marker `89`, offset 39 stores the positive stitch tolerance as an f64 in source centimetres, and offset 47 repeats marker `89`. Offset 51 stores a marked reference to scope index plus two followed by two zero bytes; offset 64 stores a marked reference to scope index plus one followed by two zero bytes. The paired indexed header begins at offset 77 of this tail. The class-369 frame has no owner-local ordinal-one tolerance record.

#### Constant-radius edge chains
