A recipe-backed constant-radius group resolves by a chain proof. Every member contributes all of its radius-qualified deleted predecessor edges, including candidates outside that member's changed boundary; an individually proven member also contributes its proven edge. A member with neither contribution is topology context and is permitted only when its changed-boundary-edge set is empty. The group resolves to the increasing stable-slot-order union of these contributions. One operand can therefore denote more than one edge in a connected treatment chain. A transition-derived radius-candidate vector on a persistent identity describes the complete operation transition and alone can prove only a one-member group. A Fillet group whose identity members share one transition edge set and one radius selects that set when each member's deleted boundary edges form a nonempty subset and their union equals the set. A one-member group also selects the transition set when the set is a nonempty subset of the member's deleted edges and every radius candidate on the member lies in the set. Every edge in the set must blend at that radius. Except for this complete-coverage proof and the compact exact-deletion cardinality proof, a multi-member persistent-identity group requires an exact edge contribution from every member.

The transition of a constant-radius `Fillet` feature states its edges. The feature names exactly one parameter scope. The scope's history state and its preceding state occur as one pair in the scope's bound history, else in exactly one history; both states have topologies, and the transition of the history state starts at the preceding state, which is the input state. When the scope has no bound history and several histories hold the pair, the edges come from the one history in which the blend proof replaces the selection of at least one group and every group then has a historical selection, where a history whose transition binds through the covering rule counts only when no history binds without it; this reading is reported as `history.edge-history-inferred`, and the feature's input topology and outputs come from that history. When more than one history or none meets this condition, the selections stay. The fillet replaces each edge that it rounds with a blend face on a new surface carrier at the radius of the edge's group. A blend carrier is a surface of the result topology with one cylinder row, or a torus: a surface with one axis row whose origin is finite, one radius row, and no cylinder row. The axis direction of a blend carrier is finite and nonzero. A cylinder blend replaces a straight edge whose axis row and midpoint tangent are parallel to the cylinder axis. A torus blend replaces a circle whose axis row is parallel to the torus axis, whose midpoint tangent is perpendicular to the torus axis, and whose centre is within `1e-6` mm of the torus axis line. Two directions are parallel when the cross product of their unit vectors has a norm of at most `1e-9`, and perpendicular when the dot product of their unit vectors has an absolute value of at most `1e-9`. The supports of a blend face, as defined above, share zero or more preceding edges of that geometry. When they share one, it is the replaced edge, and the transition deletes it. When the supports of a cylinder blend share no preceding edge along its axis, the replaced edge is read from candidates. A candidate is a preceding edge on the boundary of a support that runs along the axis, lies more than `1e-6` mm beyond the radius from the axis line, lies within `1e-6` mm of the axial extent of the blend, and has a support owner on a plane that touches the cylinder. Candidates rank first when they have exactly two owner faces and the other owner is a face that the transition removes and that meets another support at a preceding edge that runs along the axis, lies within `1e-6` mm of the radius from the axis line, and lies within `1e-6` mm of the axial extent of the blend; then by increasing distance from the axis line; then by increasing slot. The replaced edge is the best-ranked candidate that the transition deletes. This reading is reported as `history.fillet-edge-inferred`, and as `history.fillet-edge-ambiguous` when other candidates exist. When the supports of a cylinder blend share several preceding edges along its axis, the replaced edge is read by the covering rule. The span of a shared edge runs between the axial positions of the point rows of its start and end vertices. A shared edge covers the blend when its span reaches within `1e-6` mm of each end of the axial extent of the blend. Exactly one shared edge covers the blend; it is the replaced edge when its interior sample point lies more than `1e-6` mm beyond the radius from the axis line and the transition deletes it. The blend consumes every other shared edge that the transition deletes. This reading is reported as `history.fillet-edge-covering`. The position of an edge is the position of its interior sample point, and the axial extent of the blend spans the interior sample points of its boundary edges. A plane touches the cylinder when its normal is perpendicular to the axis and its distance from the axis line is within `1e-6` mm of the radius. When the transition inserts at least one face on a new carrier, every face that the transition lists as inserted has one carrier, every face that the transition inserts on a new carrier is a cylinder or torus blend with one finite positive radius, every face of the preceding and result topologies has a rebuilt boundary and one carrier, every face that owns a coedge on a boundary edge of a blend has a rebuilt boundary and each such edge has another owner face, every result face on a new carrier is new to the result and listed as inserted, or persists from the preceding topology unlisted on a carrier of the same geometry as its preceding carrier (planes with parallel normals through the same points, or cylinders on one axis line with one radius, within `1e-9` mm), every result face adjacent to a blend that persists from the preceding topology has one preceding carrier, every result face adjacent to a blend on a preceding carrier or without one carrier maps to one preceding face, every support has a rebuilt preceding boundary, every preceding edge that two supports of a blend share has a finite axis and a finite nonzero direction and tangent, the supports of each blend share exactly one preceding edge of the geometry that the blend replaces, or the blend is a cylinder whose supports share none and the candidate rule above reads an edge, or the blend is a cylinder whose supports share several and the covering rule reads an edge, and the transition deletes that edge; for both rules, the cylinder row has a finite origin and a radius within `1e-6` mm of the blend radius, and every boundary edge of the blend has one finite interior sample; for the covering rule, every shared edge has one vertex row, each of its vertices has one point row, each such point has one finite position, the covering edge has one finite interior sample, and no edge that the blend consumes is replaced by a blend or consumed by another blend; for the candidate rule, every preceding edge on the boundary of a support whose midpoint tangent does not run across the axis has a finite axis and a finite nonzero direction and tangent, every such edge along the axis has one finite interior sample, every support carrier that owns such an edge within the distance and extent bounds has no plane row, or one plane row with a finite origin and a finite nonzero normal and no cylinder, axis, or radius row, and such an edge without a touching support owner has a plane row on each support owner; no edge has two blends, and each blend radius is within `1e-6` mm of the radius of exactly one constant-radius group, the edges of each group's blends are that group's edges when the selection of every group of the feature agrees with the edges of its blends. A native or unresolved selection states no edge and agrees. A partial historical selection agrees when every edge that it states is one of these edges, and a complete historical selection agrees when it states exactly these edges. Every other selection disagrees. When every selection agrees, the edges of a group's blends replace its native or partial selection when the group has at least one blend, the native reference of the selection names exactly one construction group with the scope's record index and native stream, and that construction group has members. The replacement is a complete historical selection in the input topology that lists the edges in increasing stable-slot order. A complete selection, every other selection, and the selection of a group that does not meet these conditions stay.

The transition of a `Chamfer` feature states its edges with the scope, input state, and history rules of a `Fillet` feature. The chamfer replaces each edge that it bevels with a bevel face on a new plane carrier of the result topology. The supports of a bevel face share exactly one preceding edge whose midpoint tangent has a dot product of at most `1e-9` in absolute value with the unit normal of the bevel plane. That edge is the replaced edge, and the transition deletes it. Both supports are planes. The setback of a bevel on a support is the distance from the replaced edge to the line where the bevel plane cuts the support, measured within the support and perpendicular to the edge. A bevel belongs to the group whose `Distance` specification equals both setbacks, or whose `TwoDistances` specification equals the two setbacks in either order, within `1e-6` mm. When a bevel face has no such edge or more than one, a support is not a plane, the transition keeps the edge, two bevels replace one edge, a bevel matches no group or more than one group, a new carrier of the transition is not a bevel, or a selection disagrees with the bevel edges, no group of the feature binds.

#### Edge-recipe incidence matching

For each selector, an edge is an incidence match when, for every present clause entry, its incident loops contain both encoded boundary-count and coedge-ordinal incidences. Each selector retains all matching changed historical edge slots in stable slot order and separately retains the edge slot when that set is a singleton. Primary operand resolution uses the complete selector/reference intersection. An explicit reference run whose every candidate set is empty suppresses selector incidence and boundary-count proofs. It does not suppress a topology-triplet or deleted-topology proof, because those proofs derive the edge identity independently; every nonempty reference candidate set, when present, still intersects that identity. When the primary intersection is empty, exactly one singleton persistent-reference edge resolves the operand when the edge also belongs to the deleted boundary set and appears in a selector's incidence, boundary-count, or topology-triplet candidates. A construction group with a known preceding history state retains that state and every ordered operand identity even when none of its edge identities resolves.

A suppressed edge-treatment scope resolves its recipes against the unique terminal topology of its ASM history. The terminal state is the feature's replay input state. An operand's terminal face context is the ordered, deduplicated union of its primary persistent-reference faces and each prefix reference's exact-selector faces, falling back to that reference's alternate-selector faces only when its exact set is empty. Incidence, boundary-count, and common-triplet proofs operate on the resulting terminal boundaries without transition-only changed-edge filters and must resolve to one common slot. More than one terminal state in a history, or matching terminal states in more than one history, does not select a topology. Deleted-edge, treatment-radius, changed-context, and scope-partition proofs require an executed transition and do not apply. When the terminal recipe graph has no complete group proof, every proven edge and every unresolved operand identity form a partial historical selection.

#### Captured component positions

A Position scope has type GUID `8EE00B00-76BB-49AB-8C25-E837FEC5BDA5`, version 4 or 6. Its stored kind can be `Position` or `Posición`. The inline prefix starts with the eleven-byte indexed header in version 6, followed by eighteen zero bytes at offset 11 and a u32 row count at offset 29. Ordered rows start at offset 33. The count includes every row in source order; repeated targets remain separate rows. An empty row sequence has count zero.

Each Position row starts with byte zero at offset 0, a marked same-segment reference at offset 1, and a matrix marker at offset 12. The reference stores marker 1, a u64 record index at offset 2, and a zero u16 at offset 10. The record index fits u32. Matrix marker 0 is followed by sixteen row-major finite f64 coefficients at offset 13; that row spans 141 bytes. Matrix marker 1 omits the coefficients; that row spans 13 bytes.

The Position suffix spans 83 bytes in version 6 between the rows and the normal ordered-reference count. It stores u32 zero at offset 0, u32 value 36 at offset 4, the UTF-16LE text `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` at offset 8, and three zero bytes at offset 80. The last row ends at the suffix start. The suffix ends at the scope's ordered-reference count.

The version-4 prefix before the ordered-reference count spans 319 bytes. A u32 row count of one occurs at offset 95. The 141-byte row at offset 99 stores one matrix, with coefficients starting at offset 112. The version-4 suffix starts at offset 240 with the u32 GUID length, followed by the same UTF-16LE null GUID and three zero bytes.

Each row target selects an operand-path locator of type `2E3AC990-483D-4A55-8662-C064B976A957`. Version 4 uses locator version 3. Its 62-byte identity locator stores u32 discriminator one at offset 56. Version 6 uses locator version 5. The locator's backlink names the Position scope. Its ordered typed path records and wrapper use the assembly operand-path envelope. The ordinary marker-one wrapper is valid for a version-4 identity locator. A version-4 identity locator also uses a 37-byte wrapper of type `FF415D89-A1DB-44AC-B824-E9A772B86ED4`, version 1. The indexed header precedes ten zero bytes, marker zero at offset 21, u32 one at offset 22, and a marked reference to path record `N+1` at offset 26.

#### Assembly operands

A 297-byte `MotionLink` scope of type `29098FE8-08FC-4FD8-9D31-42CF164F73EB`
version 3 stores a marked relation reference at scope offset 43. In the
166-byte two-revolute form, that reference names the preceding indexed
record. The relation index is the scope index minus one. The relation type
is `3A218162-55F3-492E-93A4-390F8A56FBEA` version 2.

The 166-byte two-revolute relation stores u32 parent count 2 at offset 20
and two 15-byte parent entries at offsets 24 and 39. Each parent entry is
an eleven-byte marked reference and a u32. The reference names a version-5
Joint record. Marked references at offsets 63 and 74 repeat the two joint
identities in parent order. The u32 freedom codes at offsets 85 and 89
are both 2 for rotation about connector Z. The zero-phase, same-direction
form stores f64 zero at offset 93 and six zero bytes at offset 101.
Evaluated f64 angles at offsets 107 and 115 are in radians and correspond
to the two repeated references in order. The second angle divided by the
first gives the second joint's angular change per unit of first-joint
angular change.

The four direct-construction 421-byte `As-built` generations use one exact class and offset map:

| Scope primary / paired class | Scalar owner primary / paired class | Operand-carrier classes in reference order | Solved frame primary / paired class | Frame span; marker, matrix, and paired-header offsets | Limit source order and domain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `364 / 272` | `293 / 272` | `351 / 307`, `350 / 307` | `376 / 272` | 389 bytes; marker `+45..48 = 01 01 00 00`, matrix `+49`, pair `+389` | `AngleMinimum`, `AngleMaximum`; angular |
| `420 / 262` | `378 / 262` | `426 / 273`, `400 / 273` | `327 / 262` | 390 bytes; marker `+46..49 = 01 01 00 00`, matrix `+50`, pair `+390` | `DistanceMaximum`, `DistanceMinimum`; linear, reverse source order |
| `417 / 263` | `318 / 263` | `432 / 263`, `332 / 263`, `312 / 263`, `332 / 263` | `448 / 263` | 390 bytes; marker `+46..49 = 01 01 00 00`, matrix `+50`, pair `+390` | `DistanceMaximum`, `DistanceMinimum`; linear, reverse source order |
| `457 / 258` | `418 / 258` | `296 / 258`, `264 / 258`, `363 / 258`, `264 / 258` | `297 / 258` | 385 bytes; marker `+45..48 = 01 01 00 00`, matrix `+49`, pair `+385` | `DistanceMinimum`, `DistanceMaximum`; linear |

The class-430/262 `Assemble` generation uses class-313 parameter-owner
records with 103-byte owner frames. Its 744-byte scope uses the compact
operand-frame form: operand references at offsets 24 and 164, transforms at
offsets 36 and 176, and the two operand-path locators at offsets 362 and 373
after the count at offset 358. Its 748-byte scope uses the standard form:
operand references at offsets 28 and 168, transforms at offsets 40 and 180,
and the two operand-path locators at offsets 366 and 377 after the count at
offset 362. Both forms have eight owners. Owner ordinals 0 through 3 are
placement lanes; ordinals 4 through 7 are angle, X, Y, and Z alignment lanes.
The class pair is part of the admission key because the same frame lengths
occur in other scope families.

The version-3 `Assemble` scope has type GUID
`8DFDD543-F823-43AA-BDAF-C638E023F0A0`. Its version-three prefix contains the
eleven-byte indexed header, nine zero bytes, and an expansion byte `E`.
`E = 0` selects the compact prologue; `E = 1` adds four zero bytes. A facing
byte and two zero bytes follow. Each of two connectors contains a nonnull
local construction reference, an identity byte, and a row-major rigid 4×4
matrix when the identity byte is `0`. Identity byte `1` supplies the identity
matrix. All nonnull references in the scope have width `W`: eleven bytes for
plain local references or 51 bytes for typed local references. A typed
reference's inline GUID equals its target's registered type GUID.

Four zero bytes precede four nonnull alignment-owner references in angle,
Z-offset, X-offset, Y-offset order. Two zero bytes and a u32 additional-owner
count `K` follow. A positive count supplies `K` nonnull owner references and
selects the extended tail below. These owners follow the four alignment
owners in local-ordinal order and occur in the scope reference table.
The zero-count form occupies six zero bytes. U32 locator count `2`, two
nonnull locator references, and a nonnull joint reference follow. The joint
reference selects a version-3, version-4, or version-5 record of type GUID
`7F5A0426-1D2A-4DC4-9F06-58631F69D2F5`, including a joint shared by several
scopes. A length-prefixed UTF-16 GUID with 36 code units and three zero bytes
precede the counted scope-reference table. The table contains `R` nonnull
references. The four alignment-owner targets occur in this table. The current history word, the length-prefixed UTF-16 stored feature-family name, and
feature ordinal follow the table. The tail contains fifteen zero bytes, a
nonnull reference, an optional zero separator of length `S` (`0` or `1`), the
previous history word, a u32 word, a finite f64, an independent u32 word, a
nonnull reference, two boolean bytes, a nonnull reference, and two zero
bytes. The paired indexed header closes the scope with the same record
identity. The span from primary to paired header is
`190 + (R + 12) * W + 128 * M + 4 * E + S`, where `M` is the number of
explicit connector matrices. Owner references select alignment lanes
independently of owner ordinals and owner count. Locator type GUID
`2E3AC990-483D-4A55-8662-C064B976A957` and its registered version select the
locator envelope. Its counted wrapper joins consecutive version-4 occurrence
paths of type GUID `96CBEA21-17E0-4BCB-BA77-04EA87B47934`. The ordered
occurrence GUIDs traverse child occurrences within the selected insertion,
including child occurrences that insert another document. The scope
connector belongs to the innermost occurrence in that path.

The extended version-three tail adds a nonnull reference immediately after
the first tail reference and uses `S = 0`. Its target has type GUID
`074F9459-89C2-4B7D-8AB4-DCE67AE944FE`, version 1. Its span is
`190 + (R + K + 13) * W + 128 * M + 4 * E`. The native alignment retains
this additional reference and its marker offset as `additional_tail_reference`.
The plain-reference tail, from the feature ordinal through its final zero
bytes, has the fixed fields in
[the layout table](../layouts/f3d.md#assembly_version_three_extended_tail).
The typed-reference extended tail has four 51-byte references with inline
type GUIDs. Its previous-history word follows the added reference. Its fixed
fields are in [the typed layout table](../layouts/f3d.md#assembly_version_three_typed_extended_tail).

Version 5 uses the same type GUID and field order with these extensions.
Its joint reference selects type version 6.
Nine zero bytes follow the facing byte's two zero bytes. Each connector
stores six zero bytes between its reference and identity byte, and an
LP-UTF16 GUID of 36 code units after its identity byte or explicit matrix.
Two zero bytes follow the angle-owner reference. An additional nonnull
reference follows the first tail reference. This tail uses separator length
`S = 0`. One zero byte separates its two boolean bytes from its last
reference. Version 5 uses eleven-byte plain local references. Its span is
`377 + (R + K + 12) * 11 + 128 * M + 4 * E`. The four explicit owner references
select angle, Z, X, and Y lanes.
An additional-owner run follows the four explicit alignment references.
It stores two zero bytes, a u32 count `K`, and `K` nonnull plain local
references. These references name the scope's additional parameter owners
in local-ordinal order, starting at ordinal four. Their targets also occur
in the scope reference table. Each additional reference follows the count
or the preceding reference without padding. The four alignment owners
remain separate from this run.
Additional owners carry rotation and translation limits and rest values,
including `RotateMinimum`, `RotateMaximum`, `RotateRest`, `SlideMinimum`,
`SlideMaximum`, `SlideRest`, `YawMinimum`, `YawMaximum`, `YawRest`, and `RollRest`.
The version-five
expanded two-matrix layout with `R = 16` spans 945 bytes; its complete field
table is in [the layout table](../layouts/f3d.md#assembly_version_five_scope).

Version 4 uses the version-5 extensions with these differences. Its joint
reference selects type version 5. [Eight zero bytes](../layouts/f3d.md#assembly_version_four_prologue)
follow the facing byte's two zero bytes. Each connector stores a plain local
reference, six zero bytes, an identity byte, and its explicit matrix when
the identity byte is zero. The second connector follows the first connector
frame directly. Four zero bytes follow the second connector frame. No zero
bytes follow the angle-owner reference. The tail stores u8 `1` before its
two boolean bytes, and no zero byte follows them. Its span is `222 + (R + K + 12) * 11 + 128 * M + 4 * E`.

The span formulas count the eight code units of the stored family name
`Assemble`. A stored family name of `L` UTF-16 code units adds `2 * (L - 8)`
bytes to the span.

Each connector reference identifies a construction in its Design stream.
The operand path supplies the occurrence or document context that contains
that construction. The connector frame and alignment values remain fields
of the scope independently of the referenced occurrence's placement.

The scope matrices are operand-local connector frames. Let `C0` and `C1` be
these frames after composition with their operand poses. The mate equation
is `C0 = C1 * T(X, Y, Z) * Rz(angle) * F`. Angle is in radians; offsets and
matrix translations are in centimetres. Facing byte `0` selects identity
`F`; byte `1` selects a half-turn about the local X axis. The product order is
translation, rotation, facing. This equation defines the joint
relation. Occurrence transforms retain their stored placement.

The expanded two-matrix version-5 `Assemble` scope with sixteen reference-table
entries spans 945 bytes and uses the wide operand-frame form. It stores
`u8 1` at offset 20, four zero bytes, the frame-sense byte at offset 25, and zero
bytes at offsets 26 through 36. Its operand references are at offsets 37 and
259. Seven zero bytes follow each reference, rigid row-major transforms start
at offsets 55 and 277, and an LP-UTF16 GUID follows each transform. Its explicit
owner references select angle, Z, X, and Y alignment lanes. The
operand-path-locator count is at offset 537 and the two marked locator
references are at offsets 541 and 552.

The 806-, 850- and 861-byte `Assemble` scopes use the compact wide
operand-frame form. Bytes 11 through 20 are zero, byte 21 is the frame-sense byte,
bytes 22 through 31 are zero, the operand references are
at offsets 32 and 254, seven zero bytes follow each reference, rigid
row-major transforms start at offsets 50 and 272, and an LP-UTF16 GUID follows
each transform. The four parameter owners are the angle, X, Y, and Z alignment
lanes in owner-local order and are the first four entries of the reference
table. A u32 limit-owner count at offset 526 is `0` in the 806- and 861-byte
scopes. The 850-byte scope stores count `2` and the marked references to its
two limit owners, owner-local ordinals 4 and 5, at offsets 530 and 541; its
six owners are the first six entries of the reference table. The two
operand-path locators are wide operand-path locators; their marked references
are at offsets 534 and 545 in the 806- and 861-byte scopes and at offsets 556
and 567 in the 850-byte scope, after the count 2.

A frame-sense byte uses the facing term of the version-3 mate equation. An operand frame that names an occurrence path is in the space of the path's innermost occurrence. The frame sense is the projected joint's `operands.frame_sense`.

A wide version-five locator has prefix word 2 or 3. A null construction reference occupies one zero byte at 56. With flag 0 at 57, the rigid matrix starts at 58, the separator is at 186, the scope backlink at 187, the wrapper reference at 198, the discriminator at 209, and the two-byte zero tail at 213. This null-construction matrix locator spans 215 bytes. For version-three, version-four and version-five Assemble scopes, the scope connector supplies the operand frame; the locator path supplies its occurrence qualifier.

The null-construction identity variants span 77 bytes with a null wrapper and 87 bytes with a present wrapper. Their flag is 1 at 57, separator at 58, backlink at 59 and wrapper at 70. The discriminator and zero tail start at 71 and 75 for the 77-byte form, and 81 and 85 for the 87-byte form. A qualified operand requires a present wrapper.

A wide operand-path locator is the locator of the 945-, 806-, 850- and 861-byte `Assemble` scopes.
Its record type GUID is `2E3AC990-483D-4A55-8662-C064B976A957`. Its eleven-byte
header is followed by 28 zero bytes, a u32 prefix word at offset 39, 13 zero bytes,
a nonzero marked same-segment reference at offset 56, and an identity flag byte
at offset 67. Flag `0` is followed by a row-major rigid 4×4 transform at offset
68; flag `1` stores no transform. One zero byte follows the flag or the
transform, then a marked backlink to the assembly-operation scope, a marked
reference to its wrapper record (`N+2`, or `N+n+1` when the path continues),
u32 value 2, and two zero bytes. The locator
is 97 bytes with flag `1` and 225 bytes with flag `0`. Its path record and
wrapper follow it as in the common locator, or its typed path continues over
further typed path records `N+2` through `N+n`: the wrapper is then record
`N+n+1`, stores path count `n` at offset 22 and a marked reference to each
path record in order from offset 26, and is `37 + 11(n-1)` bytes. The
continuations' occurrence GUIDs extend the occurrence path in order. Each
record keeps its own four identity GUIDs in record order, so a path over `n`
records has `4n` identity GUIDs; when its root occurrence is not local, the
first record's first identity GUID is the unresolved external-document
identity. Each record's occurrence identity lists are kept in record order.

The class-283/264 and class-347/260 `Assemble` generations use class-289
parameter-owner records with 103-byte owner frames. Both use the standard
operand-frame prefix: operand references are at offsets 28 and 168, rigid
row-major transforms start at offsets 40 and 180. In the direct-path subform,
the operand-path-locator count is at offset 362 and the two marked locator
references are at offsets 366 and 377. The second transform ends at offset 308. The variable reference
trailer can start at that offset; there is no fixed zero tail marker. The total
scope span varies with the owner and reference trailers. Owner ordinals 0 through 7 are two placement groups. Owner ordinals
8 through 11 are the signed angle and signed local X, Y, and Z alignment
lanes. Further owners are complete four-lane placement groups, optionally
followed by one two-lane minimum/maximum limit group. The owner count is
therefore `12 + 4n` or `14 + 4n`. The four alignment-owner references occur
once as one contiguous run in the scope reference table; their position is
not fixed because operand and additional-owner references can precede or
follow them.

The class-406/261 `Assemble` scope is a 671-byte standard form. It has six
owners; the final two owners are its alignment lanes. Its two operand
references are at offsets 28 and 168, and their row-major rigid transforms
start at offsets 40 and 180. The operand-path count is at offset 384, with
marked locator references at offsets 388 and 399. The paired class-261 header
starts at offset 671. Each locator uses the fixed 190-byte envelope and the
37-byte wrapper; the path record is class-307 and uses the fixed four-identity
path form.

The class-388/266 `Assemble` scope is a 968-byte legacy form. It has 28 owners.
The class-388 form stores `01 00 00 00 00 01` at offsets 20 through 25.
The two marked operand references are at offsets 28 and 168.
The two row-major rigid operand transforms start at offsets 40 and 180.
The four alignment lanes are owner-local ordinals 4 through 7.
The class-388 form stores u32 value 35 at offset 478.
Thirty-five marked same-segment reference entries occupy offsets 482 through 866.
The first 24 alignment-scope owner references are at scope reference positions 0 through 23; the final four owner references are at positions 30 through 33.
The paired class-266 header starts at offset 968.
The class-388 form stores operand-path locator count 2 at offset 362. The two
marked operand-path locator references occupy offsets 366 and 377. The marked
external component reference follows the operand-path locator run. The
class-388 form stores a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 component identity at offset 399.
The fixed scope trailer stores four `ff` bytes at offset 867.
The UTF-16LE kind length is 8 at offset 871.
The kind payload is `Assemble`.
The feature ordinal follows the kind payload at offset 891.

The class-383/258 `Assemble` scope is a 1011-byte standard form. Its 20
parameter owners all use the class-284, 103-byte owner frame. Owner ordinals
0 through 7 and 12 through 19 are placement lanes. Owner ordinals 8 through
11 are the signed angle and signed local X, Y, and Z alignment lanes. The
scope reference table has 38 entries. Entries 0 through 11, 20 through 23,
and 33 through 36 are the owners in ordinal order. Entries 12 through 19
and 25 through 32 are two interleaved operand envelope groups. Entries 24
and 37 are the two operand carriers. The operand references are at scope
offsets 28 and 168, and their row-major rigid transforms start at offsets 40
and 180. Bytes 308 through 311 are zero. The paired class-258 header starts
at offset 1011.

Each operand envelope has a leading class-387 frame, an identity class-359
frame, a child class-387 frame, a second identity class-359 frame, two
class-394 face frames, and one class-359 identity frame after each face. The
leading and child class-387 frames are 188 and 199 bytes; each class-394
frame is 215 bytes; every class-359 frame is 282 bytes; and every paired
header is class 258. The leading class-387 frame references its class-359
identity at +70 and the owning scope at +177. The child class-387 frame
references its class-359 identity at +70, its leading class-387 frame at +81,
and the owning scope at +188. Each class-394 frame references its class-359
identity at +97 and the owning scope at +204. A class-359 identity stores
two 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUIDs at +37 and +113 and the owning scope
reference at +271. The four identities in one operand envelope contain the
same two GUID values.

Each operand carrier is a 410-byte class-378 frame. Its matrix at +49 equals
the corresponding scope transform. It references the child class-387 frame
at +197, the second class-394 frame at +212, the first class-394 frame at
+223, and the owning scope at +399. Four placement-owner references occupy
+242, +253, +264, and +275. Repeated references to the child, first face,
and second face occur at +290, +301, and +312. The carrier paired class-258
header starts at +410. A scope operand reference resolves only when it names
the carrier at the corresponding reference-table position and every fixed
envelope, identity, matrix, owner, and scope backlink above agrees. The
carrier and identity envelopes are the path locator and wrapper for the
external operand; the path record is class 386.

An `Assemble` or `As-built` scope stores finite alignment parameter owners.
The serialized frame length and total owner count select the lane layout in
fixed-span generations. The class pair is an additional admission key for the
744- and 748-byte forms and is the primary admission key for the variable-span
class-283/264 and class-347/260 generations.

The 381- and 403-byte `As-built` scopes store an empty property block. A presence
byte of one at offset 20 precedes a zero u32 property count at offset 21. The
zero u32 additional-owner count is at offset 47. The u32 locator count is two at
offset 51. The two marked locator references at offsets 55 and 66 precede the
marked joint reference at offset 77. The joint has index one less than the
scope. The u32 reference count at offset 167 is nine in the 381-byte scope
and eleven in the 403-byte scope. The four alignment owners appear once and
contiguously in the reference table in `OffsetX`, `OffsetY`, `OffsetZ`, and
`AngleZ` order.

The 399-byte `As-built` form and the 627-, 633-, 637-, and 692-byte `Assemble`
forms have exactly four owners. All four are alignment lanes in owner-local
order: signed angle, signed local X offset, signed local Y offset, and signed
local Z offset. The 378-, 422-, and 444-byte `As-built` forms are one form
with a counted run of additional owners. It stores the u32 additional-owner count `K` at
offset 43 and `K` marked owner references at offsets `47 + 11k`; its frame is
`378 + 22K` bytes and its reference table has `9 + K` entries. `K` is `0` in
the 378-byte form, `2` in the 422-byte form, and `3` in the 444-byte form. Its
owners are the `OffsetX`, `OffsetY`, `OffsetZ`, and `AngleZ` lanes at
owner-local ordinals zero through three, followed by the `K` additional owners in
the order of their references; its alignment angle is the `AngleZ` value and
its offsets are the other three. The four alignment owners appear once and
contiguously in the reference table, and every additional owner appears in it. The 378-byte form stores nine reference-table entries, with the four alignment owners at zero-based positions five through eight. The reference-table counts are at offsets 163, 185, and 196 in the 378-, 422-, and 444-byte forms, respectively. The 444-byte form's additional owners are the parameters named `SlideMinimum`, `SlideMaximum`, and `SlideRest`, in that order. Its stored owner value and the joint record's rest value are equal in both 444-byte scopes: each stores `0.0` cm, equivalent to `0.0` mm. The 604-byte datum-envelope form, the 732-byte joint form, and
the class-430/262 744- and 748-byte forms have exactly eight owners. Their
four placement owners are at local ordinals zero through three, and their four
alignment owners are at ordinals four through seven in the same angle, X, Y,
and Z order. The class-406/261 671-byte form has exactly six owners: four
placement lanes followed by its two alignment lanes. The 705-byte form has
exactly six owners: one group of `OffsetX`,
`OffsetY`, `OffsetZ`, and `AngleZ` placement lanes followed by `alignAngle`
and `alignOffset`. The 772-byte form has exactly ten owners: two such
placement groups followed by `alignAngle` and `alignOffset`. The final scalar
of each axial form is an alignment offset and maps to local Z. Joint forms store two
operand frames. The 627-, 637-, and 692-byte
forms store marked operand construction references at offsets 28 and 168 and
row-major rigid 4×4 operand-local-to-model transforms at offsets 40 and 180.
The 633- and 732-byte forms store the references at offsets 24 and 164 and the
transforms at offsets 36 and 176. The 705- and 772-byte forms store operand
references at offsets 28 and 167 and transforms at offsets 39 and 178. In the
378-, 399-, 422-, and 444-byte `As-built` forms, the locator records store
the operand construction references and transforms. The 378-, 422-, and
444-byte forms' locators are wide operand-path locators: each operand frame is its wide locator's nonzero
reference and transform, or the identity when the locator's identity flag is 1.

An `As-built` scope of type `AA8B3D40-B67D-4AF1-B3CF-E1E00279B5F0` version 1
with no additional owners can use two version-3 locators. Each locator has
either the compact null-construction layout or the ordinary construction
layout. The owner count at offset 43 is zero and the
locator count at offset 47 is two. The two locator references are followed
by a marked reference to the version-4 or version-5 joint at the scope index
minus one.
The reference-table count at offset 163 is seven or nine. The four alignment
owners occur once and contiguously in the reference table, in local order
`OffsetX`, `OffsetY`, `OffsetZ`, `AngleZ`. The scope tail from the feature
ordinal occupies 87 bytes. With the eight-code-unit name the scope spans
355 or 377 bytes. Each locator supplies one frame and its wrapper
names the typed occurrence paths in operand order.

The wide locator identity frame is 97 bytes. Its zero separator is at offset
68, scope backlink at 69, wrapper reference at 80, discriminator at 91, and
two zero tail bytes at 95. The wide locator matrix frame is 225 bytes. Its
matrix is at offset 68, zero separator at 196, scope backlink at 197, wrapper
reference at 208, discriminator at 219, and two zero tail bytes at 223.

A rigid-group scope has no parameter owners and stores the kind `As-built`.
Its member count `N` is at least two. The ordinary two-member rigid-group
scope has four tail combinations: 257/76, 258/77, 268/87, and 269/88
bytes (frame/tail).
Its indexed header occupies offsets 0 through 10;
eight zero bytes follow it. The leading-block presence byte at offset 19
and the property-block presence byte at offset 20 are zero. A zero separator
is at offset 21. A marked pathless-locator reference is at offset
22, four zero bytes are at offset 33, the u32 member count is at offset 37,
and the first marked member-locator reference is at offset 41. References are
eleven bytes. The next member reference is at offset 52. For two members,
the joint reference is at offset 63, the LP-UTF16 GUID is at offset 74,
three zero bytes are at offset 150, the empty reference-table u32 count is
at offset 153, the history-state u32 is at offset 157, and the LP-UTF16
`As-built` kind starts at offset 161. Its feature ordinal and scope tail
start at offset 181. For `N` members the joint reference and all later
fields shift by `11(N - 2)` bytes. The paired indexed header starts at
`159 + 11N + T`, where `T` is the tail width.

An alternate ordinary prologue stores nine zero bytes after its indexed
header. The leading-block presence byte at offset 19 is zero. The
property-block presence byte at offset 20 is 1, and the u32 property count
at offset 21 is zero. This is a present, empty property block. The canonical
form has property-block presence 0 and no property count. A zero separator
follows the block at offset 25 in the alternate form and offset 21 in the
canonical form. Both forms have no property entries; a nonempty property
block is outside these fixed layouts.
The alternate form's marked pathless-locator reference is at offset 26.
Four zero bytes at offset 37 precede the member count at offset 41.
Its member references start at offsets 45 and 56. The joint reference and
all later fields are four bytes after the corresponding canonical fields.
The alternate form uses the same member count, eleven-byte references,
empty reference table, and ordinary tail grammar. Its paired indexed header
starts at `163 + 11N + T`.

The ordinary rigid-group tail starts at the end of the LP-UTF16 kind.
It stores a nonzero u32 feature ordinal, fifteen zero bytes, an eleven-byte
local reference at offset 19, an optional eleven-byte local reference,
the preceding history-state u32, a u32, an f64, a u32, a local reference,
a variable-width field, a final local reference, and two zero bytes.
The variable-width field starts with a tag byte: tag 0 selects two bytes
in total; tag 1 selects three bytes in total. Other tags are refused.
Its payload has one byte for tag 0 and two bytes for tag 1.
The optional reference and field width are independent.

The 76-byte tail has no additional reference and has field tag 0.
The history-state word is at offset 30; the u32, f64, u32, and next local
reference are at offsets 34, 38, 46, and 50. The variable-width field is at
offset 61, the final reference at 63, and the two zero bytes at 74.
Tag 1 moves the final reference and zero tail one byte later and gives a
77-byte tail. The 88-byte tail has the additional local reference at offset
30 and field tag 1. The history-state word is at offset 41; the u32, f64,
u32, and next local reference are at offsets 45, 49, 57, and 61. The field
is at offset 72, the final reference at 75, and the two zero bytes at 86.
Tag 0 moves the final reference and zero tail one byte earlier and gives an
87-byte tail.

The optional reference is selected by unique exact closure. Its absence
and presence each give one candidate position for the field tag. Each
candidate must have valid local references and zero runs. Exactly one
candidate ends at the paired indexed header. Zero or multiple complete
candidates are refused. The member count and kind end also close the
scope prefix.

The typed two-member rigid-group scope is 537 bytes. Its indexed header and
eleven zero bytes have the same positions. The pathless-locator reference at
offset 22 is a 51-byte typed local reference. Four zero bytes start at offset
73. The u32 member count is at offset 77; the typed member-locator references
start at offsets 81 and 132. The typed joint reference is at offset 183,
the LP-UTF16 GUID is at offset 234, three zero bytes are at offset 310,
the empty reference-table u32 count is at offset 313, the history-state u32
is at offset 317, and the LP-UTF16 `As-built` kind starts at offset 321.
Its feature ordinal and 196-byte typed scope tail start at offset 341.
For `N` members the joint reference and all later fields shift by
`51(N - 2)` bytes. The paired indexed header starts at `435 + 51N`.
The tail form selects the reference width; the stored member count and
paired header must close the complete scope at that width.

A rigid-group member locator has type
`2E3AC990-483D-4A55-8662-C064B976A957`. Its registered type version and length
select the frame together. A length that does not match the version is refused.
In versions 2 and 3, its indexed header is followed by ten zero bytes and a
construction reference at offset 21. The reference is null or nonzero and local. Version 2 uses a 51-byte typed nonnull reference;
version 3 uses an eleven-byte nonnull reference. A null reference is one zero byte.
The identity flag immediately follows the reference. Flag 0 stores a rigid
matrix immediately after the flag; flag 1 omits the matrix. Version 3 stores
one zero byte after the flag or matrix. Version 2 has no such separator.
The scope backlink, wrapper reference, u32 discriminator and two zero bytes
close the locator. Both closing references use the version's nonnull local
reference width. A member locator has discriminator 2. The separately
referenced pathless locator has discriminator 0 and is not a member locator.
A nonnull construction reference selects the frame carrier. With a null
construction reference, the locator itself is the frame carrier.

A version-3 compact rigid-group locator is 180 bytes with a matrix and
52 bytes with identity. Its construction reference is null at offset 21;
the identity flag is at offset 22. The matrix starts at offset 23. The matrix
form has separator at offset 151, scope backlink at offset 152, wrapper reference at offset 163,
discriminator at offset 174 and zero tail at offset 178. The compact identity
form has separator at offset 23, scope backlink at offset 24, wrapper reference
at offset 35, discriminator at offset 46 and zero tail at offset 50.

A version-3 construction-bearing rigid-group locator is 190 bytes with a
matrix and 62 bytes with identity. Its construction reference starts at
offset 21 and its identity flag is at offset 32. The matrix starts at offset
33. The matrix form has separator at offset 161, scope backlink at offset 162,
wrapper reference at offset 173, discriminator at offset 184 and zero tail at
offset 188. The ordinary identity form has separator at offset 33, scope
backlink at offset 34, wrapper reference at offset 45, discriminator at offset
56 and zero tail at offset 60.

A version-2 typed rigid-group locator with a nonnull construction reference
has its identity flag at offset 72. The matrix form is 309 bytes, with matrix
at offset 73, backlink at offset 201, wrapper reference at offset 252,
discriminator at offset 303 and zero tail at offset 307. The identity form is
181 bytes, with backlink at offset 73, wrapper reference at offset 124,
discriminator at offset 175 and zero tail at offset 179.

A version-2 null-construction rigid-group locator has a null reference at
offset 21 and an identity flag at offset 22. The null-construction matrix form
is 259 bytes, with matrix at offset 23, backlink at offset 151, wrapper
reference at offset 202, discriminator at offset 253 and zero tail at offset
257. The null-construction identity form is 131 bytes, with backlink at offset
23, wrapper reference at offset 74, discriminator at offset 125 and zero tail
at offset 129. Version 5 uses the wide operand-path locator frame: 97 bytes
with identity or 225 bytes with a matrix.

A positive-count null-construction member path projects only through a
concrete local occurrence carrier or placement carrier join. Without that
join, the member remains native and contributes to `AssemblyJointUnprojected`.
A null construction reference does not select deletion or suppression.
A document identity does not select an occurrence.

Each member locator ends exactly at its first path record. The consecutive
path records end at the wrapper. The wrapper stores ten zero bytes after
its indexed header, byte 1 at offset 21, the u32 path-record count at offset
22, and its first path reference at offset 26. Each path has one reference
in that run. The wrapper uses 51-byte typed local references for a version-2
locator and eleven-byte references for versions 3 and 5. Its complete length
is `26 + CW` for path count `C` and reference width `W`. The next indexed
header starts exactly after the wrapper. Locator indices are distinct and
member envelopes do not overlap.

A typed root operand path is a 277-byte frame. Its indexed header has a
u32 tag length of 3, a three-digit ASCII class tag, and a u64 record index.
This fifteen-byte indexed header is followed by six zero bytes, u32 count 0
at offset 21, and the
LP-UTF16 root key `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` at offset 25.
Offset 101 stores u32 0, offset 105 stores u64 1, and offsets 113 and 189
store the two LP-UTF16 identity GUIDs. Offset 265 stores u32 2; eight zero
bytes at offset 269 close the frame. This path selects the current document
root and has no occurrence member. Its two identity GUIDs remain ordered.

The linked rigid-group joint motion has no freedom entry. Each member's
locator transform maps the common group frame into that member's local
space. The member placements compose with these transforms to give the
same frame. All member frames mate aligned.
Matrix translations are in centimetres. Alignment
angles are in radians and alignment offsets are in centimetres. The alignment
owner references are one ordered, contiguous scope-reference run unless an
exact generation layout specifies fixed positions. Each value is the
evaluated scalar duplicated from its parameter record by its parameter owner,
independent of the owner-frame class and width.


In a 421-byte `As-built` scope of the direct-construction generation, the eleven-entry reference table starts with its marked entry at offset 189. Offset 185 stores u32 value 11. Entries 0 and 1 form the first operand-carrier pair, entries 2 and 3 form the second pair, entries 4 through 7 are the placement owners in `OffsetX`, `OffsetY`, `OffsetZ`, and `AngleZ` order, entry 8 is the solved connector-frame carrier, and entries 9 and 10 are the two degree-of-freedom limit owners. Offset 310 stores four `ff` bytes, offset 314 stores u32 value 8, offset 318 stores the UTF-16LE string `As-built`, and offset 334 stores the feature ordinal. The canonical alignment values are the `AngleZ` value followed by the three offsets. Each row in the generation map supplies the carrier pair, solved frame, paired header, and limit interpretation. The frame carrier stores one solved connector-frame matrix; it does not store either operand-local frame. The two operand-carrier pairs are direct construction/selection pairs and do not use the operand-path locator run of the 399-byte form.

The first direct pair is a point construction followed by a face-recipe selection. The second is a point-and-direction Hole construction followed by a face-recipe selection. The primary construction classes and selection classes are the four class pairs listed in the generation table, in reference order. The construction record header is the `byte_offset` named by scope reference 0 or 2; the paired selection header is the `byte_offset` named by scope reference 1 or 3. The point position and Hole position are model-space centimetres. The Hole direction equals the third column of the solved frame's rotation matrix. No construction carrier stores an independent connector orientation.

The two face-recipe selections store their asset UUID, context UUID, recipe record, recipe family, and ordered recipe references. These UUIDs qualify a selection namespace in the current document; the 421-byte form contains no occurrence path, external-object envelope, or external-document identity. The selection record and recipe record indices remain part of the native identity because two selections can share a namespace and recipe family. The first neutral joint operand is the point/face pair and the second is the Hole/face pair, in that order. Both operands have no occurrence and no external-document qualifier. Their object identities are keyed by the selection asset UUID, context UUID, recipe identity, selection record index, and recipe record index.

The neutral connector frame for each pair copies the solved frame's complete rotation basis and replaces its translation with the paired construction position. Its reference record is the point or Hole construction record, its reference offset is the corresponding scope reference entry, and its matrix offset is the solved-frame matrix offset. The solved frame remains a separate native carrier. Alignment offsets and connector-frame translations convert from centimetres to millimetres; rotation bases and the alignment angle remain unchanged.

In a 705- or 772-byte scope, a component operand's frame reference names a paired construction carrier after the scope's paired header. The fixed span from the primary header through the paired header is 391 bytes. The carrier's row-major rigid transform starts at offset 48 and equals the operand-frame transform. Marked same-segment axis-record references start at offsets 192 and 208. The carrier's paired indexed header starts at offset 380 and has the same record index as its primary header. The two axis-record indices are distinct. Each axis record has one primary and one paired indexed header before the construction carrier. For each axis-record index `A`, the scope reference table contains exactly one consecutive `(A, A+3)` pair; `A+3` is the selector-record index.

An axial selector primary record has a 37-byte fixed prefix: its eleven-byte indexed header, eleven zero bytes, a marked same-segment reference to the selector-record index plus three, and u32 value 1. Two 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 GUIDs follow in selector-asset and selector-context order. They are followed by u32 values 2, 0, and 1, a nonzero marked same-segment occurrence reference, and u32 value 1. The external-object reference then stores byte 1, a nonzero u64 object reference, byte 1, a u32 segment, an LP-UTF16 asset GUID, one zero byte, a nonempty LP-UTF16 link name, and an optional-tail byte. Optional-tail value 0 ends the reference. Value 1 adds an LP-UTF16 property GUID and a nonempty LP-UTF16 version identity. The external asset GUID equals the selector asset GUID. The selector's paired indexed header has the same record index and follows the external-object reference. The occurrence-role record at selector-record index plus five starts with its eleven-byte indexed header, ten zero bytes, u32 value 1, and the u32 code-unit count of a 36-code-unit LP-UTF16 role GUID; the role GUID payload starts at offset 29.

The two selectors of one construction carrier have the same selector GUIDs, external-object reference, segment, external asset GUID, link name, optional property GUID, version identity, and role GUID. Their axis-specific occurrence references can differ. The common role GUID uniquely identifies the `Component Insert` scope whose component construction carries that role. The insertion's projected occurrence qualifies the operand, and the selectors' common external-object identity names its connector. A frame reference can instead equal one `JointOrigin` scope record index while its transform equals that origin's solved frame. This form selects the current document root: the neutral operand has no occurrence or external-document qualifier, and its object is the `JointOrigin` feature.

The 705- and 772-byte forms store no occurrence paths. Each other two-operand form stores a u32 count of two followed by two marked same-segment operand-path-locator references. The 378- and 399-byte `As-built` forms store the count at scope offset 47 and the references at offsets 51 and 62. The 422- and 444-byte `As-built` forms store them `11K` bytes later, after their `K` additional-owner references: at offsets 69, 73, and 84, and at offsets 80, 84, and 95. The 627-, 637-, and 692-byte forms store the count at scope offset 362 and the references at offsets 366 and 377. The 633- and 732-byte forms store the count at offset 358 and the references at offsets 362 and 373. The class-430/262 744-byte form stores the count at offset 358 and the references at offsets 362 and 373; its 748-byte form uses offset 362 and offsets 366 and 377. Each reference resolves to exactly one locator envelope after the scope's paired indexed header. The locator record indices are distinct, and the two envelopes do not overlap. The first locator reference qualifies the first operand frame and the second locator reference qualifies the second operand frame. For the 378-, 399-, 422- and 444-byte `As-built` forms, each locator's nonzero reference at locator offset 21 is the operand construction reference and its transform at locator offset 33 is the operand frame.

The direct-path subform of the class-283/264 and class-347/260 generations uses a 180-byte locator envelope. Its rigid transform starts at offset 23, one zero separator is at offset 151, its owning-scope backlink is at offset 152, its path-wrapper reference is at offset 163, u32 value 2 is at offset 174, and two zero tail bytes occupy offsets 178 and 179. One or more consecutive class-330 path records immediately follow the locator. Each contributes its ordered occurrence GUID and four identity GUIDs to one operand path. A class-330 path whose first occurrence GUID is not a current-document occurrence identifies an external operand; its first identity GUID is the external document identity. The class-397 wrapper follows the final path record. Its byte at offset 21 is one, its u32 at offset 22 is the path-record count, and its marked reference at offset 26 names the first path record. Each further path record has one marked reference in an eleven-byte run starting at wrapper offset 37. The wrapper length is therefore `37 + 11(C - 1)` for path-record count `C`.

The class-307 JointOrigin scope is 366 bytes and has a paired class-264 header. It is a pathless operand qualifier for the current document root. Marked references occur at +21 and +33. One 36-code-unit identity GUID starts at +44. A three-byte separator starts at +120. A u32 reference count 12 at +123 introduces twelve marked references starting at +127. Four FF bytes follow the reference table. The 11-code-unit `JointOrigin` kind starts at +263, and the feature ordinal is at +289. An operand frame that references this scope uses the scope's solved transform and projects an operand with no occurrence or external-document qualifier. A variable-reference `Assemble` can pair this qualifier with a class-363 occurrence-path qualifier; operand-frame order fixes operand order.

An assembly joint has a joint record and, when the joint has relative motion, a motion record. An adjacent-joint `Assemble` scope references the joint record whose index is one less than its scope's; the motion record stores a marked same-segment reference to the joint record at offset 24. In the earlier generation, which has no `Assemble` scope, the motion record's index is one more than its joint record's, and the motion record references the joint record. A motion record stores one freedom entry for each degree of freedom: byte `1`, f64 `0`, f64 π, a u32 word, and the u32 freedom code. The word is `3` or `1`, and an entry whose word is `1` stores an f64 after its code. A word-`1` entry can store f64 `0` in place of π; a motion record whose entries store π stores no such entry. A joint whose motion record has no freedom entry is rigid. Freedom code `1` is a rotation about the joint's local y axis, code `2` a rotation about its local z axis, and code `8` a translation along its local z axis. Eleven bytes after its marked self-reference, the joint record stores two limit flag bytes, each `0` or `1`. Twenty-three bytes after the self-reference it stores the finite f64 maximum followed by the finite f64 minimum. A rotation's limits are in radians and a translation's are in centimetres. A joint without limits stores flags `0 0` and zero values. Thirteen bytes after the self-reference, after the two limit flags, the joint record stores the rest flag byte, `0` or `1`. Thirty-nine bytes after the self-reference, after the minimum, the joint record stores the finite f64 rest value in the same unit. The rest value can be nonzero while the rest flag is `0`.

A version-3 motion record of type `8C188F11-5D1B-4E1C-8E87-AF7214CA3C83`
stores its parent count at offset 20 and its first parent reference at
offset 24. Each 15-byte parent entry stores an eleven-byte marked reference
followed by a u32. Version 2 uses the same parent run. In the compact
As-built form, the final parent reference
names the joint. Version-2 motion names a version-4 joint. Version-3 motion
names a version-5 joint. The preceding entries, when present, name
occurrence records of type `CE2913AA-CFE0-4F04-9102-24424ED3BCFA` version 2.

The class-363 carrier subform uses the operand-frame reference as its locator.
The class-363 frame is 389 bytes and has a paired class-264 header. Its rigid
transform starts at +49 and equals the operand-frame transform. References at
+197 and +213 name a leading class-360 node and a terminal class-386 node.
Four placement-owner references occupy +232 through +275. The leading and
terminal references repeat at +280 and +291. The owning-scope backlink is at
+378. A class-360 node references its class-388 identity at +70. Its 188-byte
leading form references the scope at +177. Its 199-byte child form references
the leading class-360 node at +81 and the scope at +188. A terminal class-386 node is 215 bytes;
it references its class-388 identity at +97 and the scope at +204. Both have
paired class-264 headers. A class-388 identity stores the occurrence GUID at
+37 and component identity GUID at +113. Its short compact form is 612 bytes
and backlinks to the scope at +601. Its compact form is 614 bytes and
backlinks at +603. Its extended form is 690 bytes and backlinks at +679. All
forms have a paired class-264 header. Two reduced forms are 490 and 501 bytes;
their scope backlinks are at +479 and +490. The two identities of one
carrier contain equal GUIDs. The occurrence GUID qualifies the operand and the
component identity GUID identifies its external component.

In the standard two-operand form, an operand-path locator is a fixed 190-byte indexed record with record index `N`. Its eleven-byte header is followed by ten zero bytes, a nonzero marked same-segment reference at offset 21, one zero byte at offset 32, a row-major rigid 4×4 transform at offset 33, one zero byte at offset 161, a marked backlink to the assembly-operation scope at offset 162, a marked reference to record index `N+2` at offset 173, u32 value 2 at offset 184, and two zero bytes at offset 188. The occurrence-path record starts at locator offset 190 and has record index `N+1`. The next indexed record is its wrapper at record index `N+2`. The wrapper is exactly 37 bytes: its eleven-byte indexed header, ten zero bytes, byte value 1 at offset 21, u32 value 1 at offset 22, and a marked reference to path record `N+1` at offset 26. The next indexed record starts at wrapper offset 37.

In a compact placement or rigid-group `As-built` scope, a version-3 locator at
index `N` can reference a version-1 wrapper of type
`FF415D89-A1DB-44AC-B824-E9A772B86ED4` at index `N+3`. The version-4
occurrence path at `N+1` stores two consecutive occurrence keys and four
identity GUIDs. The 37-byte wrapper immediately follows the path and names it
as its sole member. The first key names the parent occurrence and the second
names its child. For an external placement, the child belongs to the member
document.

The class-388/266 legacy locator run uses class `451` for each 190-byte locator and class `369` for each wrapper. A class-451 locator keeps the same fixed offsets and backlinks as the common locator. Its wrapper reference names the class-369 record at `N + count + 1`, where `count` is the class-369 path count. A class-369 wrapper stores ten zero bytes, byte value 1 at offset 21, and path count 1 or 2 at offset 22. A class-369 wrapper stores marker 1 and its path count. A class-369 wrapper with path count 1 is 37 bytes. A class-369 wrapper with path count 2 is 48 bytes. Count 1 uses one marked path reference at offset 26 and a 37-byte span. Count 2 adds a marked path reference at offset 37 and has a 48-byte span. A class-369 wrapper stores one marked path reference at offset 26. A class-369 wrapper stores two marked path references at offsets 26 and 37. The referenced class-412 path records have consecutive indexes `N + 1` through `N + count` and each has a 425-byte span. A class-412 path record is 425 bytes in the class-388 legacy envelope. The class-412 path prefix stores ten zero bytes, marker 1 at offset 21, and three zero bytes at offsets 22 through 24. A class-412 path stores one occurrence GUID followed by four identity GUIDs. The class-412 path stores u64 value 2 between its identity pairs. The class-412 path stores u32 value 2 before its zero tail. The wrapper order is the occurrence order. The occurrence GUIDs from all wrapper members form the ordered occurrence path; the four identity GUIDs from the final wrapper member form the identity suffix.

A class-329 path begins with its indexed header, six zero bytes, a positive u32 path count, and exactly that many LP-UTF16 occurrence GUIDs in outermost-to-innermost order. It either ends at the wrapper after the occurrence run or continues with the identity suffix. A class-294 or class-299 path begins with its indexed header, six zero bytes, u32 value 1, three zero bytes, one LP-UTF16 occurrence GUID, two LP-UTF16 identity GUIDs, u64 value 2, two more LP-UTF16 identity GUIDs, u32 value 2, and a zero tail ending at the wrapper. The class-329 identity-qualified form and class-386 and class-390 paths append two LP-UTF16 identity GUIDs, u64 value 2, two more identity GUIDs, u32 value 2, and a zero tail ending at the wrapper after the occurrence run. The first occurrence GUID names the component occurrence containing the selected connector. Remaining occurrence GUIDs are the ordered descent path within that component. A descent key selects the occurrence placed directly below the previous one whose source occurrence key it equals, whether that occurrence is local or an external placement (§1.4); keys after the last selected occurrence remain operand subelements. In a standalone document, a different rule applies to the joint of an `Assemble` scope that has a frame-sense byte and a registered type of version 3, 4, or 5, other than the 945-byte two-matrix scope of a version-4 or version-5 type: when each operand is either the document root with no remaining keys or an occurrence operand whose descent selects no ambiguous child and ends at an occurrence with no keyed child occurrences, the remaining keys of each occurrence operand form the nested occurrence path inside that occurrence's document. A keyed child occurrence is a child whose local occurrence carrier or external placement stores an occurrence key. Below an external placement, a member root occurrence without its own occurrence key consumes no descent key, and the next key selects a child whose local occurrence carrier stores the same occurrence key, without regard to letter case. A member root with its own occurrence key is selected by that key like any other child. A descent key selects an occurrence only when the child match is unique; two matching children make the descent ambiguous. The four identity GUIDs are retained in source order. A class-294 or class-299 path whose root occurrence key resolves in the containing Design stream identifies that occurrence. A placement's source occurrence UUID can supply that key. A class-386 path whose root occurrence is not local uses its first identity GUID as the unresolved external-document identity. The positive-count form of a path record whose type GUID is `96CBEA21-17E0-4BCB-BA77-04EA87B47934` has the identity-qualified form whatever its dynamic class tag: the occurrence run, two identity GUIDs, u32 value 2, a u32 pair word, two more identity GUIDs, u32 value 2, a second u32 pair word, and the zero tail. Each pair word is 0 or 1. In place of the zero tail after its second pair word, such a path can store a positive u32 list count and that many lists; each list is a u32 key count of at least 2 followed by that many LP-UTF16 occurrence identities, each a decimal occurrence key or an occurrence GUID. The path ends at the wrapper after the last list. Its root occurrence can be external, and its first identity GUID is then the unresolved external-document identity. Occurrence translations, connector-frame translations, and the three alignment offsets are in centimetres. The alignment angle is in radians.

A Design circular-pattern scope stores one seed operand group with role `0x0000000400000000` or `0x0000000800000000`, one count owner at owner-local ordinal zero, one total-angle owner at owner-local ordinal one, and one axis construction. Role `0x0000000400000000` selects faces through entity-selection operands. Role `0x0000000800000000` selects bodies through whole-body recipe operands. The count is a positive integer including the seed. The total angle is a positive scalar in radians. Both owner values are duplicated from their parameter records and are independent of the owner-frame class and width. The 195-byte axis record stores a three-component origin in centimetres at offset 25 followed by a three-component displacement in centimetres at offset 49; the neutral unit axis direction is the normalized displacement. The displacement is nonzero and finite. Its marked selection reference identifies the persisted axis operand. A scope can contain this record and an earlier axis record. Exactly one 195-byte record supplies the solved axis when it is present. An earlier record supplies the axis only when the scope contains no 195-byte record and contains exactly one earlier record. Multiple 195-byte records or multiple earlier records without a 195-byte record leave the axis unresolved. The earlier axis record has a 129-byte and a 130-byte two-wrapper form and a 118-byte compact form. Both begin after the indexed header and ten zero bytes. The two-wrapper form stores u32 one, a marked wrapper reference, u32 one, the marked seed-member reference, u32 one, a second marked wrapper reference, and the marked scope reference. The compact form stores u32 zero, u32 one, the marked seed-member reference, u32 one, one marked wrapper reference, and the marked scope reference. All then store a repeated nonzero u32 around a finite f64, marked references to axis-record indexes plus two and one, and a second marked scope reference. Two zero bytes separate the references to the indexes plus two and plus one; the 130-byte form stores `u8 1` and two zero bytes there instead, and each later field is one byte later. Each wrapper stores a nonzero u64 lane, the asset and context GUIDs, a nested two-record chain, and a persistent u64 identity. Both wrappers in the expanded form carry the same persistent identity. A historical edge, coedge, curve, pcurve, vertex, or point identity supplies the unique analytic carrier axis in the feature's preceding history topology. If the scope has no preceding history state, the identity must yield the same model-space axis line in every state containing it. A face identity supplies the axis of its unique analytic surface carrier: a planar carrier uses its normal, and a cylindrical, conical, or toroidal carrier uses its axis; a surface identity supplies the axis of its unique analytic carrier, using a planar normal or a cylindrical, conical, or toroidal axis. An identity that does not resolve directly is a snapshot-local record ordinal only when exactly one archived record occupies that ordinal and the record is an edge; the record's positive revision identity selects the historical edge. A selected historical edge uses the axis of its line, circle, or ellipse carrier. An edge without such a carrier uses the common model-space axis line of its incident cylinder, cone, and torus surface carriers. Missing carrier bindings, multiple bindings for one selected face, or conflicting incident surface axes leave the axis unresolved. A whole-body recipe member selects the unique body in the preceding history topology identified by its persistent recipe. When no preceding history state exists, the recipe's Design id and selector join to one current persistent body link; if candidate faces are present, that body must occur in their body incidence. Without that link, a direct model-body selection resolves only when every reference maps to one common body, displayed bodies take precedence over cache bodies, and group members map to distinct bodies. Pattern face operands name result-face equivalence classes. A selected source face is the unique changed face in the preceding history topology whose procedural surface radius equals the one radius shared by every result face in that equivalence class. Missing radii, unequal result radii, or more than one matching changed face leave the source face unresolved. A circular-pattern axis record can have the 221-byte form of the rectangular-pattern direction record with selection kind `8`. The axis passes through the origin at offset 25 along the normalized displacement at offset 49, as for the 195-byte record. A 221-byte record supplies the axis only when the scope contains no 195-byte record, and exactly one 221-byte record supplies it; it takes precedence over an earlier axis record. The instances turn counterclockwise about the displacement. A total angle of one turn places adjacent instances the total angle divided by the count apart. A smaller total angle places the last instance at the total angle and adjacent instances the total angle divided by count minus one apart. A circular-pattern scope can store an indexed circular-pattern payload. After the indexed header and ten zero bytes, payload offset 21 stores the symmetric byte: `1` places the instances on both sides of the seed, half the total angle to each side, and `0` places them on one side. Marked references to the total-angle owner and the axis record start at offsets 22 and 33. A u32 reference count at offset 44 and that many marked references follow. The circular distribution block comes next: eight zero bytes, u32 `2`, a u32 seed kind (`0` faces, `1` features, `2` bodies), u32 `0xffffffff`, and byte `1`. A u32 entry count, that many sixteen-byte entries, a u32 instance count equal to the pattern count, and that many marked references to generated-instance records follow. The payload closes with the 37-byte suffix of the rectangular-pattern payload: marked references to the count owner, the pattern scope, and the seed construction-operand group, and four zero bytes.

A Design rectangular-pattern scope stores four parameter owners in owner-local order: U instance count, V instance count, U extent, and V extent. Each count is a positive integer including the seed. A direction with count one holds only the seed, and its extent can be nonzero. A direction with count greater than one and a nonzero signed distance is active, and at least one direction is active. A direction with count greater than one and zero distance repeats the seed in place: its instances coincide with the instances of the other direction. Distances are stored in centimetres. A pattern payload with a distribution block states the distance type of both distance owners. In a scope without that block, a 220-byte or 196-byte direction record makes the distance the seed-to-final-instance extent, and a 221-byte or 195-byte direction record makes it adjacent spacing. Adjacent spacing is the extent divided by count minus one. Each value is the evaluated scalar duplicated by its parameter owner, independent of the owner-frame class and width.

When exactly one rectangular-pattern direction is active and the scope reference table holds no direction record, the scope references the seed record, the four parameter owners, a metadata record, one generated-instance record per non-seed instance, and an aggregate record. The seed and generated-instance records contain a unique common-basis transform run whose translations divide the signed seed-to-final extent into equal intervals. Transform translations are stored in centimetres.

A rectangular-pattern direction record has a 220-byte, 221-byte, 195-byte, or 196-byte form. The 220-byte form has its paired header at offset 220. The scope reference table stores direction records in U-then-V order, and the reference after each direction record is its selection operand. The 220-byte form stores one record for each active direction or carries V in the pattern payload. A scope can also store both direction records, direction one first, when one direction has count one; the record of that inactive direction places no instance. The 221-byte form can store the U record and carry V in that payload. When direction one is not active and a pattern payload with a V displacement is bound, the decoder reads the one record that the payload names as its U-direction record as the direction-one record, direction two takes the payload V displacement, and `feature.rectangular-pattern-direction-one-record-assumed` is charged; DR-895 records this reading. After the indexed header and ten zero bytes, a direction record stores a u32 selection kind `8` or `16` at offset 21, a three-component origin in centimetres at offset 25, and a three-component displacement in centimetres at offset 49. Selection kind `8` selects a linear edge: the origin is the edge start point and the displacement is the edge vector. Sixteen zero bytes follow the displacement. Offset 89 stores u32 `8`, and offsets 93, 101, and 109 store f64 `-1.0`. Offset 117 stores u32 `1`, and the marked selection-operand reference starts at offset 121, followed by two zero bytes. Offset 134 stores u32 `1`, and a marked reference starts at offset 138. Offset 149 stores u64 `0x0000000400000000`, followed by ten zero bytes. Offset 167 stores a nonzero u32, offset 171 a finite f64, and offset 179 the same u32. Marked references to the direction record's index plus two and plus one start at offsets 183 and 197; `u8 1` and two zero bytes separate them. One zero byte and the marked scope reference at offset 209 close the frame. The displacement is nonzero and finite; selection kind `16` stores a unit displacement. For both selection kinds the direction of the pattern is the normalized displacement, and a negative extent reverses it. When a scope stores both a direction record and a generated-instance transform run of one active direction, the run states the direction; a record that states another direction charges `feature.rectangular-pattern-direction-record-disagrees`.

The 221-byte spacing direction form has the same header, selection kind, origin, displacement, and sixteen zero bytes as the 220-byte form. Offset 89 stores u32 `7` or `10`; offset 93 is a zero byte. Every field from the 220-byte form's offset 93 onward is one byte later. Its paired header starts at offset 221. All direction records in one scope have the same form. The direction record's selection reference names the following selection operand.

The compact spacing direction form is a 195-byte frame. Its paired header starts at offset 195. It stores the indexed header, selection kind, origin, displacement, zero runs, and distance type at the same offsets as the 220-byte form through offset 92. Distance type is `7`. The selection count starts at offset 93. Fields from the 220-byte form's offsets 117 through 193 are 24 bytes earlier.
